title: The platform-admin login stamps a claim of its own, so the gateway can refuse tenantless tokens except platform admins (KS-619 follow-up)
description:
**BLUF:** KS-619 needs a marker that does not exist yet. The gateway should refuse a token that carries no tenant, except for a platform admin; but nothing in a platform admin's token says it came from the platform-admin login, and the roles that login mints are not in the shared platform-role list, so a refusal keyed on role locks them out of the whole gateway. The fix Kam chose: the platform-admin login stamps one claim that only that branch sets; the gateway's tenant refusal excepts it; refresh tokens carry it; platform admins re-login once after it deploys. Two services (auth and api-gateway), tier 1, security. Kam ruled the split on 2026-11-09 17:20:38 (card `secuura-ks619-platform-admin-login-no-marker-1109`, option a, "Split"); the tenant-refusal half of KS-619 comes out of PR 2128, which keeps only the user-id and role guard (no lockout), and this ticket carries the rest.

## The ruling, quoted

Kam, verbatim (live board, 17:20:38): "Decision secuura-ks619-platform-admin-login-no-marker-1109: a — Split". Option a: "PR 2128 keeps only the user-id and role guard (no lockout). KS-619 becomes its own ticket: the platform-admin login stamps one claim and the gateway excepts it. Two services, tier 1; platform admins re-login once after it deploys."

## Facts, each with its source

1. **The refusal locked a population out (gate 285, finding G285-1, MEDIUM).** Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-09_gate285-tier1-pr2128-ks1208-ks619/verdict.md`, from line 21, on PR 2128 head `aff0f43e4079`. The login issues the roles `platform_admin`, `platform_viewer` and (the Azure default) `admin`, with no tenant. The shared `isPlatformRole` (`Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts`) is false for all three (the gate measured it with node on the built dist; controls `super_admin`, `system_admin` and `Super_Admin` are true). With the refusal in place and a token shaped as that login mints it, the gate's cells read: platform_admin on a required mount, develop 200 and head 401; platform_viewer on a required and on an optional mount, develop 200 and head 401; controls (a super_admin with no tenant, and an owner token) unchanged. It fails closed, so the gate did not call it a hole.
2. **Reach was not measured.** The gate did no live count. The note in KS-1536 says a Kintsugi count found no `platform_admin` rows on that path; `platform_viewer` and `admin` were not counted, and Azure was never counted.
3. **The code today, re-read by me.** At develop `6beac8734a2f` (Wednesday's addendum cites Seat G 31st's read of the same lines), the platform-admin login in `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` builds its `syntheticUser` with `tenantId: undefined` and `tenantSlug: undefined` (lines 394 to 410) and mints with `role: platformAdmin.role` (lines 470 to 473). `generateAccessToken` in `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts` (lines 187 to 209) builds one claim set for every login mint (`userId`, `email`, `role`, `organizationId`, `verificationLevel`, `sessionId`, `type`, `tenantId`, `tenantSlug`, then scopes or the OAuth labels), and `signToken` (lines 175 to 182) signs with the single provisioned key with no issuer or audience option. So no claim distinguishes a platform-admin login from any other mint, which is why the refusal had to go by role.
4. **The build shape is Kam's** (card above, option a): the login stamps one claim only that branch sets; the gateway's tenant refusal excepts it; refresh tokens carry it; platform admins re-login once after the deploy. Which claim name and value, and how the gateway verifies it, are for the build to propose.

## Not done, not measured

No live count of platform-admin rows (point 2). I did not re-read the gateway's present handling of a token with no tenant claim, or the refresh-token path. Nothing was run.

## Related

KS-619 (the gateway falls through to the caller's tenant header when a token has no tenant claim; this ticket is its remaining half) and KS-1208 (a verified token without a role or userId claim; PR 2128 delivers its guard). Both are linked as related.

## Searched before filing

Board, includeArchived, title and description and every comment of each open candidate; controls pass (the positive control hit its known ticket KS-1379, a random token hit 0). `KS-619`: 13 candidates, 10 open literal hits (KS-621, KS-1032, KS-1084, KS-1091, KS-1536, KS-1553, KS-1673, KS-1704, KS-2109, KS-2145), none a ticket for a login claim; KS-619 itself was read (its description to 2,600 characters and its two newest comments). `platform-admin login`: 94 candidates, 5 open (KS-783 and KS-919 on TOTP recovery and the demo account's MFA, KS-1132 on an infrastructure failure read as no admin, KS-1384, KS-2120): KS-2120 was read, it rewords one comment about this login (PR 2112) and carries no claim work. `tenantless token`: 93 candidates, 4 open (KS-1406, KS-1652, KS-1655, KS-1740): KS-1406 was read, it is the users lookup and stub guard that fails open for a tenantless token, a different route and fix. `platform_admin`: 108 candidates, 18 open, judged by title and search context; the near neighbours are KS-1536 (the role vocabulary) and KS-1132. No open ticket carries the claim-and-exception work.

title: Anchoring docs must say, after KS-1384 stage 1: one anchor row per document, a paid transaction per share and lifecycle event
description:
**BLUF:** The platform-k pages that describe anchoring do not yet record how anchoring behaves now that KS-1384 stage 1 is on both boxes (Stuart's words, 2026-11-09). They must state two facts, and nothing else new: (1) there is one anchor row per document and network; (2) until KS-1384 stage 2, every admitted share and lifecycle event pays its own Cardano transaction on that same row, and the row then names only the latest transaction. Stuart asked for this ticket before KS-1807 closes: it is the part of the S<->K contract that systemTest most needs written down. This is a DOCS build item: a build seat writes the pages. No code changes, and nothing is built for the paid-transaction behaviour (Kam's ruling below).

## What the pages must state

1. **One anchor row per document and network.** The unique key on `(document_id, network)` is migration 031. A repeat post upserts that row instead of adding one.
2. **Until KS-1384 stage 2, each admitted share and lifecycle event pays its own transaction on the same row.** An admitted event carries a new payload, so no earlier attempt counts as the same one; it builds a new transaction, and the row then names only the latest transaction hash. Stage 1 did not add this and was not built to stop it: its shared-coin rule covers repeat attempts of one payload. Stage 2 gives each event its own row, on its own schedule.
3. **Do not write** that stage 1 stops an event paying again, or that a share is "idempotent" at the transaction level. The route's code comment says "idempotent: reuses the document's existing anchor", which holds for the anchor id and not for the transaction.

## The authority, quoted

Kam's card `secuura-ks1384-share-pays-second-tx-before-stage2-1106`, ruled option a at 2026-11-06 21:04:52 (AEDT): "Leave it until stage 2". The option's own words: "Admitted events keep paying one fee each. Nothing is built for this. Stage 2 gives each event its own row, on its own schedule."

## The measurement behind it (KS-1384, two comments of 2026-11-06, read whole)

* Comment e0731289 (08:36:03Z): the share route calls `emitLifecycleAnchor`, which posts to `POST /api/anchors`; the upsert sets the row back to pending with a null hash and `processAnchor` runs again. Every post stamps its own `timestamp`, so the payload differs. Measured on the real submitter and wallet view with a stand-in chain and the upsert simulated from its SET list: a share whose payload replaces the stored one built a second transaction on a second coin and the row ended naming the second hash. Transfer-custody, revoke and lifecycle events use the same emitter, so by code they behave the same; not observed. Not measured: the fee of either transaction, which route posted the share, any other document.
* Comment 2126a1f7 (08:40:40Z): a read-only box read on kintsugi at 2026-11-06 08:34:59Z found 1 row in the anchor table for the document, status confirmed, naming the share's transaction; the upload's transaction was in 0 rows. The comment's own limit: one table at one moment, no history, no chain read.

## Where today's docs stand

`Blockchain/Dev/docs/S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT.md` still marks the anchoring part ON HOLD until the KS-1384 build lands: line 17 ("ON HOLD until the KS-1384 build lands and not assessed: flat-anchor `onBehalfOf`, `metadata.rowHash` ...") and line 302 ("The flat-anchor part is ON HOLD (KS-1384)"), read at develop `204e62acdc35`. Stuart's comment of 2026-11-09 05:09Z on KS-1807 says the same: that section "is still marked on hold until the KS-1384 build lands. Stage 1 is on both boxes." The builder finds any other page that describes anchoring; I read only the contract's lines above, not the other pages.

## Not decided here

When stage 2 lands, what it changes in the pages, and whether the flat-anchor `onBehalfOf` and `rowHash` parts can come off hold: those stay with KS-1384. This ticket records today's behaviour only.

## Related

KS-1807 (the docs-up-to-date ticket; it stays open until these pages land, by Stuart's request) and KS-1384 (the build; stage 2 is its next part). Both are linked as related.

## Searched before filing

Board, includeArchived, title and description and every comment of each open candidate; controls pass (the positive control hit its known ticket KS-1379, a random token hit 0). `one anchor row`: 89 candidates, 4 open literal hits (KS-607, KS-1384, KS-1385, KS-1664): KS-1384 is the build this ticket documents; KS-607 (anchor and verify statuses disagree), KS-1385 (emitted anchors carry no documentType) and KS-1664 (recertify anchors before it writes its row) are different subjects, judged by title and search context. `anchoring pages`: 100 candidates, 1 open (KS-1807, the docs umbrella, which holds Stuart's request as a comment and is not a ticket for these pages). `one fee each`: 1 open, KS-2107, read whole: it rewords five code comments in originate (PR 2103), text only, no documentation page. `its own Cardano transaction`, `anchoring documentation` and `anchor row per document`: 0 open hits. `ON HOLD until the KS-1384`: 1 open (KS-1807). `stage 2`: 4 open (KS-1384, KS-1385, KS-1807, KS-2107). Read whole besides KS-2107: KS-1384's two comments of 2026-11-06 and KS-1807's newest comment. No open ticket tracks the anchoring documentation pages.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** PR 2136 (head `b907ba03bea2`, one commit on develop `e8d23ce366e2`) puts the two anchoring facts on the pages Stuart asked for. Docs only, no product source file changed. It is waiting for review; nothing is merged or deployed.

- One anchor row per document and network: the unique key on `(document_id, network)` (migration 031), and a repeat post updates that row.
- Until stage 2, each admitted share, transfer-custody, revoke and lifecycle event pays for its own Cardano transaction on that row, which then names only the latest transaction hash. The pages do not say stage 1 stops this, or that a share is idempotent at the transaction level.
- Pages: `S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT.md` (a dated note; the hold wording stays), `VOCABULARY.md` (an "As shipped" entry) and `WORKFLOWS.md` (steps 4 and 5). `DATABASE-SCHEMA.md` is not covered.
- Read from code at develop `e8d23ce366e2`, not observed live; the pages say nothing about what is deployed. One clause beyond the two facts cites KS 1200: the unique is declared only by migration 031 and anchoring's own table creation.
- Checks: path and symbol existence 10 of 10, an untouched-lines proof with planted controls, the audit gates and the test-type check green, merge-tree against the open contract PR clean. What stage 2 changes in these pages stays with KS 1384.

title: pre-push hook: a failing git diff reads as no change and the hook exits 0 before leg 1, so a RED commit pushes (gate 263 G1)
description:
**BLUF:** The real pre-push hook treats a failing `git diff` as an empty change set. With `git config diff.orderFile` naming a missing file, `git diff` exits 128 with no output, the changed set stays empty, and the hook exits 0 before leg 1: a RED commit pushes with rc 0 and no preflight line. Gate 263 measured this on the hook fixture at `35bcfa000`; the same lines are on develop `6c9a593df4ab`. High is Wednesday's call.

Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-09_gate263-tier1-x8-prerun-driver-r3/verdict.md`, finding G1 (a note outside the tool under test, which the gate calls the most important thing it found). Not a PR-merge item: it waits on no PR. A build seat fixes the hook; this ticket only records it.

## What was measured, and what was only read

* MEASURED AT RUNTIME by gate 263 (scratch worlds, local bare origins): `git config diff.orderFile <missing file>` makes `git diff` exit 128 with empty output, while `status`, `rev-parse` and `merge-base` still exit 0. The gate probed 17 `diff.*` and `core.*` faults and found this one shape. The real hook fixture, called directly with a new-branch stdin line on a RED commit: with the fault, rc 0 and "Blockchain/Dev changes detected" is never printed; without the fault, rc 1, the preflight ran and failed. Evidence in the gate folder: `evidence/order.out`, produced by `evidence/g263_order.py`.
* On the same fault the pre-run tool (X 8th's) still runs the preflight, so the pre-run path is stronger than the hook here.
* READ ONLY (the board seat, at develop `6c9a593df4ab`; I did not run the hook): in `.githooks/pre-push`, lines 129, 143 and 252 end `|| true` after `git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-renames --name-only ...`. Line 251 sets `_informative=1` before the diff at line 252, so the KS-882 branch at line 271 (every base contains HEAD, run unconditionally) does not fire. With `changed` empty, line 372 `[ -z "$changed" ] && exit 0` returns success before the preflight message at line 374. These are the lines the gate cited at `35bcfa000`; the gate's fixture hook is not necessarily develop's current hook, and the lines match.

## Why it is the same class as two fixed holes

The hook's own comments record KS-854 (lines 156 to 160: an unresolvable base left `changed` empty and the hook returned success before leg 1) and KS-882 (lines 181 to 187, banner at line 272: a base equal to HEAD gave an empty diff and the same exit). Both fixes treat "cannot compute" as "run the preflight" (lines 276 to 277 and 284 to 285 set `changed` to an unconditional marker and `st_all=1`). A diff that fails is the same case: an uncomputable change set is not a clean one.

## Fix shape (READ ONLY, not applied)

Capture the diff's exit status at lines 129, 143 and 252 instead of discarding it with `|| true`; on a non-zero status take the KS-854 and KS-882 path (banner, unconditional marker, `st_all=1`). Regression test: in a scratch repo set `diff.orderFile` to a missing path, push a RED commit, expect rc 1 and the "changes detected" line; the same push without the fault expects the same result.

## Related, not this defect

* KS-1483 (Backlog): the hook diffs HEAD, not the pushed ref. A different cause, same symptom class.
* KS-2091 (Backlog): no hook suite proves that a red preflight makes the hook refuse a push.
* KS-989, KS-1063, KS-1482 (Done): earlier holes in the same hook.
* Gate 263's G2 (the pre-run's own copy of the changed set, Minor) and G3 (clean means clean to `git status`) concern the pre-run tool and are not filed here.

## Searched before filing

Board, includeArchived, title and description and every comment of each open candidate; controls pass (a made-up token hits 0; `msgpackr` hits KS-1379). `orderFile` 0 hits; `gate 263` 0; `gate263` 0; `skips the preflight` 1 open hit (KS-1483, different cause); `pre-push` together with `git diff` 6 open and 3 closed hits, none holds a failing-diff case.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** PR 2118 (head `08cf86d0ec5f`, one commit on develop `273de443c30c`) makes the pre-push hook run the preflight when its `git diff` fails, instead of reading the failure as "no change" and passing the push before leg 1. It is ready for its gate (tier 1: the push gate itself); nothing is merged or deployed, and this ticket stays open (the PR says Refs).

- **The change.** The three diffs in `.githooks/pre-push` that compute what a push changes (remote branch, upstream, merge-base for a new branch) now read their exit status instead of ending `|| true`. On a failure a new helper prints a KS-2127 banner, sets an unconditional changed marker and checks every systemTest package, the answer the hook already gives a base it cannot compute. A push whose diffs succeed takes the old path.
- **Red on the old hook.** A new suite plants the fault this ticket names (`git config diff.orderFile` pointing at a missing file) in local fixtures with a stubbed preflight. On develop's hook all 5 fault cells fail (a RED commit pushes with rc 0 and no preflight line) and the 3 controls pass. On the fixed hook 8 of 8.
- **The hook still does its job.** Without the fault a RED commit is refused and a clean one passes, and the 9 existing suites that run or read the hook give identical tallies before and after (264 cells), including the cases for a base that cannot be resolved and a base that already contains the commit.
- **Each site is pinned.** Putting any one site back to `|| true` reddens exactly its own cells; removing the helper's marker reddens the four push-outcome cells.
- **Round 2 (gate 278, GO WITH NOTES), head `cd8b80e38a4b`:** a push whose tip is not HEAD is refused under the fault, and that refusal now names KS-2127 (it gave no cause); a cell pins that the format gate is asked for `--all`. The suite is 12 of 12 (develop's hook: 7 fault cells fail, 5 controls pass).
- **Not covered.** Other shapes of failing diff. A tag on a new commit whose diff fails used to pass silently; it now runs the preflight if it is HEAD and is refused otherwise (measured by the gate; no cell here pins tags).

_Edited 2026-11-09 for round 2 (gate 278): the tag sentence corrected from the gate's measurement, and the round-2 line added. Edited in place, not stacked._

title: api-gateway: admin-minted connector keys share the identity connector:api-key, so one tenant's key can list and delete another's inbox rows
description:
**BLUF:** Admin-minted API keys carry no connector id, so the gateway gives every one of them the same `userId`, `connector:api-key`. Gate 246 measured that tenant B's key can then list, and delete, a notification row that tenant A's key placed in that inbox. PR 2072 (KS-1448, merged as `7eda23b34d3b`) now refuses a `userId` other than the caller's, with a connector key allowed its own id; for this population "its own id" is the shared one, so that ruling does not close it. The identity sharing predates PR 2072, which narrows the route. High is Wednesday's call.

Source: gate 246 (PR 2072, KS-1448), finding 72-1, recorded by Wednesday as G246-F1: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate246-tier1-services/verdict.md`, and her note `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/2_Project_Files/fleet/briefs_staged/2026-11-08_B99_answer_notes_2072.md`. Every line number below I read myself at develop `7eda23b34d3b7a413ca8f9c0945c7843708ce9f4`, which is the merge of PR 2072.

1. Where the identity comes from. `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts` line 572 builds `userId: connector:${meta.connectorId || 'api-key'}`, and line 312 sets `connectorId: data.connectorId || ''`. The comment at lines 52 to 55 of the same file says `connectorId` is null for admin-minted keys, so every such key gets the one userId `connector:api-key`: "one bucket across all tenants".
2. What PR 2072 ruled. `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/notifications.ts` lines 315 to 327: `if (userId !== getUserId(req))` answers 403 for every principal, and a connector key may create for its own id. For a key with no connector id, its own id is `connector:api-key`, the same string for every such key of every tenant. Neither the PR nor its ticket comment says so.
3. The steps. Evidence class: MEASURED at runtime by gate 246, for the route through the real `authenticateToken` with the security service's answer stubbed to `connectorId: null`. (1) Key A, of tenant A, posted `type: security` with an `actionUrl` to `connector:api-key`: 201. (2) Key B, of tenant B, listed the row: 200. (3) Key B deleted it: 200. (4) Key A posting to `victim`: 403, so PR 2072's rule holds for every other id.
4. Not measured. Whether admin-minted keys exist on any live box, and whether anyone reads such an inbox. The gate notes that connector inboxes are unlikely to have human readers.

Shared root: every API key without a connector id is the one principal `connector:api-key`. KS-1685 records that for vc-issuer and says cross-tenant stays separated there; the notification routes act on that string with no tenant check, as measured above, so here it does not. The transfer service's `GET /api/notifications` has the same root: KS-2119.

Fix shapes, the gate's: refuse admin-minted keys on this route, or derive a per-key id; at minimum, name the gap, which this ticket does. The regression test to add: two keys with null `connectorId` cannot see each other's rows.

Not claimed: no run by me, and no reading of any live box.

Related: KS-1448 (PR 2072's ticket; the facts-only line to Peter about his strict xfail marker goes there separately, after approval), KS-1685 (the shared principal), KS-2119 (the transfer-notification read), KS-2001 (the same fallback on an integrations lookup).

Priority: High, Wednesday's call.

Duplicate search before filing (board account, includeArchived; open tickets read with all comments; output in `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-09_seatS-38th/evidence/search_q1245.out` and `search_q1_more.out` in the same folder): `connector:api-key` 6 open: KS-1685, KS-2001 and KS-2081 read whole (none records the notification inbox; KS-1685 says cross-tenant stays separated for vc-issuer); KS-772, KS-843 and KS-1579 by title. `routes/notifications.ts` 5 open: I read KS-1448 whole (6 comments; no mention of the shared identity or of a second tenant), and KS-2076, KS-1346 and KS-1410 by title. `x-user-id` 9 open, other subjects. I found no ticket for the cross-tenant inbox.

title: Connector-key rotate answers rotated true with no warning while an older organisation key with no connector id still validates
description:
**BLUF:** The connector-key rotate (register-connector with rotate on) answers `rotated: true`, a count of 1 and no warning while an older key of the same organisation, one that carries no connector id, still validates. It happens on the retry after a count of 0, and also on the first call when the organisation holds both kinds of key, so no 0 is needed. The cause is in security's retire, which matches only the connector id; the gateway cannot see the older key. Gate 257 measured it on real PostgreSQL. It is old behaviour that PR 2073 narrows (the 0 itself is now honest) and does not remove. Priority High is Wednesday's call; the gate graded the finding Medium. Wednesday's ruling on the fix direction, under Kam's card `secuura-ks-1152-rotate-says-rotated-when-old-key-lives-1106` = b ("Keep rotating, but answer 'rotated: false' and say why", ruled 2026-11-06 15:00:34 AEDT, read with `tools/decision_queue.sh show`): the fix extends that honest answer to these keys; it does NOT retire them.

Source: gate 257, tier 1, round 2 of 2, PR 2073 (KS-1152 R-880-1), finding F1 and the section "For Kam, at the top", `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-08_gate257-tier1-pr2073-r2/verdict.md`, lines 17 to 34 and 40 to 49. Wednesday's ADDENDUM to the board seat, 2026-11-08 11:39:30Z, orders this filing. Seat Y 8th had recorded the retry case first (its probe P2, in its entry in `5_Project_History/history.md`) and proposed a distinct code for Kam's and Stuart's monthly agenda.

1. What was measured. Evidence class: MEASURED by gate 257 on real PostgreSQL 15 (the gate's own cluster), through a real gateway route over real security, at PR 2073's head `2684a29d8f576ff74634f07ad6576af5bd00370b` and again on the develop merge.
   * G2a, the first call with a count of 0: 200, `rotated` false, `priorKeysRevoked` 0, `PRIOR_KEY_STILL_ACTIVE`. The older key and the new key both validate.
   * G2b, the retry: 200, `rotated` true, count 1, no warning. The older key is still valid; the key the 0 call returned is no longer valid.
   * G3, an organisation that holds both an older key with no connector id and a key with the connector id, first call: 200, `rotated` true, count 1, no warning. The older key is still valid; the connector key is retired.
2. Where. Evidence class: READ. `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts` at PR 2073's head, line 979: `rotated: rotate && existing.rows.length > 0 && priorKeysRetired && priorKeysRevoked >= 1`. `Blockchain/Dev/services/security/src/index.ts` at develop `abd044f63a9dd5673f1b9ff7a2b1e42e1c26de82` (the file is not changed by PR 2073), lines 239 and 246: both retire statements end `WHERE connector_id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2::uuid AND id <> $3 AND is_active = true`, so a key with no connector id is never matched.
3. Why it is old behaviour. By the gate's reading, develop answers `rotated: true` on the 0 itself, on the retry and on G3. PR 2073 makes the 0 honest and leaves the retry and G3 as they were.
4. The fix direction. Ruled by Wednesday (ADDENDUM 11:39:30Z): extend the honest answer, `rotated: false` with a reason, to these keys; do not retire them. The gate's two fix shapes were that security reports how many active keys of the organisation remain after the retire, or that the retire also takes the organisation's keys that have no connector id. The first fits the ruling; the second is what the ruling excludes. A regression test the owner should add (the gate): G3's shape, asserting that `rotated` is not true while the older key validates. If this behaviour stays for now, the gate asks for one sentence each in `Blockchain/Dev/docs/S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT.md` and in the spec: "`rotated: true` says nothing about an older key with no connector id; a retry after a 0 answers `rotated: true` with that key still active."
5. The cost the gate names in Wednesday's ruling A2. One code now carries two instructions, so a client that reads only the code retries after a 0 and lands in G2. The PR body calls that retry "futile, not harmful"; the gate disagrees, because the retry ends in a false all-clear. The gate leaves that trade-off to Kam.
6. Who reads `rotated`. By the gate: rotation is platform-admin only (its GUARDRAIL 1), so a K admin reads the reply; whether Platform S reads `rotated` is unknown; the only code reader is systemTest, which stops at `rotated: true`. The contract Stuart's team reads says a retry does not help but not that the retry answers `rotated: true`, and it does not mention G3.

Not claimed: how many keys with no connector id exist on any box (the gate did not measure it); whether Platform S reads `rotated`; any run by me. PR 2073 is not merged: the line numbers for `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts` are at its head and may shift when it merges.

Related: KS-1152 (PR 2073's ticket, another seat's; I do not comment there). KS-1966 is the failed-retire case that PR 2073's round 1 answers, and KS-577 is revoke-on-rotate; I read both by title only.

Priority: High, Wednesday's call in the ADDENDUM.

Duplicate search before filing (board account, includeArchived, open tickets read with all comments): `PRIOR_KEY_STILL_ACTIVE` 1 open literal hit (KS-1152, PR 2073's own ticket); `priorKeysRevoked` 8 open (KS-577, KS-772, KS-1152, KS-1533, KS-1868, KS-1904, KS-1966, KS-2074); `rotationWarning` 1 open (KS-1152); `rotated: true` 2 open (KS-1152, KS-1966); `S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT` 4 open (KS-577, KS-1174, KS-1807, KS-1859) and 5 closed. KS-1966 is the failed-retire case, a lock timeout on the retire (I read its description), so another subject; KS-1152 is PR 2073's ticket; the others I read by title only. title: anchoring: an empty or null 2xx reply from a configured chain client reads ABSENT, which can lead to a second fee-paying transaction
description:
**BLUF:** with a configured chain client, a 2xx reply with an empty body or a JSON `null` counts as the chain answering and reads ABSENT in the anchoring confirmation poller, and a body of `{}` reads confirmed with no block hash. A false ABSENT lets guard 3 schedule the ordinary retry, which is a second fee-paying Cardano transaction; its fee and its on-chain record cannot be undone. QA gate 248 found it while gating PR 2081 (KS-1171 8k). It is older than that PR, which cannot add the outcome (1,364 attempt sequences, 0 widened). Kam's card `secuura-anchoring-second-fee-on-empty-reply-1107` = a, "Merge PR 2081, and fix the empty reply before anchoring next deploys (recommended)", ruled 2026-11-08 at 20:31:42 +11:00; its detail: "Two tickets by a board seat, High for the empty reply and Medium to measure the mint on an image. A build seat fixes the empty reply next, tier 1 gate. Anchoring's deploy stays held for your word." This is the High ticket. The Medium half is carried on KS-562, whose gate 70 comment already records the open question, "whether the anchoring image's install layout reproduces the split in a built container". Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME for the client and the poller result, with the real client and poller; guard 3's retry from this input follows from an existing cell's path (cell C1) and was not driven end to end.

**Measured (gate 248):** the real blockfrost-js 6.1.1 on a loopback listener returns an empty string for an empty 200 and for a 204, `null` for a body of `null`, and `{}` for a body of `{}`. HTML on a 200 throws; a 404 and a 502 throw with their status. The real provider and the real poller on the production schedule, at develop and at the PR 2081 head, with the transaction lookup resolving each body: an empty string and `null` give `polled` 30 and `definitelyAbsent` true; `{}` gives `confirmed` true with no block hash.

**Why it matters (gate 248):** the code's own comment defines an answer as "the transaction or not found". An empty 200 is neither. It is the same second-fee harm that PR 2081 closes for the no-client case, on the configuration that really pays fees, where 8k itself has no route. PR 2081's sentence "An empty 200 is '', so it still counts as an answer, as it does today" is true, but nothing there says it reaches guard 3.

**Likelihood (gate 248):** low. It needs an upstream or a proxy answering 2xx with no body. Not seen in service; no box was read.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/cardano/confirmation.ts`, lines 94 to 103 at the PR 2081 head (gate 248's tree). On develop `a65ae7ed1d60` the same polling logic starts near line 81, where the `polled` counter is incremented. Gate 248's probes are in the evidence folder next to its verdict.

**Fix shape (gate 248, for the owner):** decide whether the poller counts only `null` and a real transaction as answers, and pin it. That touches the 2026-09-25 definition of "answered" (card `secuura-ks1171-when-is-an-anchor-absent` = c); Kam's ruling above sends it to a build seat under a tier 1 gate. Anchoring's deploy stays held for Kam's word.

**Not measured:** a real Blockfrost, a real node or a real unreachable chain; any box, image or gateway path; guard 3's retry end to end from this input; how often a provider sends an empty 2xx.

**Source:** gate 248 verdict, finding F1 and the chain-cost section, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate248-tier1-pr2081-ks1171/verdict.md`. This seat re-read the verdict and the line locations and ran nothing else. Related: KS-1171 (the ticket PR 2081 belongs to), KS-562 (the thread-token mint question).

**Board search (2026-11-08, closed and archived tickets included, paginated; controls held: the control term msgpackr hits KS-1379, a random token hits 0):** "definitelyAbsent": 1 open hit, KS-1171 (the mixed-window rule; a scan of its description and six comments for an empty or null body found none). The anchoring confirmation path: open KS-485 and KS-1171, closed KS-489 and KS-1810 (the reconciler's 24 h give-up cannot tell an outage from an absent transaction; a different matter). "empty 200": KS-485, KS-772 and KS-1673 (unrelated). No duplicate.

title: originate publishEvent swallows every Redis failure in an empty catch: a failed user.erased publish is silent and the log says published
description:
**BLUF:** originate publishes `user.erased` through its own `publishEvent`, and the `catch` at lines 143 to 145 of `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/events.ts` is empty. A Redis failure while publishing is therefore silent: the erasure returns success, `gdprService` logs `user.erased event published`, and no stream entry exists, so no downstream service ever erases the subject's copy. With `REDIS_URL` unset the same happens. The `warn` branch in `gdprService` that says the cascade may be incomplete cannot fire on a Redis failure, because `publishEvent` never throws. Found in Seat U 17th's walk of the erasure; no fix here.

**Measured (MEASURED AT RUNTIME), Seat U 17th, 2026-11-06:** the real compiled originate on PostgreSQL 15.19 and redis-server 8.10.3 at develop `b7d433fda83c` on Node v26.8.1; not a box, not Kintsugi, not demo. Evidence file `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatU-17th/evidence/walk/run_erasure.out`, lines 12 and 13, quoted:

* `E8 dead Redis {"result":{"label":"E8","success":true,"tables":["users","pii_subject_keys"],"ms":89},"warned":false,"newEntries":0,"status":"deleted","walletKept":true}`
* `E9 REDIS_URL unset {"result":{"label":"E9","success":true,"tables":["users","pii_subject_keys"],"ms":95},"saidPublished":true,"newEntries":0}`

Seat U 17th predicted a `warn` for E8 before running it (`predictions_erasure.txt` line 10 in the same folder) and the run showed none: success true after 89 ms, no warn line, 0 stream entries, and the log line `user.erased event published`. Its STATUS of 2026-11-06 about 11:55Z (item W1) records the same.

**Where (READ at the same sha):**

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/events.ts`: `publishEvent` (line 118) returns at once when there is no client (`if (!redis) return;`, line 123); otherwise its `try` runs `xadd` and the `catch` at lines 143 to 145 holds only the comment `// Fire-and-forget — never let event publishing break the service`. `initEventBus` warns once at start-up when `REDIS_URL` is unset (line 62); no later erasure says anything.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/services/gdprService.ts`: lines 962 to 981 wrap `await publishEvent(EventTypes.USER_ERASED, ...)` in a `try`, log `user.erased event published — downstream services will cascade` after it (line 970) and log `Failed to publish user.erased event (cascade may be incomplete)` in the `catch` (line 980). That `catch` is unreachable for a Redis failure.
* What does not happen when the entry is missing, per the same run: auth deactivating the user (E3) and wallet-connector deleting the wallet's session rows (E4); per KS-1955, kyc's deletes. KS-1955 also says originate marks the data-subject request completed at step 12, before the publish at step 13.

**Not measured:** a Redis failure that appears only after the `xadd` is accepted, and the running Kintsugi or demo originate (neither was touched).

**Board search (2026-11-06, includeArchived, paginated):** 0 open and 0 closed literal hits for `originate/src/events.ts` and `event published`. `user.erased` has 7 open hits, none about the publisher: KS-239, KS-485, KS-772, KS-1868, KS-1931, KS-1955, KS-2060. KS-1955 (Backlog, High, 0 comments) is the handler half: a failed kyc or wallet-connector handler after the bus, and its text does not name `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/events.ts` or `publishEvent`. KS-2004 is an empty catch in the demo user seed, a different file. `publishEvent` appears in KS-1651 (the `ownership_transferred` payload) and `initEventBus` in KS-1868 (unguarded thrown-value reads); neither covers this empty catch.

**Possible shapes (mine, not a decision):** have `publishEvent` return whether the entry was added, or log inside the catch with the event type and the error message, and make the `gdprService` info line depend on that result so the existing `warn` can fire.

title: governance POST /api/governance/proposals/:id/execute checks no role: any signed-in user of any tenant executes a queued proposal
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/governance/proposals/:id/execute` checks only that the caller is signed in. It checks no role, no proposer or committee membership and no tenant. Measured on a real compiled service: a user of one tenant with the OWNER role executed a queued proposal created by a user of another tenant and got 200 with `status` `executed`. Limit: today execution only logs each action and flags it executed (no contract call), by Seat U 17th's read, so the effect is the proposal's status moving to `executed`. Found in Seat U 17th's walk of the governance service; no fix here.

**Measured (MEASURED AT RUNTIME), Seat U 17th, 2026-11-06:** the real compiled governance service on PostgreSQL 15.19 at develop `b7d433fda83c` on Node v26.8.1; not a box, not Kintsugi, not demo. Evidence file `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatU-17th/evidence/walk/run_base.out`, line 14, quoted (T1 and T2 are the two tenants of the walk):

* `X8 execute a T2 queued proposal as T1 OWNER {"s":200,"t2Status":"executed"}`

A 200 also means the timelock check passed, because the service answers 409 before the proposal's execution time. Sibling routes in the same walk do check the caller: cancel by a non-committee user answered 403 `Only proposer or constitutional committee can cancel` (line 11), and process-expired by an OWNER answered 403 where a SUPER_ADMIN got 200 (line 13).

**Where (READ at the same sha):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts` lines 300 to 315: the handler reads `userId`, answers 401 when it is absent, and calls `governanceService.executeProposal(req.params.id, userId)`. `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts` line 1103: `executeProposal(proposalId: string, _executorId: string)`. The executor id is named `_executorId` and appears nowhere else in the file; the body checks that the proposal exists, is `queued` and is past its timelock, then marks its actions executed and saves.

**Not measured:** a rule in front of the service. The walk's STATUS lists originate, auth, wallet-connector and governance as the compiled services, so whether the api-gateway narrows this path is not measured.

**Board search (2026-11-06, includeArchived, paginated):** 0 open and 0 closed literal hits for `proposals/:id/execute`, `executeProposal` and `_executorId`. The nearest tickets are the same class on other services: KS-1814 (the document anchor route) and KS-2038 (the transfer doors).

**Possible shape (mine, not a decision):** a check like the cancel route's (proposer or committee) or a role set on `execute`, with a cell for the 403.

title: governance castVote counts a delegator's stake twice: the delegator still votes with it and the delegate's vote adds it again
description:
**BLUF:** In the governance service a delegator keeps full voting power after delegating it, and the delegate's vote adds the delegated power on top, so the same stake is counted twice in `votes_for`. Measured on a real compiled service: with one stake of 1000 delegated, `votes_for` reads 3000; in both controls (no delegation, and after the delegation is revoked) it reads 2000. Found in Seat U 17th's walk of the governance service; no fix here.

**Measured (MEASURED AT RUNTIME), Seat U 17th, 2026-11-06:** the real compiled governance service on PostgreSQL 15.19 at develop `b7d433fda83c` on Node v26.8.1; not a box, not Kintsugi, not demo. Evidence file `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatU-17th/evidence/walk/run_base.out`, lines 2 to 5, quoted (a is the delegator, d the delegate, each owns a stake of 1000):

* `4B control no delegation {"a":1000,"d":1000,"status":[200,200],"votesFor":2000}`
* `4B delegate {"s":200,"delegatedPower":1000}`
* `4B delegated {"a":1000,"d":2000,"status":[200,200],"votesFor":3000}`
* `4B after revoke {"a":1000,"d":1000,"votesFor":2000}`

The delegator's own vote was accepted (status 200) and counted 1000; the delegate's vote counted 2000, its own 1000 plus the delegated 1000.

**Where (READ at the same sha):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts`. `castVote` (line 946) gives every voter `voter.votePower` plus `getDelegatedPowerFor(voterId, proposal.category)` (lines 982 and 983) and nowhere checks whether the voter has delegated their own power away. `delegateVote` (line 1193) stores `delegatedPower: delegator.votePower` (line 1224) and leaves the delegator's own `votePower` as it was. `getDelegatedPowerFor` (line 1259) sums `delegatedPower` over the delegate's active delegations. The early-finalise check (lines 1038 to 1045 of the same file) reads `votesFor`, so the doubled figure can decide an outcome.

**Not measured:** a category-scoped delegation (`categories`), several delegators to one delegate, and a proposal whose outcome flips because of the extra power.

**Board search (2026-11-06, includeArchived, paginated):** 0 open and 0 closed literal hits for `getDelegatedPowerFor`, `delegated power` and `votes_for`. `castVote` has 0 open hits and 5 closed ones, none about delegation (KS-450, KS-1940, KS-1942, KS-1950, KS-1951).

**Possible shapes (mine, not a decision):** refuse or zero a delegator's own vote while an active delegation covers the proposal's category, or subtract the delegated-away power in `castVote`; either needs a test cell holding the 2000 and 3000 figures above.

title: Security: a role change at PATCH /api/users/admin/:id leaves a person's sessions alive, so the old token keeps the old role until it expires
description:
**BLUF:** When an administrator changes a person's role at `PATCH /api/users/admin/:id`, the person's sessions stay alive, so the token minted under the old role keeps working, with the old role, until it expires. The handler ends a user's sessions only when the new status forbids a credential, never for a role-only change. Seat Y 6th measured the walk-around this opens: a demoted org admin uses the old token to raise a second account to org admin, and that second account then passes the live-row check built for KS-2063. High, the same priority as KS-2063 (priority 2, read at source 2026-11-06 about 21:12 AEDT). Kam has ruled that it be built: his card `secuura-ks2063-add-session-end-on-role-change-1106` reads status ruled, choice a, "Both", ruled_ts 2026-11-06T21:04:39+11:00, and its option detail reads "live-row check as ruled, plus session end as its own small PR (recommended):Y's recommendation and mine. A new ticket, red-first cells, tier-1 gate, Kintsugi only." This is that new ticket. Evidence class: MEASURED by Seat Y 6th (two separate probes, no real stack, as recorded on KS-2063 and on the card); the handler lines READ ONLY by me at origin develop `a6cd828e820d`, nothing run by me.

**Where**, at origin develop `a6cd828e820d69b7a48f9d28d54023bc1a628437` (read 2026-11-06 by Seat S 32nd through the GitHub contents API at that sha), all in `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/routes/users.ts`:

* Line 693: `userRoutes.patch('/admin/:id', authenticate(), ...)`, the route commented at line 691 as "Admin: update a user (role, status, etc.)".
* Line 813: the write, `userRepo.updateUserPlatformScope(id, safeUpdates)`. Nothing between it and the response touches sessions except the block below.
* Lines 838 to 841: `if (accountStatusForbidsCredential(updatedUser))` calls `revokeAllUserSessions(id)` and logs "Admin status change revoked active sessions". The comment above it (lines 819 to 837) records that KS-360 added the revoke for suspend and deactivate, and that KS-796 derived the condition from the credential doors' status allow-list. A role-only change makes the condition false, so no session is revoked.

**Measured by Seat Y 6th** (KS-2063's description and its comment 6642212f; the card's BLUF carries the same):

* A role-only demotion leaves the session alive. Through the gateway the old token still works until it expires (1 hour by the code default, 1 day by the compose default; the real value on a box is unread).
* On the key routes, 4 of the 8 non-live shapes still reach them through the gateway while the session store is up: the role-only demotions. The deleted and suspended shapes changed through the same `PATCH` end the session first, so the gateway answers 401 and forwards nothing. While the gateway cannot reach the store it forwards anyway. Measured as two separate hops with an in-process stand-in for the store: no real Redis, no box, no real login.
* The card reports that ending sessions on a role change stopped the walk-around in the probe, adds no database read, and covers every route.

**What the session end does not close, as the card states it:** a Redis outage (the gateway forwards by design), a row edited by hand, and keys minted before the demotion. **Its cost, as the card states it:** anyone whose role changes, promotions included, is logged out at once.

**Asked for, by the card's option a:** the session end as its own small PR: red-first cells, tier 1 gate, Kintsugi only. Seat Y 6th builds it (Wednesday's ANSWER to Seat Y 6th, 2026-11-06T10:08:50Z); the change is one condition at the line 838 block plus cells, in the auth service only. The live-row check for KS-2063 is a separate build under that ticket.

**NOT measured:** a real demotion through `PATCH /api/users/admin/:id` against a real Redis or a box; the real token lifetime on any box; whether any user on a box holds a live token under a stale role. I read nothing about a deploy: the demo is frozen and nothing here has been built.

**Source:** KS-2063 (description and its comments 6642212f and b7eb928b); the card named above; Seat Y 6th's plan mail to Wednesday of 2026-11-06T10:08:06Z, which gives this ticket's title. Related: KS-2063 (the live-row check; this ticket is its sibling), KS-2032, KS-360 (closed; the original suspend and deactivate revoke), KS-1407 and KS-1692 (session handling in the same service, judged by title).

**Board search before filing** (2026-11-06, Seat S 32nd, board_search tool, both controls held: the term msgpackr hit KS-1379 among open tickets and a random token hit 0; includeArchived; open candidates checked on title, description and all comments): `PATCH /api/users/admin` 90 candidates, 5 open hits (KS-485, KS-591, KS-1017, KS-1364, KS-2063) and 8 closed; `role change` 100 candidates, 1 open hit (KS-2063) and 3 closed; `role-only` 100 candidates, 1 open hit (KS-2063) and 2 closed; `session end` 100 candidates, 1 open hit (KS-2063), 0 closed; `keeps the old role`, `sessions alive` and `ends the session` 100 candidates each, 0 hits; `revokeAllUserSessions` 9 candidates, 5 open hits (KS-1407, KS-1690, KS-1691, KS-1692, KS-1969) and 3 closed (KS-360, KS-570, KS-1967). Read whole: KS-2063. None of the others records a session end on a role change; KS-1407, KS-1692 and KS-360 were judged by title.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Correction to the comment above: "Closes: the walk-around" is true for a request sent after the role change only. A request already in flight while the sessions end can bring the session back. Kam ruled the wording corrected and the race ticketed High: card secuura-ks2083-session-end-race-in-flight-1107 = a, 2026-11-08T20:32:11+11:00. PR 2075 round 2, head 32aa0d06bc0a, changes the two fragments and the PR text only. Gate 254, a compare of that head against gate 245's, is GO WITH NOTES; its three notes are in the PR body.

* **The race (gate 245 F1):** each request's activity write reads the session record and writes it back whole (`services/auth/src/services/session.ts:286`). A revoke between the two is undone, with a fresh 24 h lifetime, and no later revoke of all the person's sessions finds it. The gate measured it on a stand-in store with the real session code, not on real Redis. The same race is on develop today for every revoke, so the PR does not widen it. It is to be ticketed High by a board seat.
* **Also not closed (gate 245 F2):** if the session store drops after `authenticate()`, the PATCH answers 200 with nothing revoked and logs `sessionsRevoked: 0` at info (`session.ts:332`, `routes/users.ts:846`).
* **Also not closed (gate 245 F4):** re-sending the role the row already holds cannot end a stale token, because the route compares with the row, not the token (`routes/users.ts:844`).
* **Now measured, not read:** auth's own `authenticate()` fails closed on a store outage: 401 with the store flag down, 500 with the store rejecting (gate 245).
* **Two figures corrected (gate 245 F5):** in the ks949 alone-run, the 7,047 ms cell was a cold import ("is NOT seeded when DEMO_SECUURA_PASSWORD is unset"), not the walk; the walk cell took 5,001 ms. Both were vitest timeouts. KS 1155 records ks949 in its comments of 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-27; its title is about the packages/shared guards.

title: security: a revoke or mint acknowledged while the database flag is down is never written (boot race write side, gate 225 on PR 2046)
description:
**BLUF:** Gate 225 (PR 2046, KS-1377) found that the write side of the security service has the same flaw PR 2046 fixed on the read side. While the database availability flag is down, a key revoke or a key mint is acknowledged to the caller, is never written to the database, and the key behaves wrongly after recovery. Facts only, no fix is built. Priority High on Wednesday's reading. PR 2046 merged on 2026-11-06 at 07:39:23Z as squash `35bcfa000b44`. This seat measured nothing at runtime; every runtime figure below is gate 225's, on a stubbed store.

## Source and what was checked here

* Gate 225 verdict: GO WITH NOTES at head `dadd6e3df78a`, PR 2046, KS-1377, tier 1, round 1 of 2. File: `0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate225-tier1-pr2046-ks1377/verdict.md` in the coordinator's tree. The items below are quoted from it.
* This seat read the cited lines of `services/security/src/index.ts` at the merged sha `35bcfa000b44` through the GitHub API (read only, nothing run). They hold the code the verdict names: line 403 is the `!isDbAvailable()` branch in `saveKeyAndRetirePriors`, line 482 is `if (!isDbAvailable()) return;`, line 560 is `if (isDbAvailable()) {`, line 620 is `memApiKeys.clear();`, lines 2011 to 2014 are the row-gone branch, line 2023 reads `revokedInMemory`, line 2026 is `memApiKeys.set`, line 2055 is the second `memApiKeys.set`.
* One ticket with several items, because one test pass proves them (Kam, 2026-09-07 13:23, the standing ticket-creation line).

## Priority and class

* Wednesday's reading: High (Linear priority 2).
* The verdict's words for F1: "Major by class, low likelihood, NOT a regression (base identical)".
* The oracle the verdict names: Kam's card text "A revoked key is never honoured", and the KS-888 ruling as quoted at `services/security/src/index.ts` line 1680 (the source comment names card `secuura-ks888-revoke-validate-on-failed-save`, option a: a revoke whose save did not persist is not acknowledged; the verdict says it did not read that card itself, and neither did this seat).

## Item F1: a revoke acknowledged during a boot race is not stored, and the key answers valid:true after recovery

* Anchors: `services/security/src/index.ts` lines 482 (dbSaveApiKey returns at the flag), 560 (dbGetApiKey falls to memory), 620 (loadFromDb clears memory on recovery).
* Found: the save side still decides from the flag alone, the same flaw `databaseExpected()` removes from the read side.
* Measured by gate 225 at runtime, twice with equal results, real routes on a stubbed store and flag (`evidence/table_read.txt`, case S4 in the gate folder). Flag down, URL set, database reachable: validate answers valid:true and caches the key; DELETE /api/keys/:id answers 200 "API key revoked" with 0 writes and the stored row still active; validate answers "Key revoked" in this process; then with the flag up and loadFromDb run, validate answers valid:true.
* Control S4 with the flag up: 1 write, and "Key revoked" after the reload.
* Reachability, read only in the verdict: it needs a revoke in the window between the database coming up and the next retry probe (the backoff in the security service's database module, at most 30 s), on a key already cached in that window. An uncached key answers 404, which is visible. Other processes read the active row throughout.

## Item F2: a key minted during a boot race is issued and cannot be used

* Class in the verdict: Minor, pre-existing, its visible effect changes on head and the PR does not name it. Anchors: `services/security/src/index.ts` lines 403, 482 and 2011 to 2014.
* Measured by gate 225 at runtime on a stubbed store (case S5). Base: mint answers 201 with a key and 0 writes; validate in the race answers valid:true whether the read fails or the database is readable; after recovery "Key not found". Head: mint answers 201 with a key and 0 writes; validate in the race answers 503 when the read fails, and "Key not found" with the entry evicted when the database is readable; after recovery "Key not found".
* Oracle in the verdict: the KS-888 rule, as quoted in the header of the KS-888 failed-mint test in the security service (the card was not read), that a mint whose save did not persist is never acknowledged. Base loses the key at recovery, head loses it at first use.

## Item F4: no test pins a row that is gone during a boot race, nor an empty DATABASE_URL

* Class in the verdict: Minor, test gap. Anchors: `services/security/src/index.ts` lines 2011 to 2014 and 1954.
* Measured by gate 225 (`evidence/tampers.json`, `evidence/tampers_live_proof.json`): tamper G3 (row gone with the flag down answers valid:true from memory) survives the whole unit suite, 514 of 514. Tamper G1 (an empty URL counts as configured) also survives 514 of 514. Both tampers are live: the gate's table sees G3 in 2 cells and G1 in 9. Head's real behaviour is correct in both states; only the pin is missing.
* Regression cell owed (the verdict): boot race, cached key, no rows answers "Key not found" and evicts. G3 is the one that matters: a deleted key honoured in a boot race would pass every suite.

## Item N5: an in-flight validate undoes a KS-888 in-memory revoke

* Class in the verdict: Note, pre-existing, not touched by PR 2046. Anchors: `services/security/src/index.ts` line 2023 reads `revokedInMemory` from the object held before the await, and line 2026 overwrites memory.
* Measured by gate 225 at runtime, twice, base and head equal (case S7): a validate holds its read open; a revoke whose save fails answers 503 and memory reads revoked; the validate finishes valid:true and memory reads active; the next validate answers valid:true. The revoke caller was told it was not stored, so the harm is narrow.

## Item: saveKeyAndRetirePriors retires prior connector keys in memory only

* Anchor: `services/security/src/index.ts` line 403. Same family as F1.
* Read only. The gate read this function and did not drive it ("NOT tested ... saveKeyAndRetirePriors in a boot race"). Its behaviour in a boot race is unmeasured at runtime.

## Item F3 documentation half: a false sentence in the flow fragment

* Class in the verdict: Minor, documentation and ruling premise. The sentence "Only keys minted in this process can be cached during a boot race." sits in `Projects Documents/fragments/flow/KS-1377-validate-answers-503-in-a-boot-race-on-both-arms.html`, line 2, and is on develop at `35bcfa000b44` (read by this seat through the GitHub API). The verdict names two other places it appeared: the PR 2046 body ("Keys minted in this process during the race are the only cached ones") and the coordinator's ANSWER of 2026-11-06 01:24:12Z.
* It is false by gate 225's measurement: the cell (flag down, URL set, cache none, read active) reads the stored row, answers valid:true and leaves it cached (`cachedAfter: true`, `services/security/src/index.ts` line 2055). A key minted in the race has no row, so under the stated premise cells B2 and B3 (the verdict's names) could not happen; they can, through this path. The cached-key arm guards stored keys, including ones revoked elsewhere.
* No code change follows from this item. PR 2046 has merged, so the correction is a new change. Whoever builds this ticket corrects the sentence in the same change.

## Fix shape (a proposal quoted from the verdict, read only, not decided)

* F1: "refuse the revoke with the existing 503 when databaseExpected() is true and the flag is down, or attempt the save and classify the failure".
* F2: "refuse the mint in this state, as F1".
* N5: "read the current map entry after the await".
* Regression tests the verdict names: a revoke in this window is either stored or refused, and validate after loadFromDb is not valid:true; plus the F4 cell above.

## Not known and not tested (from gate 225's NOT tested list)

* No running stack, no real PostgreSQL or pgbouncer. F1, F2, N5 and every table result are on a stubbed store. The real-driver arms covered only a closed port and a silent listener.
* Still unproved: a real database coming up mid-race (the flag flip, loadFromDb under FORCE RLS, F1 and F2 on a real row), the read under the real application role during the window, pgbouncer's error shape and delay, the gateway and auth against a live security service.
* The verdict states a live sweep is owed before KS-1377 is Done, including a real start with postgres stopped and then started.
* Everything ran on Node v26.8.1, not an LTS line. Not run: the four platform suites, integration suites, any box, any deploy.

## Adjacent, not duplicates

* KS-1569 (Backlog): the revoke route writes memory before its database save commits and fails 40001 under REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE. A different failure from F1.
* KS-1556 (Done): read `saveKeyAndRetirePriors` for a failed COMMIT, not for a boot race.
* KS-888 (Done): holds the rule these items break.
* KS-1377: the read side, PR 2046, merged; it stays open for its own owed checks. KS-1370 is its parent.
* Gate 225's N6 (merge order with KS-2032) and N7 (a cached key now waits on the database, the cost the card accepts) are not items here.

## Searched before filing (board, includeArchived)

Read-only, run 2026-11-06 with controls: a known term hit KS-1379, a random token hit 0, and the non-zero control `KS-1377` gave 4 candidates, 2 open literal hits, 1 closed. Counts are candidates, open literal hits, closed or archived literal hits.

* `dbSaveApiKey` 12, 7, 3. `saveKeyAndRetirePriors` 3, 2, 1. `loadFromDb` 21, 12, 6. `databaseExpected` 1, 1, 0 (KS-1377's own PR 2046 comment). `revokedInMemory` 5, 0, 0.
* `services/security/src/index.ts` 125, 37, 28. `KS-888` 9, 5, 3. `boot race` 100, 1, 0 (KS-1377). `revoke acknowledged` 100, 0, 0.
* Then the full text (description and every comment) of KS-1370, KS-1377, KS-1569, KS-1556, KS-888, KS-577 and KS-1732 was read for these items. None states F1, F2, F4 or N5. This is "not found by these searches", not proof of absence.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** PR 2085 (head `4d4726ca41d9`) makes the write side of the boot race refuse: with `DATABASE_URL` set and the first database probe not yet good, a revoke, a mint and a rotate answer 503 and are never acknowledged and lost. It is tier 1, uses `Refs`, and is not merged or deployed. This ticket stays where it is until the owed checks and the deploy. https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/2085

**What changed**

* F1 and F2: a revoke answered 200, a mint 201 with a key, nothing written. Now 503 with the existing bodies. A revoke keeps its in-memory copy, per the KS 888 card's option a. Memory-only and flag-up answer as before; 400 and 403 still come first.
* The rotate, which the gate did not drive. On develop in the race: 201, `priorKeysRevoked: 1`, 0 writes, and after recovery the old key validates and the new key is gone. Now 503, no key, no count, nothing changed in memory.
* A revoke of a key not in memory: 404 became 503. This goes one step past the gate's F1, on the coordinator's ruling.
* N5 on both arms: a validate holding its read open no longer undoes a revoke that lands meanwhile.
* F4 pinned, the gate's tampers G3 and G1 now red. F3: the false sentence in the KS 1377 flow fragment corrected in place. One test-config line sets `DATABASE_URL` empty for the default unit run.

**Who ruled what**

* Refuse rather than attempt: the coordinator's ruling on the shape. With the flag down the mint skips its organisation lookup, so an attempted write could store a key under the wrong tenant.
* The KS 888 card rules a save that failed and says nothing about a skipped one. It covers this by its purpose, not by its letter; that reading is the coordinator's. No card found names a mint.

**Proof** (measured by Seat G 29th on Node v26.8.1, not an LTS line)

* Red first on develop: 21 of 38 new cells, all by assertion. On the branch 38 of 38. 29 planted tampers as declared, 2 of them declared survivors with their reasons in the PR.
* Security unit suite 55 files, 552 of 552, also with `DATABASE_URL` exported. Integration suites on a private PostgreSQL 15: 9 files, 148 of 148. `tsc` rc 0, the test-type ratchet rc 0, eslint rc 0, the docs check OK.
* Pre-push hook, verbatim: “PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.”.

**Not done**

* No live check on a stack: no real PostgreSQL was stopped and started behind this service, and pgbouncer's error shape is unmeasured. One scratch run on real rows through a TCP relay, with the real driver and the real flag flip, held 23 of 23 written expectations; it is not pinned by a committed cell. The callers (gateway 502, tenant provisioning, admin UI) were read, not run.
* The four platform suites, hook legs 3, 4 and 8, Node 24, any box.
* Deploy owed: the security service on both boxes, kintsugi first; demo is frozen.

title: staking reads and writes svc_accumulated_rewards, a table no migration creates: absent on Kintsugi, the boot readiness check fails
description:
**BLUF:** The staking service reads and writes `svc_accumulated_rewards`, a table that no migration in the repository appears to create (a code search finds the name in one source file only). On Kintsugi the table is absent: staking's boot logged `relation "svc_accumulated_rewards" does not exist`. The reward-balance, claim and compound routes use it. Pre-existing; the date 2026-03-20 is Seat D 57th's and was not verified here. Nobody has called those routes on a database without the table, so what a request returns is a reading of the code.

## What D 57th measured on Kintsugi (read-only, 2026-11-06, 06:23 to 06:41Z)

* The staking database holds `svc_reward_claims`, `svc_revenue_distributions` and `svc_stake_positions`. `svc_accumulated_rewards` is absent. A table name that cannot exist is absent too (the control).
* After the swap, staking's boot logged "\[Staking\] DB ready" with 0 stake positions, then an error-level line "\[Staking\] Failed to verify DB readiness for rewards" carrying the relation error. 0 later error lines. The +15 minute watch counted that one line as staking's only error-level line.
* The table name occurs 3 times in each of the three staking images (the rollback tags pre-20261101k15 and pre-20261106k22, and latest), and the failed-readiness string once, so the code that names it is in all three.

## What the code does (read at develop c5c26b2835df08e7e6addc1aec30939cf5531377, `Blockchain/Dev/services/staking/src/routes/rewards.ts`)

* Line 80 reads the table (`dbGetAccumulatedRewards`). Line 89 writes it (`dbSetAccumulatedRewards`, an INSERT with ON CONFLICT on `address`). Line 138 counts it in the boot readiness probe.
* Callers: GET `/:address` (line 187), POST `/claim` (212 read, 228 write of 0), POST `/compound` (259 read, 275 write of 0) and POST `/add-mock` (463 and 465).
* A code search on the default branch, main (not the pin), finds the name in this one file only (total 1; a nonsense string returned 0), so no migration or SQL file creates it.
* The unit suite cannot see this: KS-177's comment of 2026-06-11 says its in-memory fake implements the four staking tables, this one included.

## What is NOT known

* Whether the table exists on demo (not read) or on any other box.
* What a request to those routes returns on Kintsugi. D 57th read and did not run it; the seat filing this ran nothing. Kintsugi's staking holds 0 stake positions.
* Whether a migration once created the table and was lost.

## Owed

A migration that creates the table with the unique `address` column the upsert needs, then a check that GET `/:address`, POST `/claim` and POST `/compound` answer on a database built only from the migrations.

## Searched before filing (2026-11-06, includeArchived, titles, descriptions and comments)

* "svc_accumulated_rewards": 0 issues, 1 comment (KS-177, a description of the test fake). "accumulated_rewards": 0 and 1. "DB readiness for rewards": 0 and 0.
* Controls: "KS-1539" hit, a nonsense symbol returned 0.

Source: Seat D 57th's STATUS B (06:44Z) and its files F1_stakerel.txt, F1_stakerel2.txt and E14_watch15.txt in its record folder. Filed on Wednesday's ADDENDUM of 2026-11-06 06:47Z, priority High (money-shaped).

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** PR 2067 (https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/2067, head `0d08681c616d`, base develop `cd773edc2bb8`) gates staking's whole rewards router behind a new default-off flag, `STAKING_REWARDS_ENABLED`, on only for the exact string `true`. It carries no migration. This corrects the "Owed" line above, which prescribes creating the table. Not merged. QA gate pending.

* **Why no migration.** Wednesday's ruling, 2026-11-06 07:32:58Z (not a ruling by Kam). A migration is forward-only, and creating the table would switch on routes that check for a token and nothing else: `rewards.ts` reads no role and no owner, and takes the address from the path or the body. Read from code, not run: nothing in the repo credits the balance except `POST /add-mock`, and nothing in the repo calls these routes over the network. The gateway sends public `/api/rewards` traffic to the referral service.
* **"Whether a migration once created the table" is answered: none did.** The name entered `rewards.ts` in `ba078c8df` (2026-03-20). `git log --all -S` over `*.sql`, `*.sh` and `*.js` across 994 refs finds 0 commits; the control `svc_reward_claims` finds 4.
* **What changed.** With the flag off, all eight rewards operations answer 404 to a valid token and reach no handler. A missing token is still 401. The boot probe does not run, so the error line staking logged at every boot should clear. `GET /api` stops listing the routes. `rewards.ts` is unchanged, and `/add-mock` and `/simulate-distribution` go off with the rest.
* **Turning it on.** The flag is in `services/staking/.env.example`. staking's compose block has no `env_file` and passes no such variable, so on a compose box only a compose or override change can turn it on.
* **Proof.** A new test file boots the real `index.ts` with the real `authenticate()` and an RS256 token. Red on develop: 24 of 32 failed by assertion, 8 controls passed, 0 skipped. After: 32 of 32. 14 of 14 tampers reddened exactly the predicted cells. Staking suite 99 of 99 before, 131 of 131 after. Node v26.8.1, not the images' Node 24.
* **NOT covered.** No PostgreSQL ran: the database in the cells is a stand-in, so how a real box boots is unmeasured. No image, stack or box. The four platform suites were not run. Whether anything outside the repo calls these routes directly is unmeasured.
* **Owed by others after merge.** The staking image at the next Kintsugi round, and a read of staking's access logs there. Demo is frozen, so demo keeps today's failing routes.
* **Open.** Whether a rewards product is planned goes on the monthly agenda with this finding (card `secuura-ks2071-is-a-staker-rewards-product-planned-1106` = a, ruled by Wednesday on Kam's word to go with the recommendations). The routes stay off behind the flag until then. The older reward cells in `staking.test.ts` set the flag on, so they pin code no deployment runs.
* **Also seen, not changed here.** `Projects Documents/Secuura-Architecture-Reference.md:279` still routes `/api/rewards` to staking. `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:1057` says the dev-debug override re-publishes staking, and that override has no staking lines. `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1054-1055` says direct hits on the staking port still work, which this PR makes stale for `/api/rewards`.

title: Nothing schedules the base-image watch that the KS-365 ruling relies on: the cron is retired and the replacement script is run by hand
description:
**BLUF:** Kam's card on KS-365 accepts a critical vulnerability (CVE-2025-68121, in the gosu binary of the postgres:15-alpine image) on the strength of "the weekly image watch tells us when it clears". At source nothing runs a weekly watch: the workflow that ran it monthly is retired, and its replacement script is run by hand. Evidence class: READ ONLY. No fix shape is chosen here.

## Evidence

* **The card.** secuura-ks-365-postgres-image-gosu-vulnerability-1106, option a, "Accept until the upstream rebuild; re-scan weekly"; detail, verbatim: "No work; the weekly image watch tells us when it clears." Ruled 2026-11-06T14:59:40+11:00.
* **The workflow.** At develop 038e8ab5ae2d, read in a read-only clone: `.github/workflows/base-image-refresh.yml` opens "THIS WORKFLOW NO LONGER RUNS" and keeps only a workflow_dispatch trigger, with no cron. Its last scheduled run was 2026-08-01 (KS-365 comments db01e8bc and d27de4b7). GitHub Actions is retired for this repository (Kam, 2026-08-27).
* **The replacement.** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/base-image-watch.sh` is run by hand. Its usage line calls the plain run "the monthly run", and KS-365 comment 8fe9efd6 says Wednesday runs it on the 1st of each month from a Secuura session. That is monthly and by hand, not weekly.
* **The last recorded re-scan.** KS-365 comment f00e3aa5 (2026-09-08): digest sha256:fe0737ba... unchanged, the CVE present. KS-365 records no re-scan after that date.
* **Board search**, includeArchived, by symbol (controls fired: the term msgpackr hits KS-1379; a random token hits 0). `base-image-watch`: 3 open literal hits and 3 closed. `base-image-refresh`: 2 open and 1 closed. The open hits are KS-365; KS-1446 (Renovate and EXCLUDED_BASES); KS-1669 (Renovate against the Dependabot ruling); and KS-636 (the node:24-alpine critical that the 2026-08-01 run flagged and nobody read). None of them owns scheduling the watch. KS-636 is the nearest, and was written on 2026-08-14, before Actions was retired.
* **Wednesday's scheduled jobs** were not found to run it, by Wednesday's read of her launchd list and scheduler folder just before her mail of 2026-11-06T05:45:38Z. Her read was a name grep, so it says little about a job under another name.

## UNMEASURED

* Whether anything outside the repository schedules the watch under another name. The instrument that closes it is the list of scheduled jobs read by what each job runs, not by its name.
* Whether the script has run at all since 2026-09-08. KS-365 records no run.
* Whether the hand run that KS-365 comment 8fe9efd6 describes happened on 2026-10-01 or 2026-11-01.

## Related

KS-365 (the ticket whose accepted residual relies on this watch) and KS-636 (the unread-alarm channel for the same watch). Who runs the watch, how often, and where a failure should land are not decided here.

title: Security: a demoted or deleted ORG_ADMIN or ISSUER_ADMIN whose token is still live can mint and revoke API keys (tenant-level and own organisation)
description:
## BLUF

A user whose token says ORG_ADMIN or ISSUER_ADMIN, and whose `users` row no longer holds that role or is no longer active, can still mint and revoke API keys: 201 and 200 on every shape measured, tenant-level and own-organisation alike. The key routes read no `users` row for these two roles. It is the same harm as KS-2032, for the two roles a login actually issues. KS-2032's predicate is ADMIN-only and its card rules ADMIN, so it does not reach them. Facts only; nothing is built. Whether the rule extends is Kam's.

## Measured

Seat Y 6th, 2026-11-06. The real `POST /api/keys` and `DELETE /api/keys/:id` on real PostgreSQL 15.19 as the least-privilege app role, on develop `299b9d6a3827` plus the KS-2032 working tree (which does not touch these two roles). Node v26.8.1, not an LTS line. Tokens hand-signed RS256: token role, tenant T, organisation A1, the user's id. Each row is one run of all four calls.

| token role | stored role / status | mint, no organisation | revoke a tenant-level key | mint for own organisation | revoke own organisation's key |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| ORG_ADMIN | org_admin / active (control) | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ORG_ADMIN | user / active | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ORG_ADMIN | verifier / active | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ORG_ADMIN | org_admin / deleted | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ORG_ADMIN | org_admin / suspended | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ISSUER_ADMIN | issuer_admin / active (control) | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ISSUER_ADMIN | user / active | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ISSUER_ADMIN | verifier / active | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ISSUER_ADMIN | issuer_admin / deleted | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ISSUER_ADMIN | issuer_admin / suspended | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |

Instrument control: the same mint with a token for another tenant answers 403.

Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatY-6th/evidence/ks2032/finding2_head.json`; the probe is `tools/ks2032_finding2_probe.integration.test.ts` in that folder. Evidence only, not committed to the repo.

## Read at source, not run

Lines at develop `299b9d6a3827`.

* `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:235`: for an org-bounded role, an unqualified target is allowed same-tenant. Kam's 2026-09-03 ruling for org-less keys.
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:838`: an admin's change to a user revokes that user's sessions only when the new status forbids a credential. So a role-only demotion leaves the session alive.
* `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:672`: the gateway checks the session, not the `users` row, and fails open if the session store is unreachable. So through the gateway, a status shape above should die at 401 while the store is up, and a role-only demotion should not. Not run through the gateway.
* `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:257`: `mapDbRole` issues ORG_ADMIN and ISSUER_ADMIN from stored rows, and has no key for ADMIN. So, by reading, these two roles are the ones real logins carry, and ADMIN is not (KS-2032's PR records that).
* `services/security/src/adminScope.ts:45`: `LIVE_ADMIN_USER_PREDICATE` is ADMIN-only and cannot serve these roles.

## Not measured

* A real demotion through `PATCH /api/users/admin/:id`, or any of this through the gateway.
* The real token lifetime on any box (compose default 1 day, code default 1 hour; the box values are not read).
* Whether any user on a box is in one of these states with a live token.
* Whether a tenant-level key reaches more than an organisation key: KS-2032's open item, still open.

## Open question (a decision, not made here)

Should these two roles also need a live `users` row holding that role at mint and revoke? It would be a new authorisation rule, not KS-2032's predicate, and it costs a database read on these roles' mints and revokes. Wednesday cards it for Kam with this figure.

title: governance: an admin in one tenant can set stake and flags on another tenant's existing participant row
description:
**BLUF:** A platform admin in tenant T1 can change the stake, DRep status and committee status of a participant row owned by a user in tenant T2. QA gate 219 measured this at PR 2039 and at the develop before it, so it is not a regression. Nothing is fixed here. It needs a ruling, then a migration.

**Measured by the gate** (real compiled service, real JWT verification and router, real PostgreSQL as secuura_app):

* An admin in T1 on a row owned by a T2 user: 201, and stake, DRep and committee all change.
* One wallet linked in both tenants: the T1 admin binds it to the T1 user, the T2 owner gets 409, and a T2 admin's registration then writes onto the T1 user's row.

**Cause:** svc_governance_participants has no tenant column and no row-level security. Ruling D2 (a) on KS 1951 protects only the first bind, when no row holds the wallet yet. Once a row holds it, the admin path writes without reading a tenant. The comment in db.ts saying an admin in one tenant never binds another tenant's user is true only for a new row.

**What the ruling has to weigh:**

* **Precedent:** Kam's KS 1906 ruling keeps vc-issuer's owner-less credentials with "platform administrators of their tenant". Whether that reaches governance is not ruled.
* **The seeded SYSTEM_ADMIN sits in the default tenant** (userRepo.ts:1420). Today the only way that admin can stake a user in a provisioned tenant is this path: the owner self-registers, then the admin's stake lands on the row. Closing it plainly takes that away, so someone needs a named way to stake those users.
* **Other writers:** this was measured on the register route only. The other governance routes that read this table were not walked for the same shape.

**Fix shape, read only, not tried:** a tenant column on svc_governance_participants, backfilled from users, with row-level security and the same GUC the users read uses. A row whose id is not a user id (a legacy uuid row) has no tenant to backfill from, so it needs its own rule.

**Proposed priority:** High, because it writes vote power across a tenant boundary. The priority is for the humans to set.
