title: Security: three certification write routes have NO per-record access check - POST /:id/verify, /:id/share and /:id/recertify, while /:id/revoke checks the issuer and /issue gates on a write role
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/certifications/:id/verify`**,** `/:id/share` **and** `/:id/recertify` **carry no per-record access check.** They look a certification up by primary key and act on it. The only authorization on the path is the router-wide `authenticate()` plus tenant scoping, so **an authenticated caller in the same tenant** can reach a certification they are not a party to. The sibling write `POST /:id/revoke` **does** check (`certification.issuer.id !== issuer.id` -> 403), and `POST /issue` gates on a write role — so this is a gap between sibling routes in one file, not a missing convention.

Found while building the read bound for [KS-1695](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1695) (PR #1667), by enumerating every by-id lookup in the file. **Facts only; no remedy proposed.** The read gap and this are the same class on different verbs.

## Measured at develop `7e3b9362e08b` (file: `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts`)

| route | opens | by-id lookup | `isAllowedByRoleOrScope` | `403` occurrences | per-record check |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /issue` | `:180` | — | **1** (`:234`) | 5 | role/scope gate |
| `POST /:id/revoke` | `:1064` | `:1086` | 0 | **1** | **YES** — `issuer.id` mismatch -> 403 |
| `POST /:id/verify` | `:1139` | `:1150` | 0 | **0** | **NONE** |
| `POST /:id/share` | `:1209` | `:1232` | 0 | **0** | **NONE** |
| `POST /:id/recertify` | `:1310` | `:1332` | 0 | **0** | **NONE** |

**The whole file has exactly one router-level gate:** `certificationsRouter.use(authenticate())` at `:65` — authentication, no role term, no record term. `isAllowedByRoleOrScope` appears **twice in the file in total**: the import at `:48` and the single call at `:234` inside `POST /issue`.

**Instruments, and the control for each.**

* The per-route counts are a line-span census of each route's body. **Control: the counter is not stuck at zero** — the same census returns `isAllowedByRoleOrScope = 1` for `POST /issue` and `403 = 1` for `/:id/revoke`. An earlier run of this same census was discarded because a shell quoting fault made `sed` error and every count read `0` from empty input; the zeros above come from a run whose control fires.
* A body census cannot see a middleware gate, so **all four route headers were read directly.** Every middleware array holds only `express-validator` terms (`param`, `body`) — no rbac middleware on any of them.

**A claim in the file that this falsifies.** The comment above `:234` reads: *"KS-547 (KS-540 F-2): certification issuance gates like every other document-write verb — this was the one ungated write on the platform."* On the same router, three write verbs are ungated beyond authentication. Whatever was true when KS-547 shipped, "the one ungated write" does not describe this file now.

## What each route does once it is past the lookup

* `/:id/share` takes `recipients[].email` **from the caller** (validated as an email, `:1212-1217`) and creates share records for a certification the caller need not be a party to. It checks `status === 'revoked'` and nothing about who is asking.
* `/:id/recertify` mints a verification certificate against the original (`originalCert`, lookup `:1332`) and writes a `RECERTIFY` lineage event.
* `/:id/verify` reads and returns verification data; `getUserFromRequest` is not even consulted for a 401, unlike the other two.

## NOT measured — read this before acting on the table

* **None of these three routes was run.** There is no Docker on the host this was found on, so every row above is a source read at one sha, not an observed response. No status code in this ticket was returned by a server.
* **The audience is stated as "an authenticated caller in the same tenant", deliberately.** Gate BX1's measured phrase for the *read* routes — "every same-tenant user of any organisation" — is **not** carried over here, because nothing was executed against these routes and no reader role was tried. Whether a role incidentally blocks any of them is unverified.
* **Whether a share yields the sharer content they could not otherwise see is UNREAD.** `saveShare`, the share mailer, and the lineage share surface were not opened. The documents read admits a `recipientEmail`, and share delivery emails a link — either could matter, neither was followed.
* Whether `/:id/recertify`'s minted certificate is readable by, or attributed to, the caller: not traced.
* Tenant resolution uses `getReqTenantId`, which **falls back to a fixed default tenant** when `req.tenantId` is unset (`:107`, `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`). What that means for these three routes specifically was not measured.
* **Not a duplicate, as far as a weak instrument can say.** `searchIssues` is unusable for counting here: a nonsense control term (`qqzz-control-term-no-such-thing-5417`) returned **12 hits, identical to every real term**. So candidates were read rather than counted. [KS-834](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-834) **is NOT this** — it concerns the **api-gateway's** mock verify route (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:556`) being mounted with no auth handler: a different file and a different route that shares the URL path. [KS-1664](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1664) is recertify's anchor-before-write ordering, not access. Nothing was found covering share or recertify access — stated as "nothing found", not "nothing exists".

nodes.body: @kamil.kreiser — Platform S's side, from S's code at develop `61bdbd3` (20 Oct), so the audience question has one measured client in it: **S never calls `POST /api/certifications/:id/verify`, `/:id/share`, `/:id/recertify` or `/:id/revoke`.** The only certification route S addresses is `POST /api/certifications/issue` (`CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs:308`, the declare verb, always with `parentDocumentId` and `holderEmail`); S's share, revoke and transfer verbs go to the **document** routes (`/api/documents/{id}/share`, `/revoke`, `/transfer-custody`), never to a certification by id. S holds the certification ids K returns only as anchor evidence and never addresses them. So gating these three costs S nothing, and no S traffic will appear in a census of their callers.

title: Security: GET /api/gdpr/deletion-log with no userId reads every tenant's deletion log — unfiltered SELECT on a table with no tenant_id, admitted to ORG_ADMIN
description:
**BLUF —** `GET /api/gdpr/deletion-log` **called with no** `userId` **runs an unfiltered** `SELECT` **over** `data_deletion_log`**, a table with no** `tenant_id` **column and no RLS policy, and the route admits** `ORG_ADMIN`**. So one organisation's admin can read the newest 100 deletion-log rows of every tenant on the deployment. Source-read on develop** `3a6f1810981e`**; NOT driven on a real Postgres as a second tenant's** `ORG_ADMIN` **— see Not measured.**

### The chain, with the instrument named for each count

| \# | fact | instrument |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | the route is `gdprRouter.get('/deletion-log', requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN'), …)` and passes `req.query.userId` straight through | `routes/gdpr.ts:623-626`, read at develop `3a6f1810981e` |
| 2 | with no `userId`, the service runs `SELECT * FROM data_deletion_log ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 100` — **no** `WHERE` **of any kind** | `services/gdprService.ts:1022-1034` |
| 3 | `data_deletion_log` has **no** `tenant_id` **column**: `id, user_id, dsr_id, data_type, records_affected, deletion_method, reason, performed_by, created_at` | `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:473-483` |
| 4 | **no migration attaches an RLS policy to it** | `grep -rn "data_deletion_log" migrations/*.sql \| grep -iE "rls\|policy\|row level"` → 0 lines; the same grep without the second filter returns the two migrations that do touch it (`001`, `036`), so the instrument discriminates |
| 5 | the row reaches HTTP verbatim: `mapDeletionLogRow` copies `reason: r.reason` into `DeletionLogEntry.reason`, and `res.json({ success: true, logs })` returns it | `gdprService.ts:505-517`, `routes/gdpr.ts:627` |
| 6 | it is in the API contract | `originate.openapi.ts:2863`, `deletionLog: z.array(z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())).optional()` |
| 7 | only **4** non-test references to the table exist in the whole repo (2 `INSERT`, 2 `SELECT`) | `grep -rn "data_deletion_log" --include='*.ts' services packages`, minus `__tests__`; control token on the same instrument returns 0 |
| 8 | **no existing ticket covers this read** | census of **all 678** team issues, fetched paginated and matched locally: `data_deletion_log` appears in exactly one (KS-758, which names it only in its F9 prose); control term returns 0. `searchIssues` was **not** used to establish absence — it returns 12 hits for a deliberately meaningless term |

### What an `ORG_ADMIN` of tenant B therefore sees

Rows written for tenant A's subjects: the `data_type` erased, the `records_affected` count, `performed_by` (for connector erasures, `connector:<connectorId>` — a Platform-S organisation identifier), `created_at`, and `reason`. A `user_id` is present on the resolved-subject path, so tenant A's **user UUIDs** are in that payload too.

### Why it is filed now

It was found while censusing the readers of `reason` for KS-758 F9, which asks what the unresolvable connector-erasure path should record. The answer turned on this: anything written into `reason` is published on this endpoint, which is why KS-758's option (a) — the subject's `external_ref` as written — would put a Platform-S subject reference on a cross-tenant readable response. **That is evidence for KS-758's card, and the read itself is a separate defect from what KS-758 records**, so it is here rather than folded in.

### Not measured — stated plainly rather than implied

* **This is a source read.** The endpoint was **not** driven on a real Postgres while authenticated as a second tenant's `ORG_ADMIN`. Steps 1-6 are the code path; the exploit is inferred from them and has not been executed.
* **Whether a deployment actually has more than one tenant's rows in the table** is not measured here, and per-tenant database separation would change the blast radius. (The project's isolation model is per-tenant databases with RLS inert by construction — if that holds for every environment, the cross-tenant reach may be nil in practice and the defect is then the missing guard rather than a live exposure. Unverified either way by me.)
* `requireRole`**'s own semantics** — whether `ORG_ADMIN` is scoped to a tenant by the middleware before the handler runs — was not read. If it is, step 1 still permits the unfiltered query, because the handler applies no scope of its own.
* The resolved-subject path (`user_id` present) was not separately enumerated for how many such rows a real deployment holds.

### No remedy is proposed here

The shape of the fix is a design decision on a GDPR audit surface — add a tenant column and filter, scope by the caller's organisation, or restrict the route to `SYSTEM_ADMIN` — and each has a different effect on what an `ORG_ADMIN` can legitimately audit. It is ruled before it is built.

*Found 2026-10-20 by Seat G 13th while building KS-758 F9 (option (b)); develop* `3a6f1810981e3e268e77d0e4721987d186b71810`*.*

nodes.body:
@kamil.kreiser — what of Platform S's is on that surface, from S's code at develop `61bdbd3` (20 Oct), for the ruling. **S never reads `GET /api/gdpr/deletion-log`**: S's erasure client (`Services/Erasure/PlatformKErasureClient.cs`) calls only `POST /api/gdpr/erasures` (person erasure, keyed by the person's GUID as `externalRef`) and the organisation `erase-connector` route, and reads back only their own responses. So S is not a reader here and no remedy shape costs S anything.

What the unfiltered read exposes **about** S's subjects, per your chain: on the connector path `performed_by` is `connector:<connectorId>`, which identifies an **S organisation** (its K connector), and `reason` — since #1666 (KS-758 F9) — carries a keyed hash of the S person GUID, which you have already noted is anchorable by anyone holding a reference. Those are the two S-derived values a second tenant's `ORG_ADMIN` would see, plus counts and timestamps; no email, name or file name reaches that table from S's erasures. From S's side any of the three remedies is fine; a `SYSTEM_ADMIN`-only read is the one that needs no schema change and matches who on S can request an erasure (an Administrator or the organisation's own admin, never another organisation's).

title: Security: same-tenant read gaps on certifications and owner-less documents — GET /api/certifications/:id has NO ownership check at all, and an empty owner skips the documents.ts:1124 cloak (both pre-existing, measured by gate BX1)
description:
## BLUF

**Two pre-existing read gaps in** `services/originate`**, both measured on real Postgres 15 as** `secuura_app` **(NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS) by gate BX1 while gating PR #1659.** Facts only — **no fix is proposed here**, because the remedy is a design on an auth read path and is ruled before it is built.

1. `GET /api/certifications/:id` **has no owner, holder or org check at all.** A **human-issued** certification that the documents GET *does* cloak is served **200 to every same-tenant user of any organisation**.
2. **An empty owner skips the documents cloak.** `documentRepo.ts:176` derives `''` from `owner_user_id` NULL + `issuer_user_id` NULL, and `documents.ts:1124`'s conjunction is false on `''`, so the 404 cloak never runs. Affects **bare-connector documents** (on `develop` today) and, since `3cc46ae41fed`, **holder-less connector certifications**.

Neither was introduced by PR #1659. KS-1659's fold added a new **row type** to gap 2's existing class, not a new audience, and the gate's control proves it.

## ⚠ This falsifies KS-621's central premise for one row class

KS-621 is the tracking ticket for "document reads are scoped by tenant and owner, never by organization", and it states: *"**Nothing is leaking.** Cross-org document reads are denied today, and that was proved with a control... What actually denies the read is a **per-owner 404-cloak**."* **That cloak does not run when the owner is empty.** For owner-less rows the emergent cross-org protection KS-621 describes is therefore **absent, not merely unenforced**. A comment has been left on KS-621 pointing here.

## Measured audiences (gate BX1)

**a** = same-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN`, same organisation · **a2** = same-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN`, **another** organisation · **b** = another tenant · **c** = the issuing connector.

| row | tree | endpoint | a | a2 | b | c |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| connector certification, no holder | landing | `GET /api/documents/:id` | **200** | **200** | 404 | **200** |
| **bare-connector** `POST /api/documents` (owner NULL, issuer NULL) | **develop AND landing** | `GET /api/documents/:id` | **200** | **200** | 404 | **200** |
| human-issued certification, no holder (owner = issuer = a UUID) | both | `GET /api/documents/:id` | 404 | 404 | 404 | 404 |
| **human-issued certification** | **develop AND landing** | `GET /api/certifications/:id` | **200** | **200** | 404 | — |
| connector certification, no holder | landing | `GET /api/certifications/:id` | **200** | **200** | 404 | **200** |

The owner-less 200 body carries `"owner":{"id":""}` plus title, data and contentHash. The human-certification row being 404 on the documents path is the **positive control**: the cloak works when the owner is non-empty, so these 200s are not "everything is readable".

**Audience for the owner-less class: the whole tenant, every organisation, all roles.** ⚠ **Kam's KS-1116 ruling — owner-less rows readable by the row tenant's administrators (**`ORG_ADMIN` **/** `SYSTEM_ADMIN` **with a tenant on the token) — is NARROWER than what ships today for both row types.**

**List endpoints are not affected:** `documents.ts:321` filters on `d.owner?.id === userId` and the certifications list filters on holder or issuer id. Only **c** saw the new id in a list.

## Where

* **Gap 1:** `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:956-1010` — calls `getCertification(id, tenantId)` and returns issuer, holder, data and blockchain with no access predicate.
* **Gap 2:** `services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts:176` → `id: row.owner_user_id || row.issuer_user_id || ''`; `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1124` → `if (userId && document.owner?.id && document.owner.id !== userId && !isAdmin && !isRecipient)`.

## The remedy shapes BX1 costed — options, NOT a decision

1. **Fail the cloak closed at** `documents.ts:1124` (drop the `document.owner?.id &&` conjunct). One line, covers both row types. **Cost, measured: it strands the issuing connector.** A bare connector create writes **no** `create` **row in** `action_provenance` (0 rows against 12 documents), so `wasCreatedByConnector` never admits it, and per the KS-480 §6 comment at `:1126` Platform S drives the whole lifecycle through that id. Needs a companion — record a create row, or admit a connector whose organisation matches the row's. **Does nothing for gap 1.**
2. **Cloak an empty owner to admins plus the creating connector** — the KS-1116 ruling shape. Same edit plus a tenant-admin admit; same provenance dependency; does not cover gap 1.
3. **Set the owner at write time** from the connector's organisation or a tenant administrator. Reads unchanged, but it changes custody semantics (`anchorOverwriteGuard`), needs a write-path lookup, and does nothing for existing bare-connector rows.
4. **Refuse a holder-less connector certification** (400 `HOLDER_REQUIRED`). Smallest blast radius; returns to develop's "no row" with an honest error instead of 22P02-as-payload. A **client-visible contract change for Platform S**, and the bare-document class stays as it is.
5. **For gap 1: give** `GET /api/certifications/:id` **the same predicate** as `documents.ts:1124`. **Without it, options 1 and 2 do not close certification reads.**

**Plan against Kam's KS-1116 ruling**, which is the nearest precedent: a remedy matching that audience inherits his authority; a different audience is a new decision for him.

## Not measured

No gateway and no real JWT layer — BX1 mounted the routers directly with the repo's probe-user auth mock, so **any scope gating at api-gateway is unmeasured** and could narrow these audiences in production. Also not run: `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true`, a `system_admin` or recipient reader, an `onBehalfOf` connector certification, the derived lineage row. The remedies were not built.

## Board search before filing

`owner_user_id` (control: 9 hits), "GET /api/certifications/:id ownership check", "certifications read no ownership check same tenant", "documents.ts cloak empty owner", "owner-less document readable by same tenant", "bare connector document no owner". **Controls both ways:** a freshly generated never-published token returned **0**; `owner_user_id` returned 9. Nearest neighbours: **KS-621** (the tracking ticket whose premise this corrects), **KS-1688** (the same class on `POST /api/documents/:id/version`, a different endpoint), KS-1603/KS-1652 (anchoring ownership), KS-1683/KS-1684 (vc-issuer reads). **None owns these two endpoints.**

Related KS-1659, KS-1116, KS-621.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1667 merged as 88933d5c7ebb on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (recorded deploy, 2026-11-01). Verified by code read at b1fb543640e7, not observed live (it needs same-tenant users of two organisations). Left open: gap 2, the owner-less documents cloak, is unbuilt.

- **Gap 1 is in the code:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:133` defines who may read a certification (issuer, holder or platform administrator), :161 takes the platform role from the repo's one definition, :177 is the single refusal shared with an unknown id, and :1038 binds the read on the record before the expiry write. `ks1695-certification-reads-need-issuer-holder-or-admin.test.ts` pins it (R1 to R4 at :165-:186, the refusal body byte-identical to the unknown-id body).
- **Left open, as comments a3811a16 and 1c91168b record it:** gap 2 (an empty owner skips the `documents.ts` cloak) waits on Kam's card; the PR said `Refs`, not `Closes`, for that reason.

## Correction to my own earlier comment on this ticket

**I claimed, in this thread and three other places, that *"originate recognises `platform_admin` in no predicate of its own"*. It does.**

```
services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:60
  const SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES = ['super_admin', 'SUPER_ADMIN', 'SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'platform_admin'];
services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:78      (inside resolveTenantId)
  if (u?.role && SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES.includes(u.role)) {
```

**Used, not dead.** `resolveTenantId` gives a caller in that set cross-tenant tenant resolution (`req.tenantId`, then `?organizationId`, then the user's own org), where a tenant-bound admin gets only its own organisation.

**The instrument that produced the false claim, named.** My original census was `grep -rn "platform_admin" services packages | head -20`. The run had **41** non-test lines; `head` cut it at 20 and originate's fell below the cut. *A count that passes through `head` is a count of what fitted, not of what matched* — and I repeated it four times without re-running it. This is one hop further out than the lesson I cited in my previous correction here: that one was a census keyed on a string literal missing a value from a DB column; this one is a census whose **output was truncated**.

**Untruncated, per service** (non-test lines, `git grep` at develop `88933d5c7ebb`) — **41 total**: auth 21, api-gateway 7, **originate 4**, packages/shared 3, anchoring 3, tokenisation 1, security 1, m365-integration 1. Excluding references to the `platform_admins` **table**, which are not a role value: api-gateway 7, **originate 4**, auth 3, anchoring 3, packages/shared 2, tokenisation 1, security 1. Three of originate's four are the RLS bypass sentinel `app.tenant_scope_bypass = 'platform_admin'` (`db.ts:167`, `db.ts:191`, a comment at `documents.ts:1916`) and are **not** role claims; the fourth is `adminConfig.ts:60`.

**What changes and what does not.** The **outcome** — `platform_admin` refused on the three by-id certification reads — is unchanged; it stays Wednesday's ruling (a), and Kam now holds a card carrying the corrected facts. What is corrected is the **basis**, which was a fact I supplied. And the real inconsistency is sharper than the gateway-versus-originate one I described: **inside originate**, the same token is a super-admin for tenant resolution and a stranger to its own certification reads.

**Not measured:** no live token was decoded, and I have not shown that any real principal carries this role.

Also filed from this census: **KS 1701** — four originate sites hand-write the platform-admin role set and all four omit `SUPER_ADMIN` (`documents.ts:1076` and `:299`, `certifications.ts:959` and `:123`), which is the same omission that caused the measured regression caught in this ticket's round 2.

## Gap 1 is MERGED — `88933d5c7ebbb0af6ba1a1d4504998d581ba66c0`, tree `58849ee421ba16a6c7f8d2fb8e363d143653eced`, one parent `f418cddac51498adda34cfed0bf5486a2d8cca77`

**This ticket stays open.** The PR says `Refs`, never `Closes`: gap 2 (owner-less documents) is unbuilt.

**What shipped.** All three by-id certification reads — `GET /api/certifications/:id`, `GET /:id/lineage`, `GET /:id/evidence-bundle` — are now bound on the record by one shared helper: a **platform administrator** (via `isPlatformRole`, the repo's single definition), the **issuer**, or the **holder**. An empty principal never matches, so a bare-connector row whose issuer and holder both map to `''` is not open to everyone. The refusal is emitted by the same function as the unknown-id 404, so the two bodies cannot drift and a refused reader cannot tell "not yours" from "no such certification". The check precedes **every** side effect that used to run for a refused reader: the expiry write (and the `certification_events` row it writes), the `evidence_export` **charge event**, and the **share lookup** on both sibling reads.

**The gap this closes, in gate BX1's measured words:** **every same-tenant user of ANY organisation** read 200 — **a** (same tenant, same organisation) and **a2** (same tenant, another organisation) both 200; **b** (another tenant) 404; **c** (the issuing connector) 200 on a connector certification. Measured readers were **`ISSUER_ADMIN` only**; "all roles" was an inference from source, not a measurement.

**Kept working, deliberately:** the issuing connector still reads its own holder-less certification, the issuer keeps both sibling reads (the issuer UI calls them), another tenant is still 404, an allowed reader of an expired certification still gets the expiry write, and an allowed bundle reader is still billed.

**Evidence.** Whole `services/originate` suite **136 files / 1,613 tests / 0 failed** (baseline 135 / 1,575 / 0, so +37 is exactly this PR's cells, 0 vanished). Red-proof against develop's route blob: **22 failed / 15 passed / 37**. Against the first round's own helper: **3 failed / 34 passed** — that round had introduced a regression, refusing a platform administrator whose token says `SUPER_ADMIN`, and the 3 reds are what proved it. **9 mutants, 9 killed**, each type-checked clean first and each killing a named cell by assertion, including both mutants the review gate wrote itself.

**Two differences from develop we accept knowingly, both recorded rather than smoothed over:**
- For `SUPER_ADMIN` this by-id read is **more permissive than the certification list route**, which keeps its narrower literal set. Recorded, not resolved.
- A token whose role is **`platform_admin` now reads 404** where develop answered 200 (develop had no check at all). Ruled deliberately: originate recognises that spelling in no predicate of its own. An earlier draft of mine called it "gateway-only" — **that was wrong**: auth mints it verbatim from the `platform_admins` row and the column permits it. The narrower truth is that the table is created empty on purpose and the column defaults to `super_admin`. Recorded on [KS-1536](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1536).

**Residue, carried openly:**
- An exact **holder** compare is **unpinned** — a case-insensitive holder mutant survives all 37 cells. `R17` pins the issuer compare only.
- Adopting `isPlatformRole` also adopts [KS-1591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1591): its `toUpperCase` admits a dotless-i, a long-s and an array role as `SUPER_ADMIN`. Reachability rests on reading code; no live token was decoded.
- The same class on the **write** verbs of this router is [KS-1699](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1699) (High): `POST /:id/verify`, `/:id/share` and `/:id/recertify` have no per-record access check, while `/:id/revoke` checks the issuer.
- A transferee reading by id is [KS-1697](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1697).
- Platform S reading with a non-issuer key remains **reported, not measured** — Stuart's statement from S's code, which this project's token cannot read.
- The four platform suites were not run (no Docker on the build host) and the pre-push preflight reported `13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED` on every push; nothing was exercised through a real gateway or real Postgres.

## Round 2 pushed — PR #1667 at `c502c6434cf299d09b47b7b0ca354338f5892410`

Gate CF1 returned **GO WITH NOTE** on round 1 (0 blockers, 5 notes) and round 2 was ruled. The two notes that were code are closed; the rest are recorded as residue on the PR.

**N2 was a regression I introduced, and the measurement is the point.** Round 1 hand-wrote the admit set by copying the certification list route's literal `isAdmin` (`certifications.ts:906`), which **omits `SUPER_ADMIN`** — so a real platform administrator went from 200 to **404**. It now calls **`isPlatformRole`** (`packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:140`), the repo's single definition of a platform role, which upper-cases the claim so both casings of `SYSTEM_ADMIN` and `SUPER_ADMIN` pass.

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| develop, no check at all | **21 failed / 15 passed** — every refusal cell red, and all four admin spellings **200** |
| round 1, hand-written set | **2 failed / 34 passed** — exactly the `SUPER_ADMIN` cells, nothing else |
| round 2, `isPlatformRole` | **37 / 37** |

Two consequences stated rather than hidden: for `SUPER_ADMIN` this by-id read is now **more permissive than the list route**, which keeps its narrower literal set — recorded, not resolved; and **`platform_admin` stays refused**, pinned by a cell named as a known accepted difference. That spelling was 200 on develop (no check existed). It is a gateway-only spelling — 6 non-test sites, all under `services/api-gateway`, **zero** in originate and **zero** in `packages/shared` (control: `super_admin` matches 20 files) — so admitting it here would make this route originate's first and only site for it. Recorded on KS 1536, which already is that ticket.

**N3** adds the cells the gate's own mutants found: no share lookup for a refused reader on **both** sibling reads, and an **exact** issuer compare, so upper-cased, prefix, suffix and whitespace variants of the issuer id are all refused — with a control proving the exact id is 200 so the cell can fail.

**Evidence.** Whole `services/originate` suite **136 files / 1,613 tests / 0 failed**; baseline **135 / 1,575 / 0**, so +37 is exactly this PR's cells with 0 vanished. **9 mutants, 9 killed**, each type-checked clean first and each killing a named cell by assertion — including the gate's own two. Predicted landing tree `8d61d5a1595680848790aa6337fa0e4cd4531721` against develop `c3ea4dc79af72f62ad7f211d1dbf8b9920ea094d`, two independent derivations agreeing.

**Not a pass, and not quoted as one:** the pre-push preflight reported `PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.` on both pushes — legs 3, 4 and 8 skipped for want of a local stack. The four platform suites were not run (no Docker on the build host), and nothing was exercised through a real gateway or real Postgres.

**Residue carried on the PR, not closed here:** the three ungated certification **write** routes (KS 1699); the stale E2E transfer spec (KS 1697); Stuart's Platform S statement, which is reported and not measured; and the fact that adopting `isPlatformRole` also adopts **KS 1591** — its `toUpperCase` admits a dotless-i, a long-s and an array role as `SUPER_ADMIN`, which round 1's literal set would not have. I did not pin those three as admitted, deliberately: a green cell asserting a spoofable spelling is accepted would turn a KS 1591 fix into a test failure.

This ticket stays open: gap 2 (owner-less documents) is unbuilt and waits on Kam's card.

## Gap 1 is built and at the gate — PR #1667 at `d7c2e296c9099ec9a0efd8db4d2f51210381ffc4`

**Scope: gap 1 only.** Gap 2 (owner-less documents) is untouched and still waits on Kam's card, which is why the PR says `Refs`, not `Closes` — this ticket stays open.

**What shipped.** One shared helper binds all **three** by-id certification reads — `GET /api/certifications/:id`, `GET /:id/lineage` and `GET /:id/evidence-bundle` — on the record, using the rule the certification **list** already applies in-process: a platform admin (`system_admin` / `SYSTEM_ADMIN` / `super_admin`), the issuer, or the holder. `ORG_ADMIN` is not admitted. The refusal is emitted by the same function as the unknown-id 404, so a refused reader cannot tell "not yours" from "no such certification".

**The audience, in gate BX1's own measured words:** **every same-tenant user of ANY organisation** got 200 — **a** (same tenant, same organisation) and **a2** (same tenant, another organisation) both **200**; **b** (another tenant) **404**; **c** (the issuing connector) **200** on a connector certification. Measured readers were **`ISSUER_ADMIN` only**; "all roles" is an inference from source, not a measurement.

**Why the two sibling reads are in the same PR, not a follow-up.** Both were confirmed unbound at source. `/:id/lineage` returns **share recipients' email addresses and names**, and `/:id/evidence-bundle` writes an `evidence_export` **charge event for whoever reads it**. A bound on the by-id read alone would have been one the next route steps around.

**Kept working, deliberately:** the issuing connector still reads its own holder-less certification (its id comes from the `certification_metadata` fallback), the issuer keeps both sibling reads (the issuer UI calls them), another tenant is still 404, and an allowed reader of an expired certification still gets the expiry write.

**Evidence.** Whole `services/originate` suite **136 files / 1,599 tests / 0 failed**; baseline **135 / 1,575 / 0** at the develop this branched from, so +23 is exactly this PR's cells with 0 vanished. Red-proof against develop's `certifications.ts`: **14 failed / 9 passed**, every refusal cell red by assertion and every control green. **7 mutants, 7 killed**, each type-clean first. Two cells (`R13` an empty principal, `R14` an `ORG_ADMIN` non-party) exist only because a mutant survived every other cell.

**Not measured, and worth your eye:**
- **Platform S with a key other than the issuer.** Stuart's comment above says S never calls this route, from S's code at `61bdbd3` — his statement, not our measurement; this project's token cannot read S's repo. A non-issuer S key would go to 404.
- Every `connector:api-key` principal in a tenant is the same principal (KS 1685), so "the issuer matches" admits all such keys in that tenant to certifications any one of them issued — narrower than today, but not per-key.
- The four platform suites were **not** run (no Docker on the build host), and nothing was exercised through a real gateway or real Postgres.
- A transferee reading by id is now an explicit open question, filed as **KS 1697** with facts only: an accepted transfer never rewrites the record's issuer or holder, so a transferee would 404 under any issuer/holder bound — but the E2E spec that asserts otherwise already fails three steps earlier, and no push gate runs it.

**The pre-push preflight did not fully run**, and its own words are: `PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed. legs 3 4 8 — local stack not up … This is NOT a pass. Do not quote it as one — say which legs ran.` Recorded verbatim rather than as green.

PR: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1667 · head `d7c2e296c9099ec9a0efd8db4d2f51210381ffc4` · predicted landing tree `9497977aaa7a159922089b2e6b1abd2cd8927850` computed against develop `f01ba49da56d3d55204caa02ab3348f94d63b9c0`. Awaiting the gate; no merge without a GO naming that head.

@kamil.kreiser — what this means for Platform S's rows, from S's code at develop `61bdbd3` (20 Oct), so the remedy can be costed against the real client.

**Every S document on K is in the owner-less class.** S's people have no K user, so `owner_user_id` is NULL on every S originate (confirmed on slot 4 on 19 Oct: NULL on both the originate document and its `/version` child). The originate body is `title` = **the document's file name** (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:482`, falling back to `SSD document {chainId}` only when the name is blank), `documentType: SSD_DOCUMENT`, `contentHash`, `issuerName`, `description: "SSD upload — chain {chainId}"`, `documentUuid`, `organizationUuid`, `userUuid` (the person's GUID) — plus `onBehalfOf` (email, name, externalRef). So under gap 2 as it ships today, **any same-tenant user of any organisation who holds an S document's id can read its file name, hash and the uploader's identity block** — and a file name is exactly the field KS-695 treats as personal data for erasure. The ids are v4 UUIDs S derives from its own chain id, not enumerable, and the list endpoints filter on owner, so this is a read-by-id exposure, not a listing one. S's certifications always carry `holderEmail` (never holder-less), so the holder-less certification row type does not arise from S.

**How each remedy lands on S:**
- **Option 1 (fail the cloak closed) does NOT strand S's connector** in the normal case: S sends `onBehalfOf` on every connector originate (my 13 Oct answer on KS-1557, `290ae741`), so a `create` row with S's connector id exists on every S-originated document and `wasCreatedByConnector` admits it. The exception is the three attribution-less cases named there (service-identity fallback when the organisation has no key; a system-made row with no actor; a person with no email) — those documents have no row and would become unreadable to S too; S already treats that state as degraded. Version-minted children get their row from #1654's `create:connector` (which is why that fix has to land first for S, exactly as KS-1688 says).
- **Option 2 (admins + creating connector)** — same as option 1 for S.
- **Option 3 (set the owner at write time from the connector's organisation)** — works for S if "owner" then means the organisation; S's custody flows already run on the organisation column (KS-1402 ruling (a)).
- **Option 4 (400 `HOLDER_REQUIRED`)** — a no-op for S, which never sends a holder-less certification.
- **Option 5 (gap 1)** — S never calls `GET /api/certifications/:id`, so no cost to S either way.

From S's side the preference is 1 (or 2) plus 5, sequenced after #1654.

title: auth: revokeAllUserSessions returns 0 with no throw when the session store is down, so the admin status change and the user-erasure subscriber silently revoke nothing (session.ts:317-318)
description:
## BLUF

`revokeAllUserSessions` **answers** `0` **and does NOT throw when the Redis session store is unreachable** (`services/auth/src/services/session.ts:317-318`: `if (!redisAvailable) return 0;`). Two callers treat that `0` as "there was nothing to revoke" and carry on reporting success. The sessions then validate again when Redis recovers.

**The same module throws in the same condition elsewhere:** `createSession` at `:156` raises `'Redis is not available — cannot create session'`. The inconsistency is the defect.

Filed on Wednesday's ruling after gate BO1 on PR #1655, which measured this failure mode on the password-reset route. **The two password routes are fixed in that PR** by a route-local guard; these two callers are deliberately out of KS-1407's scope and are why this ticket exists.

## Recommendation

Either make the shared function fail closed (a strict variant, or a throw plus an explicit opt-out for callers that genuinely tolerate a no-op), or give each caller its own availability check. It is a **wider ruling than one ticket's scope** because it changes behaviour for every caller at once, which is exactly why PR #1655 did not take it.

## The enumeration (every product caller, measured)

| caller | file:line | what it does with the `0` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **user-erasure subscriber** | `services/auth/src/services/userErasedSubscriber.ts:50` | `const sessionsRevoked = await revokeAllUserSessions(userId);` — an **erased** subject's sessions stay live while the store is down. This is the data-protection path and the reason this is High. |
| **admin status change** | `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:838` | inside `if (accountStatusForbidsCredential(updatedUser))` — the KS 796 path whose whole point is "cut the sessions this status cannot hold". With the flag false it cuts none and the status change still answers success. |
| password change / reset | `routes/users.ts`, `routes/auth.ts` | **FIXED in #1655** — both confirm the revocation is possible before the write and re-assert after it. |

Control for the enumeration: the same search shape finds `revokeSession` in **17 files**, so it is not blind.

## Why High rather than Medium

The erasure path is a data-protection obligation: an erasure that reports success while the subject's sessions remain usable is a compliance failure, not only a bug. The admin path is the KS 796 thesis — "this status cannot hold a credential" and "cut the sessions it already has" must not be able to disagree — and under this condition they disagree silently.

## Exposure, stated precisely

While the flag is false the old sessions are refused anyway, because `getSession` returns null. **The exposure is the resurrection after recovery, not the outage itself.** That is the gate's own framing of the equivalent reset case and it applies unchanged here.

## Not measured

I did not drive these two callers against a downed store myself; the mechanism is a source reading of `session.ts:317-318` plus the gate's measurement of the identical path on reset (probe B1: 200, token burned, 0 revoked, and the old session ACTIVE again after recovery). The inference is that the same `return 0` reaches these two callers; the probe for each is not run.

**Board search before filing:** `revokeAllUserSessions`, `userErasedSubscriber`, "admin status change revoke sessions redis unavailable", "revokeAllUserSessions returns 0 silently", "erased subject sessions survive". No open ticket covers this. **Controls both ways:** a freshly generated never-published token returned **0** hits and `revokeAllUserSessions` returned a hit, so the search discriminates.

Related KS-1407.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** QA gate 245 found a third caller of the silent zero this ticket describes: the role-change revoke that PR 2075 (KS-2083) adds. If the session store's availability flag drops after a request was authenticated, the role-change PATCH answers 200 with nothing revoked. Kam's card `secuura-ks2083-session-end-race-in-flight-1107` = a, "Merge with the wording corrected, and ticket the race High (recommended)", ruled 2026-11-08 at 20:32:11 +11:00, says a seat fixes "the store-down case next on a new ticket"; this ticket already carries that case, so no second ticket was filed. Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME, the real `initRedisSession` over a fake client with the error event fired during the write. No state, assignee or priority of this ticket was changed.

**What gate 245 measured (PR 2075, head d2245bf37fe0):** 200, the role written, and a log line `sessionsRevoked: 0` at info. After the store heals, the session is live on both checks and the old token raises a second account (200). PR 2075 names a revoke that throws (500), and not this one. The class is the one KS-1407 B1 fixed on the password path; the role-change path has it too. Narrow window, silent result.

**Where (gate 245's tree):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/services/session.ts` line 332 returns 0, and `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/routes/users.ts` line 846 takes it. This ticket's description cites lines 317 and 318 of the session file on an earlier tree, and lists the status-change caller and the erasure subscriber; the role-change revoke is a third caller.

**Not measured:** real Redis, and any box.

**Source:** gate 245 verdict, finding F2 on PR 2075, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate245-tier1-y-auth/verdict.md`. This seat re-read the verdict and ran nothing else.

**Gate BS1's note N1 is closed. PR #1669 is up at head `4728c1d613038a8082625f79e564837953bd7453` — a revocation that THROWS after the password write now maps onto the same post-write 503 the check-then-act path already produces, on both password doors. This is PR 1 of two: the `session.ts` half (the unguarded `del`, and the silent zero as it reaches the admin status change and the erasure subscriber) is PR 2 and is ruled separately.**

**The gap, in the gate's words:** *"A revocation that THROWS after the write is fail-closed on reset and only half fail-closed on change-password. No author cell pins either."* KS-1407 installed a flag check either side of the write, but `revokeAllUserSessions` can **reject** as well as answer a silent 0, and a throw skipped the post-write re-assert entirely and landed in `next(error)` as a **500 INTERNAL_ERROR**. BS1's probe C3 measured the change-password case: the password *was* written, the attacker session was **still ACTIVE** after recovery, and the natural retry with the old current password answered **400 "Current password is incorrect"**.

**The fix** wraps only the revoke and re-throws as the existing post-write 503, so a store that is DOWN and a store that THROWS are indistinguishable to the caller. Not `.catch(() => 0)` — that is the author's own A5 arm, which the gate measured reding **0 of 23** cells and which would convert this into a 200 with nothing revoked.

**The number that earned the cells: A5 now reds three of them.** The red-proof judges **14 cells — my 5 plus the 9 pre-existing** — so collateral is a failure, and none appeared:

| arm | failing cells |
|---|---|
| no mutation (positive control) | none, **14/14** |
| `.catch(() => 0)` on both routes | **T1 T2 T3** |
| the catch removed (throw → 500) | T1 T2 T3 |
| a swallow that continues to 200 | T1 T2 T3 |
| the "sign in again" clause restored in both 503s | **T3 alone** |
| the post-write re-assert removed | **B1-R2, B1-R3** — not my cells, proving they do not piggyback on the KS-1407 flag guard |

**Two things deliberately not done, both recorded in the PR body.** N4's line-cite half is a **no-op**: at this develop the head has exactly `session.ts:317-318` and `:156`, so the comment is accurate and editing it would make it wrong — the earlier correction was measured against a different tree. And an arm I had planned (A9: "make the revoke resolve 0, T1/T2 must not red") was **false** — a resolving revoke with a healthy store answers 200 while T1 expects 503 — so I replaced it with the independence arm above rather than run an assertion that could not hold.

**A finding now recorded in the route itself:** `authenticate()` already refuses a change-password request when the store is down, verified at source (`validateSession` → `getSession` returns null when the client is unavailable). So that route's pre-check is **defence in depth only**; the post-write mapping is the reachable half, because the store can drop between authentication and the revoke. Both halves are labelled in the code.

**Suite:** `105 files / 1132 → 1137 tests`, **+5, 0 vanished**, reaching `1137 passed, 0 failed, rc 0`. Leg 16 reports auth at `42 errors: 42 in the baseline, 0 new`, so the added test lines introduce no type errors — the gate's figure, not mine.

⚠ **Known residue:** one run of three showed `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity` failing at **5004 ms**, the 5000 ms boundary class already in `BACKLOG.md` across six source-scanning files; my cells failed 0 times in every run. The cells inject the throw at the mock, so they pin the route's *handling* of a rejection and say nothing about which real ioredis conditions produce one. And the change-password route's two 503s now carry byte-identical messages on purpose — T3 pins the clause on both, but nothing pins that they stay equal.

## Gate BS1 adds TWO more members to this family, and one wording fix

While gating PR #1655 (KS-1407, merged `86df4f5a52cc`), gate BS1 measured two further cases of the same root cause this ticket names — `revokeAllUserSessions` not failing closed when the session store is impaired. Verdict `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-20_gate-BS1-pr1655-ks1407-r2/verdict.md` (`sed '1d;$d' | shasum -a 256` = `8480cd2c56ef` = its trailer). Both are **outside** KS-1407's diff and belong here.

### Member: a revocation that THROWS (gate note N1, MEDIUM)
The silent zero is now fail-closed on both password routes. A **throw** is not:
- **Reset (probe R3):** `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, 1 write, **0 burns**; the old session is ACTIVE after recovery, but the retry answers 200, burns once and kills it. Fail-closed.
- **Change-password (probe C3):** `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, the password **was** written, the old session is **ACTIVE** after recovery, and **the caller is told neither**. The natural retry with the old password gets `400 Current password is incorrect`.
- A `.catch(() => 0)` on either route reds **0 of the 23** KS-1407 cells, so no author cell pins this; the gate's R3 and C3 do.
- **Gate's recommended shape:** wrap the revoke in each route and map a throw onto the same post-write **503**, with the "WAS changed / WAS reset" wording, plus one cell per route.

### Member: the unguarded index delete (gate note N2, LOW-MEDIUM, `session.ts:323`)
`revokeAllUserSessions` checks the flag once at `:316`; each `revokeSession` re-checks at `:298` and returns false silently; **`redis.del(user_sessions:<id>)` at `:323` is not guarded.** Probe R4, with 3 sessions and the store flipping mid-loop: the first reset answered 503 with the token unburned, the index set was **deleted anyway**, and the retry then found an empty set, revoked 0 and answered **200 with session 3 still ACTIVE**. The gate's own realism caveat: with real ioredis the window is narrow (a command issued during an outage either resolves after `ready` or rejects, which is the N1 class). Same root as KS-1691's missing tombstone.

### Wording fix to carry in the same round (gate note N4, trivial, mine)
Two defects of my own in the merged KS-1407 code, which the gate directed here rather than to a new PR:
- change-password's post-write 503 says *"Sign in again with the new password"*, but the caller's **own** session survives that path — the gate's C2 made the advised retry on the same bearer and got 200.
- my comments cite `session.ts:317-318` and `:156`; at the merged head the silent zero is at **`:316`** and `createSession`'s throw at **`:155`**.

**This is a later tier-1 round, not now** — per Wednesday's post-merge instruction.

title: auth: a request in flight resurrects a revoked session — updateSessionActivity and rotateSessionRefreshToken write back the stale isActive:true record with a fresh 24h TTL (session.ts:270-294)
description:
## BLUF

**A revocation can be undone by any request that was already in flight.** `updateSessionActivity` (`session.ts:270-279`) and `rotateSessionRefreshToken` (`:282-294`) both do a read-modify-write: `get` the session JSON, mutate, `setex` it back. If `revokeSession` lands between the `get` and the `setex`, the **stale** `isActive:true` **record is written back with a fresh 24-hour TTL** — and the session is live again.

Worse, it becomes **unrevokable**: the revocation already removed it from `user_sessions:<id>`, so a later `revokeAllUserSessions` returns **0** and cannot find it.

Pre-existing. Filed from gate BO1's note N2 on PR #1655.

## Recommendation

Either a **revoked tombstone** that `getSession` checks, or a **conditional write** (a Lua script or a WATCH/MULTI compare-and-set) so a write cannot resurrect a record revoked since it was read. The tombstone is probably cheaper and also fixes the orphaned-from-the-set half.

## Why it matters more than a normal race

`updateSessionActivity` runs on **every authenticated request** (`middleware/authenticate.ts:160`), so the window is open continuously under load rather than at a rare moment. An attacker hammering requests on the old token widens it deliberately. It affects **every** revocation path — logout, the admin status change, user erasure, and the new password change/reset.

## The measurement (gate BO1, probe B3)

The interleave was forced deterministically:

* after the revocation (returned n=1, record inactive), the in-flight write left `getSession` returning the session **ACTIVE**;
* the session was already gone from `user_sessions:<id>`, so a second `revokeAllUserSessions` returned **0** and could not reach it.
* **Control B3c** — the same steps *without* the interleave: the session stayed revoked. So the probe measures the race, not a broken teardown.
* **Not run:** a timing measurement against real Redis. The probe drives the real `session.ts` against a fake that implements the session commands, so the *window's width* in production is unmeasured; its existence is not.

## Where

* `services/auth/src/services/session.ts:270-279` `updateSessionActivity`
* `services/auth/src/services/session.ts:282-294` `rotateSessionRefreshToken`
* called from `services/auth/src/middleware/authenticate.ts:160`

**Board search before filing:** `updateSessionActivity` returned **0** hits; `rotateSessionRefreshToken` returned 4, none about a resurrection race (KS-756 the opaque handle, KS-1687 m365 token persistence, KS-1150 the OAuth grant, KS-329 PQC); also searched "resurrect revoked session" and "session revoked refresh token still redeems". **Controls both ways:** a freshly generated never-published token returned **0**, `revokeAllUserSessions` returned **1**.

Related KS-1407.
