title: auth: the OAuth refresh_token grant never checks the ORIGIN SESSION, so a revoked session's refresh token still redeems and mints a brand-new session (oauth.ts:988-1089)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/oauth/token` **with** `grant_type=refresh_token` **never reads** `decoded.sessionId`**, so revoking a user's sessions does not reach the OAuth refresh path.** A refresh token issued before a revocation still redeems, and mints a *brand-new* session. Measured by the gate on PR #1655 (KS-1407): after `revokeAllUserSessions` (n=1, `getSession` null), the same refresh token redeemed **200**, then **200 again**, leaving the account with **2 live sessions**.

Pre-existing; **outside** that PR's diff. Filed from gate BO1's note N1.

## Recommendation

Check the origin session on this grant (or introduce a per-user credential epoch) before minting. The oracle is already in the repo: the *interactive* `POST /api/auth/refresh` does a server-side session lookup at `routes/auth.ts:688-689`, so the two refresh paths disagree about whether a session must still exist. Wednesday or Kam should rule whether the fix rides with a KS-1407 follow-up or stands alone.

## Where

`services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:988-1089` — the `grant_type=refresh_token` branch. It verifies the JWT, checks the jti denylist, pins `user.status === 'ACTIVE'` at `:1067`, and mints a new session at `:1078`. It never consults the session named by the token it is redeeming.

## The measurement (gate BO1, probe C1)

Real `session.ts`, real `refreshDenylist.ts`, real `jwt.ts`, on the ks823 scaffold:

1. created a session and minted an OAuth pair bound to public client `pub-1`;
2. ran `revokeAllUserSessions` — returned n=1, and `getSession` then returned null;
3. redeemed the same refresh token: **200**. Redeemed again: **200**. Account left with **2 live sessions**.

* **Control in the same case:** a client-mismatch redeem was refused **400**, so the harness can produce a refusal.
* **Not run:** an authorization code issued before a revocation and exchanged after it. The code grant also mints a fresh session (`:969`), so it is plausibly a smaller sibling — unmeasured, stated as such.

## Consequence

Anyone holding an OAuth grant obtained before a password change, a password reset, an admin status change or a user erasure keeps a renewable foothold. It is the direct counterexample to KS-1407's premise that no session may outlive the password that minted it.

## Scope — what this ticket is NOT

**KS-1150 R-2 already covers the rotation/denylist half of this branch** ("the refresh grant does not rotate / denylist the presented token", `:836`/`:860`) and is still OPEN — its 2026-09-14 comment records R-1 landing as `b42e260c9897` with "R-2 / R-3 stay OPEN". **This ticket is the other half: the missing ORIGIN-SESSION check.** They are overlapping-but-distinct, not duplicates — a perfectly rotating implementation would still mint a new session for an account whose sessions were all revoked, because nothing reads `decoded.sessionId`. Do not close either as a duplicate of the other.

**Board search before filing:** `revokeAllUserSessions`, `updateSessionActivity`, `rotateSessionRefreshToken`, `decoded.sessionId`, "oauth refresh token revoked session", "session revoked refresh token still redeems". Nearest neighbours KS-1150 (the rotation half, above), KS-756 (the opaque session refresh handle, a different mechanism), KS-1280 (a revoked session's Bearer forwarded by originate, a different service). **Controls both ways:** a freshly generated token that was never published returned **0** hits, and `revokeAllUserSessions` returned **1** — so the search discriminates.

Related KS-1407, KS-1150.

nodes.body:
## Gate BS1 confirms this ticket's scoping, with TWO CONDITIONS

Gate BS1 (Opus, tier 1) reviewed the scoping of this ticket against KS-1150 R-2 while gating PR #1655, and **confirmed it is correct** — the origin-session half here, the rotation/denylist half on KS-1150. Verdict `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-20_gate-BS1-pr1655-ks1407-r2/verdict.md` (`sed '1d;$d' | shasum -a 256` = `8480cd2c56ef`, equal to its own trailer).

**Its two conditions, verbatim from the verdict (lines 136-137):**

> - (a) It must fail closed on a refresh token with no or unknown `sessionId`, or a legacy token walks around it.
> - (b) It does not cover the authorization-code sibling, which BO1 flagged as not run: a code issued before the change and exchanged after it mints a fresh session at `:969` with no origin session to check. That needs either a credential epoch or code invalidation, and it should be named in KS-1690 or KS-1692 rather than left implicit.

## What that adds to the work here
1. **The check must FAIL CLOSED.** A refresh token carrying no `sessionId`, or one naming a session that cannot be found, must be **refused** — not admitted on the grounds that there is nothing to check. Otherwise every token minted before the fix walks straight around it, which would make the fix cosmetic for exactly the population it exists to stop.
2. **The authorization-code sibling is NOT covered by this ticket and is named here, as the gate asked.** A code issued *before* a password change and exchanged *after* it mints a fresh session at `oauth.ts:969` with no origin session to consult. The gate's shape for it is a **credential epoch** or **code invalidation**. It is recorded rather than left implicit; whoever takes this ticket should decide whether to widen it or split that off.

Context: KS-1407's fix merged as `86df4f5a52cc`, so the premise "no session may outlive the password that minted it" is now true for the interactive paths and still false for this one.

title: Security: POST /api/documents/:id/version has NO per-document access check on its source - any write-role caller in the tenant can derive a new version from another organisation's document (the sibling of the certify path KS-1557/#1619 closed)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/documents/:id/version` **checks a ROLE, a SCOPE and the TENANT, and nothing about the caller's relationship to the source document.** Any write-role caller in the tenant can derive a new version from **another organisation's** document, and the derived row is a real child of it. This is the sibling of the path KS-1557 / pull request #1619 closed on `POST /api/certifications/issue`: the same defect class, the same service, still open on the versioning route. Measured on a scratch stack at develop `89956fe92956`. Facts only — no fix is proposed here.

## Where

`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, the `'/:id/version'` handler:

* `:2219` — `const ALLOWED_VERSION_ROLES = DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES;`
* `:2246` — `isAllowedByRoleOrScope(req, ALLOWED_VERSION_ROLES, 'documents:write')` — role or scope only.
* `:2281` — `const source = await getDocument(id, tenantId, (req as any).db);` followed by a 404 when it does not resolve, and a `metadata.documentType` guard. **There is no owner / recipient / creating-connector test anywhere in the handler** — the check `callerMayCertifyDocument` applies on the certify path (`routes/certifications.ts:119-128`, call sites `:223` legacy and `:441` lineage) has no counterpart here.

## Measured (scratch Postgres 15 at migration 054, real `documents` + `certifications` routers, `secuura_app`, both `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=false` and `=true` — identical results in both)

| cell | what was done | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| G1 | **a FOREIGN organisation's connector** calls `/version` on organisation A's document | **201.** The minted row is a real child: its `parent_document_id` resolves to A's document. |
| G1 (same cell) | **the discriminating control** — that **same caller**, on that **same document**, through `POST /api/certifications/issue` with `parentDocumentId` | **403** `FORBIDDEN` |
| G2 | an **interactive write-role USER of another organisation** calls `/version` on A's document | **201** |
| G3 | **the bound** — a caller in **another tenant** calls `/version` on A's document | **404** `NOT_FOUND "Document not found in this tenant"` |

G1's two halves are the finding in one line: **the two sibling routes disagree about the same caller on the same document.** G3 bounds it — it does not cross the tenant, because `getDocument` is tenant-scoped.

## Board search before filing (symbol and path, each with a control)

* `callerMayCertifyDocument` → **2** hits (KS-1557, KS-1679); `isAllowedByRoleOrScope` → **2** (KS-1202, KS-1433). Both controls fire, so the instrument discriminates rather than returning everything.
* `ALLOWED_VERSION_ROLES`, `/:id/version`, `documents/:id/version`, `parent_document_id` → each returns the 12-hit fuzzy cap, and **none of the hits names this defect.** The nearest four, each a different thing: **KS-1538** (the legacy certify path — fixed), **KS-1557** (the lineage certify path — this route's sibling), **KS-1508** (`versionedById` is server-set — same route, different defect), **KS-1228** (a refused request still writes an `action_provenance` row — same route, different defect).
* **0 open hits for the source-access check itself.**

## Sequencing — this matters before anyone gates this route

The KS-1557 fix (shape (a′): `/version` records the creating connector on the document it mints, under the action value `create:connector`) **must land before any source-access gate is added here.** Otherwise a gate written with the same predicate would refuse `/version` on a version-minted document for exactly the reason certify refuses it today: a `/version`-created document has no creation provenance row of its own, so `wasCreatedByConnector` is false for the connector that actually made it. Measured on demo: **31 of 31** `/version`-minted documents have no such row.

## Open question, UNMEASURABLE from this project

**Does Platform S ever version a document it did not itself originate?** It decides the client-visible risk of closing this gap — if S does, closing it turns some S calls into 403. It cannot be answered from here: `Secuura/platform-s` returns 404 to this project's PAT (which sees exactly one repository), so no search of S's code is possible from Platform K's identity. **Stated as a question, not an assumption, and not asked of anyone here.**

## Not claimed

* No severity judgement beyond the priority on this ticket, and no fix design.
* The derived row carries the **caller's own** `newContentHash`, so this is not an alteration of the source document's bytes; the source gains a child it did not consent to, and the derived row presents as part of its lineage.
* Not measured: whether any such cross-organisation version exists in live data.

Found by Seat C 31st while measuring KS-1557 (Stuart's comment `16e8498d`) at develop `89956fe92956`, 2026-10-20.

nodes.body: @kamil.kreiser — your 00:13 note lists "whether Platform S ever versions a document it did not originate" as unmeasurable from your side: it is answered in my comment above (19 Oct 23:36 UTC). Short form: **no** — S versions only documents its own originate (or its own earlier `/version`) returned the id for, always under the owning organisation's connector key; the one edge is an S organisation merge (PS-492), which re-homes a document to the surviving organisation's key. So closing step 2 costs S nothing provided (a) the lineage-root / `create:connector` sequencing you describe holds, and (b) the merge edge is handled one of the two ways named there. Re-confirmed at S develop `61bdbd3`, 20 Oct.

## BLUF — measured interaction with the KS-1557 fix, and why this ticket's fix must come SECOND
The KS-1557 fix (a `create:connector` provenance row recorded for the connector that mints a document) **widens what the unauthorised versioner can do to the child it minted** — though it gives that caller **no new reach into the original document**. Measured by gate BN1 on a real Postgres, in both tenancy modes, on the develop arm and at the landing. Facts only; the policy question is not settled here.

## The chain, as measured
1. **User A** creates document **D** (`owner_user_id` = A's user).
2. **Org B's connector** calls `POST /api/documents/D/version` and gets **201 on both arms** — that is this ticket's defect, unchanged by KS-1557. The 201 body already echoes **A's title** on both arms.
3. The minted child **C** (whose `owner_user_id` is **A's user**, inherited from the source) now carries `create:connector` = **B's connector**.
4. **B certifies C:** lineage path **403 → 201**, legacy path **403 → 201**. The legacy path also moves the A-owned child C from `status: draft` to `certified` (on develop it stays `draft`).
5. **B reads C:** `GET /api/documents/C` **404 → 200**, and the body carries **A's data**.
6. **Reach into A's ORIGINAL D — unchanged:** B `GET D` is **404 on both arms**; B certify D is **403 on both arms**. D gains a child at step 2 on **both** arms, which is this ticket's pre-existing effect and not the KS-1557 fix's.

**So:** the fix gives B more over the row **B itself minted** (an A-owned row), and nothing more over **D**. Refusals on a version-minted document are unchanged on both arms for every other principal measured — a foreign connector, another organisation's user, a same-organisation non-owner, a same-organisation *other* connector and an unrelated recipient are all 403/403. A **human** of org B who versions gets no row and stays 403/403. Only the minter moves 403 → 201. (A recipient whose email is in the source's `recipientEmail`, which `/version` copies into the child, is 201/201 on both arms — pre-existing and unchanged.)

## Why this matters for the ORDER of the two fixes
The KS-1557 fix must land **first**, and a source-access gate on `/version` must come **after** it. If a gate were added here using the same predicate the certify path uses, it would refuse `/version` on a **version-minted** document for exactly the reason certify refused it before KS-1557: such a document had no creation provenance row of its own, so `wasCreatedByConnector` is false even for the connector that made it. Measured read-only on demo 2026-10-20: **31 of 31** version-minted documents had no such row before the backfill.

## What this does NOT establish
- **Whether step 2 should be refused at all** is the open question on this ticket, and it is not answered by the above.
- **Whether Platform S ever versions a document it did not originate** remains UNMEASURABLE from this project: `Secuura/platform-s` is 404 to this project's PAT. It decides the client-visible cost of closing step 2.
- Not measured on kintsugi.

Recorded here by Seat C 31st from gate BN1's note N1 on pull request #1654, 2026-10-20. The same point is carried as one line in that pull request's Known residue.

@kamil.kreiser — answering the open question from S's code at develop `355e6e6` (20 Oct), with the one edge that matters stated plainly.

**In the normal case, no: S only ever versions documents it originated itself, under the same organisation's key.** `CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs`:
- `/version` is called for exactly two verbs, `watermark` and `sign-cert` (`VersionThenAnchorAsync`), always on `parentKId = doc.PlatformKTipDocId ?? doc.PlatformKRootDocId` — ids S only ever holds because its **own** originate or its own earlier `/version` returned them (`AnchorResultApplier`, `PerVerb.cs:204-205`). S has no other way to learn a K document id, so it cannot address another connector's or user's document.
- Every such call, and the anchor kick that follows it (`POST /{newId}/anchor`), is signed with **the document's owning organisation's connector key** — `OwnerOrgId(doc)` = `DocumentStore.OrganisationId`, the organisation that originated the document on K — plus `onBehalfOf` for the acting person. A recipient in another organisation who signs a shared document (PS-1126's grant) still produces a `/version` under the **owner's** key, never the recipient's. A cross-organisation rights-assign on S changes the holder, not the owning organisation, so the key is unchanged after a custody transfer too.
- **But the chain matters for your predicate:** S's second `/version` (sign-cert) is addressed to the document the first `/version` (watermark) minted. So the "document's own side" must be judged by the lineage root's creating connector, or `/version` must write the `create:connector` provenance you name under shape (a′) — exactly the KS-1557 sequencing you state. Gate this route with the per-document provenance arm as it stands today and **every S sign-cert after a watermark is refused**, the same shape as the certify regression measured on 19 Oct.

**The one edge where S versions under a different key than the originating one: an S organisation merge.** `OrganisationMergeService` (PS-492, an Administrator's tool) re-homes a dissolving organisation's documents to the surviving organisation (`doc.OrganisationId = targetOrganisationId`), and the dissolving organisation's K key is then erased through KS-695. Any later watermark or sign on those documents is signed with the **surviving** organisation's key, against a K document whose issuer organisation and creating connector are the dissolved one's. Under a strict "own side only" rule those calls would answer 403 and fall to S's flat anchor. S has no call that tells K about the merge today. Two ways to keep it working: K accepts the surviving organisation when the originating connector's organisation has been erased, or S gains a "transfer issuer" call to make before it versions — say which you prefer and S will file its half; it is rare (single-person organisation consolidation) and nothing in S's suite exercises it against K.

Everything else S sends with `/{id}` — share, transfer-custody, revoke, lifecycle-events, certify — follows the same rule: S's own K ids only, the owner organisation's key only. Nothing deployed on S since dev-ps `b7d414b`.

title: m365: no connection is bound to its organisation - any authenticated user can list every site's connectionId, then list and download another org's OneDrive files
description:
**BLUF:** In m365-integration, **nothing ties a Microsoft 365 connection to the organisation that owns it.** Any authenticated user, from any tenant, can do three things:

* list every registered SharePoint site **together with its** `connectionId` (`GET /api/sites`);
* use that id to list the files in **another organisation's OneDrive**, with that organisation's own access token (`GET /api/onedrive/files`);
* **download** one of those files into the synced-document store (`POST /api/onedrive/files/:id/sync`).

`POST /api/connections/init` takes the organisation from the **request body**, not from the caller's token. **Measured statically. Not driven live.** It only works where `ENTRA_*` is configured and a real connection exists. That is unmeasured for any deployed environment, and KS-693 shows a normal dev machine answers 503.

Found from gate AP1's note N5 on #1627 (KS-1671). Read by Seat R 55th at develop `a66cd6a4d1726794c816fd4fefec58c728d410e5` (`services/m365-integration/src/index.ts`).

## The chain

| step | route | what it does | org check |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `GET /api/sites` (`:890-903`) | with no `connectionId` query, returns **every** entry of `memSites`; each `SharePointSite` carries `connectionId` (`:104-113`) | **none** |
| 2 | `GET /api/onedrive/files` (`:1082-1110`) | `memConnections.get(String(connectionId))` (`:1087`), then lists Graph `/me/drive/...` with `connection.accessToken` (`:1091-1093`) | **none** |
| 3 | `POST /api/onedrive/files/:id/sync` (`:1121`) | same lookup by id alone, then fetches the item's metadata **and** `/content` from Graph with that token | **none** |
| — | `GET /api/connections/:id` (`:722-743`) | returns `organizationId`, `tenantName`, `status` and `scopes` for any id | **none** |
| — | `POST /api/connections/init` (`:612-640`) | `organizationId` comes from `initConnectionSchema.parse(req.body)` (`z.string().uuid()`), not from the token | **none** |

`connectionId` is `conn_<randomUUID>` (`:616`), so it cannot be guessed. **Step 1 is what makes it enumerable**, as soon as any site has been registered on that connection.

## What I read to answer "does any middleware bind the connection to the caller's org?"

* **api-gateway** `routes/proxy.ts:949-957`: `/api/m365` and `/api/onedrive` are `authenticateToken(true)` followed by `proxy('m365', …)`. That checks identity only; nothing scopes by organisation.
* **m365**: `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate({ publicOps: ['POST /outlook/verify-hash'] }))` (`:606`) authenticates. I did not read its internals, because m365 never compares anything it sets to a connection's org. `requireM365` (`:259`) is a configuration gate (503 when unconfigured).
* **Census across all 22** `app.<verb>('/api…')` **routes in the file:** **0** read the caller's organisation from `req.user` or headers, and **0** compare `organizationId`. The census is a regex. I then read the five routes above by hand.

## Also from AP1 N5 (same route)

`GET /api/onedrive/files` interpolates a raw `folderId` into the Graph path (`:1090`: `/me/drive/items/${folderId}/children`), with no type check and no encoding. The handler's `try` → `next` means this cannot crash the process. Path text is passed to [graph.microsoft.com](<http://graph.microsoft.com>) under the connection's token.

## Priority: High, and why

It is a **cross-organisation read of customer files**: list, then download, using another organisation's Microsoft token. It is open to any authenticated user, and the enumeration needs only one registered site. Wednesday's rule for this class is High.

**What would lower it, and is not measured:** whether any deployed environment has `ENTRA_*` configured with live connections. Where it is not configured, every one of these routes answers 503 (KS-693). **Checking that means reading a live box, which I have not done.** The connection store is also in-memory and reloaded from the database (`loadFromDb`), so whatever a deployment holds is reachable once it is configured.

## Fix direction (not built)

* Bind each connection to the **caller's** organisation, taken from the verified token, never from the body.
* Every lookup by `connectionId` (or site id) must refuse a caller from a different organisation, with a 404 rather than a 403 so it does not leak that the id exists.
* `GET /api/sites` must filter to the caller's organisation.

This needs a tier-1 gate, with cross-org cells that use two organisations.

## Searched before filing

Searched "onedrive files folderId", "m365 connectionId org tenant isolation", "m365 connection ownership", "onedrive connection cross tenant" and "memConnections". The negative control `zkqvplmxhwrt` returned 0.

* **KS-1670** mentions `memConnections` only for the unencoded success redirect.
* **KS-748** and **KS-619** are about API-key and gateway tenant resolution, not m365 connections.
* The PS-1075..1084 storage tickets are Platform S design.

No ticket owns this.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Not run on kintsugi: needs two organisations' logins and Entra. Delivered: PRs 1633, 1637 and 1640 merged as 9207fe336797, f7d35d628cdc and 2b205beada00 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at ee1e1b832115 (kintsugi's REVISION head, read 2026-11-04 01:59Z). Left open.

- **Owed check:** the cross-organisation m365 connection check.
- **Why not run:** It needs two organisations' test logins and `ENTRA_*` configured for m365; neither is available.

**BLUF:** Delivered: PRs 1633, 1637 and 1640 merged as 9207fe336797, f7d35d628cdc and 2b205beada00 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (2026-11-01). Verified by code read, not observed live. Left open: the 2026-10-19 comment says this ticket is done only when deployed and checked live; the cross-organisation check is owed: live sweep owed (needs two organisations' test logins, and m365 needs `ENTRA_*` configured).

- **In the code at b1fb543640e7:** every org-owned m365 resource is bound to the caller's organisation, which comes from the signed token and never from the body or query (`m365-integration/src/index.ts:388-396`); `organizationId` is absent from the connection-init schema (`:361`); `GET /api/sites` refuses a token with no organisation instead of serving an empty 200 (`:947`).
- **Tracked in its own ticket:** the second route to the same harm, KS-1682.

**BLUF: a second route to this ticket's harm, filed separately as KS-1682 (High). Different root cause, not covered by the fix deployed here.**

This ticket binds each Microsoft 365 connection to its organisation. KS-1682 is about which refresh token a connection is handed in the first place. `exchangeAuthCode` takes the **first** refresh token in a process-wide MSAL cache, not the one for the account that just signed in. So once two organisations have connected within one process lifetime, the second organisation's connection stores the first organisation's refresh token. From its first token refresh it then reads the first organisation's Microsoft 365. No attacker is needed, and the organisation binding added here does not reach it.

Measured statically and on a real msal-node cache; not driven end to end. It is dormant today: 0 connections on kintsugi and demo. Details and the line table are on KS-1682.

**BLUF: all of KS-1673's code is now merged. Part A, part B and the test follow-ups are on `develop`. Nothing is deployed yet, so the ticket stays open: it is done only when deployed and checked live.**

The last piece merged as `2b205beada00a2f0fb3144e38198e471848132b6` on `develop` (#1640, squashed, one parent `c9ab6b36ff92`). The landed tree is `fc0a930ac613667f1f1e4cc73106777b86c1693f`, exactly the tree required before the merge. The review (gate BC1, the second round) found nothing further.

**What is now on `develop` for this ticket**
- **#1633** — Microsoft 365 connections, SharePoint sites, OneDrive and synced documents are bound to the caller's own organisation.
- **#1637** — Teams webhooks are bound the same way.
- **#1640** — the Teams tests now also run on a real database engine, so a widened filter can no longer pass unnoticed. The notify API description is corrected.

**Before deploy, two things to know.** Both are recorded on this ticket and on KS-1678.
- Existing connections and Teams webhooks created by the admin setup wizard will be **owned by nobody**, because the wizard saved a tenant id where the organisation id belongs. Re-connecting or re-registering is the remedy. There were **0** of either on kintsugi and demo when last measured.
- API keys with no organisation will be **refused** on the Teams routes. That is intended under the no-admin-bypass ruling.

**Related, still open:** KS-1677 (the Microsoft sign-in callback can take over a connection given its id) and KS-1678 (the admin setup wizard).

**BLUF: the last follow-up owed on this ticket is up for review, PR #1640. It is test-only, plus one corrected API description. Nothing is merged or deployed.**

https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1640 — head `c210733f6592`, on `develop` `a4187f0f6`.

**What it closes.** Part B's Teams tests used a stand-in for the database. The stand-in could not see a query whose filter had been **widened** — for example, "this organisation's rows, *or* rows with no organisation". The security review wrote two such breakages that passed all 16 tests but leaked on a real database. This PR runs the four Teams queries — list, notify, delete, register — on a **real in-memory Postgres**. The table definition is read from the repo's own schema file each time, and ownership is checked against the database itself.

**How it was checked.**
- The review's two breakages, plus a third of mine (delete widened the same way), are now each **caught by exactly one new test**. The old 16 tests still pass under all three, which is the gap this PR closes.
- The old tests are unchanged.
- The service's full suite passes: 147 of 147.

**The API description** for sending a Teams notification no longer says it posts "to all configured webhooks", nor that other services call it. It now says what the route does: it reaches the caller's own organisation's webhooks, and a login token with no organisation is refused.

**One thing to know.** The in-memory Postgres reaches this service through another package's development tooling; this service does not declare it. If that ever changes, these tests **fail loudly** — that was checked by removing the package. They never skip silently.

**BLUF: part B is merged. Microsoft Teams webhooks are now bound to the caller's own organisation, like the rest of Microsoft 365 in part A. One test-only follow-up is still owed on this ticket. Nothing is deployed, so the ticket stays open.**

Merged as `f7d35d628cdcf1df88a6b55665f3cd2e5e2b7696` on `develop` (#1637, squashed, one parent `c129c63cf777`). The landed tree is `c1e36ae51acc351723c7021611ea5e73e68ac951`, exactly the tree required before the merge. The service's full test suite was run at that exact point: 139 of 139.

**What the security review found** (gate AX1, five notes, no blockers). It attacked as a second organisation, on a real database engine as well as on mocks. Another organisation's webhook URL or host appeared in **no** response body, header or log line, and **nothing** was sent to another organisation's channels on any refused request.

**A caller class that is now refused — please know this before deploy.** Any **API key whose record has no organisation** now gets **403** from notify, register and list, and an answer that changes nothing from delete. That is the intended fail-closed behaviour under the no-admin-bypass ruling. The review reasoned it from the code, not from live keys. For scale, the security service's code records a demo count of **18 of 39 keys with no organisation**, dated 2026-09-03.

**Still owed on this ticket:** a test-only follow-up. The tests' database stand-in cannot see a `WHERE` clause that has been widened. The review wrote two such breakages that pass all 16 tests yet leak on a real database engine. The follow-up adds tests on a real engine that catch both. It also corrects one sentence in the API description, which names a caller of notify that does not exist.

**BLUF: part B is built and up for security review, PR #1637. Microsoft Teams webhooks are now bound to the caller's own organisation, the same rule as part A. Nothing is merged or deployed yet.**

https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1637 — head `1c26f26af047`, on `develop` `0f472ec20093`.

**What changes for a caller**
- **Listing** Teams webhooks returns only the caller's own organisation's. Each webhook carries its URL, and that URL is a secret: anyone holding it can post into that Teams channel. Before, the list returned **every** organisation's.
- **Registering** takes the organisation from the login token, not the request. The response now names the real owner.
- **Deleting** works only on the caller's own webhooks. Anything else gets the same answer as an id that does not exist.
- **Sending a notification** reaches only the caller's own channels. Before, one call posted a card — with the caller's own title, author and details — into every organisation's Teams channels at once.
- A login token that carries no organisation is refused, and nothing is written or sent.

**Before deploy:** every existing Teams webhook will be **owned by nobody**, because the admin setup wizard saved a tenant id where the organisation id belongs (KS-1678). The fix is to re-register them. **There are 0 Teams webhooks on kintsugi and 0 on demo.**

**Also in this PR:** the extra test the part A review asked for. A caller using its own connection with another organisation's site id never has that organisation's SharePoint site or library sent to Microsoft.

**How it was checked**
- 16 new tests. **12 fail on part A's code and pass here**; the other 4 check that the owner keeps access.
- Seven deliberate breakages of the fix were tried, and each is caught.
- The service's full test suite passes at the exact point it will land: 139 of 139.

**BLUF: PR A is merged. Microsoft 365 connections, SharePoint sites, OneDrive and synced documents are now bound to the caller's own organisation, on 14 routes. Teams is PR B, next. Nothing is deployed.**

Merged as `9207fe336797b136f3f12fb6da169fba7fd900b7` on `develop` (#1633, squashed, one parent `05ad5d3ac472`). The landed tree is `32e0b981e2b1adb25bffa08905b738e54b504a15`, exactly the tree required before the merge and re-derived independently on the moved `develop`.

**What the security review found.** It attacked as a second organisation with 20 id shapes, 6 body shapes and 13 token variants on every bound route. It found **no path to the first organisation's data**, and **zero** calls to Microsoft on every refused request. A "not yours" answer is identical to an "unknown id" answer in status, body and headers. No blockers.

**Existing rows — please read before this is deployed.** Existing `svc_m365_connections` rows written by the admin setup wizard carry a Secuura **tenant** id in `organization_id`. After deploy they will be **owned by nobody**: invisible to everyone, their real owner included. **Re-connecting is the remedy.** There were **0** such rows on kintsugi and demo on 2026-10-20. The wizard itself is filed as **KS-1678**.

**Recorded, not fixed here:**
- the unauthenticated sign-in callback — **KS-1677**, now measured by the review;
- an owner whose connection is in the database but not in this process's memory sees its sites and documents as not found — recorded on **KS-1675**;
- a review test for the documents/sync site lookup is added in PR B.

**BLUF: the first half of the fix is built and is at security review, PR #1633. Connections, SharePoint sites, OneDrive and synced documents are now bound to the caller's own organisation. Teams is the second half, PR B, still to come. Nothing is merged or deployed.**

PR: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1633 — head `76725fd4a5b7`, on `develop` `88b8ceb9f304`.

**What changes for a caller**
- The organisation comes from the caller's **signed login token**, never from the request body. `POST /api/connections/init` no longer reads `organizationId` from the body. A caller that still sends it gets a connection owned by **its own** organisation — not an error, and never the one it asked for.
- Asking for another organisation's connection, site or document gets **exactly the same "not found" answer** as asking for an id that does not exist. The two responses were compared byte for byte, and the "not yours" one contains neither the owner's organisation id nor its tenant name.
- Listing sites or documents with a token that carries **no organisation** is refused (403). It is no longer served an empty list that would read like "you own nothing".
- A connection with no organisation recorded is visible to **nobody**. So is a site whose connection is gone, including to the organisation that created it.
- **No exceptions for any role**, as ruled.

**The defect that mattered most, now pinned by tests:** a caller from organisation B asking to list or sync A's OneDrive gets "not found" and the service makes **no call to Microsoft at all**. That is measured two separate ways, because the service reaches Microsoft two separate ways. Before this change, the same request listed A's files using A's own Microsoft token.

**How it was checked**
- 33 tests. **22 of them fail on today's code and pass with the fix.** The other 11 check that each organisation's own access still works.
- Seven deliberate breakages of the fix were tried. Each one is caught. Removing the ownership comparison alone breaks every cross-organisation test.
- The full test suite of this service passes: 114 of 114.

**Two corrections to this ticket's description**
- **The service has 24 routes under `/api`, not 22.** I counted with a stated pattern and checked the count against today's code. Fourteen are now bound. Four are Teams, for PR B. Two are deliberately left alone: the health check, which reports totals only, and the Microsoft sign-in redirect, which cannot carry our login token.
- **The published API description said `organizationId` was required** on `connections/init`. It is corrected in the same PR.

**Not run, and why:** the four full-platform test suites, and three of the sixteen pre-push checks. All of them need the whole stack running, and this machine has no Docker. The PR lists exactly which ones.

**BLUF: the fix plan for this ticket is approved (Wednesday, 2026-10-20). It will ship as two pull requests on this one ticket, each with a full security review. No code has been written yet.**

**What was decided**
* **No exceptions for any role.** No admin, platform admin or super user can see another organisation's Microsoft 365 connections, sites, documents or Teams webhooks. If an operator ever needs that, it gets its own ticket and design.
* **Teams is in scope here.** It has the same root cause and the same fix.
* **Two PRs:**
  * **PR A:** connections, SharePoint sites, OneDrive and synced documents.
  * **PR B:** Teams webhooks. It follows PR A and reuses PR A's rule for where the organisation comes from.

**How the fix works**
* The caller's organisation comes from their signed login token, never from the request body.
* A connection is usable only by a caller from the same organisation.
* A "not yours" request gets exactly the same 404 as an unknown id, so nobody learns that the id exists.
* A caller with no organisation, or a connection with none recorded, sees nothing.

**Tests the fix must carry**
* Two organisations side by side. A cross-organisation request answers 404 and makes **no call to Microsoft Graph**, while the owner's request still works.
* For Teams, a test that another organisation's webhook URL never appears in the response at all, checked on the URL text, not just the row count.

**Separate issue found while measuring:** the m365 connections table may never save or reload a connection. That is KS-1675, not this ticket.

**BLUF: no customer data is exposed on either environment today. But on kintsugi every route in this chain is live, so the first organisation to connect Microsoft 365 there would be exposed at once. The defect is also wider than this ticket said: Microsoft Teams webhooks have the same missing org binding.**

**Measured 2026-10-19 13:47Z, read-only.** I checked only names and counts, sent no request to any m365 route, and wrote nothing on either box.

| | kintsugi | demo |
| -- | -- | -- |
| m365 running | yes | yes |
| Microsoft 365 configured (the three `ENTRA_*` settings) | **yes, so these routes are live** | **no, so they answer 503** |
| connections stored | **0** | **0** |
| Teams webhooks stored | **0** | **0** |

The counts used a database role that bypasses row-level security, with a non-zero control table. A zero therefore means empty, not hidden.

**The same defect in Teams:**
* `GET /api/teams/webhook-config` returns **every** organisation's active webhooks, **including the webhook URL**. That URL is a secret: whoever holds it can post into that Teams channel.
* `POST /api/teams/webhook-config` takes the organisation from the request body. `DELETE` and `POST /api/teams/notify` have no organisation filter.
* `svc_teams_webhooks` has no row-level security either.

**Scope correction to the description above:** none of m365's 22 routes checks the caller's organisation. A fix plan covering all of them, Teams included, is with Wednesday for a ruling. No code yet.

title: A fresh clone has no pre-push gate: core.hooksPath is unset, so the 16-leg preflight silently does not run
description:
**BLUF: a working copy cloned from GitHub has NO pre-push gate.** `core.hooksPath` **is unset in a fresh clone,** `.git/hooks/pre-push` **does not exist there, so the 16-leg preflight does not run — silently. The push just succeeds. A worktree off the shared checkout inherits the gate; a clone does not.**

## Measured 2026-10-19, read-only `git config --get core.hooksPath`

| working copy | `core.hooksPath` | gate runs? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| the shared checkout `2_Project_Files` | `.githooks` | yes |
| a worktree off it (`worktrees/s-r46-ks1462`) | `.githooks` (inherited) | yes |
| a fresh `git clone` from GitHub | **UNSET** | **NO** |
| `deploy-clones/seatC25-7e2f8157cec2` (a live seat's clone at the time) | **UNSET** | **NO** |

`.githooks/pre-push` is present and executable in the clone — it is simply never invoked, because nothing points git at it.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a note

**The failure is silent and it looks like success.** A push from an unwired clone prints no warning and no leg output; it prints the ordinary "new branch" line. There is nothing in the output that says the gate was skipped, so the only way to notice is to know the leg headers should be there and see that they are not.

**It happened, on this ticket's own session.** Seat E 3rd's first push of the KS-1195 branch ran with no gate. It was rejected by the remote for an unrelated reason — the branch name collided with a stale 17-September branch — so nothing landed and no ungated commit exists. Had the name been free, an ungated push would have succeeded and been reported as pushed. That is luck, not a control.

**It is already documented**, at `Blockchain/Dev/CONTRIBUTING.md:389`:
`git config core.hooksPath .githooks && chmod +x .githooks/pre-push`
So this is a missable step, not an undocumented hole. The problem is that missing it is undetectable from the push's own output.

## Fix shapes (not chosen here)

1. **Make the absence loud rather than the wiring mandatory.** A tracked `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/*` check, or a preflight leg, that refuses when `core.hooksPath` does not resolve to `.githooks` — this cannot help the very push it would gate, so it only helps on the *second* push onward.
2. **A** `postinstall` **/ bootstrap step** that sets `core.hooksPath` when it is unset. `npm ci` is `ignore-scripts` in this repo, so a postinstall would not fire; it would have to hang off an existing bootstrap script the seats already run.
3. **Have the launcher wire it for every working copy it knows about**, including `deploy-clones/*`, rather than relying on the clone inheriting anything.
4. **A server-side ruleset** that refuses a push without the evidence the hook produces. The strongest, and the most work; also note "Require status checks" must never be enabled while Actions are retired, so this would need to be something other than a check.

Shape 1 or 3 looks like the cheapest honest improvement; the decision is not mine.

## Reproduce

```
git clone --single-branch --branch develop git@github.com:Secuura/Distributed_Secuura.git /tmp/probe
git -C /tmp/probe config --get core.hooksPath   # prints nothing, exit 1
ls /tmp/probe/.git/hooks/pre-push               # No such file or directory
```

Discovered 2026-10-19 by Seat E 3rd during the KS-1195 build (PR #1613), after the push log showed zero leg output.

title: Chain-first verify blobs hard-code `anchored: true` and drop anchoring's status/acknowledged, so a 'submitting' or failed anchor reads isAnchored: true (v1 + v2)
description:
## BLUF

**The chain-first verify branches build their blockchain blob with** `anchored: true` **hard-coded and no** `status`**, which makes the honest-anchor guard** `settled` **BY CONSTRUCTION.** An anchoring reply that is still in flight or has failed — `status: 'submitting'`, `acknowledged: false`, the KS-726 class — is therefore presented as `isAnchored: true`, in both the v1 and the v2 verify routes.

The code says so itself. `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:130-132`:

> *"KS-1628: a failed anchor is not an anchor, whatever else the blob says. The chain-first blobs carry* `anchored: true` *and no status, so they are unaffected; a stored blob that pairs* `anchored: true` *with a failed status was on-chain before this line."*

That comment reads as a reassurance. It is in fact the statement of the defect: *unaffected by the failed-status guard* is exactly the problem, because the guard is the thing that would have caught this.

Gate O1's Minor 2 on the twelve-PR batch, 2026-10-19T01:00:25Z. Pre-existing; not in those merges.

## The mechanism, measured

`isAnchoredHonestly` (`verification.ts:120`) decides the claim:

```ts
if (FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES.has(String(c.status))) return false;   // :133
const settled = c.anchored === true || c.status === 'confirmed';  // :141
```

* A **real stored** anchor row has no `anchored` boolean at all — the comment at `:136-139` says so: *"anchoring's vocabulary is pending | submitted | confirmed | failed … and there is NO* `anchored` *boolean on a real row."* For those rows only `status === 'confirmed'` earns the claim, and `'submitted'` deliberately does not, because *"the tx is in flight and may still fail — the KS-535 class."*
* A **chain-first** blob is built by hand with `anchored: true` and **no** `status` **key**. So `FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES.has(String(undefined))` is false — the failed guard cannot fire — and `settled` is true on the first disjunct, whatever anchoring actually reported.

**The four construction sites:**

| route | site |
| -- | -- |
| v1 | `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:717` |
| v1 | `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:1237` |
| v1 | `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:1259` |
| **v2** | `services/originate/src/routes/verificationV2.ts:233`, inside `chainOnlyMatch` |

The `status` argument the call sites pass does not rescue it: `verification.ts:758`, `:1297` and `verificationV2.ts:271` pass the **literal** `'anchored'`, and in any case the second argument is only consulted when there is no chain blob at all (`:149`).

**What bounds the severity.** `settled` is necessary but not sufficient: the claim also needs `typeof c.txHash === 'string'`, `REAL_TXHASH_RE` (64 hex) and `heightOk`. So the hash must already look like a real one, and it comes from the chain index. The defect is that **in-flight and failed anchors the index knows about still read as anchored** — not that an arbitrary blob does.

## Why High

On a document-authenticity platform, `isAnchored: true` is the product's central claim to a verifier. Presenting a `'submitting'` or failed anchor as anchored is the same family as KS-535 (a failed on-chain anchor reporting `status: anchored`) and KS-1634 (a simulated anchor returned unlabelled), and KS-1634 is High. The failure direction is always *over*-claiming, never under-claiming.

**Honest limit on this rating: I did not run a census.** I have not measured how many rows can reach these branches with a non-confirmed status today. The nearest evidence is KS-1634's census — 0 qualifying rows on both boxes at 2026-10-18, with kintsugi's 0 noted as contingent on one document row — and that census was for a different precondition. **A census is the first step on this ticket, and the rating should be revisited against it.**

## Recommendation

1. Carry anchoring's own fields into the chain-first blob instead of asserting the conclusion: pass `status` and `acknowledged` through, and let `isAnchoredHonestly` apply the same rules it applies to a stored row. Dropping `anchored: true` entirely is the cleaner shape, since no real row carries it — but `ks563` pins the current chain-first shape, so that is a deliberate change with a test to re-cut, not a one-liner.
2. A cell per site: a chain-first match whose anchoring status is `'submitting'` (and one that is `'failed'`) must read `isAnchored: false`. A mutant restoring the hard-coded `anchored: true` must red each of them.
3. Fold the **v2** site in with KS-1634's v2 work — it is the same four lines of construction, and splitting them across two tickets invites one to be done and the other forgotten.

## Dedupe

Over all **1,627** Secuura-PK issues including archived: `chainOnlyMatch` **→ 0 hits.** `anchored: true` → 4, each a different subject (KS-1634 the simulated-label defect, KS-1628 the route retirement, KS-834 a decision on verify auth, KS-535 the document-status variant, Done). `acknowledged` → 6, none about this presenter. `isAnchored` → 9; the nearest, KS-1637, is gate N1's residue about the removal pin reading only the router — a different mechanism, read and confirmed distinct. Positive controls on the same corpus: `verification` 360, `anchor` 313. Zero control: a nonsense token reads 0.

**Related:** KS-1634 (the same presenter, the `simulated` signal, and the v2 site it shares), KS-726 (the `status: 'submitting'` / `acknowledged: false` reply class this mis-presents; Done), KS-535 (the document-status variant; Done), KS-563 (which pins the current chain-first shape, so its cells are in scope for any change here).

---

*Filed by Seat R 51st on Wednesday's instruction of 2026-10-19T01:00:25Z, citing gate O1's verdict section "Minor 2". The Linear actor field is shared across the fleet, so authorship is this line, not the actor. Everything above the "Why High" section I verified in the source at develop* `37834600a543cb0276f427d969ac034d9df74fbd`*; the severity and the census limit are my own call, stated as such. Not fixed in these merges.*

title: GET /api/keys has no organisation arm: an ORG_ADMIN or ISSUER_ADMIN lists another organisation's keys in the same tenant
description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/keys` **has no organisation arm.** An `ORG_ADMIN` or `ISSUER_ADMIN` of organisation A lists organisation B's API keys when B is in the same tenant, using B's exact id. The mint and the revoke are both organisation-bounded for these roles; the list is the only one of the three routes that is not. **Measured** at develop `7c6b3d88`, details below. Facts only, no fix. Filed on Wednesday's ruling while building KS-1553 PR 1, which does **not** add the bound.

**What is exposed:** each key's **id, name, prefix, scopes and connector id**, plus `lastUsedAt`, `usageCount`, `isActive` and `createdAt`. **Not key material:** the list never returns the key or its hash.

**Not reached by Kam's ADMIN ruling.** That ruling (KS-1570) concerns the tenant-level `ADMIN` role on the mint. The roles here are `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN`, which are organisation-bounded on the mint (KS-1533) and on the revoke (KS-764).

## The code

At develop `7c6b3d88`, `services/security/src/index.ts:1318-1366`:

* The handler filters `k.organizationId === organizationId`, where `organizationId` is the raw query value, and then `callerIsPlatform || k.tenantId === caller.tenantId`. That second filter is KS-742's tenant bound.
* Nothing in the handler reads `caller.organizationId` or calls `isOrgBoundedRole`.
* The mint, by contrast, calls `decideTenantAccess(user, tenantId, { targetOrganizationId })` (`index.ts:1173`). That engages the organisation arm for `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES = {ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN}` (`packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts`).
* The revoke is bounded by `decideKeyRevoke` (KS-764).

## Measured

A throwaway in-process probe, using the same harness as `ks1533-key-mint-organisation-arm.test.ts` (memory-backed; the list reads only `memApiKeys`). Organisation ids contain hex letters, so the upper-case form is not identical to the original.

| caller | lists | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| platform (`super_admin`) | mints for A1 and A2 | 201, 201 |
| `ISSUER_ADMIN` of A1 | A1 | 200, 1 key |
| `ISSUER_ADMIN` **of A1** | **A2, exact id** | **200, 1 key (the gap)** |
| `ISSUER_ADMIN` of A1 | A2, upper-case | 200, 0 keys (only because the compare is raw; see below) |
| CONTROL: `ISSUER_ADMIN` of a tenant-B org | A2 | 200, 0 keys (the tenant filter is real) |
| CONTROL: platform | A2 | 200, 1 key |

**After KS-1553 PR 1** the list normalises the query, so the upper-case form of A2 also lists A2's key. That reveals nothing the exact id does not already reveal. PR 1 pins both as cells labelled MEASURED GAP that name this ticket, so adding a bound later is a visible edit.

## Dedupe

I scanned all 1,560 issues, archived ones included, with their comments, for list / another-organisation / organisation-arm wording. The positive control (KS-1533 matching "organisation arm") fired, and a bogus-symbol control returned 0. Nothing covers the list. KS-742 bounded the list by **tenant** only.

## Not decided here

The shape of the bound: refuse, or filter as KS-742 and `GET /api/audit` do. Also how it treats the org-less bounded accounts KS-779 recorded as intentional.

nodes.body:
**Facts only, for whoever builds this list bound. Filed on Wednesday's GO for pull request 1533 (KS-1553 (a)), as the gate's Minor m3 (verdict sha256/16 `4fc478e33f32e0b3`). Build the bound on `normaliseOrgId` equality, because the list now compares that way.**

Pull request 1533 makes `GET /api/keys` compare `normaliseOrgId(stored) === normaliseOrgId(query)` (trim, lower-case, blank = absent; `packages/shared/src/security/orgId.ts:42`). That is the same equivalence the mint (`index.ts:1242`) and the revoke arm (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:174-175`) already use.

**What the gate measured as a consequence, all within one tenant:**
- Case- or whitespace-distinct legacy ids now fold together. `COLL-ORG` and `coll-org` stored as two keys both list under either form, where develop listed each only under its exact form.
- An NBSP-padded stored id folds into the canonical one.
- A query containing U+212A KELVIN SIGN lists an ASCII `kelvin-org` key, because JavaScript lower-cases U+212A to `k`. U+0130 does NOT collide.
- **No cross-tenant read was added.** A tenant-B `ISSUER_ADMIN` sees only tenant-B keys under every one of 31 query forms.

**Why it matters for this ticket:** with no organisation bound (this ticket), an org-bounded admin can already list any organisation in its tenant by exact id, so the folding reveals nothing new today. Once a bound exists, it must compare the caller's organisation claim and the key's stored id in the **same** normalised form, or a case variant would slip past it or wrongly refuse. The cells pull request 1533 added already show it. The gate's mutant **X6** (a bound added for org-bounded callers) turns both MEASURED GAP cells red, so building the bound will be a visible edit to those cells.

Whether two genuinely different legacy organisations differ only by case is unknown. No live data was read; KS-1565 holds the read-only count of non-canonical rows.

title: POLICY (Kam's call): role ADMIN is a KEY_ADMIN_ROLE that the KS-764 organisation arm never engages for, so a tenant ADMIN can mint a key for any organisation in its tenant
description:
## BLUF

`ADMIN` **is in** `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` **but in neither** `PLATFORM_ROLES` **nor** `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES`**, so the KS-764 organisation arm is skipped for it entirely and** `decideTenantAccess` **falls through to** `allow: 'same-tenant'`**.** After KS-1533 arm 1 closes the hole for `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN`, a caller with role `ADMIN` can **still** mint a key carrying any organisation's `organizationId` inside its own tenant — the same Path 1 shape, through one role.

**This is a policy question about who may reach an irreversible cross-organisation erasure, so it is Kam's to decide, not an engineering choice inside a PR.** Wednesday put it on his board as a card (`secuura-ks1533-admin-role-unbounded-by-org-arm-1013`) and recommended leaving `ADMIN` unbounded. **Until he rules, KS-1533 arm 1 ships leaving** `ADMIN` **unbounded and says so plainly**, and the shared role set is NOT touched.

## The three sets, read at source

```
KEY_ADMIN_ROLES    services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:43-49
                   SYSTEM_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN, ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN, ADMIN
PLATFORM_ROLES     packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:59
                   SYSTEM_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN
ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES  packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:76
                   ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN
```

The arm is `if (organisationScope && isOrgBoundedRole(user.role))` (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:173`). `ADMIN` satisfies neither predicate, so the arm is skipped and the function returns `allow: 'same-tenant'` at `:225`.

| role | what arm 1 does for it |
| -- | -- |
| `SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN` | platform — bypass the arm by design (KS-577 depends on it) |
| `ORG_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_ADMIN` | org-bounded — **the arm applies**, which is KS-1533 arm 1 |
| `ADMIN` | **neither — the arm never engages** |

## The two readings

**(a) By design, and this ticket closes as "documented".** `ADMIN` reads as a **tenant**-level admin, distinct from platform — KS-1283 is about "a widened `SUPER_ROLES` would admit a tenant `ADMIN` role on six routes", which treats it as a tenant role. On that reading, acting across organisations *inside its own tenant* is what a tenant admin is for, and arm 1 is complete as scoped.

**(b) A gap.** The sink is the KS-695 connector erasure, which is **irreversible** and destroys another organisation's titles, descriptions and name. KS-764's stated hazard is "an org-bounded admin in organisation A destroying organisation B's key" — if a tenant `ADMIN` may do the equivalent to B's *documents*, the boundary is only as strong as the weakest admin role.

**This ticket does not pick.** It records the question, the evidence, and what shipped in the meantime.

## If Kam rules (b)

`ADMIN` joins `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` in `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts`. That is a **one-line change to a shared set that also governs the revoke route**, so it is not a local edit: it would change `DELETE /api/security/keys/:id` for every `ADMIN` caller too, and it needs its own gate and its own caller-population check (the same `caller has no organisation` 403 that KS-1533 arm 1 accepts for org-bounded roles would then apply to `ADMIN` as well). It should not be folded into KS-1533.

## Where it is pinned meanwhile

KS-1533 arm 1 carries a **documenting cell** that asserts today's behaviour — a tenant `ADMIN` minting for another organisation in its tenant succeeds — labelled as undecided policy rather than as a guarantee, so that whichever way Kam rules, the change is visible as a deliberate edit to a cell rather than a silent flip.

## Dedupe

Literal, case-insensitive over title and description, archived included: `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` **1** (KS-779 — the CALLER-side population of org-bounded accounts with no organisation claim, which is KS-1533 arm 1's accepted 403 price, not this question), `isOrgBoundedRole` **0**, `tenant ADMIN` 4 and `ADMIN role` 6 (the KS-1283 / KS-1506 / KS-486 family — a widened `SUPER_ROLES`, error-handler and review tickets, none of them this question). KS-764 (Done) created the arm and deliberately scoped it to the revoke route.

*Corrected after filing: the first version of this paragraph said* `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` *0. The scan returned KS-779. The conclusion is unchanged — no ticket asks whether* `ADMIN` *should be org-bounded — but the figure was wrong and a wrong dedupe count is worth correcting rather than leaving.*

Raised by Seat V 5th while building KS-1533 arm 1, 2026-10-12. Found by reading the role sets before writing the fix, not by a test.

---

## ADDENDUM — it is TWO roles, not one, and the verdicts are MEASURED by running the predicates

I ran the real `isPlatformRole`, `isOrgBoundedRole` and `decideTenantAccess` over the whole role vocabulary rather than reading the sets. Caller is `{role, tenantId:'t1', organizationId:'oA'}`, target is the same tenant and a DIFFERENT organisation `oB` — i.e. exactly the KS-1533 Path 1 shape:

| role (as the JWT carries it) | isPlatformRole | isOrgBoundedRole | verdict naming ANOTHER org in the same tenant |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `SYSTEM_ADMIN` | true | false | ALLOW `platform-admin` — by design |
| `SUPER_ADMIN` | true | false | ALLOW `platform-admin` — by design |
| `super_admin` | true | false | ALLOW `platform-admin` — by design |
| `platform_admin` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` **— UNBOUNDED** |
| `PLATFORM_ADMIN` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` **— UNBOUNDED** |
| `ADMIN` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` **— UNBOUNDED** |
| `admin` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` **— UNBOUNDED** |
| `ORG_ADMIN` | false | true | DENY `cross-organisation` — arm 1 working |
| `ISSUER_ADMIN` | false | true | DENY `cross-organisation` — arm 1 working |
| `issuer_admin` | false | true | DENY `cross-organisation` — arm 1 working |
| `connector` | false | false | ALLOW `same-tenant` — correct: `decideMint` pins a provisioner to its own tenant on its own branch |

Both predicates upper-case the claim (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:84` and `:123`), so casing is NOT the issue — the role simply is not in either set.

### `platform_admin` is the more interesting half

`platform_admin` is treated as a **super-role by the gateway** in at least six places, while the key policy does not treat it as platform at all:

```
services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:65      SUPER_ROLES          includes platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:515     SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES    includes platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts:577        PLATFORM_SCOPE_ROLES includes platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1094,1227                       include platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts:105 adminRoles           includes platform_admin
packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:59  PLATFORM_ROLES       does NOT
services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:193               PLATFORM_ADMIN_ROLES does NOT (it has `admin` instead)
```

So a `platform_admin` is "platform" to the gateway and an ordinary tenant user to the key policy. For arm 1 that means **unbounded**; more generally it is a role-vocabulary split across seven divergent lists, which is its own problem and not this ticket's to fix.

### What this changes for Kam's decision

The card is about who may reach an irreversible cross-organisation erasure. The answer is not "ADMIN" but "`ADMIN` **and** `platform_admin`**, in either casing**". If Kam rules them bounded, the edit is to `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` (or to `PLATFORM_ROLES`, for `platform_admin`) — still a shared set that governs the revoke route too, so still not a local change and still its own gate.

KS-1533 arm 1's documenting cell therefore pins **both** roles' current behaviour, labelled as undecided policy.

*Added by Seat V 5th, 2026-10-12, after running the predicates while building KS-1533 arm 1.*

---

## ⚠ CORRECTION — `platform_admin` is NOT unbounded at the mint. It cannot mint at all. Only `ADMIN` is the open question.

**The addendum above is wrong about** `platform_admin`**, and the retitle that named it was wrong.** Measured on the running security service over real HTTP while writing KS-1533 PR A's cells, and confirmed by running the function:

```
role              decideMint (runs FIRST, as route middleware)
ADMIN / admin     ALLOW via admin   -> reaches decideTenantAccess -> unbounded   (the claim HOLDS)
platform_admin    DENY 403 "API key management requires an admin role"          (the claim was WRONG)
PLATFORM_ADMIN    DENY 403 — same
ISSUER_ADMIN      ALLOW via admin   -> the organisation arm applies
super_admin       ALLOW via admin   -> platform, bypasses by design
```

**What I got wrong, precisely.** I ran `decideTenantAccess` on its own and concluded `platform_admin` falls through to `allow: 'same-tenant'`. That is true *of that function*. But the mint route runs `requireKeyAdminOrProvisioner` → `decideMint` **first**, and `PLATFORM_ADMIN` is not in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` (`provisioningPolicy.ts:43-49`), so the request is refused 403 before `decideTenantAccess` is ever called. **Order is invisible to a function call** — the exact point KS-742's route-contract test makes in its header, and that I copied into KS-1533's. The real-HTTP cell is what caught it: I had written it to assert `platform_admin` mints (201), and it read 403 on the unfixed service.

**So, for Kam's decision:** the question is `ADMIN` **only**. `ADMIN` is in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`, passes `decideMint`, reaches `decideTenantAccess`, and — being in neither `PLATFORM_ROLES` nor `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` — keeps cross-organisation mint inside its tenant. That half stands and is unchanged.

**What still stands about** `platform_admin`**:** the role-vocabulary split (KS-1536) is real — the gateway treats it as a super-role in six places. But its consequence *at the mint* is the opposite of what I wrote: a gateway super-role is **over**-restricted here (cannot mint keys), not under-restricted. That is an availability quirk, not a security hole, and it belongs on KS-1536, not on Kam's policy card.

The title is reverted to name `ADMIN` alone. KS-1533 PR A pins both facts in cells: `ADMIN` as UNDECIDED POLICY (201 today), `platform_admin` as MEASURED (403, refused by `decideMint`).

*Corrected by Seat V 5th, 2026-10-12. The third time this session I have had to correct a claim of mine in place; this one was on Kam's board, so it matters more than the dedupe counts did.*

nodes.body:
## RULED — Kam: leave `ADMIN` unbounded for now, and change it before deployment

This ticket's question — is the tenant `ADMIN` role's cross-organisation reach by design or a gap? — **was ruled on the live board.** Times as the board stamped them (13 Oct 2026, board time, `view=wednesday`), relayed by Wednesday:

* **09:53:40** — *"Decision secuura-ks1533-admin-role-unbounded-by-org-arm-1013: a — Leave ADMIN unbounded for now | note: keep a note that this needs to be changed before deployment"*

**What it means:**

* **For now,** reading (a) stands: `ADMIN` keeps cross-organisation reach inside its tenant. The PR #1521 cell `UNDECIDED POLICY (KS-1535)` (`ks1533-key-mint-organisation-arm.test.ts:195`) keeps pinning today's behaviour — it passes on develop `7c6b3d88`, run by me today.
* **Kam's note makes it a deploy blocker.** The work it requires is **KS-1570**, filed High, which lists the candidate shapes for Kam to choose between.
* **The blocker was widened.** Kam's erasure merge-timing ruling at **09:56:23** (option b, *"Merge now and accept that every later develop deploy carries the live erasure"*) means that once PR #1497 is on develop, the `ADMIN` bound blocks **every** later deploy. Kam was told this on the panel and offered to keep the merge back.

*Facts only. This ticket's title, priority and description are unchanged. Posted by the Platform K agent on Kam's behalf.*

title: Security: an organisation-scoped admin can mint a key for ANOTHER organisation, or carrying another organisation's connector id — the mint has no organisation arm and connector_id is not bound
description:
## BLUF

**In** `services/security`**, the API-key mint is bounded by TENANT only. An** `ORG_ADMIN` **or** `ISSUER_ADMIN` **of organisation A can mint a key that carries organisation B's** `organizationId`**, and any** `connectorId`**, inside the same tenant.** KS-764 put an organisation arm on **revoke**; the **mint** never got one. Because the connector-erasure path in KS-695 trusts the key row it is called with, that minted key erases B.

**This must land before KS-695 deploys** — same status as KS-1508. Merging KS-695 does not deploy it, so the harm is after deploy, and the data destroyed (titles, descriptions, an organisation name) is another organisation's and the erasure is irreversible.

Found by the round 4 Opus gate on PR #1497 (verdict sha256/16 `df3bc694b6b41094`, section M-1). **The security-service half below is the gate's reading of the code, which I re-read at source myself; the originate half is the gate's measurement on real Postgres. Neither the mint nor the gateway half has been measured at runtime — that is the first task here.**

## The two paths

**Path 1 — a key for another organisation.**

* `services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:43-49` — `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN` are in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`.
* `provisioningPolicy.ts:95-98` — `decideMint` returns `{allow: true, via: 'admin'}` **at once** for any of those roles, before any tenancy or organisation question.
* `services/security/src/index.ts:477-491` — the body's `organizationId` and `connectorId` are free strings.
* `services/security/src/index.ts:1017` — the route calls `decideTenantAccess((req as any).user, tenantId)` **without** the third `organisationScope` argument.
* `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:161-164` says that arm is engaged *"ONLY when the caller supplies* `organisationScope`*, so the two existing callers (KS-742's list and mint) keep exactly today's behaviour"*. That was deliberate in KS-764 and is exactly the gap.
* `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1189-1192` — `/api/security` is mounted behind `authenticateToken(true)` only, so the gateway adds no organisation check.

**Measured by the gate on the originate side (cell P8, real Postgres, both modes):** a key row for org B carrying a forged `connector_id` — which is what the mint above writes — gives `200 completed documentsBlanked:1`, B's name and document `[erased]`, and B's own provisioned key still active.

**Path 2 — a key for A's own organisation carrying B's connector id.**

* `svc_api_keys.connector_id` has **no uniqueness constraint** (the gate read the live indexes: pkey, org, prefix, tenant only).
* The erasure matches `versionedById = 'connector:' + connectorId` **by value**.
* **Measured by the gate (cell P6, both modes):** two organisations whose keys share one `connector_id`; A erases and gets `200 documentsBlanked:4`, taking B's unissued connector root and B's connector derivatives.
* Not hypothetical: `register-connector` writes `connectorId: platform-s:${externalRef}` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:702`), so the id is a predictable function of a value an org admin can read, and the tenant metering key already uses a constant `platform-s` id (`tenant-provisioning/src/meteringKey.ts:56`).

**Path 2 is not closed by the organisation arm alone.** Both arms are needed.

## What this ticket asks for

1. **The organisation arm of the mint.** An organisation-scoped admin may mint only for its own organisation. The shape already exists — pass `organisationScope` at `index.ts:1017` as the revoke path does at `keyRevokePolicy.ts:243` — and `decideMint`'s early return for `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` must stop short-circuiting past it. Platform roles keep their current reach.
2. **The connector-id binding.** A connector id belongs to exactly one organisation; a mint naming one already bound to another organisation in the same tenant is refused. The org-less tenant metering key must keep working.
3. **It lands before KS-695 deploys.** Tracked like KS-1508.

## Acceptance

A mint request from an `ORG_ADMIN`/`ISSUER_ADMIN` of organisation A naming organisation B, **or** naming a `connectorId` already bound to B, is refused **on the running service over real HTTP** — not only in a unit file — with the caller's own organisation unaffected, and a control proving the same admin may still mint for its own organisation.

## Dedupe before filing

Literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description across Secuura-PK, **archived included**: `organisationScope` **0**, `organizationScope` **0**, `connector_id has no unique` **0**, `provisioningPolicy` 2 (KS-742 tenancy, KS-835 OAuth consent), `decideMint` 2 (KS-742, KS-486), `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` 5 (KS-742, KS-643, KS-642, KS-486, KS-1514 — all either the tenant boundary or a response-shape issue), `ORG_ADMIN` 33 (so the scan can see). **The nearest neighbours are the tenant boundary (KS-742) and the revoke-only organisation arm (KS-764, Done); neither covers the mint's organisation arm or the connector-id binding.** KS-1107 is the same class on a different surface (`POST /api/auth/register` accepting a client-supplied `organizationId`) and is not this.

## Not measured, and whose it is

Counts of existing keys that already share a `connector_id` across organisations on Kintsugi are **not** measured here — that is the J lane's to run, per Wednesday. Nothing in this ticket was run against a live box.

Filed by Seat V 5th from the PR #1497 round 4 Opus gate, 2026-10-12.

## What each one means

### 1. The org-less accounts — the behaviour stays as PR #1521 ships it

An org-bounded caller (`ORG_ADMIN` / `ISSUER_ADMIN`) whose token carries **no** organisation claim can **no longer mint a key that names an organisation** — it gets a 403 naming the organisation boundary. It **can still mint an unqualified, tenant-level key**, so provisioning by omission survives.

* `:179` — *RULED (KS-779, Kam 2026-09-04)*: naming an organisation → **403**.
* `:189` — *RULED*: an unqualified mint → **201**.

**Nothing is changed on any account.** This ruling accepts a standing operational cost; it does not trigger a data fix.

### 2. The tenant-level `ADMIN` role — stays unbounded for now, must change before deployment

`ADMIN` is in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` (`services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:43-49`) but in **neither** `PLATFORM_ROLES` nor `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` (`packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:59`, `:76`). So the KS-764 organisation arm — `if (organisationScope && isOrgBoundedRole(user.role))` — **never engages** for it, and `decideTenantAccess` returns `same-tenant`. A tenant `ADMIN` can therefore mint a key carrying **any organisation's id inside its own tenant**: the Path 1 shape, through one role.

**Pinned at develop** as undecided policy, `:195` — *UNDECIDED POLICY (KS-1535)*: `ADMIN` naming another organisation → **201**. Its own comment says that if `ADMIN` is ruled bounded, the cell flips to 403 and that edit becomes the record of the decision.

Which deployment the note covers (the KS-695 part (ii) erasure deploy, or every deploy) is being confirmed with Kam by Wednesday.

The policy record for `ADMIN` is **KS-1535**, which set out the two readings and named this card. It is linked here.

### `platform_admin` is NOT a Path 1 vector — MEASURED

`:204` — *MEASURED*: role `platform_admin` **cannot mint at all**. `requireKeyAdminOrProvisioner` → `decideMint` runs **first**, and `PLATFORM_ADMIN` is not in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`, so it is refused **403** (*"API key management requires an admin role"*) before the organisation arm is ever reached.

That cell corrected V 5th's own first reading, which had called `platform_admin` unbounded from running `decideTenantAccess` alone — route order is invisible to a function call. So a gateway super-role is **over**-restricted at the mint, not under-restricted (the vocabulary split itself is KS-1536).

**Provenance, stated plainly:** these three behaviours are asserted by **passing cells at develop** `b28bfaec`, written by Seat V 5th for PR #1521 and run in memory through the real route stack (the file runs without a database).
