## Tickets filed from the gate's notes
- **KS-1690** (Bug, High) — the OAuth `refresh_token` grant never reads `decoded.sessionId`, so a revoked session's refresh token still redeems and mints a new session (gate measured 200 twice, 2 live sessions). Scoped to the origin-session half: **KS-1150 R-2 already covers the rotation/denylist half of that branch and is still open.** Overlapping but distinct; neither should be closed as a duplicate of the other.
- **KS-1691** (Bug, Medium) — an in-flight request resurrects a revoked session, which is then missing from `user_sessions:<id>` so a second revoke returns 0 and cannot reach it.
- **KS-1692** (Bug, High) — the silent zero as it reaches the erasure subscriber and the admin path.

## Still not covered
- **The four platform suites did not run** (no local stack, no Docker for this seat). This touches a runtime surface, so that is a real gap.
- **No real Redis was driven** — the gate's probes used a fake too.
- **N5** (a login straddling the write) is reasoned, not run, and left as residue.
- **N-1382-2** untouched, which is why this stays `Refs`.
- No migration, schema or config change.

## BLUF
**N-1382-1 is BUILT and raised as PR #1655 (https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1655), head `8e5308a87e14d4a4796e5f838de30dae0838a5bf`, READY FOR GATE, tier 1.** Both password doors now revoke the account's sessions. **The behaviour change a reviewer must agree to: change-password revokes the caller's OWN session, so the client must sign in again.** Nothing is deployed. N-1382-2 stays open, so this is `Refs`, not a close.

## Recommendation
Gate it as tier 1 — it is a session and credential surface, and it does not merge on a green run alone. Merge on a GO naming head `8e5308a87e14d4a4796e5f838de30dae0838a5bf`; then an auth deploy, which has not happened.

## What changed
| door | file | placement | why there |
|---|---|---|---|
| change-password | `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts` (+3/-0) | after `updateUserOrThrow` | the write throws if it did not land, so a revocation can never follow a non-write |
| reset-password | `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` (+4/-1) | after the write, **before** `consumeResetToken` | a revocation that throws leaves the single-use token **unburned**, so the user can retry instead of holding a changed password and a dead token |

`revokeAllUserSessions` is account-wide and nothing spares `req.sessionId`, so the caller's own access token stops validating after a successful change. That is deliberate. The alternative (`getUserSessions` + `revokeSession` minus the caller's own) needs two functions the existing session mock does not provide; it was neither built nor ruled.

If the revocation throws (a Redis fault) **after** the password was written, the request answers an error although the password did change. Reset: the token is unburned, so a retry works. Change-password: the user retries with the new password as the current one.

## Evidence
- **Red-first, reproduced here rather than quoted: 6 failed / 14 run** — 3 of 7 in each new cell file, the three RED assertion cells, with all 8 CONTROL cells green and 0 load-failure signatures. Green after: **14 passed / 14 run, 0 skipped**. `tsc --noEmit -p services/auth` rc 0.
- **`services/auth` suite, both ends measured on real trees:** baseline **99 files / 1096 tests / 0 failed** on a clean checkout of the base; after **101 files / 1110 tests / 0 failed**. +14 cells, **0 vanished**.
- **13 mutation arms, 13 killed, 0 survivors, so no cell was added.** Including two that pin *which* account is revoked (revoke a different account id reds R1 on both doors). Each arm proved its anchor unique before tampering, type-checked (a mutant that will not compile is inadmissible, not a survivor), and restored by content with a sha256 equality assertion.
- **Who this breaks: nobody, measured.** No in-repo client calls either route. `me/change-password` has 8 hits, every one the route, the generated spec, the OpenAPI registration or a test; `auth/reset-password` has **zero** call sites under `frontend/` or `sdk/`. Controls: the same search shape finds `auth/login` in 6 files under `frontend/` and 105 repo-wide. `frontend/admin/src/pages/Profile.tsx:49` `handleChangePassword` posts to `/api/auth/password/reset-request` — it emails a reset link and never calls this route. Both SDKs expose no password or session surface. **Equally: no in-repo client exercises this behaviour at all.**
- Pre-push preflight, in-hook: **`PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.`** Legs 3, 4 and 8 need a local stack that was not up. Quoting it as the gate printed it, including its own line *"This is NOT a pass."* Leg 16 type-checks auth's test files against the ratchet baseline: **152 files examined, 42 errors, 42 baselined, 0 new**.

## Not covered
- **The four platform suites (Schemathesis / Akto / Playwright / Performance k6) did not run** — they need the local stack, and this seat is held off Docker on this machine. This does touch a runtime surface, so that is a real gap, stated rather than skipped.
- **No real Redis was driven.** Both cell files replace the session service, so what is pinned is that the call is made, once, for the right account, at the right point in the sequence — not that Redis actually drops the sessions.
- **N-1382-2 untouched** — the e2e case at `tests/e2e/tests/security-bad-actor.prelaunch.spec.ts:1155,1182` posts to `/api/auth/change-password`, a route that does not exist.
- No migration, no schema change, no config or environment value.

The two patches are a local-model (Spark) pass applied byte-for-byte from each run's canonical `patch.diff`; the measurement above is mine.

title: auth GET /api/users/lookup refuses connector tokens, so every Platform-S transfer-custody 401s and falls back to a flat anchor — KS-739's users:read ruling cannot take effect
description:
## BLUF

**No Platform-S rights-assign or rights-reassign reaches** `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` **successfully.** originate resolves `newHolderEmail` by calling auth's `GET /api/users/lookup` with the **caller's** `Authorization` header, and `/lookup` accepts only access tokens (`authenticate()`). Platform-S authenticates per Organisation with a **connector** token, so auth answers 401 *"Invalid token"*, originate passes it through ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)'s 4xx rule), and S degrades to a flat `/api/anchors` anchor. No `custody_events` row is written and `documents.owner_user_id` never moves.

[KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) (Done, archived) ruled 2026-09-02 that *"Platform S provisions* `users:read` *on its connector key; K does not widen* `ALLOWED_LOOKUP_ROLES`*"*. That ruling cannot take effect: the scope check sits behind an authenticator that rejects the token type before any scope is read. A missing scope would answer **403**; what S receives is **401 Invalid token**.

## Code (platform-k `develop` `0736d8b78`)

* `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1665-1671` — email-only path: `fetch(${AUTH_SERVICE_URL}/api/users/lookup?email=…, { headers: { Authorization: <caller's header> } })`.
* `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1708-1730` — a 4xx from the lookup is passed through; 401 → *"The credential on this request was rejected by the user lookup. Re-authenticate and retry."* ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)).
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:266` — `userRoutes.get('/lookup', authenticate(), …)` — access tokens only.
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:357-359` — "[KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) *(Option A): this ONE route also accepts a connector token — see authenticateAccessOrConnector. Every other route keeps plain authenticate()."* — `/stub` was widened; `/lookup` was not.
* Platform-S side: `ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs` `TransferCustodyAsync` sends `{ newHolderEmail, reason }` + `onBehalfOf` with `Authorization: Bearer <connector access token>` (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:1527`).

## Measured — local pair, slot 3, 2026-10-01

platform-s `f370236c` (+ [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) systemTest changes only) ↔ platform-k `0736d8b78`, fresh databases, 33/33 K containers up, `/health/deep` 200, S provisioning key accepted, 10/0/0 organisations registered.

**4 of 4** transfer-custody calls refused, identical body, under Organisation 3's connector key:

```
transfer-custody status=401 body={"success":false,"error":{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"The credential on this request was rejected by the user lookup. Re-authenticate and retry. Upstream said: Invalid token"}} … using /api/anchors fallback.
```

* 09:21:55Z — 2 calls ([PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914)'s date-sort seed: two documents delegated to a same-org colleague).
* 09:22:55–09:31:06Z — 2 calls during `npm run test:k-live` (`verb_matrix.spec.ts` rights-assign + rights-reassign on K document `7af2374a-dd61-47e7-be50-122dcb5e412b`).

In the same window, Organisation 3's connector token **succeeded** on `originate` (201) and on lifecycle events (`rights-unassign`, `delete`) — so the key is valid; only the auth-service lookup refuses it.

## Why nothing went red

The platform-s `@k-live` cell "rights-assign and rights-unassign each reach K" asserted only that the S edge carries an anchor K resolves as not-failed — which the flat fallback also satisfies. It passed (17 passed / 1 skipped) while both custody calls 401'd. [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) tightens that cell to assert the custody transfer K records — `GET /api/documents/{id}` `owner.id` must move off its pre-assign value (measured: it reads `""` before and after today's refused transfers). The cell is **red until this ticket ships**, deliberately, and turns green once K records the transfer. Platform-S's `TransferCustodyAsync` carries a comment naming this ticket.

## Options (Kamil's call — no K code changed)

1. **Widen** `/lookup` **to** `authenticateAccessOrConnector()`, as [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) did for `/stub` — makes [KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)'s `users:read` ruling effective (the connector key then needs that scope).
2. **originate resolves the holder with its own service credential**, not the caller's header — removes the dependency on the caller's token type.
3. **Platform-S sends** `newHolderId` — requires S to know the K user id of the recipient (S-side; it does not today).

Whichever is chosen, a recipient with no K account still gets the typed 404 `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) measurement A) — worth confirming the S holder exists in K once the 401 is gone.

## Related

[KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) (Done, archived — ruling this ticket shows cannot take effect) · [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) (Option A connector scoping) · [PS-681](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-681/systemtest-k-live-every-share-and-rights-verb-times-out-waiting-for) (Done — Stuart's original 502 report) · [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) (platform-s: the k-live cell that hid this).

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Yes, Kintsugi wrote one custody event for every accepted call: seven events for your document, at the seven times you listed, to the second. The document's owner moved to a single invited user that Kintsugi created 32 ms before the first event. None of the seven events recorded an anchor. I cannot confirm that the invited user's address is firsttime@lhsg.com, and I cannot show the reason for the refused anchors, for the two reasons under "Not measured".

All times are UTC, with AEDT (UTC+11) in brackets. Each figure says how it was read. Sections 1 to 3 are from SELECTs on Kintsugi on 29 Oct between 04:53 and 05:01 UTC [15:53 and 16:01 AEDT], in read-only database sessions. Section 4 is from the box's REVISION records, read at 05:04 UTC [16:04 AEDT].

**1. The invited user**
- Kintsugi holds one user created inside the 26 Oct 03:00 to 03:20 UTC window: status `invited`, role `user`, created 2026-10-26 03:09:24.532 [14:09:24 AEDT], in Kintsugi's default tenant. It was created 32 ms before the first custody event.
- It is the recipient of all seven events and the owner of the document now. It owns no other document.
- Its address is not shown here. See "Not measured".

**2. The custody events** (the K document you name, `427c4864-fde0-4713-9e36-7e50d0097a49`, is stored on Kintsugi as the document's external id)

| # | created (UTC) | [AEDT] | from | to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 2026-10-26 03:09:24.564 | [14:09:24] | none | the invited user |
| 2 | 03:10:24.746 | [14:10:24] | the invited user | the invited user |
| 3 | 03:11:24.832 | [14:11:24] | the invited user | the invited user |
| 4 | 03:12:24.896 | [14:12:24] | the invited user | the invited user |
| 5 | 03:13:25.046 | [14:13:25] | the invited user | the invited user |
| 6 | 03:14:25.113 | [14:14:25] | the invited user | the invited user |
| 7 | 03:15:25.262 | [14:15:25] | the invited user | the invited user |

- Count: 7, all inside 03:09:00 to 03:16:00 UTC; the gaps between them are 60, 60, 60, 60, 60 and 60 seconds. Control on the same query: the 28 Oct document from your KS-1384 table has 1 event. So events 2 to 7 are repeats of the same transfer: each wrote a row that moves the document from the invited user to the same user.
- Ownership: the document's owner is the invited user. That user did not exist before 03:09:24.532 on 26 Oct and the document was created on 23 Oct 09:10, so the owner changed in this window. The document's `updated_at` is 03:15:25.262, the time of event 7, and its status is still `draft`.
- All seven events have an empty "transferred by" and an empty anchor transaction. The provenance table holds seven `transfer-custody` rows for the document, first 03:09:24 and last 03:15:25.
- Kintsugi's audit trail holds seven `POST …/transfer-custody` requests answered 201, at the same seven times.

**3. The anchors**
- Kintsugi's audit trail holds seven `POST /api/anchors` requests answered 400, each 8 to 37 ms after a transfer-custody request. Those seven are the only `anchors.create` requests answered 400 in the trail, which begins on 20 Aug (7 of its 12 `anchors.create` rows). The trail records no error text for them.
- Kintsugi's anchor table holds 0 rows for this document; control: 1 row for the 28 Oct document.
- So no anchor was created for any of the seven transfers, and the transfer route answered success each time. From the audit trail alone I cannot tell whether those 400s are the calls S made after each transfer or the route's own internal call; their timing fits the calls S made.

**4. Which build**
Kintsugi ran develop `1ae6f17d19a8` for all seven events (deployed 26 Oct 00:46:20 UTC [11:46:20 AEDT], replaced 26 Oct 07:55:24 UTC [18:55:24 AEDT], read from the box's REVISION records). Your comment names `bcc51903d`, which was the build before that. Kintsugi now runs `5dccdcb29ec2`.

**Not measured**
- Whether the invited user's address is firsttime@lhsg.com (as you gave it). Kintsugi stores addresses encrypted. Its address-lookup column did not match a plain hash of a known address in a control test, so I could not search by address without decrypting, and I did not decrypt.
- The reason for the refused anchors, and whether the transfer route's own anchor call also met a 400 `Invalid DID`. Originate's log on Kintsugi starts on 29 Oct 01:05:59 UTC [12:05:59 AEDT], after later redeploys, and no file on the box holds 26 Oct log lines. The "Lifecycle anchor emission failed" and "Custody transferred" lines for 26 Oct are therefore not available.

Update, 03:17 UTC: **S stopped the loop at 03:15:58 UTC.** The transfer for document `427c4864-fde0-4713-9e36-7e50d0097a49` reached Kintsugi **7 times**, at 03:09:24, 03:10:24, 03:11:24, 03:12:24, 03:13:25, 03:14:25 and 03:15:25 UTC, each answered 2xx with no anchor reference. Nothing more will arrive from S for it. On Stuart's instruction S's row was given a local marker and parked. A count of `custody_events` for that document over 03:09–03:16 UTC would show whether K wrote one row per call. The S fix is filed on the S side. For context, that document's own upload on 23 Oct 09:10 UTC (same Entra-verified actor) was created on K, but its anchor was refused for the same `did:jwk` reason, and S parked it as FAILED.

@kamil.kreiser — **live custody transfer on dev-ps against Kintsugi `bcc51903d`, 26 Oct 2026 03:09 UTC: K accepted it, but returned no anchor reference.** Read from S's side (dev-ps app log and its `DocumentTransaction` row; S develop `4fb15e7`).

- **What ran:** stuart@obeden.com assigned S document 15 (K document `427c4864-fde0-4713-9e3…`) to firsttime@lhsg.com, a person who had never received custody or a certification, so K had no user for them. S row 96, chain id `5008820d82c743fd971cbc4d99729a20`.
- **K's answer to `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody`: 2xx**, with no `transfer.anchorId` / `transfer.anchor.id` in the body. S logged `transfer-custody OK but no ref in payload for tx 5008820d…; using /api/anchors fallback`. So the old 404 `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` and the 500 are gone on Kintsugi. **Please confirm from your side:** an invited stub for firsttime@lhsg.com in `users`, and the `custody_events` row(s) with the owner moved.
- **Why no anchor reference, as far as S can tell:** the assigner is Entra-verified, so S's identity block carries a `did:jwk` `actorDid`. S's flat fallback (`POST /api/anchors`) was then refused 400 `Invalid DID — expect did:key:… or did:web:…` at `identity.actorDid` (the KS-1175 widening). That suggests the custody route's own anchor call met the same 400 and the route returned success without it, the same shape as KS-1709 on certify. Can you confirm from originate's log?
- **The S-side problem this exposes, which matters for your tables:** S's background drain re-sends any row that has no K reference on every pass, with no limit. For this row it has re-sent the same transfer-custody **once a minute: 03:09:24, 03:10:24, 03:11:24 …, 4 calls by 03:13 UTC**, each answered 2xx by K and each followed by a refused flat anchor. If K writes a `custody_events` row per call, Kintsugi is accumulating one duplicate transfer a minute for this document. A count of `custody_events` for that document would tell us. It continues until S stops it (I'm asking Stuart now) or K accepts `did:jwk`. It is the only row in that state on dev-ps.

The S fix (do not re-send a side-effecting verb K has already accepted; park the row instead) will be an S ticket.

**#1620 measured end to end, 19 Oct 12:13–12:31Z, slot 4, K develop `115797747` (fresh DB, 54 migrations), S develop `b7d414b`:** the PS-992 cell's rights-assign to `firsttwo@lhsg.com` — a person this K had never seen — now answers **201**: S logs `'rights-assign' → transfer-custody ref anchor_ff9fea6c-…`, K's `users` gains one **invited** stub (2 → 3), `custody_events` holds 1 row with `transferred_by_id` NULL, and originate's log has no 22P02 beyond its startup probe. Zero `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` in the run. The cell then fails on its custodian read-back (`GET /api/documents/{id}` → 404 to the k-live client after ownership moved), the shape already filed to Peter on PS-1299 — so on this build the transfer half is green and the read half is the estate's.

On PS-1091 reading Canceled: that was done **because** the K side changed, not on the assumption it would not — it was cancelled at 09:55Z quoting Kam's (a) verbatim, with the note that #1620 makes S's pre-transfer stub call unnecessary and that Kintsugi keeps answering 404 until it takes #1614 + #1620 together. No second look needed; the S-side residue is the closer cell's read-back (PS-1299, Peter).

Read #1620 merged at `a0da739b6` and KS-1662's fix at `115797747`. Stuart's slot-1 K was rebuilt at `115797747` today (originate image 11:34Z carries the stub path), so the next S run against it will exercise the mint for real; the dev-ps pairing stays as you describe — 201 locally, 404 on Kintsugi — until the round.

## BLUF

**The invited-stub holder is merged — not deployed.** PR #1620 landed on `develop` at
`a0da739b6954d42333640ea190d877f031803c7f`. A custody transfer naming a recipient Platform K has
never seen now **mints an invited stub user and records the transfer**, instead of answering
`404 RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND`. That completes the build half of Kam's ruling. **Nothing is live**, so
Platform S still sees the old 404 on every environment until a deploy round carries this.

## Recommendation

1. **Deploy needs a rebuild, and both KS-1402 changes should travel together** — the 500 fix with
   migration `052` (merged earlier at `80868551e679`) and this stub holder. A box with one and not
   the other is a state no suite covers. Rebuilding **either** the `migrations` image **or** the
   `api-gateway` image lands `052`; afterwards check `custody_events.transferred_by_id` reads
   `is_nullable = YES` — the runner prints `applied=N failed=0` even when it ran a stale image, so
   the column is the evidence, not the summary line.
2. **This ticket stays In Progress** until it is deployed and live-checked.
3. One follow-up is open and worth doing before anyone leans on the tenant guarantees: **KS-1662**.

## Detail

**What landed.** On the email path's zero-row case only, the route calls auth's
`POST /api/users/stub` with the caller's credential forwarded — the shape `certifications/issue`
already used for `holderEmail`, which is the precedent Kam's card names. auth stays the only writer
of `users`, so its PII encryption, the email lookup hash, the cross-tenant rule and the
claim-on-registration flow are not duplicated. **No auth change, no new scope, no migration**:
Platform S's connector key already passes that endpoint's gate.

**What is deliberately different from Kintsugi.** Kintsugi answers 404 for an unknown recipient;
Platform K now answers 201. Recorded separately on this ticket with a case-by-case table — only that
one branch diverges.

**Gaps in the shipped coverage, stated rather than left to be discovered (KS-1662):**
- The route's **tenant predicates are not independently proven**. `users` is FORCE RLS for the
  application role, so dropping a predicate still leaves the suite green — RLS hides the row anyway.
  A cell without RLS is needed before anyone treats those predicates as tested.
- The non-2xx fallback has no cell (it fails safe).
- Two code comments name an auth test as a scope tripwire; it is not one. The real tripwire is an
  api-gateway test. Corrected in the PR body; the comments are in KS-1662.

**Review.** Tier-1 gated twice. Round 1 returned NO GO on two blockers — the race fallback was
written for a database constraint that does not exist, so it could never run in the real race, and
the tenant re-read had no cell on the branch where auth skips its own tenant check. Both fixed, each
with a cell that reds without the fix, and the gate's own mutant now reds the new cell. Round 2
returned GO, and the landed tree equals the figure predicted before the merge.

**Also noted:** PS-1091 — the Platform-S ticket for this 404 — now reads **Canceled**. If that was
done on the assumption the K side would not change, it is worth a second look now that it has.

Read, 19 Oct 10:00 UTC: #1614 merged (`80868551e`), Kam's ruling (a) — **K creates the invited stub on transfer, as `certifications/issue` does** — and the divergence table. Three S consequences, recorded on the S side:

1. **PS-1091 (S stubs the holder first) is withdrawn** — the ruling makes it unnecessary; the ticket is cancelled with the ruling quoted.
2. **The PS-992 closer cell will pass on a K at or after #1620 for its transfer** — and then still needs its custodian read-back fixed (my comment above; filed to Peter on PS-1299), so a red there after #1620 is the read, not the transfer.
3. **Deploy pairing noted:** #1614 (migration 052) and #1620 ship together, and until Kintsugi takes them a rights-assign to a new person succeeds locally and 404s on dev-ps; S's dev-ps proof (PS-1284) will state which build it ran against.

One privacy fact for KS-1655, posted there: S's person erasure already sends K a `POST /api/gdpr/erasures`, so the retention question for S-minted stubs is whether that erasure reaches an `invited` row.

## BLUF

**Platform K now deliberately diverges from Kintsugi on one answer, and it will stay diverged until
Kintsugi takes this build.** For a custody transfer naming a recipient email with no Platform K
user: **Kintsugi answers `404 RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND`; Platform K `develop` answers `201`**, minting an
invited stub holder. This is Kam's ruling, not a defect — recording it because "Kintsugi still
answers the correct 404" was load-bearing evidence earlier on this ticket, and a future reader
comparing the two boxes will otherwise read the difference as a regression.

## Recommendation

Treat the divergence as expected until a Kintsugi deploy round carries this change. Two
consequences worth holding:

1. **The deploy order now matters in the other direction.** Earlier on this ticket the risk was that
   a Kintsugi round would make Platform S *worse*. It is now the reverse: Platform K leads, and
   Kintsugi keeps refusing these transfers until it is updated.
2. **Two things ship together or the gap widens**: the KS-1402 500 fix (merged, `80868551e679`, with
   migration 052) and the invited-stub build (**PR #1620**, at review, head `dbb00e65dfb0`). A box
   with one and not the other is a state neither suite covers.

## Detail

**What changed, measured.** The old answer was pinned by a cell that passed:
`KINTSUGI — a connector naming a holder K does NOT know still answers 404 RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND and
writes nothing`. It has been rewritten and renamed rather than deleted, and it keeps its
writes-nothing assertions.

**The divergence is exactly one branch, not a behaviour change across the route:**

| Case | Kintsugi | Platform K after this build |
|---|---|---|
| Recipient email has a K user in this tenant | 201 | 201 (unchanged) |
| Recipient email has **no** K user | **404 `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND`** | **201** + an INVITED stub minted |
| Recipient email belongs to **another** tenant | 404 | 404 (unchanged) |
| Unknown `newHolderId` (by id, not email) | 404 | 404 (unchanged) |
| Malformed email | 400 | 400 (unchanged) |

**Authority:** Kam, card `secuura-ks1402-who-creates-the-holder-1019` = (a), 2026-10-19:
*"K creates an invited stub user on transfer. As certifications/issue already does for holderEmail."*

**What it means for anyone measuring the two boxes.** A rights-assign to a brand-new person will
succeed against Platform K and 404 against Kintsugi. Neither is broken; they are at different
commits. The S-side ticket for the 404 itself is PS-1091.

**Not deployed.** Nothing has been run against either deployed box for this work — the readings
above are from code and from local suites, not from the live boxes.

**Measured before the merge, as offered: #1614 (`ddd54b836`) fixes the 500, and K now records S's custody transfers.** Slot 4, 19 Oct 07:16–08:44 UTC: K built from a local branch = develop `722e07f19` + #1613 + #1614 (`f5c6c0ff2`), fresh database, migration 052 applied (54 of 54); the running originate image carries the new actor helper. S develop `2c1d179`, fresh database, `PII_LOOKUP_HMAC_KEY` present on originate.

**Where the holder resolves (a person K already knows as a user or INVITED stub), the transfer now succeeds:**
- Five S `rights-assign` events during the full suite went through `POST /{id}/transfer-custody` and came back with a custody anchor (`'rights-assign' → transfer-custody ref anchor_…` at 08:14:32, 08:15:05, 08:19:50, 08:23:01, 08:35:29Z) — no flat-anchor fallback.
- K's `custody_events` holds **5 rows, `transferred_by_id` NULL on all 5** — exactly the "resolved user, else NULL" the fix specifies for S's people; `documents.owner_user_id` moved (e.g. document `81aec073-…` → owner `8802e2e2-…` at 08:35:29Z).
- originate log since the run began: **0 × `22P02`, 0 × "Failed to transfer custody"** (the only 22P02 in the whole log is a startup probe with the literal `test-123`, before any S traffic).

## Recommendation

Two things, in order:

## Detail

- **What the 500 was.** `custody_events.transferred_by_id` is `UUID NOT NULL` (migration 023),

  `::uuid` cast, that raised `22P02` inside the custody transaction and fell to the route's outer

  typed `404 RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` before the INSERT, which is why the defect stayed hidden until a
  holder existed.
- **Not a regression.** The same chain is present in Kintsugi's `65d7722f8`.

  user, else NULL — plus migration `052` dropping the NOT NULL. Without `052` the `22P02` merely
  becomes a `23502` and the transfer still 500s.
- **Attribution is not lost.** The connector stays recorded on the KS-480 `action_provenance` row
  when `onBehalfOf` is supplied. A *bare* connector transfer stores no actor at all — a real gap,
  not a regression (the write previously failed outright), tracked in `BACKLOG.md` alongside the
  same gap on `/share` and `/lifecycle-events`.
- **Review.** Tier-1 gate, round 1 of 2: GO at `ddd54b836394`, 0 blockers, 5 non-blocking notes.

  #1613's two api-gateway files) and the landing tree was predicted as `9fec48e29e34` before the
  merge and measured equal after it.

**Still open on this ticket:** who creates the holder. Kam ruled that Platform K creates an invited
stub user on transfer; that build is designed but not written, and this ticket stays In Progress
until it and the deploy are done.

For Platform S's people, who have no K user, the actor is NULL. Migration 052 makes the column nullable; without it the 22P02 only becomes a NOT NULL violation.
- **The holder.** Who creates it is a separate question, and that question is with Kam.

Either way the Platform-S `@k-live` rights-assign cell (PS-992) stays red until K records the transfer; S's `TransferCustodyAsync` needs no change for either option.

**KS-1402 is fixed on develop, and here is exactly what changed and what is still unverified.**

Kam ruled this on 2026-10-02 (live board, card `secuura-ks1402-lookup-refuses-connector-tokens`), option (a): *"Widen /lookup to accept a connector token, as /stub already does (KS 564)."*

`GET /api/users/lookup` now authenticates through `authenticateAccessOrConnector()`, the same door `POST /api/users/stub` has used since KS 564. |---|---|---|

A connector token without a tenant claim would skip the cross-tenant 404 on this route. Read in the code, the token exchange always issues a tenant claim, so this was not reached in testing; it is tracked in KS-1406.

**@stuart.jamieson — one thing needs checking on the S side, and it is the difference between a fix and a half-fix.** Whether Platform-S's connector key actually carries `users:read` is **not measurable from Platform K**. If it does, the transfer-custody call now succeeds. If it does not, S moves from **401 Invalid token** to **403** — still a refusal, but the correct one, and the scope is then the thing to fix. UNMEASURED from here.

title: The e2e-v2 harness is platform-k's only browser, portal and accessibility coverage — 222 tests, runnable by hand, named in no gate and absent from the gate inventory
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/` holds **24 spec files and 222 tests** across four tiers — including every browser journey and the only accessibility coverage platform-k has — and it is wired into nothing. It is not in `.githooks/pre-push`, it has no row in the "Manual CI-gate equivalents" table that `KS-685` commissioned, and the workflow its own README points at (`.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`) does not exist on `develop`. Meanwhile the suite people *are* pointed at, `systemTest/playwright`, is API-only: 3 spec files, 11 tests, no browser. So the documented estate says platform-k has a Playwright tier, and the thing that actually opens a browser is the one nobody is told to run. Counted on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026. Nothing was executed — this is about wiring, not results.

## What is there

Measured from the tree, not from the docs:

| Tier | Specs | Tests | What it covers |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `tier1-api` | 12 | 174 | API over HTTP |
| `tier2-smoke` | 5 | 43 | Smoke journeys |
| `tier3-e2e` | 4 | 40 | **Real browser journeys** — issuer, admin, verifier |
| `tier4-a11y` | 3 | 6 | **axe on admin, issuer and verifier** |
| **Total** | **24** | **222** |  |

It is runnable today. `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/package.json` declares `test`, `test:api`, `test:smoke`, `test:e2e`, `test:a11y`, `install:browsers` and `report`, and `playwright.config.ts` defines the four matching projects (`api`, `smoke`, `e2e`, `a11y`). `@axe-core/playwright` is a devDependency there.

## What is missing

1. **No gate names it.** `grep -rn "e2e-v2" .githooks/pre-push Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` returns nothing. The manual-gate table at `DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143` maps *former CI job → local command* for 13 rows and has no row for e2e-v2, and none for accessibility at all.
2. **Its README cites a workflow that does not exist.** `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/README.md:4` sends the reader to `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`; `git ls-tree origin/develop .github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml` is empty.
3. **The plan doc under-reports it.** `Blockchain/Dev/docs/E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:324` still says *"only the verifier portal has a tier-4 spec. Issuer + admin coverage is a follow-up."* That follow-up is `KS-44`, which is **Done** — there are three tier-4 specs in the tree today. The row understates the coverage that exists.

## Why it matters

* It is the whole UI answer. Without it the honest statement about platform-k is that no browser opens anywhere in the estate — `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts:12-18` says so itself, and `DEV-PROCESS.md:141` spells it out: *"Despite the name, this suite drives no browser… Read a green here as '12 API assertions passed', not as 'the portals work'."*
* It is the whole accessibility answer. There is no `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` anywhere in the repo and no axe inside any frontend, so `tier4-a11y` is the only thing that would catch a regression against WCAG 2.2 / EN 301 549 — relevant to the same obligations the platform-s side tracks. WCAG 2.2: [https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/](<https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/>) · EN 301 549 v3.2.1: [https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/03.02.01_60/en_301549v030201p.pdf](<https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/03.02.01_60/en_301549v030201p.pdf>) · EAA Directive 2019/882: [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj](<https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj>)
* An ungated suite rots quietly. `KS-557` / `KS-560` are the precedent — the tier reported 126 failures, of which only 11 were real, and the cause was a harness defect that had gone unnoticed. `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:358` keeps that lesson as a standing rule.
* Actions being retired makes this the *only* route to the coverage, not a redundant one.

## Suggested shape

1. Give e2e-v2 a row in the `DEV-PROCESS.md` manual-gate table: the exact command, the pass criterion, and a measured wall-clock — matching the 13 rows already there.
2. Decide the tier split deliberately. `tier4-a11y` is 6 tests and needs only a running stack; it is the cheapest thing in the estate to make routine. `tier3-e2e` is slower and flakier (single-session collisions, `E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md` § "Worker-session collisions") so it may belong in a nightly/manual tier rather than a per-push one.
3. Fix the two stale pointers: the dead workflow reference in `tests/e2e/README.md:4`, and the tier-4 row in `E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:324` that `KS-44` has already overtaken.
4. Say in `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` where the browser tier actually lives, so "Playwright" stops meaning two different things in the same repo.

## Acceptance

* `DEV-PROCESS.md`'s gate table has an e2e-v2 row (or rows) with a command and a measured time.
* A named person can run the a11y tier from the runbook without reading source.
* No document points at `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`, and the tier-4 row reflects the three specs that exist.

## Decision needed before fixing — naming the three Playwright estates

Worth settling the naming in the same pass: `systemTest/playwright` (API-only, 11 tests) and `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2` (browser, 222 tests) are both "Playwright", and a third corpus sits at `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e` (`KS-734`, In Review — not a workspace member, cannot install from a clean checkout; `KS-1038`, Backlog — races its own lockout). Three Playwright estates with one name is the reason a reader can believe the portals are covered when the suite in the gate never opens a browser. One decision about which survives, which is gated, and what each is called would close this ticket and shrink two others.

## References

`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/package.json` · `playwright.config.ts:29-73` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143`, `:141` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:316-345` · `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/README.md:4` · `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts:12-18` · `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:358` · related: `KS-1076` (Urgent, Todo — no Playwright e2e on a PR since 7 Sep), `KS-734` (In Review), `KS-1038` (Backlog), `KS-44` (Done), `KS-637` (Backlog), `KS-685`.

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — no stack started, no suite executed; all counts measured from the tree at that commit. GitHub Actions executes nothing on this repo (billing), so no workflow is a live alternative to the local route.

**BLUF:** Hi Kamil, thanks for picking this up. While grounding a plan for this ticket I found six more things that bear on it. Each one was re-checked from source on `develop` **`8c810023f`** (29 Sep), not taken from memory. The most important is #1: once e2e-v2 is named in a gate, a bare local run of it hits slot 1's gateway without saying so. Nothing was edited or run. These are notes for you to take or leave as you see fit.

**1. e2e-v2 has no slot awareness, so a local run naming no slot targets slot 1.**
- `playwright.config.ts:3` defaults `GATEWAY_URL` to `http://localhost:6882`.
- `fixtures/api-client.ts:17` and `:22` do the same for the API and issuer bases.
- Nothing under `tests/e2e-v2` reads `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` or `STACK_SLOT` (0 matches).

On a shared machine that means another ticket's stack. The systemTest harnesses refuse this case (KS-1016), and e2e-v2 would be the one browser suite that doesn't.

The good news is that `systemTest/slot-target.sh:99` already exports a slot-derived `GATEWAY_URL`, and that's the first variable e2e-v2 reads. So wrapping the gate command, e.g. `systemTest/run-in-slot.sh <N> npm --prefix Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2 run test:a11y`, would target the right stack and hold the per-slot lock with no typed port. A small refusal guard in the config would cover the bare `npm run` case. That's your call.

**2. The runbook the acceptance line relies on is itself stale.** "Run the a11y tier from the runbook without reading source" needs these fixed first.
- `RUNBOOK.md`:
  - `:16` lists tier 4 as 2 tests; there are 6.
  - `:189` says a11y is "admin/verifier-only"; issuer is covered too.
  - `:63-72` give the decommissioned Container Apps demo URLs.
  - `:48` hand-rolls `docker compose up -d` rather than `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh`.
- `README.md`:
  - 8 lines still carry the dead secuura01 `yellowground-ae96b9b1` URLs, which KS-333 repointed elsewhere.
  - `:24` says "3 Tiers"; there are four.
  - Its credentials table names the retired admin password, which may already fall under KS-965's documentary cleanup if it isn't one of its 55 files.
- `tests/tier4-a11y/README.md`:
  - `:11` says to install axe at `Blockchain/Dev`; it's in e2e-v2's own `package.json` and lock now.
  - `:71-73` describe `button-name` / `color-contrast` as demoted under KS-45; no spec passes `knownIssueRules` any more.
  - `:26` runs against `GATEWAY_URL=https://secuura.com`, a domain we don't own. That's the KS-669 class, in a README rather than the spec.

**3. The admin a11y test needs `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, and no e2e-v2 doc says so.** `fixtures/api-client.ts:61` leaves it empty when unset. That's deliberate (KS-964, no published fallback), so this is a docs gap rather than a code bug. But anyone following the runbook will get a failed admin login and nothing telling them why. The variable is documented only in `systemTest/playwright`'s docs.

**4. Stale suppression in `tests/tier4-a11y/_axe.ts:15`.** `// @ts-expect-error — package is not yet in the e2e-v2 lockfile`. It is in the lockfile now (`package-lock.json:16`). Nothing type-checks e2e-v2 (see #5), so this has never surfaced. Under a real `tsc` it would likely become an "unused @ts-expect-error" error.

**5. e2e-v2 has no quality gates of its own.**
- The package has no tsconfig, Prettier config or ESLint config.
- The repo-level `Blockchain/Dev/eslint.config.mjs` only targets `services/`, `packages/`, `sdk/`, `scripts/` and `frontend/`.

So a gate row for e2e-v2 would run specs that nothing lints or type-checks. Worth deciding whether a minimal `typecheck` belongs in the same change.

**6. A timing measurement can't use a current build yet (KS-1380).** The acceptance asks for a measured wall-clock, but `develop` still doesn't build: `packages/shared` locks `@types/express-serve-static-core` 4.19.9 and `@types/pg` 8.23.1, while analytics, billing and governance still lock 4.19.8 / 8.20.0. Until KS-1380 lands, a timing run would need a stack built at `8af6ab821`, as other slots have been, and the evidence should say so.

**Smaller count notes:**
- The gate table in `DEV-PROCESS.md` has 14 rows at this commit, not 13.
- `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml` is also cited at `docs/REVIEW_NOTES.md:276` and `CHANGELOG.md:73`, as well as `tests/e2e/README.md:4`. The CHANGELOG line is history and probably wants to stay.

**Related, already tracked:** KS-1393 row 1 (31 uncovered specs; its note already suggests doing it together with this ticket and KS-734), KS-965 (retired admin credential in docs), KS-669 (URLs on domains we don't own), KS-1380 (build).

Happy to help with any of it if useful. Thank you!

title: A clean image build of platform-k develop fails: services/governance does not compile (TS2742 on router's inferred type) — a new slot cannot start until the image exists from an older build
description:
## Seen (2026-09-29, develop `0aa9b52c6`; origin/develop `b4461d1e2` is three commits ahead, none touching governance)

Starting a fresh stack slot with no cached images (`Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` via platform-s's `up-slot.sh 4`) fails at the governance image:

```
docker compose -p secuura_slot4 build --progress=plain governance
#19 1.611 src/routes/governance.ts(19,7): error TS2742: The inferred type of 'router' cannot be
      named without a reference to '@secuura/shared/node_modules/@types/express-serve-static-core'.
      This is likely not portable. A type annotation is necessary.
#19 ERROR: process "/bin/sh -c npm run build" did not complete successfully: exit code: 1
```

Reproducible: the same `docker compose build governance` fails the same way on a second run. Slots 1–3 on this machine start only because they hold `secuura_slot{1,2,3}-governance` images built up to two weeks ago; slot 4 had no image and could not be built. A new developer machine, or a slot torn down with `--rmi all` (the test-discipline teardown), hits this.

The first attempt on the same slot failed one image earlier — `nft-certificate` at `npm ci --ignore-scripts` — and that one built cleanly on retry, so it was transient; governance is not.

## Suggested fix

`services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts:19` — give `router` an explicit type (`const router: Router = express.Router()`), the usual TS2742 remedy when a workspace package (`@secuura/shared`) carries its own `@types/express-serve-static-core`. Worth a `tsc --noEmit` over every service in the PR gate so a non-portable inferred type cannot land again.

## Impact on platform-s

Blocks pairing an S slot with a fresh K slot for the gate run on platform-s PR #889 (the S↔K remediation branch); recorded there and on [PS-928](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-928/k-live-goes-red-on-the-second-full-run-on-a-slot-the-anchor-refresher). Related: [KS-955](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-955/a-fresh-clone-cannot-run-the-four-platform-suites-and-fails-in-a-way) (a fresh clone cannot run the suites).

@kamil.kreiser — the rebuild evidence, as asked. Read it before deciding; on your own criterion it does **not** close this ticket.

- **Command:** `./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild` (Stuart, by hand, from his `~/obd-dev/platform-k` clone, clean on `develop` at **`78cb3c393`**), slot 1, 2026-10-18 22:45:40Z → 23:02:58Z. The script builds **serially**, one `docker compose --progress=plain -f docker-compose.local.yml build <service>` per service with `COMPOSE_BAKE=0`; it passes **no `--no-cache`**, so the layer cache was warm from the 15 Oct build — not a cold build. `governance` built 22:53:14Z → 22:54:38Z (image `2f87233cfc20`), then the script went on to `issuer-frontend`; all 33 services came up healthy, `/health/deep` 200, migrations `applied=0 skipped=51`.
- **The variable you named:** inside `platform-k-governance:latest` there is exactly **one** copy of `@types/express-serve-static-core`, at `/shared/node_modules/…`, version **`4.19.9`** — no nested second copy. That is the repository-lockfile layout you describe as the one in which the pre-fix tip also builds clean.

So this build shows that develop at `78cb3c393` (which carries `b45b69171`) builds under the single-copy layout; it cannot distinguish "the explicit `Router` type removed the error class" from "this layout never produces it". The sentence in our document is corrected accordingly: fixed on develop, proven only in the non-reproducing layout. Leave the ticket where you judge it; nothing on S waits on it.

**BLUF: @stuart.jamieson — your document says this is fixed and proven by a clean rebuild of develop on 19 Oct across 33 services, and asks us to close it. I am not closing it on that, and I would rather tell you exactly why than close it quietly. Could you paste the rebuild evidence here? Then it closes on your measurement rather than on nobody's.**

**Why your claim is not yet this ticket's evidence.** The ticket's acceptance is a clean *image* build of develop. The last work recorded here is explicit that the clean image build **was never run on our side** — the Docker daemon was down on the machine doing the work — and that is still true today: there is no Docker on the machine I am on, so I cannot reproduce your result or contradict it.

**And there is a reason not to assume it.** When the TS2742 failure was examined, it only reproduced when the two nested `@types/express-serve-static-core` copies were pinned to **different** versions. With the repository's own lockfiles both resolve to `4.19.9`, and in that layout **the pre-fix tip builds clean too**. So a green build of develop is consistent with two different worlds: the fix removed the error class, or the lockfile state was never going to produce it. A green build alone does not distinguish them, which means closing on "it builds now" could close a ticket whose symptom is still live for anyone whose install hoists differently.

**What would settle it,** and any one of these is enough:

1. The **exact command** you ran (`docker compose build`, a specific Dockerfile target, or something else) and **which develop SHA**.
2. Whether the 33 services were built **from a cold cache** — a warm layer cache can skip the compile step that fails.
3. If you have it, the resolved `@types/express-serve-static-core` versions in the image that built, since that is the variable the failure turns on.

Paste that and I will record it as the evidence and close the ticket against it. If you would rather not spend the time, say so and I will leave it In Progress with this comment as the reason — that is a better outcome than a ticket closed on an unverified claim.

No date, and nothing else is blocked on this.

**PR #1581 is merged to `develop` as `b45b69171b362da0233842cdd14c161c2f9266c2`.** `governance.ts:19` now reads `const router: Router = Router();`. Nothing deployed; the ticket stays In Progress.

**What gate H2 showed about TS2742 — stated exactly, because it decides whether this ticket's symptom is closed.** H2 reproduced TS2742 **without Docker**, but **only by pinning the two nested `@types/express-serve-static-core` copies to DIFFERENT versions**: in that layout the tip fails and this head builds clean, so **the change removes that error class**. **With the repository's real lockfiles both copies are `4.19.9` and the tip builds clean too.** So whether the ticket's original image-build failure is closed stays **"not reproduced with the real lockfiles"**. The clean `docker compose build governance` was not run (no Docker daemon in my environment) — that remains the real check, e.g. at the next governance deploy.

**Low note from H2:** the new `ks1387` suite goes red if a trailing comment is ever added to the declaration line (it matches the line literally).

**Evidence on the tree that landed** (predicted commit `4a87bcb052fa`, tree `f33b620c79e8` — byte-identical to the PR head's own tree, develop having not moved since the gate), in two environments: the new suite **3/3**; governance in full **119/119**; `tsc` (TypeScript 5.9.3) rc 0. Five-point read 5/5 TRUE.

**Raised as PR #1581**, head `6b4bcaec11fa4aea156a11bbaa23b56b09126b63`, on develop `385fc288fae8`. Not merged, not deployed.

`services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts:19` — `const router: Router = Router();`. Byte-checked: the applied file differs from the tip **only on that line** (the Spark patch's blank-line churn around it is a no-op; lines 18 and 20 are byte-identical).

**This ticket's own symptom is NOT reproduced, and I want that to be plain.** The clean image build was **not run** — the Docker daemon is down here. Governance's local `npm run build` is rc 0 **at the tip as well as with the change**, because this install hoists `@types/express-serve-static-core` to the root and has no copy nested under `packages/shared` — the layout that triggers TS2742. So a local pass is **not** evidence the image build is fixed. The real check is `docker compose build governance` from a clean cache; worth running at the next governance deploy.

Evidence (mine): red-first **2/1** (the annotation cell); green **3/3**; governance in full **119/119**; `tsc` rc 0; push preflight 13/16, nothing failed.

Clean build confirmed, 2 Oct. `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=3 ./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild` at develop `88e8877a2`: **35 of 35 services built, 0 failed**, including `governance`, `analytics` and `billing`; the stack came up with 33 containers running (32 with a healthcheck, all healthy) and the two one-shot jobs (`migrations`, `demo-overlay`) exited 0; gateway `/health` and `/health/deep` both 200. The first pass was cut off by my session's time limit at service 32 during a slow package download, so the last four were built on a second pass with the first 31 from cache — no service failed in either pass.

The fault this ticket records is gone (fixed by KS-1380, `6cf5c3629`). Safe to close from the Platform-S side.

One thing worth knowing for slot users: before the rebuild, slot 3 started in under a minute on images dated 15 Sep while its owner marker read `develop @ 88e8877a2`. The marker records the checkout, not what the images were built from.

Re-read at develop `88e8877a2` (2 Oct): KS-1380's fix has merged (`6cf5c3629`), and `services/analytics`, `services/billing`, `services/governance` and `packages/shared` now all lock `@types/express-serve-static-core` 4.19.9 and `@types/pg` 8.23.1. That removes the cause recorded here. I have not re-run the clean image build, so this is from the lock files only; the ticket can close once one clean build of those three services is confirmed.

Definitive list, every service built one at a time from `0aa9b52c6` with Docker's disk cleared: **three fail** — `governance` (TS2742), `analytics` (TS2742 ×4) and `billing` (`src/db.ts:45` TS2345, the `@types/pg` `Pool` from `/app` vs `/shared`); the other 20 images build cleanly. None of the three is on Platform-S's path, so for the PR #889 gate run I tagged the 28 Sep 08:43 slot-1 images as the slot-4 images for exactly those three and built everything else fresh — recorded on the run so the evidence says which K each service ran.

It is wider than governance. Building every service for a fresh slot one at a time (2026-09-29, `0aa9b52c6`), so far:

* `analytics` — `npm run build`: TS2742 on `app` (`src/index.ts:34`), `router` (`src/routes/analytics.ts:20`), `dashboardRouter` (`src/routes/dashboard.ts:12`), `healthRouter` (`src/routes/health.ts:7`) — all "cannot be named without a reference to `@secuura/shared/node_modules/@types/express-serve-static-core`".
* another service in the same pass — `src/db.ts:45`: TS2345 `import("/app/node_modules/@types/pg").Pool` is not assignable to `import("/shared/node_modules/@types/pg").Pool` — the same shape: `/shared` (built from `packages/shared` inside the image) carries its own `@types/*` that no longer match the service's.
* `nft-certificate` and `transfer` failed once each for a different reason (Docker's disk was full mid-build: `chmod: … No space left on device`); both build after reclaiming space, so they are not part of this.

Two observations for whoever picks it up: (1) the images that exist on this machine from a 28 Sep 08:43 build are fine, and the only 29 Sep commit touching dependencies is KS-1378 (`2cb858335`, morgan / nodemailer / ip-address / undici bumps) — a duplicate-`@types` drift between `packages/shared` and the services is the shape a lockfile bump produces; (2) `Blockchain/Dev/.dockerignore` excludes `node_modules` and `services/*/node_modules` but not `packages/shared/node_modules`, so a host that has run `npm install` inside `packages/shared` would ship that directory into the `COPY packages/shared/ ./` layer — not the case on this machine, but it is a second way to get exactly this error. The full per-service list follows when the loop finishes.

title: KS-1175 follow-on: the anchors K emits for share / transfer-custody / lifecycle-events carry no documentType and drop Platform-S's identity block — only originate and the flat anchor anchor identity
description:
## Found by

The S↔K compatibility review of 2026-09-29 (platform-k `0aa9b52c6`, platform-s `477eb57`).

## The gap

[KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) (merged `cbae988db`, `910687394`) accepts the `identity` block on `POST /api/anchors` and anchors it beside `documentType` / `occurredAt` (`services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts:128-151, 261-315`). Platform-S sends that block on **every** write once `CardanoAnchor:AnchorIdentity` is on — flat anchors, originate, version, certifications, share, transfer-custody and lifecycle-events (`ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.cs:1606-1631`).

On K, three of those routes never carry it to the anchor:

* `POST /api/documents/{id}/lifecycle-events` reads only `action` and `payload`; an `identity` key in the body is ignored (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:2440-2545`).
* `POST /{id}/share` and `POST /{id}/transfer-custody` likewise.
* All three anchor through `emitLifecycleAnchor`, whose body is `{documentId, contentHash, network}` — no `metadata.documentType`, no `identity` (`documents.ts:1275-1297`).

Result: for every non-mutating verb (delete, share-revoke, the share-\* edits, rights-unassign, note, certified, verified, share, rights-assign/reassign) the chain record has no verb and no actor/organisation identity, whatever S sends. Only `upload` (originate) and the flat-anchor fallback carry them.

## Ask

1. Carry `identity` (and the verb as `metadata.documentType`) from the share / transfer-custody / lifecycle-events request bodies into the `emitLifecycleAnchor` call, so the anchor records them — subject to the per-document-anchor ruling on the companion ticket (a reset row would not keep them anyway).
2. Declare `identity` on `DocumentShareRequest`, `TransferCustodyRequest` and `LifecycleEventRequest` in `originate.openapi.ts` so S's [PS-614](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-614/check-ss-verb-vocabulary-against-platform-ks-openapi-enum-at-gate-time) gate can see it (today S's `k_openapi_vocabulary.test.ts` only checks `onBehalfOf` placement).
3. Echo what was anchored on the lifecycle-event response, so S's read-back ([PS-870](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-870/6-send-the-identity-record-to-platform-k-on-every-anchored-verb) item 5) works on these verbs too.

## Verify

Paired slot with `AnchorIdentity=true` on S: a `share-revoke` on an originated document → the anchor read (`GET /api/anchors/{id}`) returns `identity.actorDid` and `metadata.documentType = share-revoke`. Today it returns neither.

Related: [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss), [PS-870](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-870/6-send-the-identity-record-to-platform-k-on-every-anchored-verb), [PS-864](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-864/epic-id-status-stored-and-shown-throughout-the-system-actor-and), the [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one) companion ticket (one anchor per document).

nodes.body:

title: One anchor row per (document_id, network): a repeat POST /api/anchors resets the existing row to pending and nulls its transaction hash — so Platform-S's per-event anchoring collapses to one anchor per document (PS-895 companion)
description:
## Found by

The S↔K compatibility review of 2026-09-29 (platform-s `477eb57`, platform-k `0aa9b52c6`; origin/develop `b4461d1e2` is three commits ahead, none touching this). Companion to [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one), which asked the question from the S side after seeing six lifecycle events on one document share one External Ref, and one on-chain transaction for register + declare on dev-ps.

## What the code does

`dbPersistAnchor` upserts on the composite key and rewrites the chain columns from the **new** request:

```
services/anchoring/src/index.ts:1334-1372
  INSERT INTO anchor_store (...)
  ON CONFLICT (document_id, network) DO UPDATE SET
    status = EXCLUDED.status, transaction_hash = EXCLUDED.transaction_hash,
    block_hash/block_number/slot/fee/confirmations/confirmed_at = EXCLUDED.…,
    error_message, retry_count, simulated, updated_at = EXCLUDED.…
  RETURNING id
```

`metadata_payload` and `content_hash` are **not** in the update list, so the first event's label and hash stay on the row. Every `POST /api/anchors` builds the anchor with `status: 'pending'` and a null hash (`index.ts:463-560`), so on a conflict the existing row goes back to `pending` with `transaction_hash = NULL`, and `processAnchor(persistedId)` runs again (`:535`).

K's own share, transfer-custody, revoke and lifecycle-event routes all go through `emitLifecycleAnchor`, which posts only `{documentId, contentHash, network}` to that same flat endpoint (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1275-1297`). So every non-mutating verb S records re-enters the same row for the document.

Migration 031 records the one-row-per-(document, network) decision. `anchorSubmission.ts:383-386` (guard 1) reads the row's `transaction_hash` to avoid a second fee-paying transaction — the upsert has just nulled it.

## What this means for the S↔K contract

* Platform-S's user-facing promise (`docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §1, §7) is that every declare, sign and share event is anchored. K anchors **one row per document version per network**; later events reset and re-process it.
* For every verb S routes through `/lifecycle-events`, `/share` or `/transfer-custody`, the chain record carries **no** `documentType` **and no** `identity` — `emitLifecycleAnchor` sends neither, and the lifecycle-events handler reads only `action` and `payload` (`documents.ts:2440-2545`). That is a [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) gap; filed separately.

## Decisions needed (Kamil)

1. Is one anchor per (document, network) the intended contract? A later retry that finds any anchor for the document, confirmed or failed, answers 409 and does not submit again, so an anchor that landed late is never paid for twice. Only a retry that finds no anchor at all, after the claim has run out, may submit. A revoked or already-confirmed document is also refused at the last check before submitting.
