**Thanks, Stuart. Our approach for KS-1384, in two stages. No date yet: we will update this ticket as each stage makes progress.**

**Stage 1: make today's one-anchor-per-document model safe (in build now).**
- The reconciler stops giving up too early: it judges a row by its last update, not its creation time, and it no longer fails a row because the chain provider was unreachable (KS-1808, KS-1810).
- Anchoring stops a refused or retried event from paying twice or getting stuck: every attempt anchoring makes for the same request spends the same wallet coin, so at most one of them can land on chain.
- A sweep ends a stranded row honestly as `failed` instead of leaving it pending, and never mints.
- The retry route checks anchoring's own row first: an attempt still in flight answers 409 and nothing new is posted.
- The reconciler change can ship on its own; the other three deploy together on each box, after a wallet check.

**Stage 2: one anchor per lifecycle event (the fix for what you describe above).**
- Each event (upload, version, share, transfer, and so on) gets its own anchor row and its own transaction, so S can name the transaction for each event rather than the document's first one.
- This needs a database migration and a backfill, and it follows stage 1.

**On your verify observation** (verify-by-hash reporting an anchor id as confirmed while that id's own row reads failed with a different transaction): noted, and tracked as KS-1809.

**Document `deb6d3c3-…`'s outcome, seen from S: the two verify calls at 08:56:52 UTC on 29 Oct were S's own. They left S's share and transfer rows claiming the upload's transaction.**

This answers KS-772's "who sent the calls is not measured" (Kamil, 09:09 UTC).

- **The calls.** At 08:56:14 UTC K marked `anchor_c09c1b1f-…` failed. On its next tick S's refresher read "failed" for rows 108 (share) and 109 (rights-assign). For each row it ran its PS-577 corroboration: `VerifyByHashAsync(ContentHash)`, which is `POST /api/verification/verify` with the document's hash. Two rows gave two calls, 22 ms apart. S stamped the rows at 08:56:52.93 and 08:56:52.95 UTC (dev-ps `DocumentTransaction.AnchorConfirmedAt`).
- **What K answered.** Your note says verify healed the document to `confirmed` against `b1cc72f9…` and named the same anchor id, `anchor_c09c1b1f-…`. S only overturns a "failed" when verify names *that* anchor id, says it is anchored and not simulated, and gives a real 64-hex transaction (`CardanoAnchorRefresher.CorroboratesAnchor`). All four held, so both rows now carry `b1cc72f9…`, block 4801203.
- **Why that is wrong.** On preview, `b1cc72f9…`'s metadata (label 674) is the upload: type `document`, hash `00cf73f4…`. Neither the share nor the transfer is on chain, yet S shows both as confirmed by the upload's transaction. Meanwhile the anchor row they point at reads `failed` with `e1df3f61…`. Verify answered for the *document* and used the *anchor's* id, and under the one-row-per-(document, network) upsert those two are not the same thing.
- **The same shape on demo-pk, by the ordinary poll.** uat-ps document 18, 29 Oct from 05:53 UTC: the sign-cert version, certified, share and share-attach-consent all got `anchor_50fa7aab-…`, and all four S rows carry `77363baf…`, block 4804071. On chain that transaction is the version alone: type `document`, hash `466fc0b5…`, documentId `doc-1793253222231-45177f17`.

Both are what this ticket predicted: one anchor per document means S can't name a transaction for each event. Per-event anchors (option (a), ruled 9 Oct) remain the fix on K's side. On S's side we will stop crediting the shared transaction to the later rows; that is tracked under PS-895. Nothing is asked of K beyond a date for per-event anchors. One observation for the design review: verify-by-hash should not report an anchor id as confirmed when that id's own row reads failed with a different transaction.

**Live evidence, 28 Oct 2026: dev-ps S (develop `c07be07`, image built 27 Oct 08:23 UTC) ↔ Kintsugi K `061c3a4f6`.**

stuart@obeden.com (Entra-verified) uploaded one document, shared it, then assigned its rights. S sent each action to its own K route, and K returned **the same anchor id for the share and the transfer**.

| S row | S doc | Action | Added (UTC) | K route | Ref K returned | Confirmed? (09:19 UTC) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 107 | 19 | upload | 08:55:20 | `POST /api/documents` (originate, auto-anchor) | `deb6d3c3-1d79-4993-82a1-7a49a75aae00` (K document id) | **no** |
| 108 | 19 | share → iss3@lhsg.com | 08:55:45 | `POST /{deb6d3c3…}/share` | `anchor_c09c1b1f-c639-49e3-8afc-f1fb31906732` | **no** |
| 109 | 19 | rights-assign → iss2@lhsg.com | 08:56:02 | `POST /{deb6d3c3…}/transfer-custody` | `anchor_c09c1b1f-c639-49e3-8afc-f1fb31906732` (**same**) | **no** |
| 110 | 20 | upload (control: no later action) | 08:56:47 | `POST /api/documents` | `4c3e74b0-5319-4746-885e-dcd82c2ef08d` | **yes**: tx `43549e9a3f0ba36ba4a91ddd6d80a03650d3373e4ee264d486fb7d96ed3018be`, preview block 4801208, within ~4 min |

S app log, verbatim apart from trimming:
- `tx 84c4d91e… 'share' → share ref anchor_c09c1b1f-… (parent deb6d3c3-…)`
- `tx 20b5a812… 'rights-assign' → transfer-custody ref anchor_c09c1b1f-… (parent deb6d3c3-…)`
- After that, every refresher tick logs `status poll made 2 platform-k read(s) for 3 row(s) — 1 answered by a read already made this tick`. The two rows share one ref, so one read answers both.

**What this shows**
1. **One anchor per (document, network), confirmed live.** `/share` and `/transfer-custody` both go through `emitLifecycleAnchor` → `POST /api/anchors` → `dbPersistAnchor`'s `ON CONFLICT (document_id, network)` and return the existing row's id (`services/anchoring/src/index.ts`, the KS-281 upsert, at `061c3a4f6`). S therefore has no separate on-chain reference for the transfer.
2. **The reset holds the document unconfirmed.** Document 20, with nothing after its upload, confirmed in about 4 minutes. All three rows on document 19 are still unconfirmed **23 minutes** after the last action. That fits the description: each repeat resets the row to `pending` with `transaction_hash` NULL and re-processes it. I have not verified from K's side whether the upload's own transaction was submitted and then overwritten, or never submitted.

**Not verified (needs K data, Kamil):** for `anchor_store` where `document_id = 'deb6d3c3-1d79-4993-82a1-7a49a75aae00'` on preprod/preview, please give:
- the row's current `status`, `transaction_hash` and `retry_count`;
- how many Cardano transactions anchoring submitted for that document between 08:55 and 09:20 UTC (question 3 above: did the reset mint a second fee-paying transaction?).

**For S, if one-anchor-per-document is the intended contract (decision 1):** S needs to change. Today it shows one tick per action and records the share and the transfer under one ref. When the row eventually confirms, both rows will be stamped with whatever transaction the row last carried, so the earlier action is attributed to the later action's transaction. That is the KS-1119 / KS-1561 false-attribution shape on the S side. It is PS-895's question, now answered live.

Will add the final state when the rows confirm or park.

**Kam has ruled: design now, merge after the Kintsugi round lands.**

Kam's words, verbatim:

> Design now, merge after the Kintsugi round lands

Card `secuura-ks1384-schedule-per-event-anchors-1019`, option **(b)**. Ruled on the live board 2026-10-19 between 18:22 and 18:23 AEDT; recorded 18:28.

What that means for this multi-PR project:

- **Design work may start now.** No merge to `develop` until the Kintsugi round has landed.
- Per the card, the small **interim ownership check** on the flat-anchor route goes ahead now, on its own, and is not held behind this project — that is **KS-1603**, already in flight on its own seat.

**Nothing is built or merged by this comment.** This records the ruling and the sequencing.

**BLUF: @stuart.jamieson — Kam ruled the shape of this on 2026-10-09: option (a), one anchor per lifecycle event. That ruling never reached this ticket, which is why your document still records KS-1384 as unruled. That is our miss. The shape is settled and it is the one you prefer. WHEN the work starts is still with Kam — a card is on his panel today. No date.**

## Kam's ruling, 2026-10-09 10:06:00 AEDT

Option (a), verbatim:

> One anchor per lifecycle event

So the structural answer is the one you have argued for on both this ticket and KS-1612 — a row per event rather than one row per `(document_id, network)` — and not a narrower guard on the existing single row.

## What is ruled, and what is not

**Ruled:** the target shape. One anchor row per lifecycle event, which is also what removes the overwrite you had to word around in PS-1285 and closes KS-1603's exposure for good rather than guarding it.

**Not ruled:** when it starts. This is a multi-PR project, not a patch — a migration and backfill on the live anchor table with three source rules, five code writers to bind to the tenant, six SQL files and two services (the sizing is in `4384fa9a` on this ticket). Scheduling work of that size against a deploy round that is already queued is Kam's call, and it is in front of him now.

**Deliberately not stated:** a start date or a landing date. Anything merged to `develop` rides the next deploy round, and that round has conditions outside our control.

## Your measurement is recorded and it holds

Your `750da63c` of 2026-10-18 answers the one residual the round-3 write-up left open — whether an id chosen outside K is predictable enough to be squatted. At S develop `7cb1a4e`: a fresh v4 GUID per ledger row from `Guid.NewGuid()` in `TransactionService.BuildBaseTransaction`, 122 bits from the platform CSPRNG, no counter and no time component, and never known outside S before the anchor exists. We are not treating that as an open risk.

## Interim

The small ownership check on the flat-anchor route (KS-1603) is tracked separately and does not wait on this project. If Kam schedules KS-1384 to start now, that check is subsumed; if he holds the project, the check still protects your existing rows. Either way nothing is being asked of you here.

@kamil.kreiser — on the "reverse order" residual you record above ("an id chosen outside K, such as S's hyphenated ledger chain id on a flat anchor, is only as unpredictable as its source, which K cannot measure"): the S measurement, at S develop `7cb1a4e`.

- **The id is a fresh v4 GUID per ledger row**: `Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")` in `TransactionService.BuildBaseTransaction`, hyphenated for the wire (`ToHyphenatedGuid`). 122 random bits from the platform CSPRNG, no counter, no time component, no derivation from the document or the organisation.
- **It is never known outside S before the anchor exists.** S writes the row and dispatches the anchor in the same request (`TryAnchorAsync`) or on the refresher's next tick (≤ 30 s locally); the id is visible only inside S, to signed-in members of the owning organisation, on pages that render after the row is written. It is not in any S email, share link or public URL.
- So pre-registering a `documents` row under one of S's flat-anchor ids requires guessing a v4 GUID inside a window of seconds. For S's ids the "reverse order" residual is theoretical; migration 051's forward refusal covers the case that matters for S.

That does not change S's preference (this ticket's tenant column is still the answer that needs no reasoning about id entropy), but it lets you record the S source as measured rather than unmeasurable. The S flat-anchor write site is the one you list as unguarded, `originate/src/routes/anchors.ts:109` via `POST /api/anchors/` — S sends it only under the owner organisation's connector key, for its own rows, one id per event.

**BLUF: #1568 round 3 did NOT take this, and the reason is scope, not merit. Platform S prefers it, I agree it is the structural answer, and it should be planned as its own piece of work rather than squeezed into a review round.**

**Stuart's position, from his KS-1612 comment of 2026-10-18T11:42:31Z, verbatim:** *"S's preference is unchanged: (iii) KS-1384, one anchor row per event with a tenant column, which also removes the overwrite S had to word around in PS-1285."*

**Why round 3 took the smaller option instead.** Kam allowed #1568 exactly one more round (card `secuura-ks1612-third-round-after-cap-1018` = (a); a further NO GO stops for him). Round 3 therefore closes the round-2 gate's MAJ-A with one predicate — migration 051, which refuses a `documents` row that claims an id an `anchor_store` row already holds and that no document owns. Ruled by Wednesday 2026-10-18T20:14:35Z.

**What this ticket is, as sized against the writer census I ran at develop `83ed01af70fd5ed6cca9ac66f28ddcb8a1034105`:**

* a hot-table migration on `anchor_store` plus a backfill with **three distinct source rules** — document anchors from `documents`, certification anchors from `documents.id`, and orphan/flat anchors that have **no recorded first caller at all** (→ NULL → correctly frozen against cross-tenant updates);
* **every writer must bind the tenant** — there are five: `anchoring/src/index.ts:1372` (the main upsert), `anchoring/src/index.ts:1755`, `anchoring/src/anchorStatusUpdate.ts:114`, `originate/src/routes/anchors.ts:109` (unguarded), `demo-service/src/seed/index.ts:162`; plus six migration/init writers (001, 003, 007, 031, `docker/init/06-consolidate-anchors.sql`, `deployment/azure/migrate/init.sql`);
* a new refusal path in the upsert's `DO UPDATE` (`WHERE anchor_store.tenant_id = EXCLUDED.tenant_id`, NULL-tenant legacy rows refused — fail closed);
* and the guard's per-organisation rule still needed **on top**, because a single-tenant box puts two organisations in one tenant.

That is multiple PRs across two services, a seed and six SQL files — not a round.

**What it would close that 051 does not.** KS-1603 (the unconditional columns on both upserts). The **reverse order** residual 051 names: 051 refuses a document claiming an id an anchor already holds, but cannot stop a document being pre-registered under an id that can be *predicted* before the anchor exists — and an id chosen outside K, such as S's hyphenated ledger chain id on a flat anchor, is only as unpredictable as its source, which K cannot measure. With a tenant column the anchor row carries its own owner and none of this is inferred from `documents` at all.

*Seat J 13th. Nothing deployed. Related: KS-1612, KS-1603, KS-1630.*

A live example from dev-ps against Kintsugi, for whoever rules on this.

dev-ps app log, 30 Sep 2026 09:49:47 UTC (S build `277bd43`, Kintsugi on develop's 28 Sep spec):

```
CardanoAnchor: tx 31136770… 'sign-cert' → K version doc-1790761787089-b7cbe588 anchored anchor_1199917f-ce48-498d-9f08-ace579037e1d
CardanoAnchor: tx a8950073… 'certified' → lifecycle-event ref anchor_1199917f-ce48-498d-9f08-ace579037e1d (parent doc-1790761787089-b7cbe588)
```

Two distinct S ledger events, 27 ms apart, came back with the same anchor id. That is the upsert described above, unchanged at develop `88e8877a2` (`services/anchoring/src/index.ts:1359`, `services/originate/src/routes/anchors.ts:121`). I have not read the row's status or transaction hash back from Kintsugi, so what the second call did to the first anchor's chain record is still unmeasured.

title: Slot-1 URLs outside KS-1355's four spots: m365's Entra redirect URI defaults to :6882 (compose + three code fallbacks), bootstrap leaves FRONTEND_URL / CORS_ORIGINS / LLM_BASE_URL at slot 1, 20 service .env.examples and two smoke scripts pin slot 1, and dead VITE_* compose values name :6882
description:
## BLUF

On a slot-N stack, **platform-k's M365 integration builds its Entra OAuth redirect URI on slot 1's gateway** (`http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback`) unless someone sets `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` by hand — the compose default and three fallbacks in `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts` all name `:6882`. And `bootstrap-env.sh` **derives only** `DATABASE_URL` **/** `REDIS_URL` **per slot**, so a fresh slot-N `.env` keeps slot 1's `FRONTEND_URL`, has no gateway origin in `CORS_ORIGINS`, and keeps `LLM_BASE_URL` on slot 1's Ollama — all three had to be edited by hand on slot 2 today. This is the remainder after [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (compose `FRONTEND_URL` / `CORS_ORIGINS` defaults, `preflight.sh:94`, `start-local.sh`, `dev-reload.sh` — excluded here). Slots are dynamic; each value should derive from `stack_env.sh`'s exported ports.

## The spots (platform-k `develop` `0aa9b52c6`, tracked files, re-read line by line 29 Sep)

**Runtime — the M365 callback points at slot 1**

| File:line | Value |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:888` | `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI=${ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI:-http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback}` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:481, 595` | `process.env.ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI \|\| \`${process.env.FRONTEND_URL || '[http://localhost:6882](<http://localhost:6882>)'}/api/m365/callback\`\` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:993` | `… \|\| 'http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback'` |

**Bootstrap — derives two URLs per slot, not the rest** (`scripts/bootstrap-env.sh:229` `DATABASE_URL`, `:240` `REDIS_URL`; nothing writes these)

| Template (`env.example` is canonical since [KS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1081/config-drift-two-tracked-env-templates-disagree-by-39-vars-bootstrap); `.env.example` is its fallback) | Key | Slot-1 value |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/env.example:146` | `CORS_ORIGINS` | `:6100–:6102` only — no gateway / website origin on any slot |
| `Blockchain/Dev/env.example:372` | `LLM_BASE_URL` | `:11434` (Ollama is offset per slot in `stack_env.sh`) |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local.example:117` | `FRONTEND_URL` | `:6882` (lines 23–63 also document every social-login callback on `:6882`) |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example:92, 95, 190` (fallback template) | `FRONTEND_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS` | `:6882`, `:6881` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/*/.env.example`, `services/billing/env.example` — **20 files** | `DATABASE_URL` `:6432`, `REDIS_URL` `:6379`; api-gateway `CORS_ORIGINS`; m365 `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI`; billing `API_GATEWAY_URL` | slot 1 |

**Scripts — default to slot 1**

| File:line |  |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/auth-matrix-smoke.sh:31` | `API_URL="${API_URL:-http://localhost:6882}"` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh:15` | `GATEWAY="http://localhost:6882"` — no override |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/setup-dev-environment.sh:323–324`, `start-environment.sh:241` | print slot-1 URLs whatever the slot (display only) |

**Dead config — inert, but a slot-1 literal that reads as live**

`Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:1841, 1876, 1910–1912` set `VITE_API_URL` / `VITE_ORIGINATE_URL` / `VITE_ANALYTICS_URL` to `http://localhost:6882/…` in the issuer, verifier and admin frontends' **runtime** `environment:`. Those images are static Vite builds (`RUN npm run build`, then nginx — `frontend/{issuer,verifier,admin}/Dockerfile`), `import.meta.env.VITE_*` is fixed at build time, and no build arg or `.env` supplies it, so the bundles use their relative `'/api'` fallback — correct on every slot. The values are never read; delete them so nobody takes them as the source of truth.

## Fix shape (Kamil's call)

Pass `GATEWAY_PORT` into compose for `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` and drop the three `:6882` fallbacks in m365 (fail if neither `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` nor `FRONTEND_URL` is set); have `bootstrap-env.sh` write `FRONTEND_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS` (gateway + website origins) and `LLM_BASE_URL` from `stack_env.sh` as it does `DATABASE_URL`; source `stack_env.sh` in the two smoke scripts; remove the dead `VITE_*` lines. [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s proposed `check-stack-safety.sh` pin could take a "no literal slot port outside `stack_env.sh`" rule to hold all of it.

## Acceptance — comprehensive slot unit tests in the same PR

Slots are dynamic: a developer picks, drops and re-picks them at will, several sessions share one host, and slot numbers are never fixed. A value right for the slot it was checked on is wrong on every other — and the failure is silent (a request lands on someone else's stack, or an OAuth callback on the wrong gateway). That makes this a high-risk area, so the PR is not done without unit tests that prove every changed value **for every slot 1..4, not only slot 1 or the slot the author used**:

* `scripts/__tests__/bootstrap_env_slot_ports.test.sh` extended: for `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` = 1, 2, 3, 4, a fresh bootstrap writes `FRONTEND_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS` (gateway + website origins) and `LLM_BASE_URL` on that slot's ports from `stack_env.sh` — and no other slot's port appears in the output.
* A render test (`docker compose config` per slot) asserting `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` resolves to that slot's gateway, and a unit test that `services/m365-integration` has no `:6882` fallback left (no-`ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI`, no-`FRONTEND_URL` case refuses rather than defaulting).
* The two smoke scripts target the named slot's gateway for 1..4 and refuse locally when no slot is named.
* A static guard (e.g. in `check-stack-safety.sh`) failing on any literal published port of ANY slot 1..4 outside `stack_env.sh` — bite-checked: plant one, see it red, remove it.
* Tests are hermetic: run unslotted AND under each slot's environment with identical results (the offline-suite rule), never spawned with the shell's slot variables leaking in.

## Not in this ticket

[KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s four spots. `Blockchain/Testing/**` `TARGET_BASE` defaults → [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default) (the Internal Audit Harness, Kamil). The build break → [KS-1380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1380/develop-does-not-build-since-ks-1378-1339-analytics-billing-and). `docker-compose.production.yml` (deployed, not slotted).

## Correction history

First filed 29 Sep 08:29 UTC with the `VITE_*` values as the headline ("the frontends call slot 1's gateway"). Re-checked against the Dockerfiles the same morning: they are build-time variables never supplied at build, so that claim was wrong and is now listed as dead config; the template counts and canonical-template references were also corrected.

## Environment

Peter's Mac, fresh K worktree at `0aa9b52c6`, slot 2, 29 Sep 2026. Found while pairing platform-k slot 2 for the platform-s [PS-914](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-914/data-testid-coverage-audit-scan-every-page-and-ui-element-razor-views) run.

## Shared acceptance — slot derivation group (added 6 Oct 2026)

This ticket is one of five platform-k tickets that must all take slot values from `stack_env.sh` and never fall back to slot 1: [KS-1355](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355>), [KS-1381](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381>), [KS-1389](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389>), [KS-1382](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382>), [KS-1162](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162>). None of them is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance above:

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
5. **Tests cover every slot.** Slots 1–4, hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

**This ticket's part:** points 1, 2 and 5 — the static guard in this ticket's acceptance is the point-1 guard, shared with [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s `docker-compose.yml` pin (both tickets edit that file), and the two smoke scripts follow point 2.

nodes.body: Delivered: KS-1355's PR 1526 (af2366e7e), the only change linked here, is in the kintsugi deploy b1fb543640e7 (2026-11-01); it created the shared guard scripts/check-stack-safety.sh that this ticket's acceptance says it extends. Verified by code read at b1fb543640e7, not run. Left open: this ticket's own items are still in the tree. services/m365-integration/src/index.ts has 6 lines naming http://localhost:6882 (the FRONTEND_URL fallbacks and the ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI fallback at line 650), docker-compose.yml:898 still defaults ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI to http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback, the VITE_API_URL values at docker-compose.yml:1861, :1896 and :1930 still name :6882, and two service .env.example files (api-gateway, m365-integration) still name 6882, the same count as before PR 1526. No commit under this key changes them.

## The slot-derivation group's shared static guard now EXISTS — created by KS-1355, and this ticket extends it

Facts only, from the KS-1355 build (Seat K 8th, 2026-10-13). KS-1355 is the first of the five to
land, so by this ticket's own acceptance point 1 — *"the first ticket to land creates it; the
others extend it; nobody adds a second guard"* — it created the guard.

**Where it is:** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-stack-safety.sh`, section **3c**. The file went
from 100 to 105 invariants.

**Its scope is deliberately NARROW, and stated in the guard itself:** scripts that run the
**platform** compose stack with `up` / `run` / `restart` / `down`. It does **not** yet cover the
env templates, the 20 service `.env.example` files or the two smoke scripts this ticket lists.
**That widening is KS-1381's**, and the guard's own comment says so by name. Do not add a second
guard.

**What it asserts today:**
- Every declared platform launcher sources `stack_env.sh` — `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh`,
  `Blockchain/Dev/stop-secuura.sh`, `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/start-local.sh`. It replaced a
  `for f in "$START" "$STOP"` loop that covered two of them, which is how `start-local.sh`
  brought the platform stack up slot-blind with the gate green.
- `LAUNCHER_EXCEPTIONS` — each entry `path|reason`, with a ticket. Current entries:
  `start-environment.sh` and `stop-environment.sh` (**KS-1550**), `observability.sh` (KS-200,
  standalone stack), and two Akto side-stack scripts.
- A **census**: a NEW tracked script that runs the platform compose and is in neither list fails
  the gate.
- Both directions of the list: an exception that is **no longer** a launcher is reported stale,
  and an exception with **no reason** is refused.

**Measurement worth having before you extend it:** a naive text match for a compose
`up|run|restart|down` hits **19** tracked `.sh`, of which **7 are false positives** — the only
mention is a comment or a line that *prints* a compose command to the operator
(`check-slot-credentials.sh`, `setup-dev-environment.sh`, `stack_guard.sh`,
`verify-slot-credential-isolation.sh`, `systemTest/__tests__/slot_target.test.sh`, and two Akto
scripts). Filtering comments and printer lines (`echo`/`printf`/`say`/`print_info`/…) gives the
real candidate set of **8**. An exception list padded with false positives is one nobody reads.
The detector lives in the guard; a copy is at
`5_Project_History/2026-10-13_seatK-8th/tampers/detect2.sh`.

## This ticket's "Dead config" section is CONFIRMED by independent measurement

Measured during the KS-1355 build **before** reading this ticket, and it agrees with what is
written here — so both readings are controls on each other:

- The issuer, verifier and admin images build in stage 1 (`RUN npm run build`) and stage 2 is
  nginx serving static `dist/`.
- **No** frontend Dockerfile declares an `ARG` or `ENV` for any `VITE_*` — zero matches across
  `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/*/Dockerfile`.
- Source reads `VITE_API_URL` in **10** files, `VITE_ORIGINATE_URL` in **2**, and
  `VITE_ANALYTICS_URL` in **ZERO**.

So the five values are dead config, as this ticket says. KS-1355 did **not** touch them: they are
**named exceptions** in both of its guards, each carrying KS-1381 as the reason, so they stay
visible rather than silently tolerated. No duplicate ticket was filed.

## Also relevant to this ticket's acceptance

- **`env.example:146`** (this ticket's bootstrap table) **is done** — KS-1355 commented it out
  with a pointer to `docker-compose.yml:503`, whose default now derives from `GATEWAY_PORT` /
  `WEBSITE_PORT` and also carries the `:6103` origin the old line omitted. Measured on the way:
  `bootstrap-env.sh` really did copy that line into a generated slot-2 `.env`, so it was a live
  defect and not only a template smell.
- **Group point 3** (one preflight change): KS-1355 did spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`. **KS-1389's
  leg 13 is not built**, so there were no KS-1389 checks to re-run; whichever lands second
  re-runs the other's.
- **Group point 5** (slots 1–4, hermetic): KS-1355's render proof covers all four slots and
  clears ambient slot variables.


The guard landed in PR https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1526 (KS-1355), head `f0278d3b267b7a09374690810a6a578b71e87b57`.

title: develop does not build since KS-1378 (#1339): analytics, billing and governance images fail `tsc` — packages/shared now locks @types/express-serve-static-core 4.19.9 / @types/pg 8.23.1, those three services still lock 4.19.8 / 8.20.0
description:
## BLUF

A clean build of platform-k `develop` at `0aa9b52c6` fails: `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild` stops with *"Build FAILED for: analytics billing governance — not starting containers"*, so no stack comes up. The previous clean build on this Mac, at `d9ce1403d` (28 Sep), succeeded. Between the two, no `package.json` or Dockerfile of those three services changed; what changed is [KS-1378](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1378/five-new-advisories-block-every-push-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address) **(**[Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1339](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1378-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address-and-undici-off-five-815a0a16d4c7), `2cb858335`**)**, which refreshed `packages/shared/package-lock.json` and several services' locks — but not these three.

## Evidence

`packages/shared/package-lock.json` (top-level `node_modules/@types/*`):

|  | before `2cb858335` | after | `services/analytics` lock at `0aa9b52c6` |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `@types/express-serve-static-core` | 4.19.8 | **4.19.9** | 4.19.8 |
| `@types/pg` | 8.20.0 | **8.23.1** | 8.20.0 |
| `@types/express` | 4.17.25 | 4.17.25 | 4.17.25 |

Each service image copies the built `/shared` (with its own `node_modules`) beside the service's `node_modules`, so `tsc` sees two copies of the same declarations:

```
analytics  src/index.ts(34,7): error TS2742: The inferred type of 'app' cannot be named without a reference to '@secuura/shared/node_modules/@types/express-serve-static-core'. This is likely not portable.
           (also routes/analytics.ts:20, routes/dashboard.ts:12, routes/health.ts:7)
billing    src/db.ts(45,32): error TS2345: Argument of type 'import("/app/node_modules/@types/pg/index").Pool' is not assignable to parameter of type 'import("/shared/node_modules/@types/pg/index").Pool'.
           (plus TS2742 on index.ts:33, routes/billing.ts:26, routes/webhooks.ts:29)
governance same TS2742 family
```

`#1339`'s file list refreshes the locks of queue, security, timestamping, prism and others; `services/analytics`, `services/billing` and `services/governance` are not in it.

**The mismatch is wider than the three that fail (re-checked from every lock at** `0aa9b52c6`**).** Eleven service locks still carry `@types/express-serve-static-core` 4.19.8 / `@types/pg` 8.20.0 against shared's 4.19.9 / 8.23.1: analytics, billing, governance (fail) and **kyc, nft-certificate, referral, staking, tenant-provisioning, tokenisation, transfer, wallet-connector** (built fine in the same run — none of their exported types is inferred across the boundary today, so they are latent, one annotation-less `const app = express()` away from the same error). `services/shared` locks 4.19.8 and `vc-issuer` a third `@types/pg` (8.21.0). At the last good commit `d9ce1403d`, `packages/shared` itself locked 4.19.8 / 8.20.0 — every lock agreed, which is why that build passed. All 35 images were attempted in this run; exactly these three failed.

## Likely fix (Kamil's call)

Refresh the failing three — and the eight latent ones — to the same `@types/express-serve-static-core` / `@types/pg` versions `packages/shared` now pins (or pin those `@types` in shared to what the services use). A check that every service lock agrees with `packages/shared` on the `@types` it re-exports would stop the next bump doing this — [KS-953](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-953/class-editing-api-gatewaysrcindexts-silently-reddens-packagesshared) is the same class (a change in one package silently reddening another).

## Reproduce

```bash
git worktree add --detach <path> origin/develop      # 0aa9b52c6
cd <path> && SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=<N> ./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild
```

## Environment

Peter's Mac, Docker Desktop 8 CPU / 31.3 GiB, fresh K worktree at `0aa9b52c6`, slot 2, 29 Sep 2026 \~09:25–09:50 BST. Found while bringing up a paired K for the platform-s [PS-914](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-914/data-testid-coverage-audit-scan-every-page-and-ui-element-razor-views) gate run. Not caused by that work (no platform-k change on it).

title: PR #1339's standalone locks were re-resolved from bare manifests: ~1,000 non-target moves, incl. runtime bullmq/msgpackr 2 and @azure/identity/msal-node 6
description:
Raised from **gate41's finding N-1339-2** (Major, non-blocking) on PR #1339 (KS-1378, the four-package advisory bump). Wednesday ruled this a ticket rather than a fold-in for round 2, because the only mechanism the gate's own fix-shape offers is `npm install --package-lock-only`, and host npm 11.5.1 dies with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')` on this machine — measured by Seat B 43rd even on a bare `package.json` in an empty temp dir, so it is the host npm build and not the workspace layout.

## What happened

#1339's 13 standalone `package-lock.json` files were regenerated **from their bare manifests** rather than from their committed locks. That resolved every dependency afresh, so about **1,000 versions moved that the bump did not target**. All are inside their declared ranges, so nothing is a range violation — but nothing exercises them either: the suites run from the **root** lock, which moved **0** non-target versions.

## The moves that matter (gate-measured)

* `services/queue`: **bullmq 5.76.2 → 5.81.5**, pulling **msgpackr 1 → 2** — runtime.
* `services/m365-integration` and `packages/shared`: **@azure/identity 4.13.1 → 4.13.3**, pulling **@azure/msal-node 5 → 6** — runtime.
* `services/originate`: minimatch 3 → 10, plus dev-only eslint-cache majors.

## Fix-shape, quoted verbatim from gate41's report

> Fix-shape: regenerate each standalone lock FROM its committed lock (`npm install <pkg>@<ver> --package-lock-only`), or declare the drift and add a standalone-install smoke (build + boot) per service.

## The condition attached to #1339 merging without this

Wednesday's ANSWER to Seat B 44th, 2026-09-29T03:54:40Z: the two runtime moves above **get a clean standalone** `npm ci` **plus that service's own suite in the next gate**, so what ships untested by the root-lock suites is tested once. **Merged is not deployed:** no deploy carries these until this ticket is done or Kam says otherwise.

## Blocked on, and why it is not just "run the command"

`npm install` in any form is unavailable on this host. Seat B 43rd's workaround for #1339 was `node:24-alpine` (npm 11.19.0), mounted at `/src` — **never** `/dev`, which clobbers the container's `/dev/null` and dies rc 127 before starting. Whoever takes this needs either that container route explicitly permitted, or a working host npm.

## Neighbours (cross-reference only)

KS-1290 (an npm command inside a workspace member moves platform discriminators silently) and KS-1154 (the root lock carries only the darwin rollup binary) are the same family — lockfile regeneration doing more than it was asked to — but neither covers this drift.

Discovered 2026-09-29 by gate41 on PR #1339; ticketed by the Platform K build seat under Wednesday's ruling.

title: Security: certifications ends RLS FORCE with no tenant_isolation policy on every fresh database, permanently
description:
**Found by the gate39 QA pass over PR #1332 (N-G39-1, Major). Facts only.**

## What is wrong

On a **fresh bare database**, `public.certifications` ends with row-level security **ENABLED and FORCED but with no** `tenant_isolation` **policy**. RLS with no policy is **default-deny**, so the table is unreadable and unwritable by the application role — and unlike the defect #1332 fixed, **this does not heal on a later boot**. It is permanent for the life of that database.

Measured across all four head paths (gateway runner boot 1 and boot 2, `scripts/run-migrations.sh`, and both combined): identical, `4c59e2ebdc37`. The **merge-base differs** (`fd91b0ab5a48`) and **does** carry `CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON public.certifications` — so the merge-base heals it and the current tip does not. An app-role `INSERT` carrying the tenant GUC is **refused**.

## Why it changed

`migrations/038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` (added in #1332) creates `certifications` **before** 039 runs. 039 then finds the table present and applies its RLS `ENABLE`/`FORCE` block to it — but the branch of 039 that creates the `tenant_isolation` policy does not cover it on that path. Before #1332, `certifications` did not exist when 039 ran, so 039 skipped it entirely and a later boot created it with its policy intact.

## A FALSE CLAIM IN THE MERGED CODE, filed here deliberately rather than separately (N-G39-4)

`038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` lines **16-17** describe this exact condition — `certifications` with RLS forced and no `tenant_isolation` policy — as one of the things the migration **fixes**. **It does not fix it; it is the cause of it.** The same header's claim that the schema equality is "proved … across … the docker/init seeded path" is also **wider than true**: the equality holds for `certifications` only, and fails for `oauth_apps` and `svc_webhooks` because of a pre-existing docker/init DDL difference (extra indexes and the `svc_webhooks_app_id_fkey` foreign key). Both header claims need correcting in the same change that fixes the policy, so the file does not keep asserting a fix it does not deliver.

## Fix shape (from the gate)

A migration numbered **after 039** that applies 039's `tenant_isolation` block to `certifications`, plus a **real-PostgreSQL cell driven as the application role** (`secuura_app`) asserting that an `INSERT` carrying the correct tenant GUC succeeds and one carrying a foreign tenant is refused. A source-text assertion is not sufficient here: the defect is a runtime default-deny, and only a driven app-role probe distinguishes "policy present" from "policy absent but table reachable as owner".

## Scope

Not fixed in #1332 — that PR was round 2 of 2 under the class cap and shipped GO WITH FINDINGS with this as named residue. No board ticket covered it before this one (searched by symbol: `certifications` + `tenant_isolation`, `tenant_isolation policy certifications`, `038a`, `certifications RLS force default-deny`, `certifications no tenant_isolation` — zero title-relevant results; three positive controls each returned their expected ticket first, so the search was working).

Refs KS-1054

- Still there: Blockchain/Dev/migrations/038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql, read at origin/develop 035685291b9d, lines 16 and 17 still say the migration fixes tenant isolation on oauth_apps, svc_webhooks and charge_events and on certifications (RLS forced, no tenant_isolation policy).

Only charge_events, oauth_apps and svc_webhooks have a tenant_id column; certifications has none in either definition, and no ALTER TABLE certifications under Blockchain/Dev/migrations adds one. title: Security: a revoked credential resubmitted with any other id verifies TRUE — neither verify route wires a didResolver, so the proof's id binding is never checked outside production
description:
**BLUF — the gate measured this at runtime on the merged code (gate38 finding N-1330-1, Major). A credential revoked through** `POST /api/credentials/:id/revoke`**, resubmitted with any other** `id`**, answers** `verified: true` **with** `checks.status: true`**.** Measured at the PR head and at the merged END.

This is not a defect of #1330 against its ruling — an edited id *is* an unknown id, and pass-through for unknown ids is the open card's default. It is filed because the measured cost of that default is **wider than the card prices it**.

**The mechanism, as the gate read and drove it:**

* Both revocation resolvers key on the caller-supplied `credential.id`, and the stored-record arm abstains on `found: false` (`services/vc-issuer/src/services/revocationResolvers.ts`; `packages/shared/src/vc/verifier.ts` :478-:484).
* **Neither verify route wires a** `didResolver`, so an Ed25519 proof gets a structural check only unless `NODE_ENV === 'production'` (`verifier.ts` :372-:396, read).
* The proof payload **does** cover `id`, so a wired didResolver would catch the edit.
* In production every Ed25519 credential already fails with `No DID resolver configured…` (pre-existing, read, not driven).

**Why it matters more than the card says.** The card `secuura-ks1352-unknown-credential-id-verify-policy` (open, `ruled_ts` null) prices its option a as "a revoked credential whose record was lost still verifies true" — an accident. The measured behaviour is deliberate and trivial: **any holder of a revoked credential can un-revoke it on a development-mode stack by editing one field.**

**Fix-shape (the gate's, quoted):** "wire the issuer's DID resolver on both verify routes so the proof binds `id` (then an edited id fails signature), or key revocation on a proof-bound value."

**Regression cell (the gate's, quoted):** "revoke R1, submit `{...doc, id: 'urn:x'}`, expect `verified: false`."

**Relation to the shipped work.** #1330 (squash `9caa42ad05f145251db820ba43eaf7941316668f`) is what makes revocation reachable at all; before it, verify consulted no authority. This finding is the remaining hole in the id-keyed approach. The unknown-id policy question itself is KS 1368; this ticket is the measured cost that should inform it.

**Board search before filing, with controls:** `didResolver`, `revocationResolvers`, `id-edit`, `edited id`, `No DID resolver` all returned **0**; the positive control `statusListResolver` on the same literal query shape returned **1** (KS-1352), and a nonsense control returned 0.

The facts this ticket did not hold: a revoked credential resubmitted with another LIVE credential's id also verifies true on both verify routes, and a forged subject also verifies. title: Akto scans are now paced to fit the platform's rate limit — test times went up; which way should we go?
description:
## BLUF

Kamil, when you have a moment: **we need your decision on how the platform's rate limit should treat our Akto scans.** To stop 429s being counted as passes, the scans are now slowed to 1,500 requests/min using Akto's own rate limit (systemTest only, no platform code changed). Coverage is honest, but **pre-merge went from 47 s to 19 m 28 s, and the security tier now takes about an hour.** Six options are below, most of them gateway-side, which is yours. Once we've agreed one, either of us can make the change. **Reducing test coverage is not an option.** Thank you.

+++ What was added, and what it costs (measured)

**The pacing** ([KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and) branch; [KS-709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-709/akto-reports-a-pass-for-a-test-that-executed-nothing-clean-0-not) for the false passes it fixes)

* Akto reads a per-account `globalRateLimit` from its Mongo once a minute. `systemTest/akto/tests/tierPacingSetup.ts` sets it per tier: **pr unthrottled; pre-merge and security at 1,500/min** (0.75 × the platform's 2,000/min, derived in `src/setup/aktoRateLimit.ts`), restored to unthrottled afterwards. `AKTO_GLOBAL_RATE_LIMIT=N` overrides it.
* Before any setup login, the harness also waits (≤61 s, probing `GET /api/auth/me`) for the 60-second window to have room, since back-to-back tiers were having their setup logins refused ([KS-1362](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1362/back-to-back-tiers-setup-logins-land-in-the-platforms-spent-60-second)).

**Measured on slot 2 of the Mac, 2026-09-28, Akto 2.35.6**

| tier | unpaced | paced at 1,500/min |
| -- | -- | -- |
| pr | 29 s — 8,702 results, 129 refused | (left unpaced) |
| pre-merge | **47 s** — only 1,057 actually tested, **8,129 refused** | **19 m 28 s** — 192 refused |
| full OWASP scan | 423.8 s — **8,730 of 50,162 refused** | **\~27 min — 0 of 50,306 refused** |
| whole security tier | — | **60 m 52 s** |

Two things to expect at any pace: Akto overshoots its setting by about 10%, and it releases each minute's allowance as a \~5 s burst, so the first minute of a paced run still sees a few refusals.

**The platform side as it stands** (read-only)

* Global limiter: `api-gateway/src/index.ts:472-485` — 60 s window, `max = RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS || (non-prod ? 10000 : 300)`; `.env.example:205` sets **2000**. Keyed per address, and every caller on the host shares `192.168.65.1` ([KS-618](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-618/client-ip-is-invisible-platform-wide-on-demo-every-ip-keyed-control)).
* Skip rules: `middleware/rateLimitSkip.ts` — read-only paths; an operator override `DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT=true` in non-prod envs; and a `Bearer test_token_` bypass when `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS=true` in `development`/`test`.
* nginx (`nginx-demo.conf:171-172`, VM demo) adds `limit_req` at 50 r/s (api) and 5 r/s (auth).

+++

+++ The options, as I see them

1. **Keep things as they are** — harness-side pacing only; no platform change. *Cost:* pre-merge \~20 min and security \~1 h locally. The limiter stays exactly as deployed.
2. **Raise** `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS` **for local stacks only** (e.g. back to the code's non-prod default of 10,000, or a figure you choose), leaving demo and production alone. The harness would pace to the new figure automatically, since it derives its rate from this value. *Cost:* local stacks stop matching the demo's limiter, so a limiter regression would be less likely to show locally.
3. **Use the existing operator override** — `DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT=true` on local non-prod stacks during scans. *Cost:* the global limiter is out of the picture entirely, including the verifier rate-limiting test's realism; easy to leave on by accident.
4. **Key the limiter per authenticated principal** (user or token) instead of per address — so the scanner's personas, k6 and a human each get their own budget. *Cost:* a real design change with security implications; overlaps [KS-618](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-618/client-ip-is-invisible-platform-wide-on-demo-every-ip-keyed-control).
5. **A dedicated, higher budget for a scanner identity in non-prod only** (e.g. a service account or a signed header, gated like the existing test-token bypass). *Cost:* a new bypass surface that has to be airtight to non-prod.
6. **Tune the harness further, no platform change** — pace closer to 2,000 (e.g. 0.85×) to save a few minutes at the price of a few more first-minute refusals, or pace fewer tiers. *Cost:* marginal gains; the limiter still sets the floor.

+++

## Where I'd love your guidance

1. Which option (or combination) fits how you want the limiter to behave?
2. Should local stacks match the demo's limits exactly, or is a looser local limit acceptable for testing?
3. Is \~20 min for pre-merge and \~1 h for security acceptable as a local gate, or is it worth a platform change to bring those down?

Once we've agreed a direction, either of us can make the change — whichever is more convenient. The one thing that isn't on the table is reducing test coverage: every option above keeps the same templates, tiers and endpoints, and changes only how fast they run or how the limit is set. No platform code has been touched so far.

## Checklist item added after the merge of PR #1347 (squash `8c810023f9c9`)

- [X] **N-1347-11 — the residue of the target-keyed pacing.** Closed by PR #1349, merged to `develop` as squash `691bb93e5c530c845ba0926ab0f369d5dc502720`: `isLocalScanTarget()` now reads `OVERRIDE_APP_URL` first and falls back to `SECUURA_API_URL`, the same precedence `systemTest/akto/src/scan/scanOptions.ts:98` uses for the host the scan attacks. With `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS=10000` reaching the harness (a raised local `.env`), a scan aimed at a remote stack through `OVERRIDE_APP_URL` alone was paced at 7500/min and is now paced at 1500, and an `OVERRIDE_APP_URL` pointing at localhost is paced at 7500. Without that raised value, and without `AKTO_PLATFORM_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE`, every target is paced at 1500, as before. Checked by unit tests only (9 cells: 4 that fail on the previous code, 5 controls); no Akto scan was run against any stack, and the demo's own `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS` has not been read.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Paced `pre-merge` runs still lose 4 to 8 percent of results to 429s. There are three possible readings and none is settled. Controlled re-run owed, not yet run. This comes from reading code at develop `cd773edc2bb8` and the figures already on this ticket; no stack and no Akto run sit behind it.

**Reading 1, overlap with other traffic.** The limiter is keyed per address, so other callers on the host can spend the same budget. It is not needed to explain the highest figure: the 2026-10-07 comment says nothing else was on the slot for the run with 1,671 refused, which is more than the 939 of 2026-10-06, when a preflight may have overlapped. It is not ruled out for 2026-10-06. Settled by: the gateway columns of `npm run scan:pacing`, all requests against Akto's per minute, on a slot with nothing else on it.

**Reading 2, the 10,000 budget not applying per scan as the harness assumes.** `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` has one limiter, per address, per 60 s window, not per scan, and the harness paces the tier as one budget. If the gateway had been at 2,000 while Akto paced at 7,500, refusals would be nearer the 70 percent measured unpaced than 4 to 8 percent. That is an inference; no stack's environment was read. Settled by: the `RateLimit-Policy` header on a captured 429, which should read `10000;w=60`.

**Reading 3, Akto bursting above its rate within the minute.** `aktoRateLimit.ts` already records this as operating fact 3: each minute's allotment leaves as a burst of about 5 s, and a run's first gateway window catches two. The headroom is still 0.75, so the loss would scale with the pace. At 1,500/min the measured refusals were 192 and 290 results; five times those is 960 and 1,450. The figures at 7,500/min are 944 (2026-10-05, "all in one ~2 s burst"), 939 and 1,671. Settled by: the per-minute rows of `npm run scan:pacing`; this reading predicts every refusal in the first minute or two of the run and none after.

**The point against reading 3.** The `security` tier's full OWASP scan refused 393 of 50,450 at the same pace, well below that scaling, although it sends about one request per result where `pre-merge` sends about four. The code does not explain that. So reading 3 is a lead, not a finding.

**Not measured.** The wall-clock of a paced run since PRs 1347 and 1349.

**What settles all three.** A disposable slot with nothing else on it, `npm run test:pre-merge`, then `npm run scan:pacing`. Controlled re-run owed, not yet run. The pacing does not change until a run supports it.

Delivered: PRs 1347 and 1349 merged as 8c810023f and 691bb93e5 on develop, both in the b1fb543640e7 tree (2026-11-01); they change env.example and the systemTest Akto harness, so there is no deployed surface. Verified by code read at b1fb543640e7, not observed live: env.example sets RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS=10000 with a 60000 ms window. Left open: the ticket asks which way to go on how the platform's rate limit treats Akto scans, and no ruling is recorded in its comments. The newest two comments (2026-10-06 and 2026-10-07) report the paced pre-merge runs still receive 429s on about 4% and 8% of results (1,671 of 21,031 on 2026-10-07), so the pace and the limit are described as not yet fitting.

## Data point: rate-limited (429) counts on Akto 2.37.1, slot 1, 2026-10-07

Kamil, for your open pacing question; nothing assumed. All runs paced at 7,500/min (0.75 × the local 10,000/min):

| Tier | Result docs | Refused (429) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `pre-merge` | 21,031 | **1,671** (about 8%) |
| `security`, full OWASP scan alone | 50,450 | 393 |
| `pr` (unthrottled) | 8,727 | 11 |

For comparison, earlier `pre-merge` runs: 944 on slot 2 on 2026-10-05 (Akto 2.36.10, all in one ~2 s burst) and 939 on slot 1 on 2026-10-06. This run therefore has about 1.8× the refusals, and I cannot separate the image bump from pacing: I have only this one `pre-merge` run on 2.37.1, nothing else was on the slot during it, and the per-minute breakdown (`npm run scan:pacing`) was not captured. The testing engine itself is unchanged between the two images (the `apps/testing` git tree is identical).

## First paced scan since #1347 / #1349: still 939 rate-limited results at 7,500/min

**BLUF.** Kamil, thank you for #1347 and #1349. One thing worth knowing, no action assumed: the first paced Akto run since your change still hit the platform limiter on about 4% of results, so the pace and the limit don't quite fit yet.

>>> Evidence (Akto `pre-merge`, local slot 1, 2026-10-06 ~14:21Z, run `pre-merge-ks-571-2026-10-06T14-20-45Z`)

* **Pacing, from the run log:** `Akto engine rate limit set to 7500 req/min (platform budget 10000/min, 75% headroom)`. The harness waited 65 s for Akto's watcher to apply it, then restored "unthrottled" at the end.
* **Verdict:** PASS — 0 vulnerable.
* **Buckets:** clean 7,953 · authz-precondition 644 · not-applicable 10,716 · not-on-stack 772 · connectivity 7 · **rate-limited 939**.
* **HTTP:** `429 939` of 21,031 non-vulnerable results (also 400 347 · 404 5,587 · 415 38).
* So **939 results (≈4.5%) weren't exercised**, even with the engine at 75% of the platform budget.

**Not measured / not ruled out:**
* The run's wall-clock time (not captured), so I can't say whether the ~20 min / ~1 h concern is settled.
* **Other traffic on slot 1:** a repo pre-push preflight was running on the same machine around then, and its spec-auth and path-resolvability legs probe the slot-1 gateway. I can't rule out that it overlapped the scan and used part of the budget. A clean re-run with nothing else on the slot would settle it.

**Possible readings, your call:** overlap with that other traffic; the 10,000/min budget not applying per scan as the harness assumes; or Akto bursting above its configured rate within the minute. A clean re-run, and measuring where the 429s cluster, would tell them apart.

Merged to `develop` as PR #1347, squash `8c810023f9c9ac060a7aff24f0933ae3b8734479`, tree `e889329f530b`, parent `8ba2da02d980`.
