The landed subject is 92 characters.

The squash subject was composed rather than taken from the PR title, because the title had become false at round 2: it said "raise the local templates" (plural) when only `env.example` is raised, and "read the platform limit" without the condition. The landed subject states the condition: `env.example` goes to 10000, and the Akto harness reads it only when `SECUURA_API_URL` is local.

Round 2 closed the three findings a review raised against round 1: the production-compose template is back to its own value, the harness no longer reads a local limit for every scan, and the derived rate is floored at 1 so it can never be zero — zero means unthrottled in that harness.

One residue remains and is recorded as a checklist item below: a scan aimed at a remote stack through `OVERRIDE_APP_URL` alone, with `SECUURA_API_URL` local or unset, still paces at the local figure. The demo's own limit was not read at any point, because its environment file is not in this repository.

This ticket stays In Progress. Nothing was deployed by the merge.

Second correction, to our comment above. Two things in it were wrong, and a review of the change found them. *(Edited after a later review: two statements in the first version of this comment were themselves imprecise, and they are corrected in place below rather than in a third comment.)*

First: we wrote "Demo and production limits are unchanged". That held for deployments already running, but not for a host seeded afterwards. Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.production.yml:16 tells an operator to copy .env.example to .env, and that file's own default is RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS:-100. The first round raised .env.example to 10000, so a production-compose host seeded from it after that change would have run at 10000. No running environment was affected, and nothing was deployed, but the statement was wrong about the seeding path.

Second: we said the Akto harness now takes the platform limit from RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS. It did, for every scan — including a scan pointed at a remote stack. The harness's configuration loader reads the local Blockchain/Dev/.env whatever stack is being scanned, so a local value of 10000 would have paced a remote scan at 7500 where it had previously paced at 1500. We cannot state the demo's own limit here: its environment file is not in this repository, and the only figures the repository carries are deployment/azure/services.bicep:681, which sets 2000 for the Azure `dev` environment and 100 for every other one. An earlier version of this comment gave "2000" as the demo's limit, which was not something we had read.

Both are fixed at head 18bc5123ce90, merged as PR #1347 (squash 8c810023f9c9):
- Blockchain/Dev/.env.example is back to 2000, with the reason recorded in the file. Only Blockchain/Dev/env.example is raised to 10000; scripts/bootstrap-env.sh reads that one as canonical. So env.example seeds local stacks, .env.example seeds production-compose, and the two no longer move together.
- The harness reads RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS only when SECUURA_API_URL resolves to a local host (an unset value is local, because the default is always a localhost port). A remote SECUURA_API_URL paces at the 2000 default. AKTO_PLATFORM_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE is an explicit override for a remote stack whose real limit an operator knows; its name is deliberately not defined by either env template, so it cannot be picked up from a local .env the way the previous value was.
- A platform limit of 1 previously derived 0, which this harness treats as unthrottled. The derived rate is now floored at 1.

One case is NOT covered, and an earlier version of this comment implied otherwise by saying "any other target paces at the 2000 default". The host the scanner actually attacks is OVERRIDE_APP_URL if set, falling back to SECUURA_API_URL (systemTest/akto/src/setup/scanOptions.ts:98), while the check above reads SECUURA_API_URL only. So a scan aimed at a remote stack through OVERRIDE_APP_URL alone, with SECUURA_API_URL local or unset, still paces at the local figure. That configuration also logs in to the local stack, so such a scan is already misconfigured, but the pacing is wrong in it and the gap is real. It is recorded on this ticket as a checklist item, with the one-line fix.

Two further things to be plain about. The .github/workflows/internal-audit.yml CI stack copies env.example, so CI now runs at 10000. And a remote stack reached through a localhost port-forward or tunnel reads as local; the explicit override is the answer there, and the change does not try to detect that case.

Hi @kamil.kreiser

I added this yesterday as a temporary fix, as I did not want to update the codebase

* systemTest/akto/src/setup/aktoRateLimit.ts:60

## BLUF
Thanks Peter, this is a clear write-up. **Our recommendation is option 2 plus one guard:** raise `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS` on **local stacks only** (to the code's own non-prod default of 10,000, which you cite at `api-gateway/src/index.ts:472-485`), leave demo and production exactly as deployed, and **add one dedicated limiter test that runs at the demo's limit** so a limiter regression still shows up locally. Coverage is unchanged; only local pacing and one config value move.

## Recommendation, answering your three questions
1. **Which option:** 2, plus the limiter test above. The harness already derives its pace from this value, so it speeds up on its own.
2. **Should local stacks match demo exactly?** A looser local limit is acceptable **for scanning**, provided one test pins the demo behaviour: at the demo figure (2,000/min), requests beyond it are refused with 429, and the read-only skip paths still skip. That keeps the realism you were worried about losing in option 2, without paying for it in every scan.
3. **Is ~20 min / ~1 h acceptable as a local gate?** No. That is slow enough that people start skipping the gate, which costs more coverage than it protects. A config change is worth it.

## Why not the others
- **3 (`DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT=true` during scans):** removes the limiter from the picture entirely and is easy to leave on by accident.
- **5 (a scanner identity with a higher budget):** a new bypass surface that has to stay airtight to non-prod; not worth it when a config value does the job.
- **4 (key the limiter per principal):** probably the right long-term design, and it overlaps KS-618 (every caller shares one address). It is a separate piece of work with security implications, so we suggest a ticket for it, not this change.
- **6:** marginal gains; the limiter still sets the floor.

## Detail
No platform code is proposed to change; demo and production limits are untouched. If you agree, either side can make the change, as you offered: the local `.env` value, and the one limiter test.

title: api-gateway failed-login lockout is inert: createBruteForceProtection installs recordFailure, but no production code ever calls it — it can never block
description:
## Summary

For when you have a moment, Kamil. The gateway's failed-login lockout (`createBruteForceProtection`, `api-gateway/src/middleware/security.ts:146-192`) looks as though it never engages: it only blocks once `recordFailure()` has run, and nothing outside its own unit test seems to call it. The auth service's per-account lockout is still doing its job, so this is about the edge layer only. Either wiring it up or retiring it would be fine; whichever you prefer. Thank you.

+++ Evidence, and the two options

**What the code shows** (read-only, 2026-09-28)

* `security.ts:173-189` attaches `req.bruteForce = { recordFailure, recordSuccess }` and calls `next()`; nothing on the login's response path calls either helper.
* Searching `services/api-gateway/src` for `recordFailure` outside `middleware/security.ts` finds only `__tests__/security.test.ts:261`, which checks the helper exists.
* So `attempts` is never incremented, `blockedUntil` is never written, and the `429 "Too many failed attempts"` branch can't be reached.

**What the logs show**

* Slot 2's gateway, six hours of traffic including failed logins: **0** `BRUTE_FORCE_LOCKOUT`, **0** `BRUTE_FORCE_BLOCKED`.
* The lockout that does work is the auth service's (`services/auth/src/services/accountLockout.ts`: (email, /24), 5 failures in 15 min → 15-min lock). It answers **401** (`routes/auth.ts:339-342`).

**Why it came up:** [KS-1362](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1362/back-to-back-tiers-setup-logins-land-in-the-platforms-spent-60-second) first put some refused setup logins down to this lockout; on a closer look they were the global request window. It seemed worth recording that this layer isn't active, so no one leans on it.

**Options**

1. Wire it: call `recordFailure` / `recordSuccess` from the login proxy's response handling (401 / 2xx), with a test that shows a block after `freeRetries` failures.
2. Retire it: remove the middleware, its `bruteForce` config in `config/services.ts`, and the doc line at `security.ts:8`.

[KS-618](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-618/client-ip-is-invisible-platform-wide-on-demo-every-ip-keyed-control) (every IP-keyed control is shared behind one address) applies either way.

**Done means:** a test red on today's code shows N+1 failed logins from one address aren't blocked at the gateway; after the change they are — or the middleware and its claims are gone.

+++

title: Security: validate reads API keys from a boot-only memory map, so a revoked key keeps authenticating AND its usage write rewrites is_active = true over the revoke
description:
**BLUF — measured from the source path at develop** `0d156d12`**, and it is worse than a multi-replica write-back concern: it is also a live authentication bypass on a single process.**

`POST /api/keys/validate` in `services/security/src/index.ts` resolves the key from an **in-memory map first** and reads the database **only on a cache miss**:

* `:1326` `let apiKey = Array.from(memApiKeys.values()).find(k => k.keyHash === keyHash);`
* `:1328-1334` the code's own comment states the map "is populated **only at boot** from svc_api_keys".
* `:1335` the DB fallback (`security_find_api_key_by_hash`) runs **only** `if (!apiKey)`, and `:1347` warms the cache.

So once a key is in memory, this process never re-reads its row. Two consequences follow, and the second is the one the KS-888 validate brief raised:

**1. A revoked key keeps authenticating.** `:1358` `if (!apiKey.isActive)` is evaluated against the **stale memory copy**. If the row is set inactive by anything this process did not do — the revoke route on another replica, an operator UPDATE, a future admin tool — this process answers `valid: true` until it restarts.

**2. The usage write then UNDOES the revoke for everyone.** `:1369` `await dbSaveApiKey(apiKey);` and the upsert at `:316-318` is `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET last_used_at = EXCLUDED.last_used_at, usage_count = EXCLUDED.usage_count, is_active = EXCLUDED.is_active`. `EXCLUDED.is_active` comes from the in-memory `k.isActive`, which is still `true`. So a validate on a stale copy writes `is_active = true` over a persisted revoke. The revoke is lost in the database, not merely missed locally.

**What is measured and what is not.** Every line above is read at `0d156d12` and quoted. The control flow is decisive on its own: memory-first, DB-on-miss-only, boot-only population, and the upsert asserting `is_active` from that copy. What is **NOT** done is a driven two-process run demonstrating the lost revoke end to end — that needs two memory maps over one database and is the natural first step for whoever takes this.

**Why it is not KS-888.** KS-888 is about what happens when the usage write *fails* (mint refuses, revoke answers 503, validate logs and continues — all shipped or pinned). This is about the write *succeeding* and carrying a stale field. The pin for validate's log-only behaviour is PR #1334; it does not touch this and must not be read as covering it.

**Board search before filing, with controls:** `EXCLUDED.is_active`, `populated only at boot`, `security_find_api_key_by_hash`, `stale memory`, `revoked key still validates` all returned **0**; positive controls on the same literal query shape returned `memApiKeys` 4, `dbSaveApiKey` 3, `is_active` 2, and the nonsense control 0. The four `memApiKeys` hits (KS-1174, KS-889, KS-888, KS-869) were each read and none covers this: they are the gateway's 401 collapsing, the connector_id backfill window, the KS-888 save-failure family, and connector_id persistence.

**Shapes worth considering (not a recommendation).** Narrowest: drop `is_active` from the upsert's SET list, so a usage write can never assert liveness. That closes consequence 2 and leaves consequence 1. Wider: re-read the row (or invalidate the cache entry) before answering, which closes both and costs a query per validate on a deliberately unauthenticated hot path.

nodes.body: **BLUF:** State moved In Review -> In Progress. Owed: "a revoke in one security replica refusing the key in another." (this ticket's newest comment, comment 7). Not closed because the ticket says: "It needs a key minted and revoked (writes) and a second security replica; no permitted login covers it". Kam ruled on 2026-11-04 12:42 AEDT (card `secuura-observation-owed-closeout-1104`, option **a**): "Run one live-check sweep on kintsugi, then close what passes"; this ticket is named in that card. This seat ran no check on a box; beyond the ticket text it read only the merge state of PR 1338 at the GitHub API (PR 1338 merged as 8af6ab821600).

**BLUF:** Not run on kintsugi: needs an API key minted and revoked. Delivered: PR 1338 merged as 8af6ab821 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at ee1e1b832115 (kintsugi's REVISION head, read 2026-11-04 01:59Z). Left open.

- **Owed check:** a revoke in one security replica refusing the key in another.
- **Why not run:** It needs a key minted and revoked (writes) and a second security replica; no permitted login covers it.

Delivered: PR 1338 merged as 8af6ab821 on develop (validate answers on the stored revoke and its usage write cannot revive one), with KS-1377's PR 1602 counting key usage in the database, in the kintsugi deploy b1fb543640e7 (2026-11-01). Verified by code read at b1fb543640e7, not observed live: services/security/src/index.ts carries both halves, the usage-only write at line 471 and :1904 and the stored-row check on a cache hit at :1820 to 1862 (stored-revoked beats cached-active). Left open: the ticket's merge comment says NOT Done, live sweep owed: a cross-replica revoke and the EXECUTE grant on the deployed database. Both need a second replica or database access and a revoke on the box, which is not a read-only probe, and neither was run here.

Merged 8af6ab8216007462e596daed6b0adcd1e87e34ee (PR #1338, services/security/src/index.ts); offline gates green; NOT Done per secuura-test-discipline §5f — live sweep owed (torn-down rebuilt stack, all containers verified up), unverified: a revoke in one security replica refused by another within the gateway's 60 s valid cache, the secuura_app role's EXECUTE on security_find_api_key_by_hash on the deployed database, and a security-DB fault's 503 -> 401 path through the gateway

---

**For the record, measured by the gate at the base (VANISHED-ROW-RESURRECTED-AT-BASE):** at the base a stale instance honours a DELETED key (200 `valid:true`) AND its usage upsert **re-creates the row** (`is_active true, usage 1`) as secuura_app under the key's tenant GUC. Any delete, including migration 019's, was undone by one validate on a stale replica. The merged head closes it (`Key not found`, evicted, no row). My own PR body called this path "defensive, not live" — that was true of today's DELETE sites but understated the base defect, and the gate's measurement is the accurate account.

**PR #1338 raised** — `feature/ks-1370-validate-reads-stored-revoke-b42-1` at head `42f8a5abc65ef9a6bc20c07797786089f2b9cd93`, base `develop`. Not merged; holding for the QA gate. Nothing deployed.

**Reproduced first, on a real PostgreSQL 18.3 (unix socket only), at develop `0de108577e61`.** Two module instances with separate in-memory key maps, driven through the real `POST /api/keys/validate`:
- a stale instance validated a key revoked by another process → `valid: true`
- after its usage write the row read `is_active` false → **true**, `usage_count` 1 → 2
- controls both ways: a never-revoked key validated; a third instance booted after the revoke refused it and the row stayed `false`, so the database held the revoke and the stale cache alone is the difference

**Both halves fixed, per the ruling on this ticket (option a):**
- (i) validate's usage write is now a usage-only `UPDATE ... SET last_used_at, usage_count`. The shared upsert keeps `is_active` because the revoke route persists through it and the KS 764 guard pins that shape.
- (ii) on a cache hit validate re-reads the stored row through the reviewed `security_find_api_key_by_hash` carve-out and decides on it, refreshing the stale entry.

**The failed-read case, per the second ruling (option a):** a failed stored read with a database configured returns 503 "Unable to verify key"; memory-only deployments answer from memory and are unchanged.

**Two shapes that follow from the rulings rather than adding to them:**
- A revoke is sticky in **both** directions — revoked if either the cache or the store says revoked. Refreshing blindly from the store would have undone KS 888's rule that a revoke whose save failed still blocks the key in that process. Cell R2 of the KS 888 file caught it, and that cell now passes unchanged.
- A row that has vanished reads `Key not found` and the cache entry is evicted. This is a defensive path: nothing outside migration 019 deletes from `svc_api_keys`.

**Evidence:** `services/security` 26 files / 275 tests, 0 failed · KS 888 validate file 19/19 (baseline 19/19; 5 declarations = 7 executed cases moved and re-pinned, reason in the mock, no pin weakened) · 9 new cells, 5 of them red at the base tip · KS 764 guard 15/15 untouched · tsc rc 0 · eslint rc 0 · 16/16 real-PostgreSQL arms with the product file restored byte-identical · push preflight 12/15 legs, 3 skipped, nothing failed.

**Not covered, stated:** the drill runs as a superuser, so RLS is bypassed and it cannot discriminate the fail-closed path that justifies the SECURITY DEFINER carve-out — the gate should drive the stored read as a non-superuser app role. `usage_count` written from a stale copy is a lost update, named as a candidate and not fixed. Runtime change on validate, so the §5f live sweep is owed.

**REPRODUCED on a real PostgreSQL. Facts only — no product change, no state change.**

**Instrument:** a driven two-instance repro. Two instances of `services/security/src/index.ts` are loaded with separate CJS module caches, so each holds its **own `memApiKeys`** (the map is exported as a test seam at `:160`). `SECURITY_DISABLE_BOOT=1` suppresses `app.listen` and `initDb`; `initDb()` is then called explicitly per instance, and each instance's real Express `app` is served on an ephemeral loopback port and driven through the real `POST /api/keys/validate` route. One PostgreSQL **18.3**, unix socket only (`listen_addresses = ''`, 0 inet sockets verified with `lsof`), schema built by the repo's own file migrations.

**Commit under test:** worktree at develop `215cc6875e2bac0b6d6b38918572384fbfcbdb77` (the local HEAD adds only an unrelated test-file change; `services/security/src/index.ts` is byte-identical to develop's, sha256 `7f29bb85765e7985`).

**Anchors re-read at this commit and unchanged from the filing:** `:1326` resolves the key from `memApiKeys` first; `:1328` states the map is "populated only at boot"; `:1335` reads the DB only on a cache miss; `:1358` tests the cached `isActive`; `:1369` `await dbSaveApiKey(apiKey)`; `:316-318` `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET ... is_active = EXCLUDED.is_active`.

**Sequence and results.** Instance B boots while the key is active, so its cache holds `isActive: true`. The revoke is then persisted (`is_active = false`). Then:

| step | result |
|---|---|
| CONTROL — key never revoked, validated in B | `valid: true` |
| revoke persisted | DB `is_active = false` |
| **(1) B validates the revoked key** | **`valid: true`** — the key still authenticates |
| **(2) DB row after B's usage write** | **`is_active = true`**; `usage_count` 1 → 2 |
| CONTROL — a THIRD instance booted AFTER the revoke | `valid: false`, reason `Key revoked`; DB stays `false` |

**Both halves of the report are confirmed.** A revoked key keeps authenticating in any process that cached it before the revoke, and that process's usage write then **rewrites `is_active = true` over the persisted revoke**.

**What the controls establish.** The first control shows the harness can answer `valid`, so answer (1) is not a harness artefact. The third-instance control shows the database genuinely held the revoke and that a fresh boot refuses the key — so the difference is the stale cache alone, not the database.

**Scope of what was driven.** The revoke was applied as the persisted row state that the revoke route's `dbSaveApiKey` produces, rather than through that route's admin-authenticated handler; instance B — the subject of the report — was driven end to end through its real route. The two instances share one process with separate module caches rather than being two OS processes; the separation under test is the memory map, which is genuinely separate.

**An earlier run of this instrument was INVALID and is withdrawn:** `initDb()` had not been called, so `loadFromDb()` returned early, no key was cached, and every answer read `Key not found` — **including the control**. A control that fails alongside the subject is the tell, and it is why that run was not reported.

**A dependency the gate38 report records, from the other side (finding N-1334-1, facts only).**

PR #1334 (squash `215cc6875e2bac0b6d6b38918572384fbfcbdb77`) pinned validate's log-only behaviour with a test-only change. The gate's note on it: *"the pin binds validate's usage write to the `INSERT … upsert` shape, so a KS 1370 fix would red 5 of its cells."*

So whoever fixes this ticket should expect `services/security/src/__tests__/ks888-failed-mint-save-issues-no-key.test.ts` to go red — specifically the V1 ×3 / V2 / V3 cases that assert the current upsert shape — and should update those cells as part of the fix rather than reading the red as a regression. The narrowest fix shape named on this ticket (dropping `is_active` from the upsert's SET list) is exactly the kind of change that would do it.

Nothing to do here now; recorded so the coupling is not discovered by surprise.

Filed at Urgent, corrected to **High** on the same day it was filed. The evidence is a source-path reading at develop `0d156d12` — memory-first lookup, boot-only population, DB read only on a cache miss, and `is_active` asserted from that copy in the upsert — every line quoted in the description. What is **not** done is a driven two-process run showing a persisted revoke actually lost. High matches KS-1352, the sibling finding that a revoked credential verifies. A driven repro is what would justify raising it to Urgent, and it is the natural first step for whoever takes this.

title: api-gateway crashes under load: onProxyReq calls setHeader after the proxied request's headers were sent — uncaught exception, 13 restarts, 502s on /api/auth/login
description:
## Summary

When you get a chance, Kamil — this one does hurt under load. During the [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) k6 runs, the api-gateway process exited on an uncaught exception thrown from its own proxy hook, and Docker restarted it 13 times in about five minutes. nginx answered 502 while it was down. The hook calls `setHeader` on a request whose headers were already sent, and nothing guards or catches that. A small guard plus an error path would likely settle it; your call on the shape. Thank you.

+++ Evidence, impact and a suggested direction

**The throw** (31 occurrences in the gateway log)

```
Uncaught exception {"error":"Cannot set headers after they are sent to the client"}
  at ClientRequest.setHeader (node:_http_outgoing:684:11)
  at ProxyServer.onProxyReq (/app/dist/routes/proxy.js:254:26)
  at ProxyServer.emit (/app/node_modules/eventemitter3/index.js:184:35)
  at ClientRequest.<anonymous> (/app/node_modules/http-proxy/lib/http-proxy/passes/web-incoming.js:133:16)
  at tickOnSocket (node:_http_client:1116:7)
```

`dist/routes/proxy.js:254` is the hook's first statement, `proxyReq.setHeader('X-Request-ID', requestId)` — source `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:246` (mapped by reading the compiled file in the running container). None of the hook's later header writes (vouch `:276`, policy headers, `Authorization`, the [KS-453](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-453/did-endpoints-getpatchdelete-apididdid-return-502-on-malformed-did) body re-stream) checks `proxyReq.headersSent` either.

**Where:** local slot 1, api-gateway built from develop `63db8a383` ([KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) changes no service code); Apple M2 Max, four stacks up. Load: k6 `scalability` (12:54–13:15Z) then `auth-spike` (13:15–13:17Z, 150 VUs on `POST /api/auth/login`). First crash 13:12:11Z; `restartCount=13`, last start 13:17:36Z; healthy afterwards.

**What callers saw**

| Signal | Value |
| -- | -- |
| nginx, `POST /api/auth/login` during auth-spike | **11,362 × 502** + 6,123 × 429 |
| scalability | thresholds 6/6, but **14.8 %** `http_req_failed`, 65,192 failed checks |
| auth-spike | INVALID — all 17,788 logins failed |
| auth service, same second as the first crash | `DB getUserByEmail failed … timeout exceeded when trying to connect` |

The auth DB-pool timeout looks like the trigger; the gateway turning it into a process exit is the defect.

**Ruled out:** slots sharing a database (each has its own Postgres + pgbouncer network), and the harness/k6 version (the trace is inside api-gateway; other k6 scenarios pass).

**Suggested direction**

1. Return early from the hook when `proxyReq.headersSent` (or the request is destroyed).
2. Let the proxy's error path answer 502/503 rather than letting a handler throw reach `uncaughtException` (the class [KS-1242](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1242/t-1-authenticatetoken-is-an-async-express-4-middleware-with-no-catch-a) describes for `authenticateToken`).
3. A regression test driving `onProxyReq` with an already-sent `proxyReq`, red on today's code.

**Reproduce:** `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD=… systemTest/run-in-slot.sh 1 bash -c 'cd systemTest/performance && npm run test:scalability'`, then `npm run test:auth-spike`; watch `docker inspect secuura-api-gateway --format '{{.RestartCount}}'` and `docker logs secuura-api-gateway | grep "Cannot set headers"`.

**Related:** [KS-1242](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1242/t-1-authenticatetoken-is-an-async-express-4-middleware-with-no-catch-a) (async middleware without a catch — same class, different site) · [KS-744](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-744/gateway-500s-on-every-proxied-route-for-a-token-lacking) (unguarded header set in `auth.ts:377`) · [KS-1362](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1362/back-to-back-tiers-setup-logins-land-in-the-platforms-spent-60-second) (back-to-back tiers' setup logins refused inside a spent request window — the 429 side of busy runs) · [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) (where it was found) · [KS-491](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-491/review-f-edge-waf-ddos-and-anti-automation) (Review F — availability under load).

+++

## Checklist item added after the merge of PR #1342 (squash `67c73393dfa0`)

- [ ] **N-1342-1 (Major, not blocking):** under keep-alive agent saturation (more than 128 requests in
  flight to one upstream), a **body-parsed** POST whose headers were already sent is delivered to the
  upstream with its `Content-Length` and **zero body bytes**. The guard skips the re-stream, so the
  upstream waits and the client gets a TCP reset at exactly 60.0 s, with **no 502 and no log line**.
  At develop before #1342 the same request **crashes** the process, so the merged change is strictly
  better — this is residue, not a regression. The raw-stream `/api/auth/login` route is unaffected
  (140/140 delivered). Evidence: `evidence/runs/probe1342b.log` and `probe1342c.log` in the gate43
  batch #1341-#1345 report directory.

nodes.body: Delivered: PR 1342 merged as 67c73393d on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (2026-11-01). Verified by code read at b1fb543640e7, not observed live: services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:256 returns early when `proxyReq.headersSent` is true, inside the onProxyReq hook (control: the hook is present, 3 hits in proxy.ts). Left open: the ticket carries an unchecked checklist item, N-1342-1 (Major, not blocking): under keep-alive saturation (more than 128 requests in flight to one upstream) a body-parsed POST whose headers were already sent is delivered with its Content-Length and zero body bytes, and the client gets a TCP reset at 60 s with no 502 and no log line. The merge comment also says a live sweep against a running environment is owed. Neither is a read-only probe, so this check did not run them.

Merged to `develop` as PR #1342, squash `67c73393dfa07c741f359c59b893cb24a89d5152`, tree `449ae9c6c10e`. Verified at source: develop equals the squash by ls-remote, the commits API reports that tree, and a contents-API blob read on each changed path equals the head's blob. The landed subject is within the 92-character limit.

QA recorded one Major finding that does not block this merge: under keep-alive saturation (more than 128 requests in flight to one upstream), a body-parsed POST whose headers were already sent is delivered with its Content-Length and zero body bytes, and the client gets a TCP reset at 60.0 s with no 502 and no log line. At develop the same request crashes the gateway, so this change is strictly better. The raw-stream login route is unaffected (140/140 delivered). Added below as a checklist item.

This changes runtime code, so a live sweep against a running environment is still owed and this ticket stays open. Nothing was deployed by the merge.

title: Stack tooling is not slot-derived end to end: stack_guard lists a project twice under mixed marker labels, dev-reload.sh / start-local.sh bypass stack_env.sh, and compose defaults FRONTEND_URL / CORS_ORIGINS to slot 1
description:
## Summary

For when you have a moment, Kamil; it matters most on a busy host. A few pieces of stack tooling still assume slot 1 instead of deriving from `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT`, so on slots 2–4 they can double-report a stack, miss its containers, carry slot-1 URLs, or preflight the wrong gateway. Each fix is small and follows the existing `stack_env.sh` pattern. The four spots are below. Thank you.

+++ The four spots, evidence and fix shapes

1. `stack_guard.sh` `list_other_stacks` **(lines 105–111)** reports one line per label tuple (`sort -u` on `project|owner|branch`), so a project with one `owner=unknown` container (the [KS-1011](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1011/ks-666-stack-marker-reads-unknown-for-ownerbranchcommitstarted-at) case) shows up twice. *Fix:* group by project and append an `unknown` count; add a case to `scripts/__tests__/stack_guard.test.sh`.
2. `dev-reload.sh` **(**`:45` `CONTAINER="secuura-$SVC"`**) and** `start-local.sh` don't source `stack_env.sh`, so they only find slot 1's containers and stamp `unknown` markers on anything they create. *Fix:* source `stack_env.sh` and use `${STACK_PREFIX}` (or retire `start-local.sh` if unused); extend `check-stack-safety.sh` so every script running `docker compose up|run|restart` must source it.
3. `docker-compose.yml` **defaults** `FRONTEND_URL` (`:767`) and `CORS_ORIGINS` (`:503`, `:2179`) to slot 1's ports. *Fix:* derive them from the exported `GATEWAY_PORT` / `WEBSITE_PORT`, so an unedited `.env` is right on every slot; pin it in `stack_env.test.sh` or `check-stack-safety.sh`.
4. **The** [KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight) **preflight's PROVISIONED legs** default to `:6882` (`preflight.sh:94`). On a slot-N worktree they probe slot 1 unless `GATEWAY_URL` is passed. *Fix:* derive from `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` via `stack_env.sh`, and fail loudly with an example command when no slot is named locally.

**Seen 2026-09-28** (Peter's Mac, `develop` `d9ce1403d`), bringing up slot 4 with slots 2 and 3 running:

```
Other Secuura stacks running on this host (NOT affected by this operation):
  secuura_slot2 — owner peterdouglas, branch feature/ks-1286-…
  secuura_slot3 — owner peterdouglas, branch feature/ks-1353-…
  secuura_slot3 — owner unknown, branch unknown
```

The `owner unknown` container came from a bare `docker compose` call in the [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) worktree at about 09:33 UTC. That's the same mechanism as spot 2, reached by hand, and slot 3 was restored through `start-secuura.sh` afterwards.

**Verify:** the guard prints a mixed-label project once; `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=N ./scripts/dev-reload.sh api-gateway` finds `${STACK_PREFIX}-api-gateway`; an untouched `.env` renders slot-N URLs (`docker compose config`); the preflight probes slot N; `check-stack-safety.sh` goes red on a revert of any of the four.

title: cardano/transaction.ts: add_json_metadatum_with_schema throws on any metadata string over 64 bytes — KS-721's identityCommitment (≥69 bytes) has never been anchorable on a real chain
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/cardano/transaction.ts:107` attaches every anchor's metadata with `txBuilder.add_json_metadatum_with_schema(label, JSON.stringify(metadataPayload), CSL.MetadataJsonSchema.BasicConversions)`. With the lockfile-pinned `@emurgo/cardano-serialization-lib-nodejs` **15.0.3** (`Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json`), that call **throws for ANY string value over 64 bytes**: `Max metadata string too long: 65, max = 64`. This is Cardano's own metadata rule (text strings and byte strings in transaction metadata are capped at 64 bytes each), surfaced by CSL at tx build.

**Consequence for KS-721:** the `identityCommitment` accepted since 2026-08-31 (#763, `436f37bed`) has the form `<label>.v<N>:<64 lowercase hex>`, whose regex minimum is **69 bytes** (`a.v1:` + 64). Platform-S's real value (`identity-commitment-l2.v1:<64 hex>`) is **90 bytes**. So every non-mock anchor carrying a commitment would fail at `buildAnchorTransaction` before submission — **the field has never been anchorable on a real chain through this code.** Nothing has hit it yet because: (a) the mock branch (`cardano/index.ts:234-238`) hands `JSON.stringify(payload)` to the mock provider and never touches CSL, which is why KS-721 could only be proven in mock mode ("no chain write was possible", history.md); (b) S ships `CardanoAnchor:AnchorIdentity = false` (PS-870), so S has never sent the field; (c) K's own originate→anchoring hops forward only `documentId`/`contentHash`/`network`. Every real preview anchor confirmed to date is all-short (64-hex hash, doc ids, ISO timestamps, verbs), so the demo's 194 confirmed anchors are unaffected.

**Consequence for KS-1175:** `actorDid`/`orgDid` (≤512 bytes) inherit the same limit. The KS-1175 PR fixes this at the tx-build boundary (see below) and `Refs` this ticket; this ticket is filed separately because it is a separate fix (KS-721's latent defect), per the one-ticket-per-fix rule.

## Measurement (2026-09-20, Seat A 15th, at develop `dc061f2bb6dff9180a0724b1d1d5c50b9a0173fa`)

Instrument: `5_Project_History/2026-09-20_seatA-15th/boot/csl_probe.cjs` — pure wasm against the worktree's hoisted CSL 15.0.3; no chain, no port, no wallet. Both directions:

| input | `encode_json_str_to_metadatum(…, BasicConversions)` |
| -- | -- |
| 64-char string | OK (78 bytes) |
| 65-char string | THROWS `Max metadata string too long: 65, max = 64` |
| minimal KS-721 commitment `a.v1:<64 hex>` (69) | THROWS |
| S's `identity-commitment-l2.v1:<64 hex>` (90) | THROWS |
| 512-char `did:web:…` | THROWS |
| array of 2 × 45-char strings | OK (107 bytes) |
| an all-short realistic anchor payload (hash/documentType/occurredAt/timestamps) | OK (305 bytes) |

And through the exact call `transaction.ts:107` makes — a `TransactionBuilder` built from fabricated protocol params: 69-byte commitment THROWS, 64-byte string OK. Wednesday reproduced the same table independently at 22:00 AEST (her `csl_probe2.js`).

`transaction.ts:107` is the **single** attach point for BOTH labels (674 single, 675 batch); `index.ts:744` (`json_metadata.secuura` off Blockfrost) is the single chain reader. No other encoder/decoder exists under `services/anchoring/src` (grep, non-test).

## Fix (shipping in the KS-1175 PR, as its own named test block)

A pure helper `services/anchoring/src/cardano/cardanoMetadatum.ts`: `toCardanoMetadatum(payload)` replaces any string > 64 UTF-8 bytes with an ARRAY of ≤64-byte chunks split on character boundaries (byte count, never `.length`); `fromCardanoMetadatum(md)` joins an all-string array back. Applied ONLY at `transaction.ts:106` and at the chain read `index.ts:744` (before the hash compare). `metadata_payload` in the DB and `buildFlatAnchorMetadataPayload`'s output stay in the logical (unchunked) form. Controls: an all-short payload encodes to a `to_bytes()`-identical metadatum with and without the helper (proves a no-op for every anchor made to date); `from(to(x))` deep-equals `x`; a multibyte string splits with no chunk over 64 BYTES. Consequence to document: an independent chain reader (Cardanoscan / raw Blockfrost) sees a long value as an array — the standard Cardano convention for >64-byte metadata strings.

## Not in scope here

A CSL version bump (it changes the on-chain encoder for every anchor — its own ticket if ever). KS-721 itself stays archived (`Deployed to UAT`); this ticket `Refs KS-721`.

## Checklist

- [ ] helper + tests merged (KS-1175 PR)
- [ ] §5f live sweep on kintsugi: one real preview anchor carrying a ≥69-byte commitment confirms and reads back joined on `GET /api/anchors/verify/:hash` (chain source) — Kam's deploy/anchor step, not the PR's

- **Read back joined on the API:** `GET /api/anchors/<id>` returns `identityCommitment` as the one 75-character string and `identity` with real booleans; `GET /api/anchors/verify/<contentHash>` returns the same, with **`source db`** — the DB row was the reader on that call.
- **Remaining leg (this ticket's close condition, the chain-source read):** the product's `source chain` path (`fromCardanoMetadatum` as the reader, index.ts:699) was NOT exercised by this round — the direct chain copy was re-joined by the operator's own concatenation, which proves the chunk bytes on the ledger, not the product's reader. One verify read where the DB row is absent (or the reader's unit path at `3bad652d1`) closes it.
- Record: `5_Project_History/2026-09-22_seatA-16th/anchor/` (payload, POST/GET/verify responses, the Blockfrost metadata and tx records); details on KS-1175.

The codec half of this ticket is in #1105 at e02d3ecb5 (with KS-1175). Cardano metadata has no boolean type — CSL 15.0.3 rejects true/false ('bools not allowed in metadata'), floats and null — so actorVerified/orgVerified are written as the strings 'true'/'false' at the tx-build boundary only and restored to booleans by the typed view on read-back (db and chain); ints stay ints; strings over 64 UTF-8 bytes are chunked on code-point boundaries and rejoined before the verify-by-hash compare. The ticket stays In Progress: Blockfrost's real json_metadata shape for a chunked string is unobserved until the §5f live sweep, which follows the deploy/anchor step (Kam's).

title: POST /api/certifications/:id/verify forwards a revoked session's Bearer to originate: the gateway's session check never runs on this route
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/certifications/:id/verify` (api-gateway `routes/verification.ts:784`, mounted with no `authenticateToken`) forwards whatever `Authorization` the caller sent to originate's `GET /api/documents/:id` (`:788`). Measured in-process: a **REVOKED** session's JWT, alone or beside a valid connector key, reaches originate as that user's Bearer, because the gateway's session check never runs on this route. On `POST /api/documents/:id/verify` (`:488`, `authenticateToken(true)`) the same revoked JWT alone is refused 401 `SESSION_INVALIDATED`. What originate does with that token is **NOT measured**.

## Recommendation

Measure originate's `GET /api/documents/:id` with a revoked session's JWT. That sets the severity, which the gate graded Minor pending that measurement.

## Detail

* Surfaced by the #1070-#1076 gate (`2026-09-19-batch1070-1076-tier1-r1`, finding N76-2).
* Pre-existing, not introduced by that batch: api-gateway product bytes are identical at develop `51dbedd39` and at every head of the batch. `verification.ts` is unchanged at develop `f9c28a8b8`.
* How the gate measured it: in-process, the real gateway app with loopback doubles; not against a live stack or a real session store.
* Related: KS-834, the pending decision on whether this route stays public. KS-834's text says a caller who sends a token "is still scoped downstream"; this finding is that a *revoked* session's token passes the gateway here unchecked.
* Also related: the revocation property established on the authenticated mounts (KS-1207, KS-1215).
* Board search before filing (Secuura-PK, archived included):
  * literal title/description contains `certifications/:id/verify`: KS-834, KS-815 (archived, a control-byte guard);
  * `certifications/{id}/verify`: 0; `verification.ts:78`: 0;
  * `api/certifications/`: 38, none about Bearer forwarding;
  * `searchIssues("certifications verify")`, literal re-match: KS-834, KS-815.
  * None records the revoked-session forwarding.

title: Connector allow-list still fails OPEN when Redis closes or errors at runtime, on a read error (catch {}), or on LRU eviction of platform-settings
description:
**From the #1038 / KS-1233 batch gate, finding N38-1: Major, pre-existing. Not #1038's regression.**

## What's wrong

KS-1233 (#1038, merged `e51686bed`) stops `platform-settings` expiring on a TTL. But a **missing** key is still read as "no restriction". The allow-list therefore still **fails open** on every other way the key can go missing or unreadable:

* a runtime Redis close or error (the gate's row R6, measured over a stateful fake);
* a read error swallowed by a bare `catch {}`;
* LRU eviction of the key.

In each case every restricted connector becomes unrestricted.

## Why it matters

It is the same fail-open class KS-1233 fixed for the TTL trigger. A connector allow-list should fail **closed** when the configuration cannot be read.

## What to do

Make the reader fail closed. A missing or unreadable `platform-settings` should refuse restricted connector operations (or fall back to a persisted source), not grant everything. Add cells for the close, error and eviction paths. Check the other readers in the gate's reader census (section C) for the same class.

---

Filed from the batch gate report `2026-09-18-batch1038-1041-tier1-r1` (FINDINGS table), at merge of develop `8b9c3f022bee76b79a47f1b8c5de8ad3ddb4a0ae`.

title: Under multi-tenancy, auth's tenant-pool statements carry no tenant GUC: with fail-closed RLS every approve's level UPDATE matches 0 rows
description:
## BLUF

**With** `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` **on, auth's** `db.ts` **sends every statement that carries a tenant argument through** `tenantManager.getPool(tenantId).query()`**: a raw pool query with no tenant GUC.** Under fail-closed RLS, a tenant-scoped UPDATE then matches 0 rows.

* On the verification approve, develop answers a false **200 APPROVED while the level stays basic**. #1032's head instead refuses every approve (503, PENDING).
* **Major while that configuration runs; latent today.** The auth container in `services.bicep` does not set `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` (read).
* **Evidence class:** MEASURED on the real `db.ts` and `TenantPoolManager` with `pg` faked and RLS MODELLED. Whether the runtime database role enforces RLS on that pool is unverified (no Postgres was run).
* Found by the #1032 round-2 QA gate (E-1, an escalation candidate).

## Recommendation

The owner's fix. Not built here.

* Route the tenant-pool branch through the GUC path (`queryWithTenantGuc`, with the GUC in the same transaction), or drop the tenant-pool branch while per-tenant databases are off.
* **Resolve the overlap first.** KS-174 (In Progress) step 1 plans this remedy: "Tenant-pool-manager (or a query wrapper) sets `set_config('app.current_tenant_id', tenantId, true)` per transaction". It never names `tenantManager`, `getPool` or auth's `db.ts`. KS-458 (Done) bundled the GUC for the default pool only. If KS-174 is the live home, merge this ticket into it; this one carries the measured location and consequence.
* **Census every** `query(…, tenantId)` **caller** before fixing. The gate's single-line grep found one, which is not a count.
* **Regression cell:** with multi-tenancy on and fail-closed RLS, an approve whose UPDATE carries the tenant either raises the level or is refused. Never a 200 over an unchanged level.

## Detail

* **Read at develop** `34cdcfb26`**,** `services/auth/src/db.ts:47-70`**:**
  * `query(text, params, tenantId)`: `if (tenantId && tenantManager)` returns `tenantManager.getPool(tenantId).query(text, params)` (`:53-60`). No GUC. The `try` does not `await`, so a rejected query is not caught by its fallback.
  * Only without a tenant manager does it use `runWithTenantId(tenantId, () => queryWithTenantGuc(getPool(), …))` (the KS-458 path).
* **When the branch is taken** (the gate's read): `initTenantManager` needs `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED === 'true'` and `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL`. `TenantPoolManager.getPool` returns the default pool unless `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB === 'true'` and the tenant resolves to another database.
* **The gate's pool table** (approve, RLS modelled on):
  * manager on, no per-tenant DB: the UPDATE runs on the default pool with no GUC and matches 0 rows. Develop answers 200 APPROVED with the level basic (a false success). Head answers 503 PENDING basic, even with no fault.
  * a distinct tenant DB: the level UPDATE lands in the tenant database while the request row stays in the default database (a pre-existing split).
* **Callers read so far:** `getUserById(id, tenantId)` (`repositories/userRepo.ts:407`) and `updateUser`'s UPDATE (`:796`). The census is not done.
* **Config** (READ; unverifiable without `az`, not run):
  * the auth container in `services.bicep` has no `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` (the only bicep hit, `:798`, is originate's);
  * `env.dev.json` / `env.demo.json` set it `true` in a shared block (whether [deploy.sh](<http://deploy.sh>) consumes it was not re-read);
  * `docker-compose.yml` auth uses `${MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED:-false}`;
  * `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` is set nowhere in deployment or compose.
* **Related:** KS-1194 (where it was measured), KS-174, KS-458, KS-1055 (per-tenant databases never receive the file migrations).
* **Searched before filing** (Linear literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included, at most 6 pages of 50 fuzzy results per term):
  * `tenantManager.getPool`: 0 of 3 scanned.
  * `getPool`: 1, KS-213 (originate's per-tenant pool fan-out through pgbouncer; a different defect).
  * `applyTenantGuc`: 0, but the search returned no results, so that zero is the search's reach, not the board.
  * `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED`: 12, and `tenant GUC`: 19. The closest are KS-174 (above), KS-458, KS-468 (GUC not seeded on gateway proxy routes) and KS-1055. None names the tenant-pool branch in auth's `db.ts`.
* **Evidence:** #1032 round-2 gate report §7 and E-1: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-ks1194-1032-430672697-tier1-r2/report.md`.
* Refs KS-1194.

title: In Redis mode platform-settings expires 24 h after the last admin write, which erases every connector allow-list
description:
## BLUF

**In Redis mode the gateway stores platform-settings with a 24 h TTL, and nothing refreshes it.** So, by reading the code: 24 h after the last admin settings write, every connector allow-list disappears and every restricted connector becomes unrestricted.

* **Major, pending measurement.** This is READ ONLY: no Redis was run.
* The same fail-open class as the container fail-open ticket filed alongside it.
* Found by the #1035 tier-1 QA gate (finding N-A).

## Recommendation

An escalation candidate (the gate's grading). Not built here.

1. **Measure first**, read-only, in a non-production gateway running in Redis mode: store an allow-list, `EXPIRE` the key (or wait out the TTL), then create as the restricted connector. The code reading predicts 201.
2. **If confirmed**, the owner decides the fix. Either platform-settings must not expire (no TTL, or a refresh), or a missing platform-settings must not read as "no restriction" for a connector that had one. It may be sequenced with the container fail-open read-side fix.

## Detail

* **Read at develop** `34cdcfb26`**:**
  * `services/api-gateway/src/services/redis.ts:27`: `privacy: 86400` (24 hours);
  * `redis.ts:680-687`: `setNotificationSettings` writes `notif:<key>` with `setex(…, TTL.privacy, …)` when Redis is available;
  * after expiry, `getNotificationSettings('platform-settings')` returns null, and `routes/verification.ts:1214-1216` turns that into `integrations []`, which means no restriction;
  * the only `setNotificationSettings('platform-settings', …)` call is `routes/admin.ts:1127` (`PUT /api/admin/settings`), so nothing re-writes the key.
* **Why local runs never show it:** the in-memory fallback (no Redis) is a Map with no TTL.
* **It also affects KS-1204's migration-residual reading.** A key past its TTL reads as absent, which means "no restriction stored anywhere", not "no malformed list". So a reading must quote the key's TTL beside the shapes.
* **Not measured:** Redis mode was not run (KS-535).
* **Searched before filing:** Linear literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included, at most 6 pages of 50 fuzzy results per term (2026-09-17 \~16:00Z):
  * `TTL.privacy`: 0 of 114 scanned.
  * `setNotificationSettings`: 0, but the fuzzy search returned no results, so that zero is the search's reach, not the board.
  * `platform-settings`: 3 (KS-1230, KS-1176, KS-37); none covers expiry.
* **Evidence:** #1035 gate report, finding N-A: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-ks1204-1035-4b1fb0621-tier1-r1/report.md`.
* Refs KS-1204.

title: mcp-server POST /hash hashes any server-local file named by a caller-supplied filePath, with no auth - measure deployed exposure first
description:
## BLUF

**mcp-server's REST mirror** `POST /hash` **returns the SHA-256 of any server-local file named by a caller-supplied** `filePath`**, with no authentication.** On error it echoes `err.message`, which tells the caller whether a path exists. **Severity is UNMEASURED:** it depends on whether the deployed port is reachable by untrusted callers. Pre-existing, found by the tier-1 QA gate on PR #1022 (finding O1).

## Recommendation

1. **Measure the deployed exposure first.** On the VM demo (and any other deployed target), establish whether `mcp-server:4023` is reachable from outside the compose network or by any untrusted caller. **Set this ticket's priority from that measurement** (the gate: Major if reachable).
2. Then fix, for example by dropping the `filePath` branch from the HTTP mirror (it has no remote use: a remote caller has no business naming server paths), and returning a generic error message.

## Detail

**MEASURED (the QA gate, 2026-09-17, report** `2026-09-17-ks1211-1022-ff49d0242-tier1-r1`**):** `POST /hash` with `{"filePath": "<scratch file>"}` over HTTP returned **200** with the file's SHA-256.

**READ (this seat, develop** `ee40d3099`**):**

* `services/mcp-server/src/http-server.ts:41-64`:
  * `const { filePath, content } = req.body;` and, if `filePath` is set, `hashFile(filePath)`, which is `readFile(filePath)` at `src/hashing.ts:5-6`;
  * the catch at `:60-62` returns `{ error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: err.message } }`.
* `:29` `express.json` and `:33` `rejectNulBytes()` are the only middleware; no auth is mounted.
* A second `doc.filePath` → `hashFile` read is at `:93-94`.
* **The image runs this server:** `services/mcp-server/Dockerfile:73` is `CMD ["node", "dist/http-server.js"]`, with `EXPOSE 4023`.
* `docker-compose.yml` sets `MCP_HTTP_PORT=4023`. The host port mapping was removed (pen-test F-04; it was `"6023:4023"`), so by repo config the port is reachable **from inside the compose network**.
* **The gateway forwards only one mcp route:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1237-1241` proxies `POST /api/mcp/generate-package` to `${MCP_SERVER_URL}/generate-package`, and no `/hash` route through the gateway was found.
* `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx{,-demo,-production}.conf`: 0 references to `mcp` or `4023` (control: 15 or 16 `proxy_pass` lines each).
* So by repo config the endpoint is internal-only. **The deployed hosts are NOT measured.** Any container on the same network, or a mis-published port, reaches it.

**Pre-existing:** the mcp-server source is identical at develop and at PR #1022's head (the gate's reading). Not introduced by the hono bump.

**Searched before filing** (Linear, team KS, title or description, archived included):

* `/hash` 12 hits;
* `filePath` 2;
* `http-server.ts` 2;
* `POST /hash` 0;
* `hashFile` 0;
* `mcp-server` 27.

The only mcp-related hits naming `/hash` are KS-713 (mcp-server scan coverage) and KS-104 (whether to expose mcp-server via the gateway), both Done and archived. Neither owns this finding; they are referenced here in text only.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** this ticket's hole (`POST /hash` hashing any server-local path) is closed by round 2 of pull request 2059 (https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/2059), head `5d8969b36a24` (base develop), the same pull request that carries the ticket for the rest of the mcp-server web interface. Raised for its second QA gate (tier 1); not merged. A deploy is owed (mcp-server, both boxes) and nothing was deployed. No state, assignee or priority of this ticket was changed; the earlier comment on this ticket still stands for round 1.

**For `POST /hash` specifically:** a truthy `filePath` of any type is refused with `filePath is not accepted by this interface; the server reads no path` (400) and the server reads no file; the `content` branch is unchanged; its 500 logs the error's message and answers the constant `An unexpected error occurred` (it used to echo the thrown text, a file-system error naming the path); a malformed or oversize JSON body now answers the same constant with its 4xx status kept, where Express's default handler used to answer an HTML page with a stack naming server paths.

**Evidence and limits:** see the pull request body. 38 new cells, 27 of 27 planted regressions caught, mcp-server suite 16 files / 169 cells pass; the pre-push hook's verdict is quoted verbatim (13 of 16 legs ran, not a pass). Packages already generated for customers keep the old server until regenerated (Wednesday takes that to Kam). The four platform suites, Node 24 and any running server were not run.

Edited 2026-11-08: corrected after gate 250 R2-1.

**BLUF:** pull request 2059 (https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/2059, head `7a644a2dd246`, base develop) removes the `filePath` branch of `POST /hash` that this ticket describes, and the same branch of `/verify`, `/register-batch` and `/verify-batch`. The PR is keyed to KS-1410, because Kam's single card `secuura-ks-1410-ks-1214-mcp-rest-mirror-file-reads-1106` = a covers both tickets. Raised for its QA gate (tier 1); not merged, not deployed. This ticket stays open and its state, assignee and priority are unchanged.

**What the PR does to this ticket's findings:** a request that still sends `filePath` is refused with the fixed sentence `filePath is not accepted by this interface; send base64 content or a contentHash` and nothing is read; the `POST /hash` 500 no longer echoes the thrown text (the file-system error that told a caller whether a path exists); the published spec text and the deployment guides no longer offer the field. The deployed exposure that the ticket asked to measure first is still UNMEASURED, and the card says it does not matter: the change closes the hole whatever the exposure is.

**Not done:** a deploy of mcp-server on both boxes (demo frozen, nothing deployed); no client was exercised; the four platform suites were not run.

**BLUF:** QA gate 82 on pull request 1897 re-read this route at source (its finding G82-F2, Medium): `POST /hash` in `Blockchain/Dev/services/mcp-server/src/http-server.ts` still answers 500 with the thrown message, and for a bad `filePath` that message is Node's file-system text with the path the caller supplied (`ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<path>'`). Facts only, read from source, not run.

* Where: at develop `d7691f35312e` the catch is `:60`-`:63` and the leak is `message: message` at `:62`. In pull request 1897 the same lines sit 15 lower (a helper was added above them).
* It is the text pull request 1897 removes from the MCP tool `secuura_hash_document` (KS 1893), here over REST. Pull request 1897 does not change this route.
* KS 1410 left it on purpose: its part A and part B tests pin the route as untouched (cell C2: the file has ten 500 answers and `POST /hash` keeps `message: message`). A change to this route therefore also changes those two cells.
* This ticket's body already records that the route echoes `err.message` and that the exposure is unmeasured; that is unchanged here (whether the deployed port is reachable by untrusted callers was not checked).
* Fix shape, not chosen: log on the server and answer the constant `An unexpected error occurred` that the other nine 500 answers of the file use since KS 1410.

## BLUF

**QA gate 46 (on PR #1850, KS 1410) re-found this defect and measured it with local probes. It is wider than the original read: `filePath` is also read by `POST /verify` and `POST /verify-batch`. The server checks no credential, though its own spec declares one. A second item, the batch routes' per-item error text, is added here.** Exposure on the deployed boxes is still UNMEASURED.

Both items are the same path: how the mcp-server REST mirror (`http-server.ts`) handles untrusted input.

## Item 1: any server path is read, with no auth (re-read at develop `cb2320368ae4`)

1. **Gate 46's probes.** These ran on a local module over HTTP, against the code, not on a deployed box (F8 in Wednesday's `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-31_gate46-1848-1850/verdict.md`).
   - `POST /hash` with `/etc/hosts` answered 200 with the file's sha256.
   - `/etc` answered 500 `EISDIR`.
   - A missing path answered 500 `ENOENT ... '<path>'`.
   - So the server gives an existence and type oracle for its own filesystem, plus a hash of any readable file.
2. **`filePath` is read in four routes, not two.**
   - `POST /hash` (`http-server.ts:41-63`)
   - `POST /register-batch` (`http-server.ts:93-94`)
   - `POST /verify` (`http-server.ts:121-123`)
   - `POST /verify-batch` (`http-server.ts:152-154`)
   - Each calls `hashFile`, which is `readFile(filePath)` (`hashing.ts:5-6`).
3. **The packaged setup tells users to expose the server.** `package-generator.ts:196-208` writes "The HTTP server must be publicly accessible. Deploy it or use a tunnel:" and then `ngrok http 7890`.
4. **The spec declares a credential the server never checks.**
   - `services/mcp-server/openapi.yaml:20-28` sets a global `X-API-Key` requirement, so `/hash` and `/register-batch` read as protected.
   - `/verify` and `/verify-batch` are `security: []` (`openapi.yaml:243`, `openapi.yaml:262`).
   - `http-server.ts` mounts only `express.json` (`http-server.ts:29`) and `rejectNulBytes()` (`http-server.ts:33`), and no route reads a credential.
5. **A caller who reaches the port acts as the server's own key.** Upstream calls send the server's `SECUURA_API_KEY` (`api-client.ts:2`, `api-client.ts:28`), not anything the caller supplied.

**Exposure, re-read.**
- `docker-compose.yml:2146-2148` keeps the host port commented out (pen-test F-04). The container listens on 4023.
- The gateway forwards only `POST /api/mcp/generate-package` (`proxy.ts:1289-1314`).
- So by repo config the server is internal-only. **The deployed hosts are UNMEASURED.**

## Item 2: the batch routes echo each item's thrown text in a 200 (gate 46 F7, Minor)

- `POST /register-batch` (`http-server.ts:104-105`) and `POST /verify-batch` (`http-server.ts:163-164`) push `err.message` verbatim into `results[i].error`, inside a 200.
- Gate 46 measured three kinds of text in those fields:
  - upstream host and port (`SECRET-E gateway 10.0.0.7:6882`);
  - filesystem errno text (`ENOENT ... open '/nonexistent...'`, `EISDIR ... read '/etc'`);
  - a 2 MB message echoed in full, up to 50 items per call.
- `/verify-batch` is public in the spec (`security: []`).
- KS 1410 lists these two sites only as surface outside its count, and PR #1850 leaves them as they are.
- The gate's suggested shape: a constant per-item error, with the cause logged server-side.

## Provenance

- Seat S 9th re-read every file and line above at develop `cb2320368ae4`. The probe results in item 1.1 and item 2 are gate 46's, from the code, not from a box.
- Priority set to High on Wednesday's triage word, 2026-10-31.

title: Security: an absolute-form request target bypasses the KS-843 erasure door's scope/role gate (a connector without subjects:erase reaches originate)
description:
## BLUF

An absolute-form request target (`POST http://<any host>/api/gdpr/erasures`, and `/api/v1/` in production) **bypasses the KS-843 erasure door's scope/role gate**: it answers **200, and originate receives the POST, for a connector WITHOUT** `subjects:erase`. The origin-form control answers 403 with no upstream hit. The `GET` status read and the user role are bypassed the same way. A credential is still required: no credential or an invalid token answers 401. **Pre-existing:** base == head. Found by the tier-1 QA gate on PR #1011 (KS-871); **not caused by that PR**.

## Recommendation

Treat as Urgent until two conditions are measured (below). One of them is already READ as true: originate does not re-check the scope. Fix shape (the gate's, described, not authored): collapse repeated slashes only in the PATH part after the scheme/host, as `middleware/normalisePath.ts` does with `pathOffset`, or gate the door on `req.path` rather than `req.url`. Regression cells: an absolute-form erasure `POST` and `GET`, in test and production mode. **Not built.** Wednesday takes this to Kam; building waits for his word on priority.

## Detail

**Measured by the gate** (`Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks871-1011-0a1f8900c-tier1-r1/report.md`, finding F-1011-4; raw runs in `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks871-1011-0a1f8900c-tier1-r1/evidence/bypass_run.out`, replicated 2× on each of base/head × NODE_ENV test/production). Setup: a connector without `subjects:erase`, `SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED=true`, a real app with a recording upstream.

| request | test (base = head) | production (base = head) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| CONTROL `POST /api/gdpr/erasures` | 403, no upstream | 307 → 403, no upstream |
| `POST http://127.0.0.1/api/gdpr/erasures` | **200, originate hit** | 307 → 403 |
| `POST http://127.0.0.1/api/v1/gdpr/erasures` | **200, hit** | **200, hit** |
| `POST http://qa-anything.invalid/api/v1/gdpr/erasures` (any host) | **200, hit** | **200, hit** |
| user role, `POST http://127.0.0.1/api/gdpr/erasures` | **200, hit** | 307 → 403 |
| `GET http://127.0.0.1/api/v1/gdpr/erasures/abc` (status read) | **200, hit** | **200, hit** |
| CONTROL absolute-form, no credential / invalid token | 401 / 401 | 307 → 401 |
| CONTROL origin-form WITH the scope | 200, hit | 307 → 200, hit |

**Suspected mechanism** (the gate's, READ, not instrumented): inside `router.use('/api/gdpr')`, `req.url` for an absolute-form target keeps its `http://host` prefix. The wrapper at `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:734-745` collapses `/{2,}` across the whole `req.url`, turning `http://h/erasures` into `http:/h/erasures`. The door's `/erasures` mount (`proxy.ts:726-728`) then never matches, and the catch-all `router.use('/api/gdpr', authenticateToken(true), proxy)` forwards the request.

**Severity conditions** (the seat A successor's READS, 2026-09-17, develop `1125607e9`):

1. **Does originate re-check** `subjects:erase`**? READ: NO.**
   * `services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts:164` runs `gdprRouter.use(authenticate())`, and the erasure routes are `gdprRouter.post('/erasures', requireRole(...CONNECTOR_ROLES), …)` (`:488`) and `gdprRouter.get('/erasures/:externalRef', requireRole(...CONNECTOR_ROLES), …)` (`:523`), with `CONNECTOR_ROLES = ['connector']` (`:431`).
   * The string `subjects:erase` appears nowhere in `services/originate/src` (git grep at the tip; the only hits are in api-gateway).
   * So a connector token WITHOUT the scope that reaches originate **executes** `gdpr.executeErasureByExternalRef` (`:498`).
   * The user-role bypass reaches originate, but originate refuses it by role (READ; not driven against a real originate).
   * Instrument that closes this: drive a scope-less connector through a real originate and check the erasure ran.
2. **Does the edge forward an absolute-form target to the gateway? UNMEASURED.**
   * Local and production compose publish NO gateway host port (`docker-compose.yml` api-gateway: "No external ports — accessed via nginx-gateway at /api/"; `docker-compose.production.yml`: "No external ports; all traffic flows through nginx-gateway").
   * Every nginx front proxies `/api/` as `proxy_pass http://api_gateway_pool$request_uri;` (`docker/nginx-gateway/nginx.conf:184-185`, `nginx-demo.conf:401`, `nginx-production.conf:337`). Whether nginx's `$request_uri` keeps the `http://host` of an absolute-form request line decides it. I believe nginx parses scheme and host apart from the URI (so it would forward origin-form), but **that is not measured**.
   * The VM demo fronts nginx with Caddy (`deployment/caddy/Caddyfile:34`, `reverse_proxy localhost:6882`). Caddy is also expected to re-emit origin-form. **Not measured.**

title: workflow-approve persists the instance approved before the forward, so a refused forward strands it: re-approve and reject answer 400, no re-forward path, the kept document unusable until TTL (KS-1087 gate F2)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/workflow-instances/:id/approve` persists the instance `approved` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:970-972`) BEFORE it forwards the pending document to originate. So after any refused forward the workflow is stranded:

* a retry answers 400 "Workflow already completed" and never forwards (originate hits 0);
* reject answers 400;
* there is no re-forward path;
* the kept pending document stays unusable (403 `PENDING_APPROVAL`, relayed) until its Redis TTL.

The persist-before-forward predates PR #1008. Before #1008 the same input also reached `approved` and silently deleted the pending document; #1008 (merged `f7c2f4acb28875e3665a61c8eaaad5c54bd3aa55`) keeps the document and answers 502, which makes the strand visible and recoverable in principle.

## Recommendation

A design call beside KS-1087 item 2, not a fix round on #1008. Two shapes:

* persist `approved` only after originate answers 2xx; or
* add a re-forward / retry path for an `approved` instance whose pending document still exists.

Regression test (the gate's): a stateful store, originate 401 then 201 → the second attempt forwards and deletes exactly once.

## Detail

Found by the tier-1 QA gate (round 1) on PR #1008 (Part of KS-1087, item 1) at `dd7086d5aa574285beffc515f9371a438621f25d`, 2026-09-17. Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1087-1008-dd7086d5a-tier1-r1/report.md`, Findings F2 and item 3.

**F2, verbatim from the report's findings table:** "Stranded `approved` instance. After any refused forward the instance is `approved`, re-approve/reject 400, no re-forward path, and the kept document is unusable until its TTL. The persist at `:970-972` predates #1008; base reaches the same instance state and silently loses the document."

* Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME (stateful store); the downstream 403 is RELAYED.
* Gate severity: **Major** (product state; data orphaned). Reach NOT ESTABLISHED: it depends on workflow-gated document types existing, and on KS-1087 item 2 (originate answering 401 today is relayed from the #951 r2 report).

**Measured rows (item 3):** approve with originate 401, then originate fixed to 201 and approve again, then reject.

* stateful store, head / merged / production / development: 1st approve **502**, hits 1, delete 0, pending kept, instance `approved` · 2nd approve **400 "Workflow already completed"**, hits **0** · reject **400** "…cannot be rejected" · final: instance `approved`, pending document kept, never forwarded.
* stateful store, base `93629700c`: 1st approve **200**, hits 1, **delete 1** (document lost; originate refused) · 2nd 400, hits 0 · reject 400 · final: instance `approved`, no document, pending deleted.

**Not tested (report):** the downstream 403 `PENDING_APPROVAL` on sign/anchor/share and `GET /api/documents/:id` answering `pending_approval` for a stranded document (relayed from the drafter's read); the Redis TTL value (`TTL.workflow * 24` at `redis.ts:565/603` was read, `TTL.workflow` was not); true concurrency on the final step.

## BLUF
Record from the tier-1 QA gate on PR #1010 (KS-1183, merged as `1125607e9`), for whoever designs this ticket's fix. After a lost 201, the gateway answers **502 with the pending document kept while originate's copy exists**. A caller retry answers **400 "Workflow already completed"**, so a retry makes **no duplicate**. **Any re-forward path this ticket adds must send a `documentUuid`, or it will mint a second document.** No state change here.

## Recommendation
If the fix is "re-forward an approved instance whose pending document still exists", make the forward idempotent. Send a stable `documentUuid` (for example the pending document id), so that originate's KS-596 idempotency answers 200 with the existing row instead of creating another.

## Detail
Measured by the gate (report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1183-1010-c3213b04e-tier1-r1/report.md`, section 5, Record R1), at the head and on the merged tree:
- `O-late-201-persist-then-lost+retry`: 502 at 804 ms, pending document KEPT, originate created 1, instance `approved`. The caller's retry answered 400 "Workflow already completed", and originate hits stayed at 1.
- Base: 200 + delete at 1,503 ms. No residual, but no bound either.
- Worse than the base only in one band. If originate takes 15–30 s, the base answered a truthful late 200, while the head now answers 502 though originate's copy exists. If originate is slower than the proxy (over 30 s in production), the base already answered nginx 504 plus a later delete, so the head is not worse. Any bound under the proxy's forces that trade.

Read at source by the gate (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:616-648`): originate is idempotent only on a caller-supplied `documentUuid` (KS-596: same hash → 200 with the existing document; a different hash → 409). The gateway's forward payload in `routes/verification.ts` is `{ title, documentType, description, contentHash, data }` and carries **no** `documentUuid`.

Nothing deployed.

title: Anchor / originate / lifecycle-event schemas: accept and anchor platform-s's non-PII actor + organisation identity fields (actorDid, actorLevel, actorSource, actorVerified, orgDid, orgTrust, orgVerified) beside identityCommitment
description:
## What platform-s needs

Follow-on to [KS-721](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-721/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-opaque-identitycommitment) (which accepted `metadata.identityCommitment`). Platform-S now needs the Cardano record to **show** who acted and at what identity level, for the actor and their organisation — readable, not only committed. The S-side ruling on what is allowed in clear is [PS-869](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-869/5-decision-the-on-chain-identity-record-did-level-source-and-verified) (decision) under epic [PS-864](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-864/epic-id-status-stored-and-shown-throughout-the-system-actor-and); the field list there is the contract:

| Field | Type | Pattern / values |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `actorDid` | string ≤ 512 | `^did:(key|web):[A-Za-z0-9._:%-]+$` |
| `actorLevel` | integer | `1`, `2`, `3` — NIST 800-63A IAL alignment |
| `actorSource` | string | `platform` | `stripe` | `entra-verified-id` |
| `actorVerified` | boolean |  |
| `orgDid` | string ≤ 512 | as `actorDid` |
| `orgTrust` | string | `unverified` | `domain` | `document` | `kyc` | `government` |
| `orgVerified` | boolean |  |
| `identityCommitment` | string ≤ 128 | already accepted ([KS-721](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-721/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-opaque-identitycommitment)); the `vN` will move to `v2` |

All optional; all non-PII (DIDs are pseudonymous, levels and sources are enumerations, no dates, no names, no emails). Consistent with [KS-240](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-240/strict-by-default-on-chain-minimisation-strip-issuername-any-human) — no free text, nothing recoverable to a natural person.

## Suggested work

1. Accept the block as `metadata.identity` (or flat under `metadata` — say which) on **every** endpoint S anchors through: `POST /api/anchors`, `POST /api/documents` (originate), `POST /{id}/version`, `POST /{id}/anchor`, `POST /{id}/share`, `POST /{id}/transfer-custody`, `POST /api/certifications/issue`, `POST /{id}/lifecycle-events`. Today `anchorSchema.ts` strips unknown keys, so S will not send until K is live (the [PS-612](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-612/rename-the-certify-verb-to-declare-across-s) ordering).
2. Carry it into the on-chain record beside `documentType` / `occurredAt` / `identityCommitment`.
3. Return it in provenance / verify / anchor-status responses so S can render "on chain: Level 2, entra-verified-id" beside its local snapshot and flag any mismatch.
4. **State which existing request fields reach Cardano metadata**: `holderEmail`, `recipients[].email`, `newHolderEmail`, `onBehalfOf.email` / `displayName`. S sends these today; the requirement is that no PII is stored on the blockchain. If any of them is written to chain metadata, file the defect and link it here.
5. OpenAPI spec + Schemathesis / Akto examples updated in the same PR ([KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage) pattern), and both K-side testing HTML docs.

## Ordering

**K deploys first**, then PS-870 adds the fields on the S request. Pair-test from S against K on paired slots (S slot N ↔ K slot N) and quote the counts.
