**BLUF:** Facts only; the ticket stays In Progress. The fresh-database sweep owed on this ticket is done, on a throw-away PostgreSQL. At develop `4ccdc3b3e7cf` this ticket's own defect does **not** reproduce: after boot 1 on a bare database `users.tenant_isolation` is in the fail-closed form, `038a` and `039` are recorded, `auth_find_oauth_app_by_client_id` exists, and as the NOBYPASSRLS app role `secuura_app` a witness row is invisible to an unset tenant and to another tenant (0 / 0) and visible to its own (1), for `users` and `certifications`. The same harness at the pre-fix merge-base `0d156d12` reproduces the old shape. The sweep also found a neighbouring window, filed as KS 2039: `rights_holders` has no RLS and no `tenant_id` until boot 2, on a bare database. The migrations image rebuild was not run.

**Method.** develop `4ccdc3b3e7cf` and the merge-base `0d156d12`, each fetched by sha. A throw-away PostgreSQL 15.19 (Homebrew) on a unix socket only: 0 inet sockets by `lsof`, with a positive control that sees 1. A bare database per tree and per runner (no `docker/init` scripts), two boots each, with both product runners: the gateway's `runStartupMigrations` via tsx (pg 8.23.0, tsx 4.23.15, the gateway lock's versions; `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` unset) and `scripts/run-migrations.sh`, unmodified. After each boot, one read-only catalog read, then a witness read as `secuura_app` (`rolsuper` f, `rolbypassrls` f): witness rows inserted as the owner inside one transaction, counted as `secuura_app` with the tenant setting unset, set to another tenant, and set to the row's tenant, then rolled back (0 left behind, read back). The read is the database, not the exit code.

**Results** (counts are `unset / another tenant / own tenant`; the owner sees every witness):

| Scenario | Failed on that boot | `users` form | `039` | function | `tenant_isolation` policies | `users` | `certifications` | `rights_holders` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| develop, gateway runner, boot 1 | 006, 008, 026, 027, 028 | fail-closed | recorded | present | 25 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 1 / 1 / 1 (RLS off, no `tenant_id`) |
| develop, gateway runner, boot 2 | none | fail-closed | recorded | present | 25 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 (own setting `app.tenant_id`: B=0, A=1; RLS on) |
| develop, `run-migrations.sh`, boot 1 | 006, 008, 026, 027, 028 (exit 3) | fail-closed | recorded | present | 25 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 | table absent |
| develop, `run-migrations.sh`, boot 2 | 026, 027, 028 (exit 3) | fail-closed | recorded | present | 25 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 | table absent |
| merge-base `0d156d12`, gateway runner, boot 1 | 006, 008, 026, 027, 028, 039, 047 | FAIL-OPEN | not recorded | ABSENT | 20 | 1 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 0 (forced RLS, 0 policies: deny-all) | 1 / 1 / 1 (RLS off, no `tenant_id`) |
| merge-base `0d156d12`, gateway runner, boot 2 | none | fail-closed | recorded | present | 24 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 (own setting `app.tenant_id`: B=0, A=1; RLS on) |
| merge-base `0d156d12`, `run-migrations.sh`, boot 1 | 006, 008, 026, 027, 028, 039, 047 (exit 3) | fail-closed | not recorded | ABSENT | 20 | 0 / 0 / 1 | table absent | table absent |
| merge-base `0d156d12`, `run-migrations.sh`, boot 2 | 006, 008, 026, 027, 028, 039, 047 (exit 3) | fail-closed | not recorded | ABSENT | 20 | 0 / 0 / 1 | table absent | table absent |

**Controls.**
- The non-RLS tracker table reads 41 to 59 as `secuura_app` in every scenario, so the instrument sees rows; the owner sees each witness; the rollback leaves 0 rows and the helper function gone.
- The merge-base tree on the same harness reproduces the old shape: gateway runner, boot 1, the seven original failures (`006`, `008`, `026`, `027`, `028`, `039`, `047`), `users.tenant_isolation` in the FAIL-OPEN form, the function absent, and the witness visible to an unset tenant (1). Boot 2 heals it. So the harness shows both states.
- The first witness run and the scripted rerun on the same boot-1 state are byte-identical; a rewritten witness script gave the same counts as its predecessor on an unchanged state.
- `rights_holders` after boot 2 is read with its own setting, `app.tenant_id` (its policy does not use `app.current_tenant_id`): another tenant 0, own tenant 1.

**What the two runners do differently** (measured):
- At the merge-base, a failed `039` under the gateway runner leaves `users` FAIL-OPEN after boot 1. Under `run-migrations.sh` the same failure leaves `users` already fail-closed, with the function absent and `039` unrecorded; `psql -f` without `--single-transaction` (READ in the script) would apply the statements before the failing one. The window this ticket describes is therefore the gateway-runner path.
- `run-migrations.sh` alone on a bare database has no CORE stage. At the merge-base that means `oauth_apps`, `svc_webhooks`, `certifications`, `charge_events` and `rights_holders` are never created (all absent after both boots, 7 failures on each); at the head `038a` creates the first four, and only `rights_holders` is still absent, so `026` to `028` fail on every boot (head: boot 1 `applied=55 failed=5`, boot 2 `applied=2 failed=3 skipped=55`). It exits 3 each time, at the merge-base and at the head; the description's "`run-migrations.sh` exits 0 when migrations fail" is out of date.

**Differences from the 2026-09-28 measurement.** That run used PostgreSQL 18.3; this one uses 15.19, the major version compose pins (`postgres:15-alpine`). It read 22 `tenant_isolation` policies at the merge-base; this harness reads 20 (not investigated). At the fix it read 25; this harness reads 25. A fresh database at the head carries 25, the same as Kintsugi; demo reads 26 (comment of 2026-11-05), so demo's extra policy does not come from a fresh build. A data point, not an investigation.

**What this does not show.**
- "Bare" means the `docker/init` scripts did not run. Compose mounts `./docker/init` into Postgres's init directory (READ, `docker-compose.yml:159`), so a compose-initialised database starts with tables this run had to wait for. Not run.
- The migrations image rebuild (needs Docker) was not run.
- Not run: `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` and per-tenant databases (the KS 1055 path), traffic across a real boot gap, PostgreSQL 18, Node 24 (the harness ran on Node v26.8.1).
- Two harness adaptations, both in the harness and not in product code: a PATH shim points `run-migrations.sh`'s TCP-only `pg_isready` probe at the unix socket, and the compose grants from `docker/init/01-create-app-role.sh` were applied to `secuura_app` after each sh-runner boot (the gateway runner provisions its own). The script wrote its fixed `/tmp/migrate-err.log`; copies are in the record.
- Whether any deployed database ran without the init scripts is UNMEASURED, and no real row was written across a boot gap by this work (KS 2039 states the same).

**Against the Done rule** (unit tests on develop plus the fix in the running Kintsugi build): the 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-05 comments already show the six PRs merged, reachable from the Kintsugi deploy, and `038a` and `039` recorded on Kintsugi and demo. This run adds the item those comments left unrun, `039` and `038a` on a bare database across two boots and `certifications` read as the app role, on a disposable database. It does not cover the image rebuild, and it adds KS 2039, which this ticket's fix does not claim to cover. I changed no ticket state.

Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatC-35th/evidence/` (`ks1054_matrix.md`, `*_boot1_*`, `*_boot2_*`, `cluster_proof.txt`), tools in `tools/`.

PR #1348 raised against `develop`, head `1bb58b4ebb97`, base `8ba2da02d980`.

This is the half PR #1346 did not carry. `verify_deployment()` in `deploy.sh` counted its errors and then returned 0, because its last command was a log line — so the deploy read as successful over failed startup migrations. PR #1346 raised against `develop`, head `2075c3ec7078`, base `0aa9b52c691b`.

Push preflight: 12/15 legs ran, 3 skipped (legs 3, 4, 8 — local stack not up), nothing failed. That is not a pass and is recorded as a ratio.

Not covered: the deploy scripts were not run against any real environment, and no migration was run against a real database. A live sweep is owed on this runtime change, so this ticket stays In Progress.

Merged 0de108577e6199de3c9402c0643a2944d86aee97 (PR #1332, migrations/038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql); offline gates green; NOT Done per secuura-test-discipline §5f — live sweep owed (torn-down rebuilt stack, all containers verified up), unverified: 039 and 038a on a bare Azure database across two boots, certifications as the app role (secuura_app; default-deny N-G39-1), and the migrations image rebuild

**Round 2 of 2 pushed to #1332 — head `f2423bf7aa6c64952cf425d4160a048a55ffaaee`** (fast-forward from `f5381338359d`, base `develop`).

Round 1 was NO GO on the gate's `N-1332-1` blocker. This commit fixes N-1332-1, N-1332-2 and N-1332-3 together.

**N-1332-1 — fix shape (b), chosen on a measurement.** A new file migration `038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` creates `oauth_apps`, `svc_webhooks`, `certifications` and `charge_events` before 039 runs, so 039 finds them present on its only pass. | tree | 039 recorded | `auth_find_oauth_app_by_client_id(text)` | policy | `tenant_isolation` policies | four tables |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| merge-base `0d156d12` | 0 (039 fails) | ABSENT | 0 | 22 | 0 |
| round-1 head `f5381338` | 1 | **ABSENT** | 0 | 22 | 0 |
| this commit | 1 | **PRESENT** | 1 | 25 | 4 |

The DDL is derived from `CORE_MIGRATIONS` at develop `215cc6875e2b` and proved schema-identical to it by `pg_dump --schema-only`, because shape (b) creates a second creator of the same tables.

**N-1332-2** — both CORE-stage catches never touched `totalFailed`, so a stage that died was served as `failed: 0`. **N-1332-3** — `error?` was declared and never passed; `applyFileMigrations` now returns a `firstError` the way `migrateDatabase` already did.

api-gateway **88 files / 795 tests, 0 failed**. Tests-including tsc **29 → 29, delta 0**. Arms **3/3** red their own cell. Push preflight **12 of 15 legs, 3 skipped** — not a pass, stated as a ratio.

**Not in this commit:** `N-1332-5` (the deploy scripts still do not read the `startupMigrations` field) — named unraised, not dropped. `N-1332-4` is not commissioned. A deploy must rebuild **both** the migrations image and the api-gateway image; nothing has been deployed.

**F-928-3 — the section of this ticket marked UNMEASURED is now measured. Split out to KS-1055.**

**BLUF: confirmed, and it is a different defect from this one.** KS-1054 is a *window* — a fresh DB is fail-open until boot 2, then heals. What I measured on a genuinely separate tenant DB does not heal on any boot: the file-migration stage never runs against a tenant database at all, so `_secuura_migrations` **does not exist** there after three boots (control: 48 rows on the main DB, same reader).

**And the consequence is the opposite sign from this ticket's.** CORE_MIGRATIONS `ENABLE`s and `FORCE`s RLS on five tables (`startup-migrations.ts:439-440, 485-486, 551-552, 633-634`) while `CREATE POLICY` appears **0 times** in that whole file (control: 19 in `migrations/*.sql`). A tenant DB therefore lands with FORCE RLS and **zero policies** — not fail-open, **deny-all**. Measured as a `NOBYPASSRLS` non-superuser role: 0 rows from `documents`/`certifications`/`audit_logs`, and still 0 with both GUCs set, while the same role reads 1 from a non-RLS table in the same database (non-zero control) and the row is provably there under `row_security=off`.

**Scope, both directions:** latent today — `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` defaults false, so every tenant points at the shared app DB, which does get the files. It goes live the moment per-tenant DBs are provisioned, i.e. exactly when KS-160 Path A ships.

**Ordering matters to whoever fixes either one:** on my fresh main DB, boot 1 failed 7 file migrations including **`039_rls_fail_closed.sql` → `type "oauth_apps" does not exist`**, and boot 2 applied them — this ticket's window, reproduced. A tenant arm added to `applyFileMigrations` without fixing that ordering just reproduces KS-1054 inside every tenant DB instead of fixing anything.

title: develop is RED on the services/originate jest suite and NOTHING catches it — the suite is a blocking gate nowhere automated
description:
## BLUF

`develop` **is RED on the** `services/originate` **jest suite right now, and no instrument in this repository objects.** Measured tonight: 2 of 4 cells in `ks444-webhooks-create-description-guard.test.ts` fail on develop's own blob. **The suite is a blocking gate NOWHERE automated**, so the mainline can be red indefinitely and nothing says so.

Filed on Wednesday's ruling as a **new** ticket rather than folded into KS-961, because KS-961 is In Review and adding scope to an in-review ticket either reopens reviewed work or buries the new scope under a review that never covered it.

## The measurement

```
npx jest src/__tests__/ks444-webhooks-create-description-guard.test.ts   (in services/originate)
  2 passed   the two NEGATIVE cells (400s an object, 400s a null)
  2 FAILED   both POSITIVES - expected 201, received 500
  EXIT=1
```

Run on blobs verified byte-identical to develop: the test file is `229a3ccde` at both `origin/develop` and `b6884888d`; `routes/webhooks.ts` is `c88eb97db` at both. **PR #926 is the fix and it is open and unmerged**, blocked on an approval.

**Scope of the redness, which the QA gate did not measure:** the full service run is **48 suites / 509 tests, 1 suite / 2 tests failed** — the ks444 positives are the *only* failures in the whole service. ⚠ That run covers **48 of develop's 49** originate suites: it was executed on a tree missing `ks754-processed-by-widened.test.ts`, which is **unswept and named rather than rounded away**.

## Why nothing catches it — four instruments, each checked with a control

| instrument | originate/jest | control on the same file |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` (13 legs, 428 lines) | **0 hits** | `step` -> 18 hits |
| `.githooks/pre-push` (244 lines) | **0 hits** | `preflight` -> 18 hits |
| 17 GitHub workflows | only `ci.yml` + `deploy-demo.yml` invoke workspace tests, **both** `workflow_dispatch`**-only** | 17 mention `test` |
| the 7 `pull_request`-triggered workflows | **none runs any service unit suite** | read their `run:` steps individually |

**This conclusion does not depend on the Actions billing state.** Even with Actions fully funded, no PR-triggered workflow invokes this suite. Actions being retired (Kam, 2026-08-27) is a second, independent reason.

## The actual gap

**The only instrument that would ever catch a red mainline is a human filling in a Test Evidence line — and it only fires if a PR happens to touch that service.** `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` requires `**Unit suites (touched services):** run/result | not run + why`. A suite that is red on develop and untouched by the current PR is invisible to that, by construction.

## The precedent that makes this concrete

`DEV-PROCESS.md` **has already made this exact argument once, for a different subject, and acted on it.** Cross-cutting guards get their own Test Evidence line specifically because, under "run `npm test` in the touched service", they *"execute only when someone touches* `shared`*, which is the change least likely to add a fifteenth service error handler"* — and it concludes **"A guard on no path that runs is not a guard."**

**The same argument applies to a red mainline suite, and nothing currently makes it.**

## Fix shapes (not a ruling - the cheapest is probably the third)

1. A preflight leg that runs the touched service's unit suite, so a red mainline blocks the next push that goes near it.
2. A periodic mainline run whose only job is to answer "is develop green" - no PR coupling.
3. A **baseline-diff** rule in the Test Evidence block: the author records develop's own result for the suites they ran, so "2 failed" is visibly pre-existing rather than silently attributed to the change. This is the same shape KS-660 already applies to Schemathesis ("the failing SET ... + its diff vs the develop baseline set, never a bare count").

## Related

* **KS-961** - the aggregate workspace suite never runs on a PR. Adjacent, In Review, deliberately not extended.
* **KS-1046** - `PREFLIGHT PASSED` printed identically whether 13 legs ran or 10. Same family: a claim whose check did not run.
* **KS-927 / PR #926** - the fix for the red itself.

## Ask

**Kam or Wednesday to pick a fix shape** (or rule that the red simply waits for #926 and no instrument changes). Nothing here is urgent in the sense of a live outage - it is urgent in the sense that the next person to read a green board about `originate` will be reading a false one.

*Filed by s162 (Platform K), 2026-09-09, on Wednesday's ruling. Measurement is mine and reproducible from the commands above.*

**Carried here from KS-826 — closed as Duplicate of this ticket and archived on 2026-09-14 (s222), under Kam's 2026-09-14 08:55 standing rule (true duplicates are closed and archived by us, no external review).** KS-826's surviving clause — its 2026-09-07 comment 920f558b gave the ks444 red to KS-927 and kept the ticket open ONLY for "no gate ever runs the four service suites" — is this ticket's ask.

What KS-826 held that this ticket did not:
- **The scope is every `services/*` unit suite, not originate alone.** Measured at `0e8d3e60a` / `055182bfe`: `referral` 5 suites / 26 tests · `staking` 3 / 61 · `vc-issuer` 8 / 86 · `originate` 44 / 476 — all otherwise green at the head, all unread by any gate. Whichever fix shape is picked above (a preflight leg / a periodic mainline run / a baseline-diff line), it covers the four, and KS-1146 (the `services/auth` instance) defers its decision here.
- **"Own it or gate it"** — KS-826's framing of the decision: (1) diagnose and fix the red so the suites are worth gating, or (2) add the suites to the gate and let the red block today; doing neither is the state to stop. Survivor: this ticket, by Wednesday's acceptance of the 2026-09-13 proposal's stated preference (it holds the measurement with four controlled instruments, the three fix shapes, the ask and the relations); KS-826 was the older id and its title still named the ks444 red it had given away.

title: No independent liveness signal for our own VMs — kintsugi was dead for 53 h and Azure health read `Available` the whole time
description:
## BLUF

`secuura02-kintsugi-vm` **was down for 53 hours and nothing told us. The first signal was Stuart's tooling — a person, not a monitor. And Azure's own platform health read** `Available` **for the whole 53 hours, which is why the one alerting surface we do have would not have fired either.**

Both halves are one logical path — *we have no independent liveness signal for our own VMs* — so they are one ticket per Kam's 2026-09-06 aggregation rule, not two.

## What happened

* Azure live-migrated the VM at **2026-09-07T03:56:13Z** (`PlatformInitiated`, *"paused 0.993s, memory-preserving"*). The guest did not survive it.
* The workload died at ~**04:00Z**. On-disk logs **stop at 03:55:01Z** with **zero** entries for 53 h (control: **53** entries in the same hour).
* It came back only because a person went looking on **2026-09-09**, and was force-reset at **09:31:45Z**.

## Half 1 — no liveness signal

Nothing watches whether kintsugi is serving. There is no uptime check, no synthetic request, no alert on absence of logs. Detection was **incidental**.

⚠ This is the same shape as **KS-670** (demo's on-chain verification down **6 days**, found by a person). Two incidents, same missing control. That is the argument for fixing the class rather than the instance.

## Half 2 — the alerting surface we DO have was lying

Azure marked the box **Available at 03:59:30Z** and said *"no additional action is required"* — while the guest was dead and stayed dead for 53 hours. `memory-preserving` migration means **no reboot**, so Caddy survived in memory and kept answering at the edge while sshd, the guest agent and dockerd were all gone.

**So a health check that trusts either Azure resource health OR a naive port-200 on the front door would have reported green throughout.** Any monitor built here has to make a request that actually traverses the app, and has to alert on **silence** (no logs / no successful synthetic) rather than on an error, because a dead guest produces no errors at all — it produces nothing.

## Why this is due now

The incident record is closed (`5_Project_History/HANDOVER-kintsugi-outage-CLOSED.md`). **Recurrence is not** — Azure live-migrates this box as routine platform behaviour and the guest does not survive one. Boot diagnostics / serial console is now **ENABLED**, so a repeat leaves evidence; nothing currently tells us the repeat *happened*.

## Suggested shape (not a decision — the approach is open)

1. An external liveness check per VM (demo + kintsugi) that traverses the app, not just the edge — the front door answered while the box was dead.
2. Alert on **absence** — no successful synthetic in N minutes, or no new log lines — not on error responses.
3. Do **not** key anything off Azure resource health alone. This incident is the counter-example, in our own record.

## What is NOT established

* Whether the demo VM has the same exposure — **not measured**; it is the same subscription and region and probably does, but I did not check.
* The remount-read-only theory for the guest's death is **strongly supported, not proven**: no kernel message survived, because it could not be written to the disk it was about.

## Provenance

Azure activity log (read in slices — the API truncates silently at 50), the guest's own journal, `df` 37% and a clean `fsck` refuting ENOSPC and corruption from inside. Recorded by s160, filed by s161.

title: tests/e2e auth-exhaustive races its OWN lockout — same commit gives 1 or 11 failures, so the suite cannot gate anything
description:
## BLUF

`tests/e2e/tests/auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` **is non-deterministic against an unchanged product.** It brute-forces logins, `playwright.config.ts` sets `fullyParallel: true`, and every run leaves **4** `lockout:*` **keys** in redis — so its own ordinary login cells race its own lockout. Until this is fixed the suite cannot be used as a gate, because a failure count carries no information.

## Measured — 2026-09-09, `develop` `b6884888d`, `lockout:*` cleared before EACH run

| run | command | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| A | three specs | **23 failed / 54 passed** |
| B | three specs | **11 failed / 71 passed** |
| C | `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` alone | **1 failed / 52 passed** |
| D | `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` alone | **11 failed / 42 passed** |

**Nothing about the product changed between any of them.** Lockout keys were counted after every run: 4 each time, so the suite reliably creates them and unreliably outruns them.

**The flapping cells move as ONE block** — both 23-failure runs carried exactly the same 23, which is what rules out twelve independent flakes and points at a single shared cause. They are all in `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts`: 2.1.1–2.1.5, 2.2.8, 2.2.9, 2.8.1, 2.9.1, 2.9.2, 2.9.4, 2.9.5.

**The deterministic remainder is 10 recruitment/wallet cells** (red in 5 of 5 runs) plus `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts:734`, whose assertion is wrong rather than the app — filed separately.

## Suggested fix (not prescribed)

Either serialise this file (`test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })` or a dedicated non-parallel project), or give the brute-force cells a **dedicated account** so they cannot lock the fixture persona the rest of the file logs in with. The second is likely better: it keeps the parallelism and removes the coupling.

## Class

This is the **KS-724** family — a harness that stops testing while still producing results. There, a scan evicted its own bearer; here, a suite locks out its own persona.

## Provenance

* the four runs, lockout counts, and the identical 23-cell block | measured live on the local stack, recorded in `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/BASELINE.md` | 2026-09-09
* Filed from KS-734's baseline work (s160), which made the suite installable and could then measure it.

title: The merge gate cannot see a WITHDRAWN approval — #813 reads approved+clean against the reviewer's written refusal
description:
## BLUF

**A reviewer can withdraw an approval and BOTH GitHub instruments keep reporting the PR as approved.** The repo's merge gate is *"approval is the signal, the author merges"* (CLAUDE.md, Kam 2026-08-25). On PR #813 that gate currently reads GREEN against the reviewer's explicit written refusal.

## The instance

Peter, on #813 (KS-791, verify-file):

* **14:52:21Z 2026-09-08** — submitted `APPROVED` at `54225cbbd`
* **14:56:21Z 2026-09-08** — submitted `COMMENTED` at the same commit: *"My earlier approval on this PR was premature and I'm withdrawing it — I'll ask a maintainer to dismiss it, since I can't retract it myself."*

Nobody dismissed it. Measured today:

| instrument | reads #813 as |
| -- | -- |
| `GET /pulls/813/reviews` | `PeterObeden: APPROVED`, `commit_id == head.sha` -> **at-head approval** |
| search index `is:pr is:open review:approved` | **matches #813** |
| `mergeable_state` | `clean` |
| Peter's own prose | **withdrawn, holding for complete systemTest evidence** |

`commit_id == head.sha` **does not catch this.** That discriminator exists for a *stale* approval — one the head moved past. A **withdrawn** approval sits at the head, because the head never moved. The check we rely on is blind to it by construction.

## It is not a one-off — swept, with the arithmetic closed

Across all **43** open PRs, exactly **two** carry an `APPROVED` later followed by a `COMMENTED` review from the same reviewer: **#813** and **#785**. Both comment bodies say *"holding"*. No others.

* **#785** (KS-229) — also holding; there the last `APPROVED` sits at a **superseded** commit, so the `commit_id` check *does* catch it — but the **search index still counts it approved**.
* So the index's headline **"10 approved"** is really **8**.

## Why it matters

A withdrawn approval is invisible to every automated read of this repo's merge gate. The only instrument that sees it is the reviewer's prose. Any session — human or agent — that clears the queue by "approved + clean" will merge #813 against a written refusal.

## Checklist

- [ ] Ask a maintainer to **dismiss** the stale `APPROVED` on #813 (Peter asked for this on 2026-09-08 and it has not happened)
- [ ] Same for #785's superseded approvals
- [ ] Add the withdrawn-approval case to the boot/pre-merge sweep: an `APPROVED` is only live if **no later review from the same user exists at or after it** — not merely `commit_id == head.sha`
- [ ] Write the rule into `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` next to the existing at-head paragraph, which currently names only staleness as the failure mode
- [ ] Decide whether a `CHANGES_REQUESTED` should be the house convention for withdrawal, since GitHub gives a reviewer no retract action

## Provenance

`/pulls/{n}/reviews` for all 43 open PRs + `search/issues` index counts (10 approved / 2 changes_requested / 30 none = 42 open at sweep time, +#918 opened during the session = 43). Measured 2026-09-09 by the Platform K s159 seat.

The description still lists five unchecked items when read today, among them asking a maintainer to dismiss the stale APPROVED on #813 and the superseded approvals on #785, and nothing on the ticket records them done.

`GET /pulls/813/reviews` at 09:14Z: `5143298493` APPROVED and `5143348040` COMMENTED ("Holding my approval… withdrawing it"), both at `commit_id 54225cbbd` while the head is `7b6fb960d` (s226's 2026-09-14 07:14Z push: the unpushed 09-11 head `7be1eccbe` plus develop M38 merged in). title: Security: 9 trust-header reads outside auth middleware (pen-test F-04) — surfaced by wiring check-no-trust-header-reads.sh in KS-926
description:
**Found by RUNNING a guard that had never run.** KS-926 wired the `check-*.sh` guards; this one had no live entry point, so its findings had never been seen. Its default level is `fail`, so it is red the moment anything invokes it.

## The 9, verbatim from the guard

```
services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1041  req.headers['x-tenant-id']
services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1042  req.headers['x-tenant-slug']
services/security/src/index.ts:968                    req.headers['x-tenant-id']
services/prism/src/index.ts:111                       req.headers['x-tenant-id']
services/originate/src/index.ts:230                   req.headers['x-tenant-id']
services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts:42          req.headers['x-user-role'] === 'connector' && x-tenant-id
services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts:43          req.headers['x-user-id']  -> sets (req as any).user
services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts:45          req.headers['x-tenant-id'] -> sets (req as any).tenantId
packages/shared/src/db/tenant-guc.ts:119              req.headers['x-tenant-id']
```

`metering.ts:42-45` **is the one to look at first:** it builds `req.user` and `req.tenantId` **from headers**, gated only on `x-user-role === 'connector'`. That is the trust-header vulnerability in its literal form if the header is reachable from outside.

## The guard's own instruction

> Use `req.user.*` (set by `authenticate()` middleware) instead of `req.headers['x-user-*']`. Direct header reads re-introduce the trust-header vulnerability.

The guard already excludes legitimate middleware paths (`/middleware/auth.ts`, `authenticate.ts`, `scopes.ts`, `tenant*`, `db/tenant-context.ts`, `security/gdpr-compliance.ts`) and lines marked `F-04-allowed`, so **these 9 are outside the sanctioned set by the guard's own definition.**

## Triage needed per site

Some may be legitimate **forwarding** (api-gateway 1041-42 sets `forwardHeaders`, which is a different act from trusting) and should carry `F-04-allowed` with a reason. Others look like real trust. **Do not bulk-annotate** — that converts a finding into a silence.

## Blocks

`check-no-trust-header-reads.sh` cannot be wired into the pre-push gate until this is 0 or the legitimate sites are annotated. Related: KS-619 (gateway tenant resolution falling through to the caller's `x-tenant-id`), and KS-926.

nodes.body:
**KS-1600** carries an open question against this ticket's effect. The pull request 1547 round-2 gate (report `ccbe317fcbf769f3`) measured that a forged `x-tenant-id` sent **directly to originate's router** is honoured — `ORG_ADMIN(A1)` + `organizations:register` + `organizationId: A1` with `x-tenant-id: T2` returns 201 with the key stored in tenant T2. The gate's reading is that KS-1032, now on `develop` `92d1316ffe31cb13b3f7e843e7891225383b2f84`, shuts that path, because `gatewayProvenance` strips trust headers when `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is unset and the KS-458 resolution reads `x-tenant-id` only on a vouched request. **That is a reading, not a measurement** — the gate's harness mounts the router without `index.ts`'s middleware, so it was never run end to end.

The instrument that would settle it, recorded on KS-1600: one end-to-end request through originate's real middleware stack on `develop` `92d1316f`, `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` unset, forged `x-tenant-id: T2`, expecting the key to land in the caller's own tenant rather than T2.

Facts only; no state change asked for here.

## BLUF

- **Recorded from KS-1041, so this residual stays on a live ticket when KS-1041 closes.** KS-1041 wrote down that services other than originate also read trust headers, and that nobody had read their sites.
- **This ticket is the live home for that class:** trust-header reads outside auth middleware, triaged per site.
- **Not commissioned and not ruled.** KS-1041's two steps did not widen to these services.
  - Step 1: #938 → `0f8fb33c3` closed nginx `/originate/`.
  - Step 2: #951 is originate's gateway-provenance middleware. It stays inert while `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is unset (KS-1083).

## Recommendation

No action needed now. When this ticket's per-site triage runs, include the services KS-1041 named.

## Detail

- **KS-1041's wording, verbatim:**
  - `923cfb00` (2026-09-10): *"`api-gateway`, `auth`, `billing`, `prism`, `security` and `tokenisation` also read these headers. **I am not asserting they are safe — I have not read their sites.**"*
  - `116ed2d6`, and PR #951's *Not in scope*: *"the seven other services that read trust headers"*.
  - Six are named and "seven" is counted. Both are quoted as written; neither was re-measured here.
- **Overlap with this ticket's 9 sites:**
  - api-gateway, security and prism appear in both.
  - auth, billing and tokenisation do not appear here. This ticket's guard excludes middleware paths (`/middleware/auth.ts`, `authenticate.ts`, `tenant*`, and others), which may be why — not checked.
  - `originate/src/index.ts:230` and `routes/metering.ts:42-45` are the originate sites that #951's middleware covers once the secret is provisioned. Until then they behave as before.
- **Board searched before posting** (literal, live tickets only):
  - `trust headers` → KS-1041 only;
  - `x-user-role` → KS-1041 and KS-1032;
  - `x-tenant-id` → 8, of which KS-1032 is the only one about reads across services;
  - `header-reading` 0 · `seven other` 0.

title: KS-754 gate F-4: DEPLOY CONDITION — apply 048 BEFORE rolling the originate image, or every connector erasure shreds the DEK then aborts forever (and run-migrations.sh exits 0 when migrations fail)
description:
🔴 **THIS IS A DEPLOY CONDITION, not only a ticket. No deploy is authorised by the #914 gate.**

## The condition — for whoever rolls originate

**Apply migration 048 BEFORE rolling the originate image, and confirm** `processed_by` **is** `text` **in the target DB first.**

## What happens if you don't — driven, not theorised (gate scenario S2)

Head code against a DB where 048 has not landed: **every connector erasure anonymises the user, destroys the DEK, then aborts.** `USER_ERASED=0`, DSR left `processing`. The cause (`22P02`) is **not transient**, so the connector's unbounded retry **never** succeeds — each iteration re-runs steps 1–11. This turns the F-1 finding from transient into **deterministic**.

## Why the existing guard does not save you — and this is its own defect

`docker-compose.yml` **does** gate originate on `migrations: service_completed_successfully`. But `scripts/run-migrations.sh` **exits 0 when migrations fail, by design** (its own closing block; BACKLOG #6). **So compose's condition is satisfied by a run in which 048 failed.**

On **Azure** there is no such ordering at all: migrations run at **api-gateway** boot (`startup-migrations.ts`) while originate is a separate app.

## Fixes — two, and they are separable

1. The deploy-ordering condition above, recorded where a deployer reads it (PR body + `DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md` / the DR runbook), not only here.
2. `run-migrations.sh` **must not exit 0 on a failed migration** — that is a gate that cannot fail (KS-926 family), and it is what makes the compose guard decorative.

## Related

F-1 (same erasure path, made deterministic by this) and the KS-926 checks-that-cannot-fail campaign.

title: Reshape the advisory gate: it is NON-DETERMINISTIC on an unchanged tree — 8 advisories in 30 min, one appeared then vanished. Warn-then-fail, keyed on REACH and SEVERITY (window length is Kam's)
description:
## BLUF

**The advisory gate is NON-DETERMINISTIC ON AN UNCHANGED TREE.** Two runs of the same commit, minutes apart, give different verdicts — because it hard-fails on a dataset that a third party edits continuously and we do not control.

**That is a correctness problem, not a throughput one.** A gate that answers differently on identical input cannot distinguish *"this commit is unsafe"* from *"you ran it at the wrong minute"*.

**Kam ruled the reshape on 2026-09-09 (**`both`**): warn for a window, then hard-fail. The WINDOW LENGTH is explicitly reserved for him and is an open question at the foot of this ticket — it is not proposed here as a number.**

⚠ **And the design must be REACH- AND SEVERITY-AWARE, or it weakens the gate in the one case it exists for.** Detail in *The design constraint* below.

## The evidence — measured across three runs in about half an hour, 2026-09-09

```
run 1  ~21:4x   audit-locks  31 advisories match, 29 baselined   ->  2 missing
run 2  ~22:0x   audit-locks  32 advisories match, 31 baselined   ->  1 missing
run 3  ~22:15   audit-gate   37 reported,         34 baselined   ->  5 missing
```

**The arithmetic is closed, which is what makes this a measurement rather than an impression.** Between runs 1 and 2 exactly **two** baseline rows were added — 29 + 2 = 31, so the *baselined* count is fully explained. **The MATCH count still moved 31 → 32.** Nothing in the repo's dependencies changed: one JSON file was edited, touching zero `package.json` and zero lockfiles.

**Eight distinct advisories touched this repo in half an hour. Three were baselined. The gap widened while it was being closed.**

### 🔴 And one went the OTHER way — this is the part that makes it non-determinism

Between runs 2 and 3, `GHSA-2wm5-q62r-hmrv` (colord) **stopped being reported by the root gate entirely**. Its own output:

```
CLEANUP (advisory): 1 baseline entry is no longer reported — remove:
  - GHSA-2wm5-q62r-hmrv (colord, KS-1024)
```

**An advisory that blocked every push fifteen minutes earlier was no longer reported at all** — with no change on our side. **The dataset does not only grow. It churns.**

## Why the obvious fix is a trap

Baselining the current five turns the preflight green **now**. Run 3 proves that says nothing about run 4. **A green preflight after a triage round is evidence that the external set was quiet for one run, not that the tree is clean** — and the same three runs above show how long "quiet" lasts.

**Triage cannot outrun publication.** That is the loop this ticket exists to break.

## ⚠ The design constraint — a FLAT window would weaken the gate

Written flat, *"warn for a window, then hard-fail"* lets a **production-reaching** advisory sit unblocked for the whole window.

**That is not hypothetical, and the counter-example arrived the same morning the option was drafted:** `GHSA-8m3c-c648-2xjj` — nodemailer's `resolveContent()` bypassing `disableFileAccess`/`disableUrlAccess` on the legacy signature — is a **production dependency of** `services/auth` **and** `services/originate`, the two services that send mail. It survives `npm ci --omit=dev` and reaches a runtime image. **A flat window would have left that unblocked.**

**So the window must key on the same discriminator that has decided every one of these triages:**

| class | behaviour |
| -- | -- |
| measured NOT to reach a shipped tree, **and** moderate or below | **WARN** for the window, do not block |
| reaches a shipped tree | **HARD-FAIL immediately**, no window |
| **HIGH or CRITICAL**, wherever it lives | **HARD-FAIL immediately**, no window |

**This preserves the property Kam wants — nobody blocked for changing nothing — without buying it with the property the gate exists for.** It is deliberately the same test as the standing authority's own clauses: *what does this reach* is the only question that discriminated all morning.

**A necessary consequence, stated so it is designed rather than discovered:** the warn path needs the reach measurement to be **automatic**. Today it is done by hand, per advisory, by whoever is blocked. A gate that warns-or-fails on reach must derive reach itself, or the window just moves the manual step earlier.

## 🔴 OPEN QUESTION FOR KAM — the window length

**He ruled the shape, not the number, and it is not being chosen here.**

Recommendation offered as a recommendation only: long enough that a normal working day is not interrupted by a third party's publishing schedule, short enough that a warn cannot be ignored into permanence. **The data point this ticket can contribute is that eight advisories arrived in half an hour, so any window shorter than that is indistinguishable from no window at all.**

## What is NOT claimed

* **No root cause for the churn.** Whether the 31→32→37 movement is newly-published advisories, a registry re-index, or an `npm audit` dataset refresh is **NOT measured**. The *effect* is measured; the mechanism is not, and the reshape does not depend on which it is.
* **Whether we actually call the vulnerable nodemailer signature** — see the linked note; unmeasured at filing.
* **No claim that any current advisory is exploitable here.** Reachability has not been measured for any of them; that has been true of this baseline since KS-470.

## Provenance

Measured by s154, 2026-09-09, on `develop` `f9296f9e` while blocked from pushing KS-754 — the three runs are its own, and the arithmetic was closed before the conclusion was drawn. Ruled by Kam 2026-09-09 08:12 (`both`), confirmed *"Okay, go ahead with your recommendation."* The reach/severity split is Wednesday's design constraint. Related: KS-1024 (the triage that produced this), KS-470, KS-531.

title: The `require-pr-gates` ruleset survived the Actions retirement: 7 required checks that can never report, 0 required approvals, and ALWAYS bypass for admins
description:
## BLUF

`develop` **and** `main` **carry an ACTIVE ruleset that enforces nothing for an admin and is unsatisfiable for everyone else.** It requires seven status-check contexts whose workflows no longer exist, requires **zero** approving reviews, and grants `ALWAYS` bypass to org and repo admins.

The retirement of Actions is well tracked ([KS-789](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-789/contributingmd-justifies-the-hooks-degradation-and-its-no-verify), [KS-910](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-910/preflight-leg-12-executes-zero-suite-cells-it-is-a-reachability-check), [KS-926](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-926/17-of-20-check-sh-guards-run-from-no-live-entry-point-including-sql)). **What is not tracked is the ruleset left pointing at it.** A branch that looks protected in the settings UI, and in the API reports `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN` on a PR with no reviews and no checks, is worse than one that is plainly unprotected — the reassurance is the problem.

Found while reviewing [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#805](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-726-write-ahead-the-cardano-tx-hash-so-a-lost-submit-reply-cannot-48dbfe970108), after asking the ordinary question "could this merge without an approval?". It can.

## What the ruleset actually says

`require-pr-gates` — `target: BRANCH`, `enforcement: ACTIVE`, conditions `refs/heads/develop` + `refs/heads/main`.

| rule | setting |
| -- | -- |
| `PULL_REQUEST` | required |
| — `requiredApprovingReviewCount` | **0** |
| — `requireCodeOwnerReview` | false |
| — `requireLastPushApproval` | false |
| — `requiredReviewThreadResolution` | false |
| — `dismissStaleReviewsOnPush` | false |
| `REQUIRED_STATUS_CHECKS` | 7 contexts (below) |
| — `strictRequiredStatusChecksPolicy` | false |
| `DELETION` / `NON_FAST_FORWARD` | both on — these two DO work |

Required contexts: `Code Security Gates` · `Standalone locks pass clean-room npm ci` · `build / Build + push platform images (fresh)` · `Schemathesis suite` · `Playwright suite` · `Performance suite (k6 smoke)` · `Akto suite (PR)`.

Bypass actors, **both** `bypassMode: ALWAYS`: organization admins, and repository role `5` (admin).

## The three problems, separately

**1 — Seven required checks that can never report.** Every recent workflow run is `startup_failure` at **0s** (`gh run list`). The workflows producing these contexts were retired. So for a contributor without admin the ruleset is not strict, it is **unsatisfiable** — nothing they push can ever go green, and the failure reads as "waiting for a check" rather than "this check no longer exists".

**2 — Zero required approvals.** A PR is required; an approval is not. On `main` as well as `develop`, which is the part I would not have guessed. `main` is meant to be the releasable branch (CLAUDE.md → Branching Model), and it currently asks for no human sign-off at all.

**3 —** `ALWAYS` **bypass for admins hides both.** Anyone who could notice problems 1 and 2 is exactly the population the ruleset never applies to. GitHub computes `mergeStateStatus` for the viewer, so an admin sees `CLEAN` and no warning of any kind.

## The demonstration

[Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#805](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-726-write-ahead-the-cardano-tx-hash-so-a-lost-submit-reply-cannot-48dbfe970108), read 2026-09-08:

```
mergeable:         MERGEABLE
mergeStateStatus:  CLEAN
reviewDecision:    null      (no reviews of ANY kind ever submitted)
statusCheckRollup: 0 checks
```

Mergeable right now, by any admin, with no approval and no green check — and nothing on the PR page says so. That PR happens to be under active review, so no harm is in flight; it is the state that is the finding, not the PR.

## Reproduce

```
gh api graphql -f query='{ repository(owner:"Secuura", name:"Distributed_Secuura") {
  rulesets(first:5){ nodes{ name target enforcement
    conditions{ refName{ include exclude } }
    bypassActors(first:20){ nodes{ bypassMode organizationAdmin repositoryRoleDatabaseId } }
    rules(first:30){ nodes{ type parameters{ __typename
      ... on PullRequestParameters { requiredApprovingReviewCount requireCodeOwnerReview requireLastPushApproval requiredReviewThreadResolution dismissStaleReviewsOnPush }
      ... on RequiredStatusChecksParameters { strictRequiredStatusChecksPolicy requiredStatusChecks{ context } } } } } } } }'
```

Note the REST endpoints (`/branches/develop/protection`, `/rulesets`) answer **403 "Upgrade to GitHub Pro"** on this private repo, which is why this is easy to miss — the obvious check reports nothing rather than reporting the truth. GraphQL answers fine.

## Suggested shape — not a decree, and deliberately not one change

These are three decisions, not one, and they belong to different owners:

1. **Drop the seven dead contexts** from the ruleset, or repoint them at whatever replaced Actions. Leaving a required check that cannot report is the worst of the three states. *(Cheap; no policy decision.)*
2. **Decide the approval count deliberately**, for `main` and `develop` separately. If 0 is intended on a 4-seat team, say so in CONTRIBUTING and this ticket closes on that; if it is a leftover, 1 on `develop` and 1 on `main` is the obvious floor.
3. **Reconsider** `ALWAYS` **bypass.** `pull_request` mode instead of `ALWAYS` keeps admins able to unblock an emergency while still surfacing the state to them.

**(1) is worth doing regardless of how (2) and (3) land.**

## Relationship to what is already tracked

* [KS-412](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-412/ci-require-all-systemtest-all-tools-pr-suites-pre-merge-to-block) (Todo, High, Peter) — *"require all systemTest PR suites + pre-merge to block merges on failure (branch protection + sign-off)"*. Points **forward** to the gate we want. This ticket is the **residue behind us**: the ruleset that already exists and no longer means anything. They should probably be sequenced — clean this up, then build [KS-412](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-412/ci-require-all-systemtest-all-tools-pr-suites-pre-merge-to-block) on the cleared ground.
* [KS-789](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-789/contributingmd-justifies-the-hooks-degradation-and-its-no-verify) — CONTRIBUTING justifies the hook's `--no-verify` bypass with *"CI is the hard gate"*. This is the same sentence, one layer down: the ruleset also asserts a gate that is not there.
* [KS-910](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-910/preflight-leg-12-executes-zero-suite-cells-it-is-a-reachability-check), [KS-926](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-926/17-of-20-check-sh-guards-run-from-no-live-entry-point-including-sql) — the Actions retirement itself and its orphaned guards. Cause; this is effect.

## Not claimed

I have not checked whether any merge to `develop` or `main` has actually gone in unreviewed — only that nothing prevents it. Nor have I touched the ruleset; changing it needs org-admin rights and is a decision, not a fix.

*Raised by Peter's session, 2026-09-08, from the #805 review. Read via GraphQL against the live repo, not from documentation.*

title: services/auth tsconfig EXCLUDES src/__tests__ — every 'tsc: 0 errors' on a test-only change in this service is a green that could not fail
description:
## BLUF

`services/auth/tsconfig.json` **excludes** `src/__tests__`**, so** `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` **type-checks NONE of that service's test files.** Every *"*`tsc`*: 0* `error TS`*"* reported on a test-only change in this service is a **green that could not have failed**.

## Measured

```
services/auth/tsconfig.json
  include: ["src/**/*"]
  exclude: ["node_modules", "dist", "src/__tests__"]
```

The gate demonstrated the consequence rather than arguing it: **a planted type error in the test file produced 0 errors, while the identical plant in** `userRepo.ts` **produced** `TS2322`**.** Same command, same invocation — one file is checked and the other is not, and nothing in the output says which.

## Why this is filed separately from the #907 residue

Different logical path, and **wider than one PR**: this is a repo-wide instrument gap, not a defect in the change that exposed it.

## 🔴 It has already produced a false evidence line, and it was mine

[#907](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/907>)'s Test Evidence block cited *"*`tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` *— 0* `error TS` *lines"* for a change that added **~110 lines of test code**. That line is true of `userRepo.ts` and says **nothing whatsoever** about the suite. I reported it as evidence covering both. The PR body now carries the correction.

**That is the point of the ticket:** the number was real, the command was real, and the conclusion was unearned — and there is no way to tell from the output. Any seat would have reported it the same way.

## Items

- [ ] **1. Decide the shape.** Either include `src/__tests__` in the type-check (a second `tsconfig.test.json` is the usual answer, since test files legitimately need looser settings), or state in writing that tests are deliberately unchecked and stop citing `tsc` as evidence for them.
- [ ] **2. Whichever is chosen, make the output honest** — a checker that silently examines a subset must say which subset. *"0 errors"* over an empty file set is the exact shape of [KS-676](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-676) (the CVE scan that reported clean having examined nothing).
- [ ] **3. Sweep the sibling services.** `auth` is where it was found; whether the other 20+ services exclude their tests the same way is **not measured** — do not assume either answer.
- [ ] **4. Add the planted-error check as a cell**, so the instrument's own coverage is pinned and this cannot silently re-open.

## Provenance

Tier-1 QA gate on #907, finding F5, relayed in Wednesday's GO of 04:41:56Z (**DKIM-verified as her relay**) and **independently re-verified here by reading** `tsconfig.json` before filing.

- `services/api-gateway` + `services/originate` — **KS-1090 stays open** (its R2-3 mint-scope item is a separate ask); its R2-2 half belongs to this class: both tsconfigs exclude `src/__tests__` (originate also `src/**/*.test.ts`); a plant in each of 3 test files rc 0, the same plant in `routes/proxy.ts` / `utils/gatewayProvenance.ts` rc 2; `--listFiles` 33 / 51 `src` files, 0 under `__tests__`. Both exclusions pre-date #951.

**Not measured by any member:** the other services (item 3). KS-993 is the `systemTest/fixtures` gap — a different directory, not this class.

**Priority:** High, this ticket's own (KS-848 and KS-933 were Medium, KS-1122 Low — nothing raised). Survivor by the rule: no member has a fixing PR; this ticket holds the most context (the class framing, the sweep item, the widest measurement); the older-id fallback was not reached.

## Measured evidence for this ticket, from the KS-732 / #872 work

`services/auth` **on develop** (at the KS-732 merge commit `133f525c8`):

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `npm run build` (`tsc`, the excluded config) | **0 errors** |
| `tsc` with `src/__tests__` **included** | **25 errors**, across **14 test files** |

Top offenders: `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity` (7), `usersAdminStatus` (3),
`ks804-authorize-get-post-agree-per-rule` (2), `ks622-backup-code-at-login` (2),
`ks431-oauth-app-update` (2). Error classes include a top-level `await` that the
module target forbids (`TS1378`), an unsound `as` conversion (`TS2352`), and
unused declarations (`TS6133`).

**The count is identical before and after my change**, measured in a separate detached worktree at the
same commit — so all 25 are pre-existing and none came from #872. Stated because a bare "25 errors"
line invites the reader to assume the branch introduced them.

**What this ticket is really about, in one line:** `npm run build` returning 0 is not evidence that
the tests compile, and on this service it has not been for some time. It bit me directly on #872 — my
new test file failed to typecheck twice (an `AnchorSnapshot` union, then optional-vs-nullable) while
the build read green throughout.

Practical note for whoever takes this: a `tsconfig.tests.json` extending the base with
`include: ["src/**/*"]` and `exclude: ["node_modules","dist"]` reproduces it in one command, and the
control that proves it is really covering them is `--listFiles | grep -c 'src/__tests__'` — 12 in the
inclusive program versus 0 in the default one on `services/anchoring`, where I checked the same thing.

title: 95 archived tickets sit in NON-TERMINAL states — measure whether a cascade put them there
description:
## BLUF

**97 archived tickets on the KS+PS boards are in non-terminal states.** Two were archived today (mine, restored the same session). **The other 95 predate this session and nobody has established how they got there.**

```
Backlog     83
Todo         6
In Progress  4
In Review    3
Blocked      1
```

**This is a hypothesis with evidence, NOT an asserted cause.** [KS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-995) established that `issueArchive` cascades onto sub-issues — including non-terminal ones — and that the parent-side check reads clean afterwards. **That mechanism would produce exactly this population, silently.** It may also be that some were archived deliberately.

## The measurement that would settle it

For each of the 95: **is its parent archived, and does the parent's** `archivedAt` **match the child's to the millisecond?**

That is the same discriminator that disproved a wrong third-party attribution during today's pass, applied backwards:

* **match → decisive for cascade.** One batch, one cause.
* **mismatch → closes nothing.** It was archived separately, which is consistent with a deliberate act.

One-directional, and that limit should be carried into whatever the measurement concludes — a mismatch is not evidence of intent.

## 🔴 Do NOT unarchive anything on the strength of this ticket

**83 tickets reappearing in Backlog changes what the team sees.** A restoration is as much a board change as an archive, and it is Kam's call on a measurement — not a tidy-up. **Measure first, report, then ask.**

## Items

- [ ] **1. Run the parent/timestamp measurement** across all 95 and report the split.
- [ ] **2. For any confirmed cascade victim, establish whether the work is still live** — an In Progress ticket archived by accident is different from a Backlog item nobody was going to do.
- [ ] **3. Only then** put a restoration proposal to Kam, with counts by state.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

Every count taken with a default query has been wrong on this board today — *twice*. `Tested Not Deployed` read 24 when it was 29, and a Duplicate census read 4 when it was 5 because the query capped at 250. **If 95 live-state tickets are invisible, every "what is open" number anyone has quoted is short by some part of 95.**

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, alongside KS-995.

title: Archiving a ticket silently archives its sub-issues, including NON-TERMINAL ones — and the parent-side check cannot detect it
description:
## BLUF

`issueArchive` **cascades to sub-issues.** Archiving 23 terminal tickets on 2026-09-08 also archived **KS-918 (Backlog)** and **KS-920 (In Progress)** — children of **KS-490**. Neither was in any target list. **In Progress is live work.**

**And the obvious verification cannot catch it:** once archived, the parent's `children` connection returns **nothing**. Asking the parent what it took with it reads clean.

Both were restored the same session. This ticket is about the mechanism, which is still live.

## Measured

```
child -> parent    KS-918.parent = KS-490      ✅ reveals the link
                   KS-920.parent = KS-490      ✅
parent -> children KS-490.children = 0         ❌ shows NOTHING
```

**The timestamps are what identified it as a cascade rather than a concurrent actor:**

```
KS-490  (mine, targeted)      archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z
KS-921  (mine, targeted)      archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z
KS-918  (NOT targeted)        archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z   <- identical ms
KS-920  (NOT targeted)        archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z   <- identical ms
```

Identical to the millisecond = one batch = one cause. **My own first diagnosis blamed a concurrent actor and was wrong; the timestamp disproved it.**

**Full accounting for the pass:** 33 intended + 2 collateral = 35 archived, measured 35. Only KS-490 had children, so the blast radius was bounded at exactly two.

## Why it went unnoticed until arithmetic caught it

The only reason anyone knows is the **census delta: −25 against an expected −23**. That is the shape most easily rationalised as a stale count. Every other signal looked clean:

* the archive calls all returned `success: true` — and they had, for the 23 asked;
* the parent-side `children` query returned **0**;
* no error, no warning, nothing in any response mentioning the children.

## The rule this produces

**Before archiving, query** `child → parent` **for the target's children and record the count. After, take a full paged census.**

```
expected delta = |targets| + |children found|
```

**If the delta is not exactly that, stop.** Asking the parent side for `children` is *the check that cannot fail* here — it reads zero both when there are none and when they have just been archived.

## Items

- [ ] **1. Make the children pre-check part of any archive procedure**, with the delta equation above as its pass condition.
- [ ] **2. Decide whether a cascade onto a NON-TERMINAL child should be refused outright.** Kam's standing ruling is that non-terminal work stays visible on the board; a cascade violates that silently.
- [ ] **3. Measure the historical population — see the sibling ticket** on the 95 pre-existing archived non-terminal tickets. This mechanism would produce exactly that.

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, from the archive pass that hit it.

title: A deploy that rsyncs the OpenAPI spec and does not restart api-gateway ships a silently stale published contract — rsync breaks the bind mount by inode
description:
## BLUF

**The demo redeploy runbook can ship a stale published API contract with every check passing.** `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` is a **file-level** bind mount into `api-gateway` (`docker-compose.yml:542`, `:ro`). `rsync` **writes a temp file and renames it, so the updated file gets a NEW INODE** — and a Docker file bind mount resolves to the inode at container-create time. The container goes on serving the **old** file indefinitely.

It is not stale cache. The container is looking at a **different file on the same path**.

## Measured during the 2026-09-08 deploy (632f16dfe → 400517aaf)

After the rsync, before any restart:

|  | md5 | bytes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| host `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` | `7e43a8d89afb…` | 1332983 (new) |
| inside `api-gateway` `/app/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` | `c014b2fce71c…` | 1329831 (**old**, dated Sep 7 03:45) |
| served `GET /api/docs/openapi.yaml` | — | 1329831 = the container's copy |

After `docker compose restart api-gateway`: container md5 `7e43a8d89afb…`, identical to the host; served bytes 1332983; the new text `BOUND TO THE` went **0 → 1** and `DIFFERS FROM the ACTING` **0 → 2**, with `organizationUuid` **1 → 2** as a control and an impossible string at 0.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a note

**The failure mode is exactly KS-978's**, which this same deploy shipped the fix for: *the published contract says something the route does not do*. KS-978 was a wrong sentence in the source. This is the **delivery mechanism** producing the same outcome from a correct source — and it is quieter, because every signal an operator would check looks right:

* `rsync` exits 0 and reports the file transferred ✅
* the file on the VM disk **is** correct ✅
* rebuilding the image does nothing (the spec is mounted, not baked) — so "I rebuilt it" feels like the fix and is not ✅
* the container is healthy, the endpoint returns 200 ✅

Nothing surfaces the divergence except comparing the md5 **inside** the container against the host.

## Items

- [ ] **1. Add the gateway restart to the runbook as a required step**, not an optional one — `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md` §Redeploy runbook. Wording should carry the mechanism (inode), because "restart to pick up the spec" reads as cargo-cult and gets dropped.
- [ ] **2. Correct the existing guidance.** The current understanding recorded in project notes is "a rebuild does not publish it, a restart does" — true but incomplete, and it does not say the container will serve the old file *forever* until something re-resolves the mount.
- [ ] **3. Add a post-deploy assertion** that fails loudly: compare `md5sum` of the host spec against `docker exec api-gateway md5sum` of the mounted path, and refuse to call a deploy complete when they differ. This is the check that would have caught it with no human judgement involved.
- [ ] **4. Audit for other file-level bind mounts with the same exposure** — `nginx-demo.conf` is the known sibling. Directory mounts are not affected; only single-file mounts are.

## Not a live defect right now

The 2026-09-08 deploy restarted `api-gateway` and the served spec is verified correct. This ticket is about the **next** deploy, by whoever does not know.

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, from the deploy itself.

nodes.body:
**Carried here from KS-1021 — closed as Duplicate of this ticket and archived on 2026-09-14 (s222), under Kam's 2026-09-14 08:55 standing rule (true duplicates are closed and archived by us, no external review).** One mechanism: `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` is a single-FILE bind mount into api-gateway (`docker-compose.yml:542`); replace the file and the container keeps the old inode. KS-1021's own words: "This is the KS-987 / KS-659 class … Filed as another instance".

What KS-1021 adds (measured by the QA gate on the local stack, 2026-09-09, the KS-1013 / PR #910 tier-1 pass):
- **A branch switch kills the inode too, not only rsync.** The local api-gateway held the head spec in memory (md5 `826735d9`, carries `format: uuid`) while the host file behind the mount was byte-identical to BASE (`7e43a8d8`); inside the container `stat` reported the head size but every read returned ENOENT. It was right for the wrong reason — it booted while the head yaml was checked out.
- **A restart is not a safe recovery action while a branch is checked out** — re-binding resolves to the current host file, so a restart would publish the BASE contract while auth enforces the new one: a contract regression with no code change, and the next person re-running a live matrix reads BASE behaviour as a regression they introduced. Worth stating wherever "restart to pick up the spec" is recommended (item 1 above).
- **The dev-only spec hot-reload can never fire again** on a dead inode — the `fsWatch` is registered on it. Silent.
- **The md5 host-vs-container comparison is the only reliable check** (item 3 above): a 200 from `/api/docs/openapi.yaml` proves nothing — the container answered 200 with the right bytes from memory over an unreadable file.
- The class is documented in code at `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:616-642` (KS-659). Not established: whether the demo VM carries the same state — it runs baked images, so the mechanism may not transfer.
- Neither consequence was observed (nothing was restarted); both are predicted from the mount state. Recorded as such.

Both tickets were unassigned; both are now on the board account per the standing instruction that every Platform K ticket has an owner.

## Possible overlap with KS-656 — check before implementing item 3

While verifying a different finding I hit `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh`, whose step **8** is:

> `8. served-spec consistency -> KS-656 (every other spec check reads the HOST file and probes the runtime separately; none fetches the spec the gateway actually SERVES, so ...)`

**That is the same instrument this ticket's item 3 proposes** — comparing what the gateway actually serves against the host file. KS-656 appears to have built it for the **local preflight**; item 3 here asks for it **post-deploy on the VM**.

**Before implementing item 3, check whether KS-656's check can simply be pointed at the demo** rather than writing a second one. Two byte-identical private copies of a check is the arrangement this repo has already been burned by (see the `normaliseOrgId` consolidation in `orgId.ts`).

**Not verified:** whether KS-656's check actually runs against a remote target, or only localhost. That is the question to answer first.

title: MAJOR: when both platform-admin rows exist the id-row rewrite throws 23505, the seed loop swallows it, and the KS-966 F3 email arm never runs — with a green cell standing over the hole
description:
**MAJOR. When both rows exist, the platform-admin remediation throws 23505, the loop swallows it, and the email-keyed arm — the whole KS-966 F3 fix — NEVER RUNS. A green cell stands over the hole.**

**"Both rows present" is not an exotic state. It is the state Kam's own row is in**: `…0020` holding one address, and a distinct row holding `admin@secuura.com`.

Found by the #888 round-2 tier-1 gate. **Pre-existing — reproduced identically against round 1's** `userRepo.ts`**, so it is not introduced by round 2 and is equally open on** `develop` **today** (merged at `9e9a88709`).

### The mechanism — and my published one was WRONG

I argued in #888 and on KS-966 that the collision came from **rewriting the address onto the row found BY that address**. That is wrong, and it matters: **writing the same address back onto the row that already holds it cannot collide with itself.**

The collision is on the **other** side:

1. `if (byId)` (`userRepo.ts:1363`) rewrites the `…0020` row's `email_lookup_hash` to the hash of `admin@secuura.com`.
2. If a **distinct** row already holds that hash, that write violates `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq` → **23505**.
3. The seed loop's `catch` (`userRepo.ts:~1506`) turns it into `logger.error('Failed to seed demo user', …)` and `continue`s — **no rethrow**.
4. `if (emailRowIsDistinct)` sits at `:1388`, *after* the throwing statement. **It never executes.**

**So I located the hazard on the wrong row, then declined a rewrite that was harmless and left standing the rewrite that actually detonates.** The gate accepted my *conclusion* (the email row should get credential-neutralisation only) and rejected my *reasoning* — and the wrong reasoning is why the hole is still open.

**The arm itself is correct and merely unreachable:** the gate neutered only the id-row guard and the email arm fired perfectly — suspended, sentinel hash, verify FALSE.

**Verified independently on** `origin/develop` **before filing:** `byId` at `:1363` precedes `emailRowIsDistinct` at `:1388`; the id-row UPDATE writes `email_lookup_hash = $3`; the loop catch logs and continues without rethrowing. And `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq` **exists and is UNIQUE on the deployed demo database** (measured read-only 2026-09-07, with controls: `users` 33 columns, `uuid_generate_v4` present).

---

## ITEM 1 — the misleading green cell. Fix this first.

`services/auth/src/__tests__/ks952…`/`ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts`:

```
it('remediates BOTH when both exist, and the id row still gets the full identity rewrite')
```

**It passes, and it is asserting that a live hole is closed, on a credential surface.** It passes because the vitest `db` double answers `{rows: []}` to every UPDATE and **cannot enforce a unique index** — so the 23505 never happens in the test and the swallow never happens either.

The tester's words: *"the one thing here I would fix before the deploy rather than after."* It could not go into #888 because what merges must be what was gated, so it is the first item here.

**A mocked** `query` **cannot express this defect at all.** The regression test must drive the same both-exist scenario against a **real Postgres carrying** `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq`. That is the important half of this ticket — more than the fix.

## ITEM 2 — the fix, three shapes offered by the gate

* **Order the two remediations email-row-first**, so the credential neutralisation lands before the statement that can throw; **or**
* make the id-row rewrite **conditional on** `!emailRowIsDistinct`; **or**
* **wrap both in one transaction**, so the credential neutralisation is not lost to the identity rewrite's failure.

Whichever is chosen, **the swallowing catch is part of the defect**: a remediation whose failure is indistinguishable from success at `logger.error` level is the same class as KS-962, where the seed failure logs at `debug` and is invisible.

## ITEM 3 — do NOT probe the demo

**Likelihood on the demo is UNKNOWN.** The gate had no authorisation to contact the box and did not. **That probe is Kam's to authorise and he has not.** Do not go and look.

---

**Related:** KS-966 (#888, where the F3 arm shipped — my incorrect mechanism is corrected in a comment there) · KS-949 (the identity half) · KS-962 (the sibling swallow, at `debug`) · KS-963 (the PII cutoff).

*Filed by s146 after the #888 merge, from the round-2 gate verdict. The mechanism above is the gate's; the develop-side verification and the deployed-index measurement are mine.*

**BLUF:** The read-only state check of the users table is made on kintsugi and demo, as Wednesday approved (SQL sha256 `5826161acf89ecac22332aef2334d8cff7ee953ea62fc784a78a9c53f280541c`, run as the owner role `secuura`). On both boxes the seeded platform-admin id row `...0020` is present, `active`, role `system_admin`; **no row carries the neutralisation signature** (password hash `!disabled:no-seed-password-supplied`), so the KS-966/968 arms have suspended nothing; and no row lacks an email lookup hash. This is the state the first boot LEFT, not the pre-deploy state the 2026-10-12 deploy note wanted: PR 1485's squash `8f674b3c46e7` is already an ancestor of both boxes' REVISION heads. One probe, P1, is invalid (see below). This comment decides nothing and moves no state.

| probe | kintsugi | demo |
| -- | -- | -- |
| total rows in `users` | 25 | 34 |
| id row `...0020` present | 1 | 1 |
| id row by status/role | `active/system_admin` (1) | `active/system_admin` (1) |
| rows with the sentinel password hash | 0 | 0 |
| rows with no `email_lookup_hash` | 0 | 0 |
| unique index `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq` present | 1 | 1 |
| P1 `SYSTEM_ADMIN` rows | **invalid, not a measurement** | **invalid, not a measurement** |

**P1 is invalid.** It printed 0 on both boxes, but its filter was the upper-case `role = 'SYSTEM_ADMIN'` and the stored word is lower-case (P2 prints `system_admin`), so it counted nothing for a reason unrelated to the data. The SQL had no control on P1, which is how it passed unnoticed until the output was read. A corrected count (`lower(role) = 'system_admin'`) has not been run; it would need its own written OK. Nothing below depends on P1.

**Where and when:**
- kintsugi: `secuura02-kintsugi-vm`, REVISION head `5fc5569ed96ac61f64823cc9e1fa841899aa1f62`, read 2026-11-05 06:19:11Z.
- demo: `secuura02-demo-vm`, REVISION head `07a2d62be6a09c9cd504864d1cf1906543d55317`, read 06:19:14Z (reads only; the demo freeze is on redeploys).
- Database `secuura`, the only one of the two non-template databases with `public.users` on each box (`secuura_platform` has none, so `platform_admins` was not read).

**Instrument and controls:** `psql` through the `secuura-postgres` container as `secuura` (current_user `secuura`, rolsuper true, rolbypassrls true), inside one `BEGIN READ ONLY ... ROLLBACK`; `SHOW transaction_read_only` read `on`. The SQL's bytes were embedded in the tool and the sha256 was compared on each box before `psql` ran (EQUAL on both). It selects words and counts only: no email, hash, id, name or password is in the output. Controls that held: total rows above 0, the id row found, the index found. No control existed for P1.

**What this does and does not say about the both-rows state:**
- The row that holds the seeded admin address (user `admin`, domain `secuura.com`) is found by `email_lookup_hash`, an HMAC with a secret; it was not computed, so whether a distinct second row holds that address is **not established**.
- The deploy note's bad outcome, the account holding the address suspended, leaves the sentinel hash behind. It is absent on both boxes, and the id row is active.
- Why it is absent is **not measured**: no both-rows state ever existed, `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` was set (the note says that re-activates the email row as a system admin, which P1 would have shown), or the seeder did not run. The environment flags and the auth boot-log lines (`Demo user NOT seeded`, `remediation FAILED`) were not read.
- The per-environment first-boot outcome stays Kam's decision card; nothing here chooses it.

**Evidence:** `5_Project_History/2026-11-05_seatU-14th/evidence/ks968_kintsugi_raw.txt` and `ks968_demo_raw.txt`; the SQL is `drafts/ks968_state_read.sql`. Nothing was written on either box.

**BLUF:** Delivered: PRs 1485 and 905 merged as 8f674b3c46e7 and ede711ca9ad1 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (2026-11-01). Verified by code read, not observed live. Left open: two items are not recorded as done: the read-only check of which state each environment is in, which the 2026-10-12 deploy note requires, and the per-environment first-boot outcome without `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, listed as a decision for Kam in the 2026-11-02 triage plan.

- **In the code at b1fb543640e7:** with both platform-admin rows present the email row is neutralised (`auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:1695`, `:1747`, `:1764`, KS-968); the regression test runs against a real Postgres (`auth/integration/ks968-platform-admin-seed-with-both-rows.integration.ts`). PR 905 warns at the column that comparing `users.email` to a literal is void.
- **Deploy note, from the 2026-10-12 09:17Z comment:** in the both-rows state without `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, the first boot of this code suspends the account that holds `admin@secuura.com`, so the deploy seat checks read-only which state an environment is in before deploying.

## BLUF
**KS-968 is merged: #1485, squash `8f674b3c46e7`, on `develop`. The ticket stays open until auth is deployed with it, and the DEPLOY NOTE below must be read first.**

## Recommendation
Do not deploy this to an environment until the deploy seat has checked, read-only, which state it is in. In the both-rows state without `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, the first boot of this code **suspends the account that holds `admin@secuura.com`**. **Do not answer that by setting `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` blindly**: the gate found that doing so RE-ACTIVATES the EMAIL row as `system_admin` (not the id row), even when that row was an `OWNER`. Which outcome each environment gets is Kam's choice.

## Detail
- **The defect, measured on a real Postgres:** with the id row and a distinct row holding the address both present and no seed password, the email row stays `['active', 'LIVE-B']` (the id-row rewrite threw 23505, the loop swallowed it, the email arm never ran). The new suite is 6/6 green on the fix and 2 of 6 red on develop's `userRepo.ts`.
- **Fix:** the id-row rewrite runs only when no distinct row holds the address; with both rows the id row is left alone and the email row is neutralised; a failed remediation logs a distinct error first. The misleading mocked cell is replaced.
- **Gate:** Opus, GO WITH NOTE at head `ebdb123d5963`, 0 Major; Wednesday's head-bound GO 2026-10-12T08:56:35Z. Gate: 9 of 11 mutants killed; 3 boots in a row and 2 concurrent boots stay correct; no state suspends the wrong row or locks out the operator's id row.
- **Not exactly "unchanged":** with a legacy plaintext email row (no lookup hash) develop suspended both rows; this leaves the id row ACTIVE.
- **Landed on a moved tip, so the strict set ran twice:** first on tree `88a9408dc01f`, then on the exact final tree `2c26402eb038` (develop moved 6 files, including a `scripts/` shell suite; none are this PR's files, overlap computed with a control): `services/auth` 90 files / 934 tests twice, tsc, `check:openapi`, `check:test-types`, the integration suite 6/6, `run-shell-suites` 82/82.
- **Verified at source:** one parent, tree equals the predicted tree, six files, each delta equal to the PR's own.
- **Carried to KS-1494:** the integration suite's loopback guard can be bypassed by `?host=`, the untested rethrow, two lookups outside the named try, the file's own tsc errors, a whitespace `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`.
- **Not run:** the four platform suites; any look at demo or kintsugi (this ticket forbids probing demo); the RLS-forced app role.

- Seat V 3rd (Sonnet 5.5), 2026-10-12. Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatV-3rd/` (`merge_1485.log`, `full_auth_1485b_predicted.log`, `ks968_integration_on_base.log`).

## BLUF
**KS-968 is built and up as PR #1485 (head `ebdb123d5963`), waiting for an Opus gate. The regression test runs against a REAL Postgres, as this ticket asked.** With both the id row and a distinct row holding `admin@secuura.com` and no `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, the remediation threw 23505, the loop swallowed it, and the email row stayed ACTIVE on its old credential. Reproduced on a real database: the email row stays `['active', 'LIVE-B']`. Fixed: the id-row rewrite runs only when no distinct row holds the address; with both rows present the id row is left alone and the email row is neutralised.

## Recommendation
Gate and merge #1485. **Before it deploys, decide the deploy order:** on any environment in the both-rows state with no `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, the first boot of this code SUSPENDS the account that holds `admin@secuura.com`. That is KS-966 F3 finally working, but it locks out anyone logging in as that address. Likelihood on demo and kintsugi is unknown; this ticket forbids probing demo, and I did not look.
