Done: PR 808 (d2fe7d6d2) publishes the documentUuid v4 constraint the runtime already enforces (divergence 2). It was approved on the PR and is an ancestor of the kintsugi deploy b1fb543640e7. The ticket's headline ask, check:openapi in the gate, was recorded on 2026-09-04 as already satisfied.

Left: divergence 1, the verify-file operations. It was kept out of PR 808 because the live endpoint answered 415 at the gateway, and it now sits on KS-791 (PR 813).

**Merged to `develop` — PR #808, squash `d2fe7d6d255a19b7bc2a809d2e1a2fe8b1139908`.**

- Approval: Peter at head `3d8b40a07f0b5052513be2cf8fb899d1520279a5` (2026-09-08T14:18:43Z), re-verified immediately before the merge: approval at head, no later Peter review or comment, Test Evidence present.
- Squash parent `7bcb6612897f012d2051b6ff848b3fbcbb7d2542` = the `develop` tip asserted before the merge; tree `689662d87a247648d93ae9cd59983222c8a036f8` = `git merge-tree --write-tree` of that tip and the head.
- Deployed: **no**. The kintsugi/demo deploy is held.

State unchanged (In Review): this PR closes divergence 2 only; Peter (2026-09-08) asked to keep KS-663 open because its third criterion, a regeneration check that fails server-side, is still unmet.

## PR #808 approved — divergence 2 verified live

Approved [#808](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/808) (divergence 2, the `documentUuid` v4 constraint). Full review posted on the PR; summarising here with the evidence, and flagging what remains open on this ticket.

Credit where due to the authoring session: divergence 1 was deliberately pulled from that PR after a live probe found `verify-file` 415ing at the gateway, so publishing its spec would have created a divergence rather than closing one. That is now KS-791 / [#813](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/813). Recorded as a finding rather than an omission, which is the right way round.

### What was verified

| Claim | How it held up |
|---|---|
| Runtime enforces v4 | `documents.ts:331` `UUID_V4_RE`, applied at `:438` |
| Published pattern matches it | `[0-9a-fA-F]` / `[89abAB]` is an exact expansion of the `/i` flag — no widening, no narrowing |
| Scoped correctly | `DocumentCreateRequest.documentUuid` only; response schemas deliberately untouched, since `ks584-p3-verify-list.test.ts:222` asserts a legacy non-v4 pkey is returned as `documentUuid` |
| `userUuid` / `organizationUuid` | Left as bare `format: uuid`, matching the KS-596 ruling that those accept any RFC 4122 version |
| Runtime blast radius | None — no spec-driven request validator anywhere in `services/` or `packages/` |

### Test evidence

Run against branch head `3d8b40a07` on a local Docker stack built from that commit (33 containers, 32 healthy), 2026-09-08.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_document_uuid_validation.py` | **9/9 passed** |
| `test_document_uuid_contract.py` | **7/7 passed** |
| Served spec carries the constraint | Confirmed at `/api/docs/openapi.yaml`, on `DocumentCreateRequest` only |

Offline property-based generation probe, 300 examples each, to rule out `format: uuid` and `pattern` starving generation:

| Spec | Populated `documentUuid` | Violating v4 | Health-check failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| PR head | 56 | **0** | none |
| `develop` | 93 | **93** | none |

The counterfactual is the useful half: on `develop` every generated value was unusable input the runtime was always going to 400. So this change does not only document the constraint — it stops the contract suite spending `POST /api/documents` draws on values the endpoint could never accept.

The four platform suites were not re-run, matching the PR author's own statement. For a spec-only change with no runtime consumer of the spec, the two modules above are the directly relevant coverage.

**One process note:** the first invocation returned `16 skipped`, not passes — no `API_TOKEN` for that stack. `scripts/setup.py` provisioned one and the re-run was green. Worth knowing, since a gate reading only the exit code would have read that first result as a pass.

### Suggest keeping this ticket open

Of the three verification criteria in the description, one is now met:

| Criterion | Status |
|---|---|
| `documentUuid`'s published constraint matches the code | **Met** — #808 |
| `verify-file` (v1 and v2) appears in the published spec | Moved to KS-791 / #813 |
| A PR that edits a verb constant without regenerating **fails CI** | **Still open** |

On the third — and this is the original ask, so worth being precise rather than assuming it was covered: `check:openapi` runs from `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:111`, a local pre-push hook. Grepping `.github/workflows/` for `openapi` still returns zero hits, on this branch and on `develop`. A local hook is bypassable and does not run server-side, so the criterion as written is not yet satisfied. It does not appear to have a ticket of its own.

One related suggestion while that is being picked up: nothing currently couples the published pattern to `UUID_V4_RE` — they are independent literals in two files, so relaxing one leaves the other silently wrong, which is the same drift class this ticket was raised about. A small assertion reading `UUID_V4_RE.source` against the generated spec would close it and would sit naturally alongside the CI wiring.

Happy to be corrected if the CI leg exists somewhere I did not look.

**PR [#808](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/808) is open** — branch `feature/ks-663-wire-check-openapi-into-the-gate`, head `3d8b40a07`, rebased onto `develop` `d928a27f8`.

This branch had been committed and **unpushed since s123**. The reason was never the code: the pre-push preflight's advisory leg hung on an unreachable npm endpoint with no timeout, so the push could not complete. **KS-788 merged this morning (#807) and bounded it — this branch then pushed in 76 seconds, 11/11 legs, rc 0.**

Scope is **divergence 2 only**. Divergence 1 (the verify-file spec) stays out: a live probe found the route 415s at the gateway, so publishing its spec would create a divergence rather than close one. That is KS-791.

## Divergence 1 — the probe changed the answer: publishing it now would CREATE a divergence, so it is blocked

I authored both verify-file operations (v1 + v2) in the generated source, regenerated (spec 307 → 309), and `check:openapi` went green — KS-424 security guard satisfied, all 405 examples resolved. Then I probed the live endpoint before finalising, and **reverted them.** Here is why.

### verify-file is unreachable through the gateway — 415 on every file content-type

The endpoint's entire purpose is *"raw file bytes as the body; the server computes the hash."* Live on the local stack (`:6882`), against `POST /api/v2/verification/verify-file` with a real body:

| request Content-Type | result |
|---|---|
| `application/octet-stream` | **415 `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`** |
| `application/pdf` | **415** |
| `text/plain` | **415** |
| none | **415** |
| `multipart/form-data` | **415** |
| `application/json` | 400 (handler reads raw bytes; JSON body-parser already consumed them) |

Only an **empty** body reaches the handler's own 400 (nothing for the media-type filter to reject). So there is no content type on which verify-file can actually receive a file through the gateway.

### This is already known — BACKLOG.md:122

> verify-file (v1 AND v2) is unreachable through the gateway — 415 from the JSON-only content-type enforcement. Where: `api-gateway/src/middleware/contentType.ts` (`enforceJsonContentType`). Verified live 2026-08-12 … raw-byte server-side-hash verification only works in-cluster (direct to originate).

Re-verified live today. The enforcement is a deliberate gateway control (content-type confusion defence); it predates this and is not a regression.

### Why I did not ship the ops

The two ops I wrote documented an `application/octet-stream` request body. **The gateway 415s that.** Publishing them would replace "absent from the spec" with "the spec says POST octet-stream and the gateway refuses it" — a spec/code divergence, which is the exact thing this ticket exists to close, and the exact KS-388 "S sends something K rejects" shape the ticket cites. A spec op for the consumer (Platform S) that 415s on use is worse than its absence.

### So divergence 1 is BLOCKED, and the two must be fixed together

To publish verify-file honestly, the gateway must first let those two paths through — whitelist them in `enforceJsonContentType`, or route them past it, so an `application/octet-stream` (or a raw binary) body reaches the handler. **Then** the spec ops (which I have, ready) can be added against a contract that actually holds. That gateway change is security-adjacent (it relaxes a content-type control for two paths) and should be reasoned about deliberately, not folded in at the tail of a session — so I am sizing it rather than rushing it.

**Recommended follow-up:** one ticket that (a) whitelists the two verify-file paths in the gateway content-type enforcement, and (b) publishes the two spec ops I drafted. I can hand over the drafted ops. Filing it unless you would rather fold it into the BACKLOG item.

## Net state of KS-663

- **Headline ask** (run `check:openapi` in the gate): already satisfied by preflight leg 1. No duplicate added.
- **Divergence 2** (documentUuid v4): FIXED, `df169eaf5`.
- **Divergence 1** (verify-file in spec): BLOCKED on the gateway 415 (BACKLOG:122). Publishing it requires the gateway fix first; the spec ops are drafted and ready to add once it lands.
- **The `emitLifecycleAnchor` observation:** unchanged, no action (as the ticket said).

Two of three parts closed; the third is correctly blocked rather than shipped as a new divergence. Leaving KS-663 In Review pending the gateway follow-up decision.

— @kksecura

## Taken up under Kam's 2026-09-02 standing instruction (a ticket needing no client-human input is ours to drive). Reassigned, In Progress. Branch `feature/ks-663-wire-check-openapi-into-the-gate` off develop `492152a81`.

## The headline ask is ALREADY satisfied — no duplicate gate added

**"run `check:openapi` in the PR workflow"** is done, by a different mechanism than the ticket anticipated. `preflight.sh` **leg 1** runs `npm run --silent check:openapi` on every push (`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:112`) — which is exactly `generate-openapi --check && check:spec-examples`, the drift check plus the example check.

It was wired when the pre-push hook became the gate after GitHub Actions was retired (**Kam, 2026-08-27**) — *after* this ticket was filed (2026-08-19), so nothing closed KS-663 against it. Verified green on develop just now: `CHECK PASS: on-disk YAML matches generated`, `every published example resolves to the fixture set`.

So the CI-workflow framing is stale (there is no CI — see KS-789), and the drift-enforcement ask is met. **I did not add a second leg for it.** A PR that edits a verb constant without regenerating fails leg 1 today.

## Divergence 2 — FIXED (`df169eaf5`)

`documentUuid` was stricter in code (`UUID_V4_RE`, `documents.ts:437`, 400s non-v4) than in the spec (`format: uuid`, any RFC 4122 version). A v7 UUID passed spec validation and 400'd at runtime.

The Zod source now publishes an explicit v4 `pattern` on that one input field. **Only `documentUuid` diverged** — the code comment states the intent: documentUuid is contractually v4, while `userUuid`/`organizationUuid` accept any version (`UUID_RE`) and keep their bare `format: uuid` because the runtime does too.

Verified: the published pattern matches `UUID_V4_RE` sample-for-sample (v4 upper+lower accepted; v7/v1/v5/garbage rejected); the whole-spec regen diff is **one line**; the pattern appears **once** (input op, not the response DTOs); `check:openapi` green.

## Divergence 1 — SIZED, not rushed

`/api/v2/verification/verify-file` (`verificationV2.ts:501`) and the v1 `/api/verification/verify-file` (`verification.ts:511`) exist in code and appear **0 times** in the published spec (control: `verify-hash` appears once, so the spec carries verify ops). The spec is **generated from Zod**, and leg 1's `check:spec-examples` requires every published example to resolve to the fixture set — so this is not a hand-edit: it needs two operations authored in `originate.openapi.ts` (request/response schemas, `security:` per the KS-424 guard, and examples that resolve). That is exacting work and I am deliberately not doing it at the tail of a long session on a downgraded model, where a botched example silently reddens leg 1 for the whole team. **Remaining work: author both verify-file operations in the generated source.**

## The "no action" observation stands

`emitLifecycleAnchor` posting only `{documentId, contentHash, network}` (no `metadata.documentType`) — confirmed still true on develop; consistent with KS-319's scope, flagged not fixed, no action taken.

— @kksecura

title: KS-78 drift check is wrong three ways — reports 7 commits of drift where 212 exist, labels `develop` as `main`, and anchors to a stock redis image
description:
## BLUF

**The KS-78 local-drift check reports a number that is real but labelled with the wrong branch, anchored to the wrong containers, and computed from the wrong kind of timestamp.** Today it printed **7 commits** of drift. The drift that actually exists, measured against the oldest code image in the running stack, is **212**.

Three independent defects, all in `Launch_Claude.command:465-481`. Diagnosed 2026-08-17 (session 43) after **two consecutive sessions (41, 42) flagged the warning as unreconcilable and moved on** — s42 recorded it in project history as an open question handed forward. That is the cost: *two sessions discounted a TRUE warning because its label pointed at a branch that had not moved.*

## Defect 1 — the label says `main`; the code measures `HEAD`

```sh
# Launch_Claude.command:475
DRIFT_COUNT="$(git -C "$GIT_REPO_DIR" log --oneline --since="$EARLIEST_START" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
# Launch_Claude.command:476-477
printf '[KS-78 drift warning] %s commit(s) on main since the running stack was built (%s).\n' "$DRIFT_COUNT" "$EARLIEST_START"
```

`git log` is invoked with **no revision argument**, so it walks `HEAD` — the currently checked-out branch. The word `main` is hardcoded in the `printf` and has never been measured.

**Discriminating control**, all against the same baseline instant `2026-08-17T00:52:38.647560758Z`:

| what was run | count |
| -- | -- |
| `git log --oneline --since=<S>` (exactly what the launcher runs) | **7** |
| `git log --oneline --since=<S> develop` | **7** |
| `git log --oneline --since=<S> main` | **0** |
| `git log --oneline --since=<S> origin/main` | **0** |
| `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` | `develop` |

The no-rev form agrees with `develop` and disagrees with `main` — that is the discriminator, not an inference.

**Why it was ever right:** KS-78 closed **2026-05-15**, when `main` *was* the working branch. Git Flow (KS-137) made `develop` the integration line on **2026-05-25** — ten days later. The check never measured `main`; it measured `HEAD`, which happened to be `main` on the day it shipped and silently became `develop` a fortnight after.

## Defect 2 — `StartedAt` is restart time, not build time

`EARLIEST_START` comes from `docker inspect --format '{{.State.StartedAt}}'`. That is when the container process **last started**, which moves on any `docker start` / `restart` / `compose up` **without any rebuild**.

Proven on the live stack rather than asserted — `secuura-redis`:

```
Created    : 2026-08-12T21:42:23Z
StartedAt  : 2026-08-17T00:52:38Z   <-- 4 days later
RestartCount: 0
```

The container was not rebuilt and not auto-restarted, yet its baseline moved forward four days.

**The practical false negative:** `docker compose down && docker compose up -d` (no `build`) sets every `StartedAt` to *now*, so `DRIFT_COUNT` becomes **0** while every image on disk stays exactly as stale as it was. The check goes silent in precisely the situation it exists to catch.

## Defect 3 — the baseline is anchored to containers that hold no repo code

`EARLIEST_START` is the **minimum** `StartedAt` **across every** `secuura-*` **container**, and that set includes stock upstream infrastructure images. Today the anchor is `secuura-redis` → `redis:8-alpine`, **image built 2026-06-22**; the oldest image of any kind in the stack is `postgres:15-alpine`, **built 2026-02-26**. Neither contains a line of this repo.

Meanwhile the oldest **code** image actually running is `secuura-website-frontend`, built **2026-07-19T00:15:56Z**.

**Measured consequence:**

| baseline used | commits on `develop` since |
| -- | -- |
| what the check used (earliest `StartedAt`, from a stock redis) | **7** — what it printed |
| oldest **code** image build time (`website-frontend`, 2026-07-19) | **212** |

**The check understates real drift by roughly 30x.** It answers "how long since you last ran `compose up`", not "how stale is the code you are running".

## Suggested fix (not applied — see below)

Compute the baseline from **image build time of code-bearing containers only**, and name the branch it actually measured:

```sh
BRANCH="$(git -C "$GIT_REPO_DIR" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo HEAD)"
# oldest .Image .Created across containers whose image is locally built (not a registry tag)
DRIFT_COUNT="$(git -C "$GIT_REPO_DIR" log --oneline --since="$OLDEST_IMAGE_BUILT" "$BRANCH" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
printf '[KS-78 drift warning] %s commit(s) on %s since the oldest running image was BUILT (%s).\n' "$DRIFT_COUNT" "$BRANCH" "$OLDEST_IMAGE_BUILT"
```

Filtering "code-bearing" is the one judgement call: `.Config.Image` for locally built services is `2_project_files-<svc>` (no registry host, no upstream tag), whereas infra is `redis:8-alpine` / `postgres:15-alpine`. That distinction is available without extra tooling.

## What I deliberately did NOT do

**No edit to** `Launch_Claude.command`**.** It is boot-path infrastructure for every session, it is **not under version control** (project root is not a git repo — git lives at `2_Project_Files/`), and there are **16 copies of the template across the workspace**, so a fix here fixes one of sixteen. Changing it is Kam's call, and Wednesday is carrying the fleet-wide fix on the WED board gated on his go-ahead, citing this ticket as the evidence.

## Acceptance

1. The warning names the branch it actually measured (or measures the branch it names).
2. The baseline is image **build** time, not container **start** time — verified by a negative control: `compose up -d` with no rebuild must **not** reduce the count.
3. Infra containers built from upstream tags do not set the baseline — verified by a positive control: the reported count matches the count computed from the oldest locally-built image.

nodes.body:
## Catalogue pass — **BOUNCE**, no state change

The remaining actor is **@kam**, named by this ticket's own text: *"Changing it is Kam's call, and Wednesday is carrying the fleet-wide fix on the WED board gated on his go-ahead."*

The reasoning stands on its own — `Launch_Claude.command` is boot-path infrastructure, **not under version control**, and there are **16 copies** across the workspace, so fixing it here fixes one of sixteen. That is a workspace decision, not a Platform K one.

Note the ticket also carries a dated **CORRECTION** to its own filed diagnosis (2026-08-18): the drift counter does *not* "count `develop` while printing `main`". Whoever picks this up should read that comment before the description.

## CORRECTION to this ticket's filed diagnosis — dated 2026-08-18

## BLUF
**The filed diagnosis is wrong in a way that would send the next fixer to the wrong line.** This ticket records that the KS-78 drift counter *"counts `develop` while printing `main`."* It does not. Read at source, it counts **`HEAD` — whatever branch happens to be checked out.** Today's preflight is the proof: it printed **18**, and neither `main` nor `develop` is 18.

## Recommendation
Correct the diagnosis in the ticket body before anyone acts on it. The fix is **not** "point it at `main`" or "point it at `develop`" — it is "give `git log` an explicit ref and make the printed label match it." **No launcher edit has been made here**: `Launch_Claude.command` is under the launcher-untouchable hold (it is the fleet boot path and Kam-class), so this is a comment only, and nobody should read it as licence to fix.

## Detail — the measurement (2026-08-18, anchor `2026-08-17T00:52:38.647560758Z`)

| Ref | Commits since the anchor |
|---|---|
| `origin/main` | **0** |
| `origin/develop` | **12** |
| `HEAD` (branch `feature/ks-487-…`) | **18** ← what preflight printed |

Preflight's exact line was:

```
[KS-78 drift warning] 18 commit(s) on main since the running stack was built (2026-08-17T00:52:38.647560758Z).
```

**Control:** the same `--since` query against a future date returns `0`, so the counter is reading the date argument correctly and the discrepancy is the *ref*, not the timestamp.

## Detail — the source line
`Launch_Claude.command:475`:

```sh
DRIFT_COUNT="$(git -C "$GIT_REPO_DIR" log --oneline --since="$EARLIEST_START" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
```

`git log` is given **no ref argument**, so it defaults to **`HEAD`**. The label on line 476 is hard-coded to say `on main`. That is the entire bug: the ref is implicit and the label is a literal, and the two have never agreed.

## Why it read as "develop" before
On sessions 44 and 45 the checked-out branch sat **1 commit** over `develop`, so `HEAD` and `develop` differed by one and the number looked develop-shaped. My branch today sits **6** commits over `develop` (12 + 6 = 18), which is what made the divergence large enough to be unmissable. The earlier reading was a coincidence of branch shape, not a wrong measurement.

## Practical consequence
The warning's purpose is to say *"your running containers are older than the code."* Counting `HEAD` means the number inflates with **your own unmerged work** — commits that were never going to be in the running stack and whose absence is not drift. On a long-lived feature branch the warning gets louder the more you work, independent of any real staleness, which is how a useful signal becomes one people learn to skip.

*Posted 2026-08-18. Comment only — no edit to `Launch_Claude.command`, hold observed and named.*

title: The extranet test board has never shown a green run — 0 passed in 22, and the latest red is E2E 210/0 with Schemathesis producing no results
description:
## BLUF

**The team's own status board has never once been green.** The extranet Testing tab has recorded **22 Platform K runs since 2026-05-25: 17** `failed`**, 5** `error`**, 0** `passed`**.** Not one.

And the most recent red is misleading: **E2E passed 210/0**, and the run is marked failed because Schemathesis produced no parseable results.

A board that is permanently red is a board everyone learns to ignore — at which point it can never signal anything, which is the whole reason it was built ([KS-138](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-138), now Done and archived).

## Measured

`GET /api/tests/platform-k/runs` (22 runs, oldest 2026-05-25):

```
failed : 17
error  :  5
passed :  0
```

Latest dashboard (`GET /api/tests/platform-k/latest`, run of 2026-08-10T00:01:44Z, target "Azure Demo"):

```
✗ Findings to fix
  Schemathesis (API contract)   FAIL   — "No Schemathesis results parsed this run."
  End-to-end (e2e-v2)           PASS   — 210 pass · 0 fail · 10 skip · 2 flaky
```

So the one suite that produced results **passed cleanly**, and the red comes from the other leg producing nothing.

`platform-s` has **0 runs**, which is consistent and expected — [KS-139](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-139) (upload the S suite) is still open.

## A verdict bug in the generator, read rather than guessed

`secuura-extranet/ci/build-dashboard.mjs`:

```js
// :39
const schemathesis = (args.schemathesis || 'unknown').toLowerCase(); // success|failure|skipped|unknown

// :181
const schemathesisClean = smt.state === 'ok' ? realFail === 0 : schemathesis === 'success';
const overallPassed = schemathesisClean && e2e.ok;

// :190  — the BADGE, which handles 'skipped' correctly
pill(schemathesis === 'success', schemathesis === 'success' ? 'PASS'
     : schemathesis === 'skipped' ? 'SKIPPED' : 'FAIL');
```

**The badge and the verdict disagree about what** `skipped` **means.** Line 190 renders a skipped Schemathesis leg as `SKIPPED`; line 181 scores anything that is not exactly `'success'` as not-clean. The workflow passes `--schemathesis "${{ steps.schemathesis.outcome }}"`, and a skipped GitHub step reports `outcome: 'skipped'` — so **an e2e-only run is structurally incapable of reporting** `passed`, while its own dashboard says the missing leg was merely skipped.

Whether that is what happened on any given run I have **not** established — per-run dashboards return 404, so `latest` is the only one readable, and its badge says `FAIL` rather than `SKIPPED`, meaning that particular run's Schemathesis leg ran and failed rather than being skipped. **The verdict bug is real in the code either way**; it is not necessarily the cause of all 22 reds.

## Next action

1. **Fix the verdict/badge disagreement** — `skipped` should not fail a run, since the badge already says it does not. Small change, `build-dashboard.mjs:181`. *(Not done in this session: the extranet auto-deploys on push to* `main`*, and this session is under the deploy hold.)*
2. **Find out why Schemathesis produces no NDJSON** on the demo target — the artifact path is `systemTest/schemathesis/output/schemathesis-reports/schemathesis-output.ndjson`. This is the substantive half.
3. **Then** get one green run on the board, so a future red means something.

## The pattern

Fourth instance today of the same defect — **signals firing into channels nobody reads** — and the only one aimed at humans rather than CI:

* [KS-637](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-637) — nightly Internal Audit, 40 consecutive failures.
* [KS-636](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-636) — base-image watchdog flagged a CRITICAL, unread 13 days.
* [KS-635](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-635) — a baseline exception expiring 2026-08-31 whose owner is archived.
* [KS-634](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-634) — no gate runs the service unit suites.

This one is different in kind and worse in effect: the others are unread, **this one is read and disbelieved.**

*Found during the 2026-08-14 backlog sweep, running the extranet skill's test-runner review that boot skipped.*

nodes.body:
**Measured 2026-09-07, in a catalogue pass over all 293 open tickets:** GitHub Actions is retired for this repo and I verified it directly rather than taking it on trust. **2,000 runs across 20 API pages are 100% `startup_failure`, back to 2026-08-20** — it never became non-uniform, so the outage is at least 18 days and widening the pages could not find its start. The three most recent runs return **zero jobs**. **16 workflow files are still in the repo doing nothing.**

**This is the cause of the symptom in this ticket.** The extranet Testing tab's runner dispatches a GitHub Actions workflow (`extranet-test-run.yml`). Actions has been dead for at least 18 days, and the board has been red for far longer — 17 `failed`, 5 `error`, 0 `passed` in 22 runs since 2026-05-25.

**So the board is not broken; it is disconnected.** No amount of fixing the parsing or the dashboard will make it green while its trigger cannot start a job. Any fix has to answer what executes the suites now that Actions does not — which is the same question **KS-652** and **KS-961** face.

Sibling **KS-139** (upload the Platform S suite so the runner executes it) is blocked by the identical cause. That one is Stuart's, so it is an escalation for Kam rather than something I have touched.

— catalogue pass 2026-09-07 (Blockchain-B, board-only seat). Measured, not inferred.

title: node:24-alpine carries a CRITICAL (CVE-2026-59873) — our own base-image watchdog flagged it on 2026-08-01 and the failure went unread
description:
## BLUF

**The base-image CVE watchdog fired on 2026-08-01 and nobody heard it.** Its scheduled run failed — which is, by the workflow's own design, the alarm — reporting `node:24-alpine`**: 1 CRITICAL / 4 HIGH — CVE-2026-59873**. That is the base image for **all ten backend services**.

Thirteen days unread at the time of filing. The watch is monthly, so without intervention the next signal is **2026-09-01**.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/base-image-refresh.yml`, run `30685775724`, `event=schedule`, `created 2026-08-01T05:24:40Z`, `conclusion=failure`. Failing step: **"Evaluate watch conditions"**. Job log:

```
=== Trivy scan (CRITICAL/HIGH) of fresh local bases ===
  node:24-alpine                            : 1 CRITICAL / 4 HIGH — criticals: CVE-2026-59873
  nginx:1.30-alpine                         : 0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH
  nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.30-alpine   : 0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH
  edoburu/pgbouncer:v1.25.2-p0              : 0 CRITICAL / 2 HIGH
  redis:8-alpine                            : 0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH
  postgres:15-alpine                        : 1 CRITICAL / 14 HIGH — criticals: CVE-2025-68121
```

The postgres critical is the known [KS-365](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-365) residual (local-dev surface only, upstream's to fix) and is **not** why the run failed. The run failed on **Case 2** of its own contract:

> The run FAILS in exactly two cases, both worth a human: … 2. any OTHER base reports a CRITICAL → a pinned base has re-accumulated a critical CVE; treat like KS-363 (refresh/bump + redeploy).

`node:24-alpine` is that other base. The workflow did exactly what it was built to do.

**Every pinned base also reported** `MOVED` — all six tags were republished upstream since the last pull, so the images we build on are behind their own tags regardless of the CVE.

## Scope

`node:24-alpine` is the `FROM` for **10 service Dockerfiles** (`nginx:1.30-alpine` for the other 2). So this is not one service — it is the whole backend, local and demo alike.

## What I have NOT established

* **Whether CVE-2026-59873 is exploitable in our usage.** I did not look it up: the project rule forbids fetching external URLs/changelogs unless asked. Someone should read the advisory before sizing this.
* **Whether it is still present today.** The scan is from 2026-08-01 and the tag has moved since. It may already be fixed upstream — a re-run answers it in minutes.

**Neither gap is a reason to leave it.** A critical on the base image of every service, flagged by our own watchdog and unread for a fortnight, is worth a human either way.

## Next action

1. **Re-run the watch now** (`workflow_dispatch` on `base-image-refresh.yml`) to get a current reading rather than a fortnight-old one.
2. Read CVE-2026-59873 and decide: rebuild on the moved tag, bump the base, or accept with a written reason.
3. If a rebuild is needed it lands behind the Kintsugi hold like everything else — it is a rebuild of every service image.

## The process defect, which is the more important half

**A failed scheduled run is this watch's ONLY notification channel**, and it is one nobody checks. The workflow header says so plainly: *"Scheduled-run failures notify via GitHub, which is the reminder."* That reminder went nowhere for 13 days.

Same shape as [KS-635](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-635) (an audit-baseline expiry whose owning ticket was archived) and [KS-634](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-634) (no gate runs the service unit suites): **we have signals that fire correctly into channels nobody reads.** Worth deciding once, for all three, where an unattended failure should actually land.

*Found during the 2026-08-14 backlog sweep while verifying KS-365.*

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Kam ruled the 31-decision card `secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109` on 2026-11-09 at 13:44:07 (live board), in these words: "Decision secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109: a — All recommendations (A and B)". Option a reads: "Every row ruled as recommended; a board seat files and moves the tickets; the KS-607 demo rows still wait for a separate yes." This ticket is row C2 of the decision pack. Section C rows are ruled by Wednesday, with Kam holding a veto, and Wednesday ruled this one as recommended: a local scheduled scan (Trivy) of the base images on a Secuura seat's schedule, reporting to the board. Each deploy also records which base image it built on. This adds a doctor check and a portability item.

Measured in the decision pack: the monthly alarm fired on 2026-08-01 and went unread, and GitHub Actions has been dead since 2026-08-20 (KS-638). The build goes to a build seat; nothing was changed in code by this comment.

Comment only: the state stays Backlog.

## Evidence only — what the Kintsugi rebuild actually baked (2026-08-15, session 35)

**No action taken on this ticket: not closed, not re-scoped, not re-prioritised, and the watch was NOT dispatched.** Adding evidence for whoever decides it.

**Why I did not re-run the watch, even though it is this ticket's own Next Action #1:** `base-image-refresh.yml` is shared CI, and dispatching it is actioning the ticket rather than informing it. Flagging that the ticket's first step is currently blocked by scope, not by difficulty — **it is a `workflow_dispatch` away for anyone who has that scope**, and it would answer the "is it still present?" gap in minutes.

## What I could measure: the demo VM after the full rebuild

The 2026-08-14 Kintsugi deploy rebuilt **all 30 service images natively on the VM**, so it re-pulled `node:24-alpine` at that moment. Read directly from the running containers today:

| | |
| -- | -- |
| Node | **v24.19.0** |
| Alpine | **3.24.1** |
| Arch | **aarch64** |
| Base rootfs (from image history) | `alpine-minirootfs-3.24.1-aarch64.tar.gz` |
| Service image created | **2026-08-14T03:31:59Z** (the rebuild) |

**Consistent across four services checked independently** — `auth`, `originate`, `api-gateway`, `anchoring` — all `node v24.19.0 / alpine 3.24.1`. Confirms the ticket's scope claim that this is one base under the whole backend, not a per-service question.

## The digest this ticket asked for is not recoverable from the VM

`docker image inspect node:24-alpine` on the demo VM returns **`No such image`** — the base tag is not retained after the build, so there is **no `RepoDigest` to read**. The build cache that would have held it was pruned during the same deploy (14 GB, to make room for the rebuild).

**So the specific artefact the next-action asks for — "the digest now baked" — cannot be produced after the fact.** The version triple above is the strongest available substitute, and it is arguably the more useful one anyway: **CVE applicability is decided by package versions, not by a manifest digest.**

**Worth carrying:** if a future rebuild wants its base digest recorded, that has to be captured *during* the build (`docker image inspect node:24-alpine --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}'` before pruning), because it is gone afterwards.

## What this does NOT establish

- **Whether `node:24-alpine` at 24.19.0 / alpine 3.24.1 still carries CVE-2026-59873.** I did not look up the advisory — the project rule forbids fetching external URLs unless asked, and the ticket already flags this same gap. **Nothing here should be read as "it is fixed" or "it is still present".**
- **Whether the demo's build pulled the same digest the 2026-08-01 scan saw.** The scan ran on x86-64 CI; the demo is **aarch64**, so they are different manifests under one tag regardless.

## Net
The demo is running a base that was **freshly pulled on 2026-08-14**, thirteen days after the flagged scan, on a tag the watch reported as `MOVED`. That is a genuinely newer base than the one scanned — **but "newer" is not "clean", and only the advisory or a re-run settles it.**

title: prism issues VCs with random bytes as the Ed25519 proof and verifies them as passed — the A-11 fraud pattern fixed in vc-issuer, never fixed here
description:
## BLUF

`services/prism` issues verifiable credentials whose `Ed25519Signature2020` proof is **64 random bytes**, and its `/verify` returns `passed: true` without checking anything. This is the identical pattern that was ruled fraud-grade and **fixed in** `vc-issuer` **under Audit A-11** — `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts:125-128` says so in its own comment. It was never fixed in prism.

**Tracking ticket in the KS-621 pattern: severity is provisional and the fix shape is deliberately blank.** The by-design-or-remediate ruling is Kam's, and it turns on the deciding question below. Filed off [KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489) Review D pass-2 (peter, 2026-07-21) — the finding has had no home since.

## The finding, re-verified at `c13b5ba9a` (2026-08-13)

Peter's citations are unmoved — verified line-by-line, not assumed:

| Site | Code |
| -- | -- |
| `services/prism/src/index.ts:658-663` | `type: 'Ed25519Signature2020'` … `proofValue: crypto.randomBytes(64).toString('base64')` |
| `services/prism/src/index.ts:787` | `checks.push({ check: 'proof', passed: true }); // Mock verification` |
| `services/prism/src/index.ts:35` | `const PRISM_MODE = process.env.PRISM_MODE \|\| 'mock';` |

## Two corrections to the original framing — both make it read differently

**1.** `PRISM_MODE` **is decorative. It is never branched on.** Peter's write-up says *"*`PRISM_MODE` *defaults to* `'mock'` *with no production gate on the issue path → a prod deploy that **forgets the flag** forges credentials."* Measured: `PRISM_MODE` occurs **5 times** in the file — the declaration (`:35`), the `/health` response (`:376`), the `/api` info response (`:390`), the boot log (`:893`) and the boot banner (`:899`). `grep -c "if.*PRISM_MODE\|PRISM_MODE ===\|switch.*PRISM_MODE"` returns **0**.

So the risk is not a forgotten flag. **The flag has no effect at all**, and it is *already set to a non-mock value in both deploy paths*: `docker-compose.yml:965` sets `PRISM_MODE=basic`, and `deployment/azure/services.bicep:980` sets `PRISM_MODE=basic`. The behaviour is byte-identical to mock.

**2. The service actively misreports its own mode.** Because `:376` and `:390` echo `PRISM_MODE` into `/health` and `/api`, prism currently answers `mode: "basic"` to any operator, monitor or auditor asking whether it is mocked — while forging every signature. That is worse than a missing gate: a missing gate is silent, this one answers the question wrongly. Anyone who checked "is this service mocked?" the obvious way would have been told no.

## Reachability — the reason severity is provisional, not asserted

Bounded to what I could prove, and it cuts **toward** lower live risk:

* **The gateway does not route to prism's credential path.** `/api/credentials` → `vcIssuer` (`proxy.ts:697-699`), `/api/presentations` → `vcIssuer` (`:712,:715-717`). The **only** prism mapping is `/api/did` (`proxy.ts:645-647`), authenticated.
* **Zero internal consumers.** Repo-wide, `PRISM_SERVICE_URL` / `prism:4001` has no caller outside the gateway's own service-config and system-status listing. No frontend calls `/api/prism`.
* **But the service is live**: `secuura-prism` is Up + healthy in the local stack, and it was in the Container Apps bicep. The forging path is **one route mapping away** from being reachable, with nothing in the code to stop it.

This is the same disposition class as [KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488)'s C-2 wallet-verify stub — **latent, not live**: reachable in principle, no current consumer trusting the result.

## The deciding question (this is what the ruling turns on)

**Does** `services/prism` **have a future in which it runs for real — or is it a stub that should refuse to issue at all?**

The question as originally posed — *"does prism ever run non-mock?"* — assumes a mode switch that could be flipped. There isn't one. So the real question is narrower and sharper:

* If prism is **dead or demo-only scaffolding** → the honest fix is to make it *say so* (refuse to issue, or label the proof honestly per the KS-520/522 precedent, where a `mock_tx_` anchor is never presented as on-chain proof), and stop `/health` reporting `basic`.
* If prism is **intended to become a real DID/VC service** → this is a Wave-2 integrity item and the A-11 remediation already applied to vc-issuer is the template.

**Fix shape deliberately blank pending that ruling.** Specifying it now would pre-decide the product question, which is the KS-621 lesson.

## Provisional severity

**High**, per Wednesday's SCORE ruling (session 25) — carried as given. Recorded honestly: the reachability evidence above argues this is *latent*, while the reachable half of the same finding class sits in the vc-issuer holder-binding ticket. If Kam re-ranks the pair, the argument for putting the reachable one first is in both tickets.

## Adjacent, deliberately not filed as a third ticket

Peter's pass-2 also carries a **Low**: `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts:100` — `const issuer = req.body.issuer || defaultIssuer`, caller-controlled, then signed with the platform `VC_SIGNING_KEY` at `:146`. The A-11 gate (`:129-145`) removed the hardcoded-key fallback but **not** the caller-supplied issuer identity, so the finding survives its own fix. The session-26 brief scoped this to two tickets, so it is recorded here rather than filed unasked — flagging it for a ruling on whether it needs its own home.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** PR 2130 (head `11a394026233`, one commit on develop `204e62acdc35`) makes prism honest, as ruled (row A6, option 1): `POST /api/credentials` now answers 501 `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` for every body and stores nothing, instead of issuing credentials whose signature was 64 random bytes; `/health` and `/api` report mode `mock` instead of echoing `PRISM_MODE=basic`. It is waiting for review; nothing is merged or deployed.

- The verify route no longer passes a proof it never checked: `verified` is false, with the reason "Proof signature not verified: not implemented".
- `GET /api` lists the issue route as not implemented.
- `PRISM_MODE=basic` in `docker-compose.yml` and `services.bicep` is left in place and is now inert.
- No code in the repo calls prism's issue route or reads its mode; the gateway sends `/api/credentials` to vc-issuer. So nothing known reaches the forging path today; this makes it refuse regardless.
- Tests: 10 new cells, 7 red on develop for the predicted reasons and 10 green with the change; one mutant per changed site; the 39 existing prism cells unchanged. Real signing (option 2) is not built.

https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/2130

**BLUF:** Kam ruled the 31-decision card `secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109` on 2026-11-09 at 13:44:07 (live board), in these words: "Decision secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109: a — All recommendations (A and B)". Option a reads: "Every row ruled as recommended; a board seat files and moves the tickets; the KS-607 demo rows still wait for a separate yes." This ticket is row A6 of the decision pack, ruled as recommended: option 1. Make prism honest now: it refuses to issue (a 501, the same fix as the wallet-verify one in PR 685) and stops reporting its mode as "basic". Small; one revert undoes it.

A build seat does the work; nothing was changed in code by this comment.

Alongside this comment the ticket moves from Backlog to Todo.

## A third instance of this pattern exists — and it was remediated on 2026-08-13, before your ruling

Recording this here **so your ruling covers three instances knowingly rather than
two blindly.** This is an input to the decision, not a pre-emption of it.

**The third instance:** `wallet-connector`'s `POST /api/wallets/verify` returned
`{ verified: true }` for any request carrying three non-empty strings. No
cryptography ran. Found as KS-488 **C-2**; fixed to fail closed with 501 in
**PR #685**.

## Why it was not held for your ruling, when KS-624 and KS-625 are

The three are the same pattern — a service asserting cryptographic validity it
does not perform — but they are not equivalent on the axis that matters here:

| | reachable? | does it *claim* to verify? |
|---|---|---|
| **prism** (KS-624) | **Latent** — gateway routes only `/api/did` to prism; `/api/credentials` + `/api/presentations` go to vcIssuer | yes — answers `mode: "basic"` while stamping `crypto.randomBytes(64)` |
| **vc-issuer verify** (KS-625) | proxied behind auth, reachable | yes |
| **wallet-connector verify** (C-2) | **live, published, gateway-routed, authenticated** | yes — the OpenAPI description asserted *"Verifies CIP-30 (Cardano) signatures via the COSE key, or EVM signatures via ecrecover"* |

"These mocks are acceptable pre-funding" is a coherent position for a latent stub
behind an unrouted path. It is a materially different proposition for an endpoint
that is **actively returning a false cryptographic assurance to whoever calls it**,
while its own published documentation tells the caller verification happened.

That distinction is our judgement, not yours — which is exactly why it is written
here rather than left implicit in a merge.

## If you rule "by design, leave them"

**Reverting C-2 is one revert.** PR #685 is a single squashed commit touching one
handler, its spec entry, one schemathesis exception and a test file. Nothing
depends on the 501. Say the word and it goes back.

Note what reverting would restore, so the choice is explicit: an authenticated,
published endpoint answering `verified: true` to any caller, with a spec that says
it verified a CIP-30 signature. If the ruling is "acceptable pre-funding", the
honest form of that is a stub that *says* it is a stub — which is the shape C-2
shipped (501 `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`), not the one it replaced.

## What C-2 did NOT do

It did not implement verification, and it did not pretend to. Real CIP-8/COSE
verification is filed as **KS-627** — it needs a breaking contract change (the
CIP-30 COSE key was removed from the request schema by KS-475 as "unread", and a
Cardano public key cannot be derived from a blake2b address, so no correct
implementation can exist against the published contract), new crypto dependencies,
and test vectors from real wallets.

## The question still open for you, unchanged

KS-624 and KS-625 remain **by-design-or-remediate**, untouched, awaiting your call.
Nothing about prism or vc-issuer changed on 2026-08-13.

title: GET /api/anchors/{id} and verify report different statuses for the same anchor — 91 UAT anchors read "failed" while verify says confirmed
description:
Raised from the S side 2026-08-12 (S ticket: [PS-577](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-577>)). @kamil.kreiser — one authenticated call settles this; details below.

## The observation

Platform S polls `GET /api/anchors/{id}` to learn when an anchor confirms. On UAT, **91 transactions are stuck reporting** `failed` — while `POST /api/verification/verify`, asked about the same document's content hash, reports the **same anchor id** as confirmed on chain.

Concretely, anchor `anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2`:

```
POST /api/verification/verify  {"providedHash":"6ffa6a0d4378007a480af701b6113cc0252544bcfde93cf11c2654c8bbe2367e"}

  verified   : true              status  : anchored
  anchorId   : anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2
  bc.status  : confirmed         txHash  : e64759a924ea314e…
  anchoredAt : 2026-08-09T06:18:39.090Z
  checks     : documentExists ✓ hashValid ✓ isCertified ✓ isAnchored ✓ integrityVerified ✓
```

S recorded its failure for that same anchor at **06:32:20** — **fourteen minutes after** `anchoredAt`. So this is not a race between a poll and a late confirmation.

A second sample behaves identically: document ref `doc-1785566174843-631e2310` (an originate/upload), `verified: true`, `confirmed`, txHash `38adf13132f6856a…`, while S has it marked failed.

## What has been ruled out on the S side

Both plausible S-side causes were eliminated before raising this:

* **Not a failed/unauthenticated read.** All six affected organisations are registered with connector keys, and each has rows that *did* confirm — org 6: 77 confirmed vs 58 failed, org 9: 39 vs 20, org 13: 8 vs 6. Reads plainly work for these tenants.
* **Not an S mapping bug.** For an `anchor_…` reference S takes the `status` field from `/api/anchors/{id}` **verbatim** — no interpretation layer is involved. S is reporting the exact word it is given.

Spread is across every verb (share 39, upload 16, share-attach-consent 13, certify 5, sign 5, watermark 4, and the share-edit verbs), so it is not verb-specific.

## The question

Does `GET /api/anchors/{id}` return a stale or different status than the anchor's true state?

Candidates worth checking:

1. The anchors read serves a row that `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` ([KS-535](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-535/a-failed-on-chain-anchor-still-reports-statusanchored-async-failure)) later healed, without the anchors view reflecting the heal.
2. There are two anchor records and the endpoints resolve different ones — the [KS-563](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-563/verify-api-iscertified-is-true-for-merely-anchored-documents-so)/584 "answer from the row that evidences its claims" family, except here it is the *anchors* endpoint that looks wrong.
3. `/api/anchors/{id}` is correct and verify is optimistic — in which case S's reading is right and the bug is elsewhere.

**The one call that settles it:**

```
GET /api/anchors/anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2
```

on demo-pk, authenticated. If it returns `status: failed` while verify reports that anchor confirmed with tx `e64759a924ea314e…`, the inconsistency is confirmed and the question becomes which is authoritative. I could not make this call myself — the endpoint requires auth — so the diagnosis above is inferred from S's behaviour plus the eliminations, not directly observed.

## Why it matters to S

1. Users see **"anchor failed" on documents that are anchored and confirmed on chain** — a false negative on a trust surface.
2. **S never collects the real transaction hash.** Those rows keep their `anchor_…` placeholder permanently, so the chain evidence K is holding is silently lost to S.
3. It makes S's anchoring-failure count unusable as an alert signal.

## What S has done meanwhile

S no longer takes a bare `failed` as final ([Secuura/platform-s#440](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-577-dont-take-anchor-failed-as-final-when-ks-own-verify-disagrees-4a8640ddf0ac), merged). When the anchors endpoint reports failed, S asks verify and prefers the evidenced answer **only** when verify names the same `anchorId`, reports it anchored, not simulated, and carries a real 64-hex transaction hash.

That is a mitigation, not a fix — it recovers the lost hashes and stops the false failures, but the two endpoints still disagree, and S is now quietly compensating for it. Worth resolving at source.

Related: [PS-577](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-577>), [KS-535](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-535/a-failed-on-chain-anchor-still-reports-statusanchored-async-failure), [KS-563](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-563/verify-api-iscertified-is-true-for-merely-anchored-documents-so).

**BLUF:** Kam ruled the 31-decision card `secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109` on 2026-11-09 at 13:44:07 (live board), in these words: "Decision secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109: a — All recommendations (A and B)". Option a reads: "Every row ruled as recommended; a board seat files and moves the tickets; the KS-607 demo rows still wait for a separate yes." This ticket is row A18 of the decision pack, ruled as recommended: option 1, for the code only: add a rule that a row with a real transaction and block cannot read "failed", built after the KS-1384 reconciler work.

The three demo rows wait for Kam's separate yes. This comment and the state move touch nothing on demo. A build seat does the work; nothing was changed in code by this comment.

Alongside this comment the ticket moves from Backlog to Todo.

@peter — **answering your gating question, so KS-608 can be written.**

## BLUF

**Same lifecycle fact, different resolution scope — NOT two facts by design.** Your outcome 4 is ruled out and **KS-608 survives**. But its invariant needs re-scoping before you write it, or it will fire false positives on 12 content hashes on demo today.

And there is a real defect underneath: **3 anchors on demo read `status: failed` while carrying a real 64-hex tx hash, a real block number, and a set `confirmed_at`.**

## Recommendation

Write KS-608, but scope the invariant to **the same anchor id**, not the same document. And add a second, stronger invariant that needs no cross-endpoint comparison at all (below) — it is self-contained, and it would have caught this class without depending on which endpoint wins.

---

## 1. Why it is not "two facts by design"

Both fields read the same column, `anchor_store.status`. Neither is a submission-vs-confirmation distinction like the one KS-563 established.

- **`GET /api/anchors/{id}`** (`services/anchoring/src/index.ts:765`) looks up **one anchor row by anchor id** and returns `status: anchor.status` verbatim. It answers *"what happened to this submission attempt?"*
- **verify's blockchain block** (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:216–262`) resolves over **every anchor for the document**, sorts by `blockNumber` descending, takes the top one, and maps `latest.status === 'confirmed' ? 'on-chain' : 'pending-onchain'`. It answers *"does this document have on-chain evidence?"*

Same fact, resolved over different row sets — one row versus best-of-N.

## 2. What that means for KS-608's invariant

*"The two endpoints must not contradict each other about the same anchor"* is correct **only if scoped to the same anchor id**. Verify is not answering about an anchor; it is answering about a document/content hash. Where a document has both a failed and a confirmed anchor, **both endpoints are correct and they still disagree**.

That is not hypothetical. On demo right now:

| content hashes with… | count |
| --- | --- |
| exactly 1 anchor | 104 |
| more than 1 anchor | 31 |
| …of those, carrying **both** a confirmed and a failed anchor | **12** |

A document-scoped invariant fails on all 12 while nothing is wrong. An anchor-scoped one holds.

## 3. The real defect — and a better invariant

demo has 92 failed anchors. They are not one population:

| class | count | evidence | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| KS-587 simulated placeholders | **83** | placeholder tx, **0** with a block number | correctly `failed` |
| `ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent"` — never landed | **6** | tx `null`, no block, `confirmed_at` null | correctly `failed` |
| `ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent"` — **landed anyway** | **3** | **real 64-hex tx, real block number, `confirmed_at` SET** | **`failed` is wrong** |

Your ticket's own sample is in the third class:

```
anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2
  status       : failed
  transaction  : 28ecec5c29ce886346…   (real 64-hex)
  block_number : 4554493
  confirmed_at : 2026-08-09 06:29:49+00
  retry_count  : 3
  error        : ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent.
                  Transaction has probably already been included"
```

The error text says the transaction probably landed; the block number says it did. This is the [KS-535](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-535) wallet race — two deployments selecting the same UTxOs, the loser recording a terminal failure for a transaction the winner already got on chain.

**So the second invariant, which I would rate above the cross-endpoint one:**

> An anchor carrying a real 64-hex `transaction_hash` **and** a non-null `block_number` must not read `status: failed`.

Single endpoint, no correlation, no ambiguity about which side is authoritative, and it catches exactly the rows S is stuck on.

## 4. One honest limit on this analysis

Your numbers are from **UAT**; I measured **demo**. The specific tx verify reported to you (`e64759a924ea314e…`) **does not exist in demo's anchor_store** at all, and the ticket's anchor carries a different tx on demo (`28ecec5c…`). So I have not reproduced S's exact verify response — what I have is the mechanism, plus three live instances of the contradiction on demo.

Also worth flagging for your 91-vs-92 arithmetic: on demo the large majority (83) are KS-587 placeholders that are **correctly** failed. If UAT splits the same way, most of S's stuck rows are not this bug — they are documents that genuinely never anchored, and S is right to show them failed. The bug is the tail.

All reads were read-only SELECTs against demo. Nothing written, Kintsugi hold intact.

## One question ahead of the investigation — it gates the systemTest leg

@kamil.kreiser — before you dig into this, there is a single semantics question whose answer decides whether the systemTest regression for this class can be written at all. It does **not** need the investigation done, the authenticated call made, or the 91 rows resolved.

> **Are `GET /api/anchors/{id}.status` and verify's `blockchain.status` the same lifecycle fact, or two different facts by design?**

## Why it matters more than it looks

The systemTest leg is filed as **KS-608** (child of KS-492, currently **Blocked** on this ticket). Its invariant is *"the two endpoints must not contradict each other about the same anchor"* — deliberately stated so it holds whichever endpoint turns out authoritative, and asserts nothing about repair.

That works under three of your four candidate outcomes, but not the fourth:

| Outcome | Effect on KS-608 |
| --- | --- |
| The anchors read is stale (a row `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` healed) | Invariant stands |
| Two anchor records, the endpoints resolve different ones | Invariant stands |
| Verify is optimistic, the anchors read is right | Invariant stands |
| **The two fields are different lifecycle facts by design** | **Invariant is wrong** — they are permitted to differ, and KS-608 gets deleted rather than adjusted |

**The fourth is not hypothetical, which is why I am asking rather than assuming.** KS-563 already established that `status` flips to `anchored` on **submission**, not confirmation — *"a chain blob is authoritative, and the status fallback applies only when there is no blob at all"*. This platform has drawn exactly that submission-vs-confirmation distinction once already. If it applies to the anchors read too, then `failed` from `/api/anchors/{id}` alongside `confirmed` from verify may be two honest answers to two different questions — and S's mitigation is compensating for a contract it misread rather than a defect.

I am not asserting that is the case. Stuart's elimination work is solid and the fourteen-minute gap makes a poll race implausible. But it is the one branch where writing the test first wastes the work.

## What I am NOT waiting on

Your investigation, the disposition of the 91 UAT rows, KS-587's re-anchor-or-mark-failed decision, and the KS-584/KS-563 row-selection family. None of those change what KS-608 asserts.

A one-line answer unblocks it. If the honest answer is *"don't know until I make the call"*, that is fine too — say so and KS-608 stays blocked on the full investigation rather than on a question you cannot yet answer.

*— posted by agent on Peter's behalf, 2026-08-12.*

title: BM-2: Verification is a configurable workflow via smart contracts — record the workflow path, not casual views
description:
## BLUF

**Verification is a CONFIGURABLE WORKFLOW, not a fixed function.** Clients configure verification workflows via smart contracts; Secuura does NOT prescribe compliance. The workflow PATH is verified against the smart contract and recorded; simple interactions like document VIEWING are NOT recorded on-chain (noise). A third-party verifier (e.g. recruiter verifying a university document) sees the inspectable steps (identity checks, domain matching). End-user sees a binary "verified"; audit/legal sees full rigor.

## Carried ruling (PS-556, Kam 2026-08-11)

A verification is a **public, repeatable READ** — it sits OUTSIDE canonical lineage (lineage = versions from certifications/modifications). If a verification act is recorded at all, **S records it for S's own reporting/lineage annotation — K does NOT become a source of record for verification acts.**

Source: 2026-08-11 technical weekly (Stuart, Phil, Kam).

title: Architecture P1: defuse the MULTI_TENANCY registry upsert — it silently collapses registrations per (hash, tenant) if the flag is ever enabled
description:
**Ask:** In the same phase that touches registration (plan-sheet requirement — not later, not beside), defuse `platform_document_registry`'s armed landmine: UNIQUE `uq_pdr_hash_tenant (content_hash, tenant_id)` + `ON CONFLICT (content_hash, tenant_id) DO UPDATE` in `registerInPlatformRegistry`. Either re-key the registry on the document UUID, or explicitly remove/disable the upsert.

**Why it matters:** the code path is dormant ONLY because `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED !== 'true'` on local and demo (0 registry rows in both DBs). If that flag is ever switched on with today's code, the upsert wakes and silently collapses registration pointers — newest write wins per (hash, tenant) — which directly violates ruling (b): duplicate bytes = two registrations, distinguished by UUID. A landmine that has been found and left armed is worse than one nobody found.

**Spec:** `1_Project_Definition/architecture/2026-08-07_K-side-plan-sheet.md` ("The MULTI_TENANCY landmine — inside P1, not beside it").

nodes.body:
## Confirmed live on `develop` `541acae81` — the landmine is still armed, both halves

**The upsert**, `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:396` (read from `origin/develop`, not the working tree):

```sql
ON CONFLICT (content_hash, tenant_id) DO UPDATE SET
  document_id = EXCLUDED.document_id, title = EXCLUDED.title, status = EXCLUDED.status, updated_at = NOW()
```

**The constraint**, from the live database:

```
uq_pdr_hash_tenant   (plus platform_document_registry_pkey, idx_pdr_hash, idx_pdr_doc)
```

So both halves are present and they compose exactly as the description says: two documents with the same `content_hash` in one tenant do not collide loudly — the second **overwrites the first's `document_id`** in the registry, and the first registration stops being findable by hash. Silent, and it looks like a successful registration to the caller.

One method note, because it nearly gave me a wrong answer: my first search matched `services/originate/dist/routes/verification.d.ts` — **build output**, which is not the authority and which does not exist at `origin/develop` at all (`git show` refused it). Reading a `dist/` file would have been reading yesterday's compile. The line above is from the `src/` file at the SHA. Also: the search only ran at all once `--include=*.ts` was quoted — unquoted, zsh's `nomatch` kills grep before it starts and the result reads as a clean zero.

Sequencing point from the description stands: this belongs in the same phase as [KS-597](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-597), not after it — registration is the write path that arms it.

No code written. Left in Todo.

title: not_a_server_error recurs — 17 raw 5xx across 8 ops (KS-431 / KS-449 / KS-497 recurrence, full-2026-08-07 sweep)
description:
## Why a new ticket

The whole predecessor chain is **Done and archived**:

* [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods) — Done 2026-07-10 · [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) — Done 2026-07-13 · [KS-449](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-449/write-path-residuals-from-ks-430-ks-431-remaining-raw-500s-request) — Done · [KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks) — Done 2026-07-29, archived

Each closed having fixed the raw-500 class down to its listed operations, and each time it has come back on different ones. Filed fresh per that precedent.

## Finding

**17** `not_a_server_error` **failures across 8 operations** — an unhandled value reaches a handler or the DB and throws, instead of being rejected with a mapped 4xx.

`GET /api/users/admin/list` · `POST /api/documents/{id}/lifecycle-events` · `POST /api/documents/{id}/revoke` · `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` · `POST /api/m365/outlook/exchange-token` · `POST /api/security/rate-limit/check` · `POST /api/users/admin/create` · `POST /api/webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret`

**Three of these are the** [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) **endpoints** — `/share`, `/lifecycle-events`, and the `documents/{id}` family. Kamil shipped the connector-actor fix on 2026-08-07 (`develop` `307483672`, PR #652) and verified all three return 201 on demo for a connector. These 5xx are on *fuzzed* input rather than the connector path, so they are likely a different trigger on the same handlers — but worth confirming they are not a regression from that change.

`GET /api/users/admin/list` and `POST /api/users/admin/create` are already documented on [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) **§2** with root causes traced (`parseInt(offset) || 0` lets `-1` through to Postgres; `data.email.toLowerCase()` with no type guard). [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) also notes **the negative-offset pattern is six sites across four services**, not the two the sweep reaches.

## Important — this count was inflated until today

`not_a_server_error` read **79 failures** on the previous sweep. It dropped to **17** once the governance active-proposal cap was cleared: the cap throws a bare `Error` that the route maps to `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, and every fuzzed proposal-create was counting as a server error. That mis-mapping is filed separately. **62 of the previous 79 were that one defect** — worth knowing before sizing this.

## Where this was run

**Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS** (kernel `7.0.0-28-generic`, **aarch64**) on Parallels, 8 vCPU / 31 GB, at `10.211.55.4`.

| Component | Version |  | Component | Version |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (aarch64) |  | Docker | 29.7.2 |
| Python (venv + host) | 3.14.6 |  | Node (services) | 24.19.0 (`node:24-alpine`) |
| Schemathesis | 4.24.3 |  | PostgreSQL | 15.18 (`postgres:15-alpine`) |
| pytest / Hypothesis | 9.1.1 / 6.165.2 |  | Redis | 8.10.0 (`redis:8-alpine`) |

Run of record: `full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z`, seed `2794626967`, 24.1 min.

## Reproduce

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r '.data.accessToken')

# KS-565 §2 — negative offset reaches Postgres
curl -i -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  'http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/list?offset=-1'

# KS-565 §2 — non-string email hits .toLowerCase()
curl -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":{},"password":"Str0ng-Passw0rd!","role":"OWNER"}' \
  http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/create
```

Full sweep: `cd systemTest/schemathesis && python3 scripts/run.py full` — 94 replayable crash files with `code_sample` curls under `output/reports/full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z/schemathesis-crashes/`.

## Fix direction

Per [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods) / [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) / [KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks): classify the error at the route boundary — map known provider/validation failures to 4xx/503, keep genuine unknowns as 500 with structured logging, and guard path params and body fields before they reach the DB. Add unit tests pinning each classifier. **Fix all six negative-offset sites, not the two the sweep found** ([KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) §2 lists them).

## Note

The report had been attributing this class to [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) **with a bare ticket reference**, which reads as ownership. PR #656 now renders `KS-431 (closed — recurrence untracked)`; this ticket is the live owner.

Refs as KS-NNN text. Found by the [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-schemathesis-integration-mode-anchor-honesty-consistency-a) sweeps, 2026-08-07.

## ⚠ The class is twice as wide as recorded — `limit` has the identical flaw

Every one of those sites also parses a `limit` the same way, and **a negative `LIMIT` is equally fatal**. Measured on the local stack:

```
SELECT 1 LIMIT -1;   ->  ERROR:  LIMIT must not be negative
SELECT 1 LIMIT  1;   ->  1                    (control)
```

**And `Math.min` is what makes this look guarded when it is not.** `Math.min(parseInt(x) || 50, 200)` clamps the *upper* bound only — `Math.min(-1, 200)` is `-1`. So the sites that appear defended are defended against the wrong direction. That covers the six above plus limit-only sites in `analytics` (`dashboard.ts:29`/`:39`, `analytics.ts:364`), `billing` (`billing.ts:464`/`:488`) and `originate` (`documents.ts:247`).

**Sizing consequence:** the recorded scope is 6 sites × 1 param. The measured scope is ~11 sites × up to 2 params, plus one derived-offset path.

## Recommended fix shape — one helper, not eleven patches

**Do not patch the sites individually.** This class has recurred through KS-421 → KS-431 → KS-449 → KS-497 → KS-593, each closing "down to its listed operations" and each returning on different ones. Per-site patching is what produces that chain: the fix travels with the operations the sweep happened to sample, and property-based generation samples rather than enumerates.

Shape: a shared `parsePaginationParam(raw, { default, min, max })` (or extend the existing `@secuura/shared` pagination package, which already exists) that returns a clamped value **or** a typed 400, adopted at every site. Then:

- **A guard test over the corpus, not the instances** — every request-derived `parseInt` of a pagination param must go through the helper, asserted as an exact set of call sites the way KS-751's caller guard does it. That is what makes the sixth recurrence not happen, and it is the part this ticket has never had.
- Sub-class B is separate work: validate the nonce/uuid **before** it reaches the cast, and assert the body carries no driver text.

- Red-before-green per sub-class, and per parameter: `offset=-1`, `limit=-1`, `page=-1` each independently, since they fail at different layers.

## Size: L, and it splits cleanly into two

- **A (pagination range):** the helper + ~11 call sites + the corpus guard — **M**, and the guard is the half that matters.
- **B (uuid-cast disclosure, 2 wallet ops):** **S**, but it is the one with a disclosure component and should carry KS-703's acceptance shape.
