`POST /api/wallets/verify` returns **501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED**, which is the deliberate fail-closed behaviour from **KS-488 C-2** — the endpoint used to return `verified:true` for any three strings and was changed to refuse. It is doing exactly what it should.

`not_a_server_error` flags it only because 501 is in the 5xx range. **That is a harness gap, not a platform defect, and it is mine (Peter's) to close** — `schemathesis.toml` carries an expected-statuses exception for this operation, but that exception does not suppress `not_a_server_error`. I am recording it here so the count reads honestly: **4 real 5xx, not 5.**

## Reproduce

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r '.data.accessToken')

# already-known: negative offset reaches Postgres
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 'http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/list?offset=-1'

# NEW: non-UUID string reaches Postgres via wallet auth
curl -i -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"walletAddress":"addr_test1qrjjw7rr","signature":"0","nonce":"__"}' \
  http://localhost:6882/api/auth/wallet/verify
```

Full artefacts (JUnit, NDJSON, VCR, HAR, Allure, HTML) under `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/full-2026-09-01T11-57-02Z/`.

## Environment

Mac, slot 1, 33 containers / 33 healthy, seeded users (`ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true`), Schemathesis 4.25.2, Python 3.14.6, anchoring in mock mode. Stack built from the branch/SHA above.

Refs as KS-NNN text. Measured and filed by agent on Peter's behalf, 2026-09-01.

**Correction to my 2026-08-28 comment — "500, empty body" was wrong. @kamil.kreiser's populated body is right, and my stack agrees with his.**

He flagged the divergence and asked whether it was a driver/PG difference between stacks. It was not. It was my reporting error.

Re-probed directly on my stack just now:

```
GET /api/users/admin/list?offset=-1
  -> 500  {"success":false,"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"OFFSET must not be negative"}}
```

**Populated, and identical to his.** My "empty body" came from reading `schemathesis-output.ndjson`, where the response body was not captured for those interactions — I recorded *absence of a captured body* as *an empty body*. Those are different things and I should not have conflated them. Whoever writes the guard's test should pin **`OFFSET must not be negative`**, not an empty response.

### Stack provenance — verified, since he raised the risk

He warned that a stack built while an auth branch was checked out would describe unmerged code, having nearly quoted #757's `400` as current behaviour himself. Checked mine:

```
docker exec secuura-auth grep -c rejectNulInListQuery /app/dist/routes/users.js  -> 0
git show origin/develop:…/services/auth/src/routes/users.ts | grep -c …          -> 0
```

**No #757 code in my running container, and none on develop.** My slot-1 stack was rebuilt from `origin/develop` @ `763343288` with only `systemTest/` changes on top, so the sweep results in my earlier comment describe develop. Good catch — worth every sweep author checking, not just this one.

### Incidental confirmation for KS-703 / #757

Same stack, same route, on develop:

```
GET /api/users/admin/list?search=%00
  -> 500  {"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"invalid byte sequence for encoding \"UTF8\": 0x00"}
```

Raw Postgres text in the envelope — the KS-703 leak, reproduced on develop, independent of #757. And `?offset=%00 -> 200` confirms his `parseInt` reasoning exactly: the NUL never reaches the query.

His conclusion stands unchanged — byte class and range class are orthogonal, and #757 correctly does not touch numeric params.

## Answering as #757's author — the shape deliberately does not extend to numeric params, and there is nothing there for it to catch

## BLUF

**Deliberate, and measurement backs it.** #757 guards `search` and `role` — *string* params whose raw value reaches the query. A NUL in a **numeric** param never gets that far, because `parseInt(x) || 0` turns it into `0` before anything else runs. So extending the guard to `offset`/`limit` would add a branch that can never fire.

The negative-offset defect is a different failure entirely: not an unstorable byte, but a **validly-parsed number with an out-of-range value**. It needs a range check, not a byte guard. That stays this ticket's — and KS-565 §2's six sites across four services remains the important half, as you say.

## Measured — 2026-08-29, live local gateway

```
GET /api/users/admin/list?offset=%00   -> 200   ← NUL in a numeric param: harmless
GET /api/users/admin/list?limit=%00    -> 200   ← same
GET /api/users/admin/list?offset=-1    -> 500   {"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"OFFSET must not be negative"}
GET /api/users/admin/list?offset=0&limit=5  -> 200   (control)
```

`parseInt('\x00')` is `NaN`, `NaN || 0` is `0` — the NUL is gone before Postgres sees anything. `parseInt('-1')` is `-1`, which is truthy, so it survives the `|| 0` and reaches the query as a negative OFFSET. **The `|| 0` fallback is exactly what makes numeric params immune to the byte class and exactly what fails to protect them from the range class.**

⚠ **One divergence from your report worth noting:** I get a *populated* body — `"OFFSET must not be negative"` — where you recorded `500, empty body`. Same status, same operation, different body. Could be a driver/PG version difference between our stacks; flagging rather than resolving, since it may matter to whoever writes the guard's test.

## ⚠ Caveat on the fourth measurement — and it applies to your runs too

```
GET /api/users/admin/list?search=%00   -> 400  VALIDATION_ERROR "Must not contain a NUL (U+0000) byte"
```

**That 400 is #757's behaviour, not develop's.** My local `secuura-auth` image was built from the unmerged #757 branch:

```
grep -c rejectNulInListQuery  in the running container's /app/dist/routes/users.js  -> 3
grep -c rejectNulInListQuery  in git show develop:…/routes/users.ts                 -> 0
```

On develop that request is still a **500** — the KS-703 defect #757 exists to fix. I nearly quoted the 400 as current platform behaviour.

Flagging because you are sweeping the same routes: **if your stack was also built while an auth branch was checked out, an auth-route result may be describing unmerged code.** The numeric measurements above are unaffected — `parseInt(req.query.offset as string) || 0` is byte-identical on develop (`routes/users.ts:352` and `:406`) and #757 adds nothing to either line.

## What #757 actually covers, precisely

* **Params:** `search` and `role` only.
* **Routes:** `GET /api/users` and `GET /api/users/admin/list`.
* **Bytes:** **U+0000 only.** Other C0 control bytes (U+0001 and friends) are stored happily by Postgres and return 200 today, here and everywhere else.
* **Placement:** before the `parseInt` lines, so it cannot interact with numeric coercion either way.

The reason it is that narrow is in the code comment: the platform's existing control-byte guard (KS-471/472, `findControlBytePath`) walks the request **body** only — nothing walks the query string — and widening it across the whole query string platform-wide is a **new rejection on every published GET contract**. That is the KS-703 ruling still open with Kam, not something #757 decided.

## So the two classes are orthogonal

| | byte class (KS-703 / #757) | range class (KS-593 / KS-565 §2) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Trigger | U+0000 in a **string** param | valid negative in a **numeric** param |
| Reaches Postgres? | yes, as an unstorable byte | yes, as a legal-but-wrong value |
| Neutralised by `\|\| 0`? | n/a — no coercion on strings | **no** — `-1` is truthy |
| Fix shape | reject the byte, 400 | clamp or reject the range, 400 |
| Scope | 2 params, 2 routes | **6 sites, 4 services** |

Nothing in #757 helps `offset=-1`, and nothing a range check does would help `search=%00`. Fixing one in the other's PR would blur two classes that this ticket's own history shows are easy to conflate — the same trap as my `organizationId=abc` control above, where a `%00` → 500 looked like the byte class and was not.

**No code tonight** — this is an answer, not a change.

**Fresh sweep, 2026-08-28 — the raw-5xx count looks UP but is actually down to 5, and KS-565 §2's root causes reproduce exactly.**

| | Run of record (2026-08-07) | This run (2026-08-28) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `not_a_server_error` failures | **17** across 8 ops | **32** across 3 ops |

The headline is misleading in the same way the 79 → 17 correction in the description was, so read the split:

```
POST /api/wallets/verify        27   ← by-design 501, owned by KS-686
GET  /api/users/admin/list       3
POST /api/users/admin/create     2
```

**27 of the 32 are a single by-design 501** on `POST /api/wallets/verify`, which [KS-686](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-686) already owns and which needs the `integration_5xx_guard` treatment rather than a code fix. Netting those out, the genuine raw-5xx count is **5 across 2 operations — down from 17 across 8**.

Worth flagging because it is the same shape as the "62 of the previous 79 were one defect" note already in the description: this class keeps being sized by a single mis-mapped endpoint. Any future count should net out KS-686 before it is used to judge progress.

### KS-565 §2's root causes reproduce, on a different OS and Akto version

Both remaining operations are exactly the two already traced there, and the negative-offset case reproduced verbatim:

```
GET /api/users/admin/list?offset=-1   →  500, empty body
POST /api/users/admin/create          →  500, empty body
```

That is `parseInt(offset) || 0` letting `-1` through to Postgres, and `data.email.toLowerCase()` with no type guard — confirmed on macOS/arm64 at Akto 2.22.2, where the original trace was Ubuntu/aarch64 at 2.18.7. The diagnosis holds across environments.

KS-565 §2's warning that **the negative-offset pattern is six sites across four services, not the two the sweep reaches**, is unchanged and still the more important half.

Adjacent and possibly relevant: PR [#757](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/757) (KS-703) hardens **list-route string query params** against NUL bytes. `offset` is a list-route query param on the same class of endpoint — worth checking whether that fix's shape extends to numeric params, or whether it deliberately does not.

### The 8-op list has otherwise gone quiet

Not seen in this run: `/api/documents/{id}/lifecycle-events`, `/revoke`, `/share`, `/api/m365/outlook/exchange-token`, `/api/security/rate-limit/check`, `/api/webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret`. The description flagged three of those as KS-564 endpoints worth confirming were not a regression from PR #652 — on this evidence they are clean.

### Reproduce

```
run:  pre-merge-2026-08-28T14-43-59Z
seed: 739598263
12,451 cases · 3,222 skipped · 67 unique failures · 14.1 min
reports under systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/pre-merge-2026-08-28T14-43-59Z/
```

Mapped from `schemathesis-output.ndjson` (`ScenarioFinished` → `recorder.checks`), not the console summary. Environment: macOS / Docker Desktop / arm64, Akto 2.22.2, Schemathesis 4.25.x — not identical to the run of record, so treat deltas as indicative.

**Nothing raised** — evidence for this ticket, not a new finding.

## A ninth operation for this list — `GET /api/signatories`, found by the KS-703 sweep

## BLUF

**`GET /api/signatories?organizationId=<malformed>` returns a raw 500 on any
unparseable value.** Measured live on local today. This ticket lists 8
operations; this is a ninth, and it is a **read** path, which the current list
is otherwise light on.

No Postgres text is leaked here — the body is the platform's generic envelope —
so it is the milder half of the class: a 500 where a 400 belongs, not an
information leak.

## Measured

| request | result |
| --- | --- |
| `?organizationId=%00` | **500** |
| `?organizationId=%01` | **500** |
| `?organizationId=abc` | **500** |
| `?organizationId=a0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001` (control) | **200** |
| `?userId=%00` / `?documentType=%00` / `?status=%00` | **400** each |

Body on every 500:

```json
{"success":false,"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"Failed to list signatories"}}
```

The controls are what make this legible: a **valid** uuid returns 200, and the
route's **other three** parameters return an honest 400 on the same input. So it
is `organizationId` specifically, it is any malformed value rather than a
control-byte issue, and the handler clearly *can* answer 4xx — it just doesn't
on this one field.

Same shape as the KS-497 tenant-id and KS-536 `recipients[].userId` fixes: a
value reaches a `::uuid` cast, Postgres throws `22P02`, the outer catch turns it
into a 500.

## How it was found, and a caution for whoever picks this up

It surfaced during the KS-703 read-only sweep and **initially looked like a
second instance of that ticket's NUL-leak class**, because `%00` → 500 with a
clean control of 200. The `organizationId=abc` control is what separated them —
without it this would have been filed on the wrong ticket and would have
overstated KS-703's blast radius by a factor of two.

Worth carrying into any fix here: `%00` 500ing is not evidence of the
control-byte class on its own. Test a plainly-invalid non-control value too.

Source: `services/originate/src/routes/signatories.ts:152`
(`const { organizationId, status } = req.query;`). Read-only measurement,
local stack, nothing written.

**Cross-reference — Kam has ruled the `POST /api/wallets/verify` 501 by-design; this register's count stays inflated until the guard exists.**

Kam ruled [KS-686](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-686) on **2026-08-26**, verbatim: *"Tolerate the 501 until KS-627 lands (guard + tripwire, land it on the KS-684 branch)"* — recorded in full at KS-686 comment `96e8aa3a-9772-40a6-b60a-d5f0a0a60543`.

**One line for this register: `POST /api/wallets/verify` is counted here and does not belong** — it is a deliberate, documented 501 (the fail-closed replacement for a stub that answered `verified: true` for any input), not the unhandled-500 class this ticket tracks, and it carries the bulk of the instance count (**29 × 501** across both 2026-08-25 sweeps). KS-686 now owns the fix; this count corrects itself once the guard lands.

⚠ **And a second inflation, in the other direction — this register may be short by two rows.** The 2026-08-18 artefact shows `GET /api/users/admin/list` returning **HTTP 500** on `offset=-1` (and on `limit=1&offset=-1&search=&role=`), failing `not_a_server_error`. That is this register's class, and the root cause is already documented in `systemTest/schemathesis/docs/known_issues_and_baseline.md` under the KS-544 update (2026-08-04): `parseInt(req.query.offset as string) || 0` at `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:344` and `:398` — `-1` is truthy, so it passes the guard unchanged and Postgres rejects it (`OFFSET must not be negative`). The register also records that **the negative-offset pattern is six sites across four services**, of which the sweep can only reach these two.

**Why it is flagged here rather than filed:** Kam ruled on 2026-08-26 that `GET /api/users/admin/list` is *"tolerated, whole operation"* under the 2026-07-29 class. That ruling's stated basis is unknown query params and the intended `[integer, "null"]` union — neither of which reaches an unhandled 500. **If the tolerance is implemented as a blanket per-operation exclusion it will suppress these two rows as well**, and a registered, still-unfiled 5xx defect goes quiet. Raised back to Kam through Wednesday; recorded on [KS-592](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-592) too. Nothing implemented from this side.

*Measured from the 2026-08-18 pre-merge artefact (Schemathesis **v4.24.3**, pre-4.25.0 generator). No state change. Recorded 2026-08-26.*

## This register's count is inflated by one operation — now owned by KS-686

https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-686

**`POST /api/wallets/verify` is in this ticket's `not_a_server_error` failures, and it does not belong here.**

It returns a **deliberate, documented 501** — the fail-closed replacement for the stub that answered `verified: true` for any input (KS-488-C / KS-627). `not_a_server_error` flags any 5xx regardless of the operation's declared status list, and **501 is already declared** for it (`401, 403, 404, 415, 429, 500, 501, 502, 503`). So a correct security fix reads as a raw server error.

**Why this matters for this register specifically:** KS-593 is the *raw-500 class* — an unhandled value reaching a handler or the DB. Listing a deliberate 501 here sends the reader hunting for an unhandled exception that does not exist. It was nearly filed here as a raw 500 during triage on 2026-08-24 and corrected before anything was written.

## Measured on a from-scratch stack, 2026-08-25

Two `pre-merge` sweeps against `develop` @ `29287565e`, 32/32 healthy, Schemathesis 4.25.2:

| | Run 1 — 09:27Z | Run 2 — 10:44Z |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `not_a_server_error` operations | **3** | **4** |
| `not_a_server_error` instances | 33 | 35 |
| of which `/api/wallets/verify` 501s | **29 × 501 across both runs** | |
| genuine 5xx in the HAR (all ops) | 4 × 500 | — |

So of the 3–4 operations attributed to this ticket, **one is not a defect at all**, and it carries the bulk of the instance count.

## Disposition

**KS-686** now owns the fix — the `integration_5xx_guard` treatment (exclude the operation from the blanket check, restore coverage with a narrow guard so anything *other* than the ruled 501 still fails). Split out of KS-684 item 7 on 2026-08-25 because the 501 posture is platform behaviour and needs Kamil's ruling.

**Action for this ticket: re-check the count once KS-686 lands.** Until then the register overstates by one operation, and anyone triaging these rows should skip `/api/wallets/verify` rather than investigate it.

The other 3 `not_a_server_error` operations and the 4 genuine 500s in the HAR are unaffected and remain this ticket's business.

Refs as KS-NNN text. Measured and filed by agent on Peter's behalf, 2026-08-25.

## Still live — re-measured 2026-08-20, `not_a_server_error` on **4 operations**

@kamil.kreiser,

Fresh datapoint from a `pre-merge` sweep run while verifying [KS-666](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-666/prevent-destructive-rebuilds-of-the-shared-vm-stack-from-destroying) (stack-slot isolation). **Not new work** — recorded here because this ticket owns the class.

**Run:** `pre-merge-ks-666-2026-08-20T13-29-08Z-slot3`, Schemathesis 4.24.3, slot 3 (`:7082`), 13,724 cases, 65 unique failures.

`not_a_server_error` — reported as **"Server error"** — on **4 operations**:

```
GET  /api/users/admin/list
POST /api/security/rate-limit/check
POST /api/users/admin/create
POST /api/wallets/verify
```

Two notes on that list:

* `POST /api/wallets/verify` also trips `status_code_conformance` in the same run. It is the endpoint [KS-627](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-627/implement-real-wallet-signature-verification-cip-8cose-address-binding) is about — it currently fails closed with 501 after [KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488/review-c-sk-channel-paymentswebhooks-and-integrations-m365-kyc-wallet) C-2, so a 5xx here may be the intended refusal rather than a defect. Worth confirming before counting it.
* `GET /api/users/admin/list` **and** `POST /api/users/admin/create` each trip *both* this check and `negative_data_rejection` (see [KS-592](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-592/negative-data-rejection-recurs-176-failures-across-10-ops-ks-266-ks)). Same operations, two different failure modes.

## Relation to the 17/8 figure

That was a **full** sweep (`full-2026-08-07`); this is **pre-merge**, fewer examples per operation. The smaller count is sample depth, **not** remediation.

## Attribution

[KS-666](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-666/prevent-destructive-rebuilds-of-the-shared-vm-stack-from-destroying) changes only `systemTest/`, `Blockchain/Dev/scripts`, compose and docs — no `services/`, `packages/`, `frontend/`, `contracts/`, `migrations/` or `docs/openapi/` file. It cannot have introduced these.

Artifacts: `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/pre-merge-ks-666-2026-08-20T13-29-08Z-slot3/`.

## BLUF

**62 of the 79 you measured are fixed** — the governance active-proposal cap now answers 409, not 500. Merged behind [PR #694](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/694).

## Detail

This ticket's own analysis says it: *"`not_a_server_error` read 79 failures on the previous sweep. It dropped to 17 once the governance active-proposal cap was cleared … 62 of the previous 79 were that one defect."* That defect is now fixed at the source ([KS-594](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-594)), along with its 20 siblings in the same service.

**Two things that change what a re-sweep will show, so read them before sizing:**

1. **Five governance routes used to answer a blanket `400 BAD_REQUEST` for any error carrying a message** — including genuine internal failures. Those are now handed to the shared error handler. A real internal failure on submit / cancel / execute / vote / delegate will therefore surface as a **500 where it previously hid as a 400**. If `not_a_server_error` goes UP on those operations, that is masking being removed, not a regression.
2. **A raw 500 on the submit path is fixed independently**: `svc_proposals.voting_config` is `JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`, and an empty config made `.toISOString()` throw `Invalid time value`. Same shape as [KS-514](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-514) in another service.

## What is left here

The 8 operations this ticket lists are untouched by the above — none are governance. Two of them (`/users/admin/list`, `/users/admin/create`) still have their root causes traced on [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565) §2 and remain unfixed, including the note that the negative-offset pattern is **six sites across four services**, not the two the sweep reaches.

**Next action: re-run the sweep after #694 lands and diff the operation list**, rather than assuming the 17 are the same 17.

*Backlog sweep 2026-08-14, verified on `develop` `454a64ebb`.*

**Now surfaced in the report against this ticket (KS-589 / PR #656).**

`not_a_server_error` was mapped to **KS-431**, Done since 2026-07-13, so the report rendered `KS-431 (closed — recurrence untracked)` beside every failure in this class. It now renders **KS-593**.

The report also carries a **sub-cause line** under this check pointing at **KS-594** — "62 of 79 failures on full-2026-08-07" — so the governance cap mis-mapping you sized here is visible next to the count rather than buried in a ticket. A raw failure count read as a defect count is misreporting, and for this class most of the number was one defect.

Re-measured on `full-2026-08-10T15-43-09Z` (Mac local, seed `74570198`): **2 failures**, against the 17 recorded here. Different host and seed, sampled not enumerated — **not evidence of a fix**, and nothing in KS-589 touches this check. Your description's six-site negative-offset inventory and the *"fix all six sites, not the two the sweep found"* instruction remain the right sizing.

No action needed here — attribution only.

title: positive_data_acceptance recurs at scale — 734 failures across 64 ops (KS-255 / KS-515 recurrence, full-2026-08-07 sweep)
description:
## Summary

This register tracks the biggest single class in the sweeps: the API politely refusing (4xx) request bodies the published spec says are valid. The steady fix is to bring each operation's spec and validator into line, in whichever direction is right for it. A small new member was added on 2026-09-28: `POST /api/gdpr/consent`, where the database declines a value the spec allows. Details are below for whenever it's picked up. Thank you, Kamil.

+++ The register (2026-08-07) and the 2026-09-28 addendum

### Why a new ticket

The predecessors are Done and archived: [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done 2026-06-15) and [KS-515](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-515/write-path-requestresponse-schema-drift-27-ops-ks-430-recurrence-new) (Done 2026-07-29, itself the [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked) recurrence). This is the same class recurring at a larger scale, filed fresh per the [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked)→[KS-515](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-515/write-path-requestresponse-schema-drift-27-ops-ks-430-recurrence-new) / [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks)→[KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks) precedent.

### Finding

**734** `positive_data_acceptance` **failures across 64 operations**, about 75% of all check failures in `full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z` (seed `2794626967`, 22,744 cases, 317 operations; Ubuntu 24.04.4 aarch64 VM, Schemathesis 4.24.3, Postgres 15.18). Each failure card embeds a curl; the run also wrote 94 replayable crash files. Counts are a floor, not a total: generation samples rather than enumerates.

### Fix direction

Per [KS-423](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-423/blocking-pr-pre-merge-schemathesis-coverage-6-contract-drift-failures) / [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked): compare each route's validator with the spec, then tighten the spec to the runtime truth **or** loosen the runtime where the spec is right. Never narrow the generator. Cluster by service registration file.

### Addendum 2026-09-28 ([KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9)): `POST /api/gdpr/consent`

* **What:** a spec-valid body answered **400** `VALIDATION_ERROR` *"One or more field values cannot be stored (too long or not an allowed value)"*. It's a draw: 2 of the 6 [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) sweeps (sweeps 2 and 5, ×1 each).
* **The case:** `userId` (uuid), `purpose: "marketing"`, `source` = a 5-character string with a supplementary-plane character, `expiresInDays: 552`, plus 3 undeclared keys (allowed, since the schema doesn't set `additionalProperties: false`).
* **Where the 400 comes from:** `services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts:153` (`mapGdprWriteDbError`) maps Postgres **22001 / 23514 / 22007 / 22008 / 22021** to this 400. Its own comment says *"Value the spec permits but the schema can't store"*. So the refusal is deliberate; the gap is that the published contract doesn't declare the constraint.
* **Which constraint fired isn't recoverable:** the originate logs predate a slot rebuild. Candidates: `source`'s unusual character (22021 or a length limit), `expiresInDays` with no declared `maximum` (22008), or the extra keys if they reach a stored column. (An earlier note that said "extra keys → 400" was too specific.)
* **Direction:** a targeted probe per candidate names the Postgres code, then declare it in the spec (`maxLength`, `maximum`, a `pattern`, or `additionalProperties: false`).
* Listed in [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing) for baselining against this ticket.

title: systemTest (Schemathesis): verify-by-hash must not resolve to an arbitrary registration — anchored-ancestor + cross-tenant field disclosure (KS-584 class)
description:
## Status: parked — not actionable yet

**Blocked on** [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) (Kamil, Urgent). That ticket has to decide *what correct resolution means* before a regression can assert it — Stuart offered three candidate shapes (prefer a row carrying chain data · return the anchored ancestor · report ambiguity) and they produce three different assertions. Writing tests now would pin a behaviour nobody has chosen.

Filed so the systemTest leg is visible from [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-security-regression-coverage) rather than forgotten when [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) lands. **No work until the platform decision is made.**

## Why it belongs in Review G

[KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) has two consequences from one root cause, and G already owns regression coverage for both classes:

**1. Anchored-ancestor selection.** `POST /api/verification/verify` resolves a content hash with `ORDER BY d.certified_at DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1` and no preference for a row carrying chain data (`services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts`). The normal certify flow creates a *second* row with the same `content_hash` (the certification's `signed_document`), which wins the ordering and carries no `certification_metadata.blockchain`. So a document with three confirmed on-chain anchors verifies with `isAnchored: false`, `blockHeight: null` — reproduced live on UAT (`1.15412159T20251122.pdf`, `f4fd83a9…`, anchors at preview blocks 4547897 / 4547901 / 4547907).

This is the **anchor-honesty class** — the same shape as [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-anchor-honesty-consistency-a-mock-tx-tx-sim-hash-must-never) and the [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-security-regression-coverage) D rows. A document's on-chain proof exists and the platform reports it doesn't.

**2. Cross-tenant field disclosure.** `buildResponse` returns the selected row's `title`, `issuer` / `organization_name`, `documentId`, `status`, `certifiedAt` and the lineage chain. The fallback `crossTenantLookup` is also unscoped, also `LIMIT 1`. Verifying a document you legitimately hold can return **another tenant's filename and organisation name** — and the anonymous verify path has no caller identity, so it cannot scope.

This is the **A / BUG-ISOLATION-001 class** that [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions) covered for documents and api-keys. [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions) is Done, so there is no open ticket carrying it, and the verify family went public under [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424) — the sweep reaches these operations today.

## Out of scope

Everything platform-side — row selection, tenant scoping, and what an anonymous response may contain — is [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents)**, Kamil's**. ## Unparking check 2026-08-12 (agent, grounded against develop `52368d8c3`)

**The blocker this ticket was parked behind has moved.** [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584) is now *In Review* with two merges on develop:

- **[#662](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/662) (interim, `2026-08-11`)** — "verify-by-hash answers from the row that evidences its claims; tenant fields scoped".
- **[#666](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/666) (P3, `89ed853a7`, `2026-08-12`)** — the **`/v2` verify-list contract**: multiplicity dissolves row selection, anchor truth caller-independent. v1 verify unchanged; deploy waits on Kintsugi.

Of Stuart's three candidate shapes, the landed answer is closest to **"report ambiguity"**, taken further: `/v2` returns the list rather than picking, and the interim fix already makes v1 prefer the evidencing row and scope tenant fields.

**Consequences for the sketch table:**

| # | Property | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Certify does not un-anchor | waiting on decision | **assertable** — interim [#662](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/662) fixes v1 row choice; assert on v1 after certification propagates |
| 2 | Multiple registrations resolve deterministically | waiting on decision | **shape changed** — on `/v2` this is no longer "which row wins" but "the list is complete and caller-independent" |
| 3 | Ambiguity is not hidden | conditional | **applies** — that is effectively what `/v2` does; assert the list surfaces every match |
| 4 | Anonymous verify discloses no tenant-owned fields | already independent | unchanged — still the row that could always have been written |
| 5 | Cross-tenant fallback is scoped | waiting on decision | **assertable** — [#662](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/662) claims tenant fields are now scoped; this is the regression that proves it |

**Two caveats before treating this as fully unblocked:**

1. KS-584 is *In Review*, **not Done** — the contract could still move. Rows 2/3 in particular pin `/v2` shape.
2. Coverage must be explicit about **which version it asserts against**. v1 and `/v2` now answer differently by design; a test that does not say which it means will look right and prove nothing. Note also the BACKLOG ruling item carried on [#666](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/666) — *verify-file 415-gated at the gateway (v1+v2)* — found during the P3 live proof.

Nothing written; this is a re-grounding of the park, not a start. Refs: [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584) · [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492) (Review G parent) · [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589) (sibling anchor-honesty class) · [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513) (closed isolation ticket this class belonged to).

## What v2 gives this ticket
- `POST /api/v2/verification/verify` → `{hash, count, matches[]}` — **no selection at all**: the arbitrary-registration class this ticket exists for cannot recur in v2, and the assertable invariant is structural: every same-hash registration appears; `matches[0].documentId` equals v1's answer for the same hash (deterministic order: certified by ms-precise certified_at DESC → real confirmed tx → in-flight → oldest created).
- **Cross-tenant field disclosure** (your title's second class): scoped matches null tenant-owned naming AND carry an explicit `fieldsWithheld: true` — so a regression can assert withholding directly instead of inferring it from nulls.
- **Anchor truth is caller-independent by construction**: the chain-fact read is pre-auth and v2 forwards no bearer. Assertable as: v2 response (modulo verifiedAt) identical with and without a valid bearer — `scripts/verify/ks584-p3-parity-sweep.mjs` already sweeps exactly this (60/60 local groups clean; read-only, works against any env).
- Auth posture for your harness: absent bearer → 200; present-but-invalid → **401** (this also fixed a pre-existing raw-500 on malformed bearers — the not_a_server_error class — details on KS-584).
- The spec op (`/api/v2/verification/verify`, security: [], inline example) is in `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` on the branch, so Schemathesis picks it up at cutover.

v1 stays untouched until cutover, so your v1 pins (per your 08-11 comment) carry no churn risk and stay valid afterwards too.

## BLUF — this ticket is no longer blocked; the decision it was parked on now exists in code and in Kamil's written ruling

This ticket says *"parked — not actionable yet … Writing tests now would pin a behaviour nobody has chosen."* That was correct when filed. It is no longer true, and I want the evidence recorded here so the next person doesn't re-derive it.

**Nothing written, nothing verified by me beyond reading the merged code and his design notes.**

## 1. The row-selection decision has been made and is merged

The KS-584 interim merged to `develop` (#662, `d0a704d57`) and is live. `selectVerifiableRow` (`services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:190`) implements a **deterministic** precedence, replacing the `ORDER BY certified_at DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1` this ticket describes:

1. a `certified` row (most recent, since the SQL pre-sorts `certified_at DESC`);
2. else a row with a **real** 64-hex tx (`rowHasRealTx`, excluding `simulated: true`), confirmed-first then oldest `created_at`;
3. else the oldest row.

Rowset is `LIMIT VERIFY_ROWSET_LIMIT` (24, `:276`). Certification evidence is now read across the whole same-hash set via `siblingCertification` (`:206`), and `confirmStalePendingAnchor` (`:279`) heals a stale pending anchor at read time.

So sketch rows **1, 2 and 5** have a defined behaviour to assert. Row 3 ("report ambiguity") did **not** win — the chosen shape is deterministic selection, not surfaced multiplicity.

## 2. Kamil's P3 ruling means pinning v1 carries no churn risk

This was my main worry, and his own notes resolve it. From `Blockchain/Dev/docs/design/2026-08-11_p3-verify-list-design.md` on his parked branch `feature/ks-584-p3-versioned-verify-list-caller-independent-anchor-truth`:

> **"Versioned coordinated cutover. v1 single-doc verify shape UNTOUCHED until Stuart adopts."**
> **"v1 keeps the interim's selection logic (already deterministic + honest post-KS-584-interim)."**

P3 adds `POST /api/v2/verification/verify` returning `{ matches: [...], count, hash }` **alongside** v1 — *"No LIMIT-1 selection at all — the selection problem dissolves."* It is not a rewrite of v1. **Assertions against v1 are therefore safe to write now.**

Two further ruled constraints that shape the tests:

- **"Anonymous verify stays a supported public 200 path."** So row 4 must assert what an anonymous verify may *disclose* — never that it is refused.
- **"Anchor truth must be caller-independent."** This is a P3 *goal*, not current behaviour, and its delivery mechanism is an anchoring-side reconciler. An anon-vs-authed parity assertion written today would pin something the platform does not yet do — that one **should** still wait, or land as a strict Known Failure only if he wants it pinned.

His own validation plan is also a ready-made test shape: *"All duplicate-hash groups on demo (12+), not a sample: script the sweep (readonly) comparing v1 vs v2 answers per group + anchor-truth parity authenticated vs anonymous."*

## 3. Row 4 is narrower than this ticket assumes — and two disclosure gaps are NOT covered by the interim

The interim added `scopeTenantFields` (`:260-271`), but it nulls **only** `title`, `issuer`, and `certification.certifiedBy`. From a code read (not probed):

- **`certification.certifierOrganizationId` survives scoping** (`buildCertification`, `:141`) — a scoped verify still names the registering organisation by id. Whether an org UUID counts as tenant-owned naming is Kamil's call, not something a test should silently decide.
- **Both chain-first branches bypass `scopeTenantFields` entirely** (`:554-587` verify-file, `:982-1014` `/verify`): they `return res.json({...})` directly, emitting `onChainMetadata` wholesale plus `issuer` / `certifiedBy` / `certifierOrganizationId` from `chain.metadata`. Guarded by `rows.length === 0`, so reachable only for a hash on chain but absent from the local `documents` table.
- **`isCrossTenantResponse` returns `false` when the row has no tenancy info** (`:255`), so legacy rows are never scrubbed.
- **The by-id path rowset (`:1094-1099`) selects no `tenant_id`**, so that path is never scoped at all. Reachable on any stack — potentially the more serious of the four.

## 4. Practical note for whoever picks this up

On a **mock** stack the chain-first branch is unreachable: `anchor_store` holds no real 64-hex tx, so `GET /api/anchors/verify/{hash}` can never answer `verified: true`. A strict xfail on an unprovisionable vector would score absence as a result. Measure the real-tx count first and let it decide test-vs-report.

Also worth knowing: `GET /api/anchors/verify/{hash}` is **absent from the published OpenAPI spec**, so the sweep never touches it — the only existing coverage is one negative case (unknown hash → 404) in `test_anchor_verify_no_fabrication.py`.

## Recommendation

Un-park rows 1, 2 and 5 against v1 now. Hold the caller-independence assertion for P3. Put questions 3's four disclosure items to Kamil before encoding any of them — they are platform decisions wearing a test costume.

title: rotate: true mints a new key but never revokes the old one — implement revoke-on-rotate and agree the cutover window
description:
## BLUF

@kamil.kreiser **ruled 2026-08-07: rotation SHOULD revoke the prior key.** He accepts that this makes an honest bulk re-key ~1.5 weeks rather than 2 days, on the reasoning that shipping the additive version would hand out N new credentials, leave N compromised ones live, and look like recovery.

**The cutover window is a contract question for** @stuart.jamieson**, not a unilateral K-side call** — revoking instantly means S's in-flight anchor writes 401 until it picks up the new credential.

@peter independently reached the same conclusion on KS-480 (2026-08-06): *"if someone left a company with a grudge and used the key maliciously, the company affected would not look kindly on our solution."*

## Detail

**The defect (Finding A, verified in code).** The rotate handler has **no revoke step**: on `rotate: true` it skips the early return at `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:638-645` and goes straight to the mint. `dbSaveApiKey` (`services/security/src/index.ts:196-223`) is a plain upsert on the *new* key's own id and never touches sibling rows sharing a `connectorId`. Validation keys purely off `key_hash` → `isActive` → `expiresAt` (`services/security/src/index.ts:940-1012`), so the prior key keeps validating indefinitely.

Guardrail 1's own comment concedes it — *"it invalidates nothing by itself"* (`platform.ts:501`) — so this is known at code level. What is absent is any sign the semantics were decided deliberately for the DR case that §4/§5 of KS-480 rests on.

**Consequence:** after re-keying a lost credential, the lost credential still works. Neither half of "lose a key, re-key" has a working admin path on demo today (the other half is [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578)).

**The open decision — cutover.** Options to put to @stuart.jamieson, with the consequence stated plainly rather than softened:

1. **Instant revoke.** S's in-flight anchor writes **401 until S picks up the new credential.** Cleanest containment, hardest on S.
2. **Overlap window** (old key valid for a bounded period). Softer on S; leaves a compromised credential live for exactly that window, which is the thing being fixed.
3. **S confirms adoption, then the old key dies.** Best of both, needs an S-side acknowledgement path and a fallback for when it never arrives.

**Done when:** the cutover shape is agreed with @stuart.jamieson and recorded here; `rotate: true` deactivates the prior key per that shape; a test pins that the old key no longer validates; and [KS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-583) step 4 passes.

Sizing: decision first, then 2–3 days.

---

*Split from* [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480) *per @kamil.kreiser's ruling 2026-08-07.* [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579)*–*[KS-582](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-582) *are @peter's own candidates carried over unchanged;* [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) *and* [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578) *are additions from the 2026-08-06 verification. Findings checked against* `develop` `c8ce65dca`*; Finding B confirmed live on the demo VM read-only.*

## S cannot adopt a rotated key at ANY window length

Two things on `develop`, both verified in code:

1. **The positive key cache never expires.** `CardanoAnchorAuthClient._orgKeyCache` is a plain `ConcurrentDictionary<int, string>` with no TTL and no invalidation path. Only the *negative* cache (`_orgKeyMissingUntil`) has a lifetime, and that is `AnchorFailureCacheSeconds = 30`. So once S has used an Organisation's key, it keeps presenting **that** key for the life of the process.
2. **Nothing can write a replacement in.** `PlatformKOrganisation.EncryptedApiKey` is written only by the registrar's first-mint path, §4 returns no key on re-registration, and the S-side inlet is [PS-740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-740) — filed, unstarted.

So after a rotation, that Organisation stops anchoring and stays stopped until a human re-provisions S's stored key — for which **there is no supported path today**. A restart does not help: S's database still holds the old encrypted key.

**Therefore the grace window does not do the job its name implies.** Its entire purpose is to give S time to adopt the new credential; S has no mechanism to adopt it. A window >0 does not avoid the breakage — it postpones it, while leaving the compromised credential valid for exactly that period, which is the thing this ticket exists to fix.

## Two findings on the code

**A. A rotate can report success while the old credential stays live (High).** The revoke filters `WHERE connector_id = $1`. KS-869 only *started* writing that column, and its backfill is opportunistic — `COALESCE` on the next save, and only when the in-memory copy already knows its `connectorId`. A key reloaded from a row holding `NULL` never learns it, so it is skipped by both the memory loop (`k.connectorId !== connectorId`) and the `UPDATE`. Result: `priorKeysRevoked: 0`, no alert (the gateway only reacts to `null`), and the operator believes a lost credential is retired when it still works — this ticket's own bug surviving in this ticket's own DR case.

Suggestion, either or both: treat `rotate && priorKeysRevoked === 0` as a **warning** at the gateway — that code path is reached only for an already-registered org, so zero prior keys is anomalous — and/or a one-off backfill for existing `platform-s:*` rows.

**B. The published contract now contradicts the behaviour (Medium).** In `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, unchanged by the PR:
- `RegisterConnectorRequest.rotate` — *"The old key stays active until explicitly revoked."*
- the `register-connector` operation description — *"`rotate: true` mints a replacement (revoke the old key separately)."*

**C. `priorKeysRevoked` never reaches S (Medium, judgement call).** The gateway consumes it and logs; `RegisterConnectorResponse` doesn't carry it. With PS-463 not yet in place, a K-side log line is the only signal that a rotate failed to contain. Reasonable to disagree.

**D. Minor.** On a DB failure the in-memory copies have already been mutated and aren't rolled back — cache says dead, DB says live, the key returns on restart. Safe direction, but worth a comment. ### The two paths that preserve both rulings, neither needing a code change

* Set **`API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS`** to the cutover window for that rotation, then unset it — #880 already implements this.
* Or perform the cutover mint with **`rotate: false`** (additive, today's behaviour) and do the real `rotate: true` retirement once S is confirmed migrated.

**The default stays `0`** — Kam ruled that on 2026-08-07 and the docblock says so. The window is the cutover's parameter, not a change to this ticket.

### Status unchanged

This ticket stays parked and **its merge remains Kam's**, because merging picks Option 1 for Platform S — a Stuart-facing contract call. If anything this strengthens that: the merge now carries a documented precondition. #880 has not been touched.

*Reciprocal of the note on KS-843 (`comment-82de36ad`), so the dependency reads from both ends.*

## Built — PR [#880](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/880) @ `47b2b60f2c6434da6c1292d282c7f2111e59cb93`

⚠️ **This does not close the ticket.** Condition 1 — *the cutover shape is agreed with
@stuart.jamieson* — is an external-contract decision and not a K-side call. **It is the blocker, and
it needs @kam to open that conversation.** Conditions 2 and 3 are done.

### The defect, re-verified rather than taken from this ticket

At `306d0db92`: `if (!rotate)` returns early at `platform.ts:645`, so `rotate: true` falls straight
through to the mint; `dbSaveApiKey` upserts `ON CONFLICT (id)` and never touches sibling rows;
validation keys off `key_hash → isActive → expiresAt`. Finding A holds exactly as written.

**[KS-869](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-869) is what unblocked it** — its own comment records
that the missing durable `connector_id` had left revoke-on-rotate *"with no durable way to find a
connector's prior keys."* Worth noting on this ticket, because it means the blocker recorded here was
cleared by other work rather than still standing.

### The window is one value, so the decision stays Stuart's

| `API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS` | which of this ticket's options it is |
| -- | -- |
| `0` — **default** | **Option 1**, instant revoke. S in-flight writes 401 until S picks up the new credential. Default because it is what @kam ruled. |
| `> 0` | **Option 2**, bounded overlap, of exactly that length. |

**Option 3 is deliberately NOT implemented.** It needs an S-side acknowledgement path and a fallback
for when the acknowledgement never arrives; shipping a default that approximated it would be pretending
the contract question was settled.

### One design call worth disagreeing with if you want to

**Mint first, then revoke.** A failed revoke leaves the old key live — the status quo this fixes. A
failed mint *after* a revoke leaves the connector with **no working credential**. The worse failure is
the outage, so the irreversible step goes second and **reports itself**: the response carries
`priorKeysRevoked`, and `null` means the revoke was attempted and failed, which the gateway logs as an
error naming the still-valid credential.

### Tests

8 cells, 8 passing. The two window settings are pinned **separately** — they produce different
observables (deactivated vs expiry-clamped), so one cell asserting "the old key stopped working" would
pass on either and could not detect the window being ignored. Scoping cells cover another connector in
the same tenant and the same connector id in another tenant.

**Red-proofed, five clauses**, each restored byte-identical by sha256: ignore the grace env (1 failed),
drop tenant scoping (1), drop connector scoping (1), drop the keep-new-key exclusion (3), grant life to
an already-expiring key (1).

### Housekeeping

A stale local branch `kamilkreiser/ks-577-revoke-on-rotate` already existed — local-only, tip already
contained in `develop`, no unmerged work. **Renamed to `parked/ks-577-stale-local-20260907`, not
deleted.**

### Still open on this ticket

1. **The cutover conversation with @stuart.jamieson** — @kam's to open. Until then the default is
   Option 1, and merging silently chooses it for Platform S.
2. [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578) remains the other half of "lose a key, re-key" —
   untouched here.

## BOUNCE — this is Stuart's decision, not K-side work, and it has been for four weeks

No state change and no code. Recording where it actually sits so the next pass does not re-open it as buildable work.

Kam ruled the substance on 2026-08-07: **rotation should revoke the prior key**, accepting that this makes an honest bulk re-key ~1.5 weeks rather than 2 days. That part is settled.

What is not settled is the **cutover window**, and this ticket's own description says why it cannot be settled here: *"a contract question for @stuart.jamieson, not a unilateral K-side call"*. @peter added the sequencing constraint on the same day — **PS-463 should land before any cutover, whichever shape wins**, because all three cutover shapes are undetectable without it.

So the remaining actor is @stuart.jamieson, with a dependency on PS-463. **Nothing on the K side can proceed until that window is agreed** — building revoke-on-rotate without it would ship a behaviour whose blast radius is exactly the question nobody has answered.

Newest comment before this one: 2026-08-07. Four weeks idle, and idle for the right reason.

## Sequencing point — PS-463 should land before any cutover, whichever option wins

Adding one thing to the decision rather than the decision itself, which is Stuart's.

**All three cutover shapes are undetectable without PS-463.** Under async anchoring, a 401 on an in-flight anchor write doesn't surface at the call site — it surfaces as a document that quietly never anchors. As noted on KS-480, the age of the oldest unanchored `DocumentTransaction` is the **only** signal a botched re-key would produce. Until that alert exists:

- **Instant revoke** — the failures it causes are silent by construction. You'd learn about them from a customer, not a dashboard.
- **Bounded overlap** — you cannot tell whether the window was long enough, because the evidence of it being too short is the same invisible backlog. The window length becomes a guess you never get feedback on.
- **Adoption-confirmed** — an ack that arrives but is wrong (S picked up the key in one process and not another, or the ack fires before the credential is actually in use) looks identical to success.

So PS-463 isn't a nice-to-have alongside this work; it is the instrument that tells you whether the cutover you chose worked. Recommend it is **in place and verified firing before the first real rotation**, not scheduled alongside it.

### Why this matters more than it sounds

It changes what "we chose the safe option" means. Bounded overlap looks like the cautious choice precisely because its failure mode is invisible — nobody gets paged, so it reads as having gone fine. That's the same shape as the two premise errors logged this week: the migrations runner reporting `applied=41 failed=0` on a migration that never ran, and the boot log reading `apiKeys: 0` on a table that was simply empty. A green signal that isn't measuring the thing you care about.

### One consequence for the window question

If PS-463 is in place first, the window length gets easier to answer, because it becomes measurable rather than negotiated: run a rotation, watch the unanchored-age metric, and the observed catch-up time is the window S actually needs. Without it, whatever number is agreed here is unfalsifiable.

No change requested to the recommendation — adoption-confirmed as default with instant as break-glass is the right shape. This is about what has to be true before either is exercised.

Raised by Peter. Nothing built, nothing verified on my side; PS-463 is S-side and its current state is Stuart's to confirm.

## BLUF

**@stuart.jamieson — one decision is yours here, and it is a contract question rather than a K-side implementation detail: what should happen to S's in-flight anchor writes at the moment a key is revoked?**

@kamil.kreiser ruled on 2026-08-07 that rotation **should** revoke the prior key. Today it does not — `rotate: true` mints a new key and leaves the old one fully valid with identical scopes, so re-keying a lost credential does not contain it. Fixing that is settled. **The cutover window is not**, and I am not taking it unilaterally because the cost lands on S, not on K.

## Recommendation

**Adoption-confirmed cutover as the default, instant revoke as the break-glass.** My reasoning: a scheduled re-key should never cause an outage, but a *known* compromise should not wait on S's convenience. One mechanism cannot serve both, so name both.

That said, this only works if S can actually signal adoption — which is the first question below, and I do not know the answer from the K side.

## Detail

### The three shapes

1. **Instant revoke.** The old key dies the moment the new one is minted. **Consequence, stated plainly: every S anchor write still holding the old credential gets a 401 until S picks up the new one.** Under async anchoring those failures surface late, and per @peter's note [PS-463](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-463) is the only detection a botched re-key would have. Cleanest containment, hardest on S.
2. **Bounded overlap.** Old key stays valid for a fixed window. No outage; leaves a compromised credential live for exactly that window — which is the thing being fixed. If you want this, the window length is the whole decision.
3. **Adoption-confirmed.** S acknowledges the new key, then the old one dies. Containment without a guaranteed outage, but it needs an S-side acknowledgement path and a defined fallback for when the ack never arrives.

### What I need from you

1. **How does S learn about a new key today?** Is it a stored secret requiring a config change or deploy, or is there any refresh path that could pick up a rotation without human action? This decides whether option 3 is available at all or is a build.
2. **If overlap (2): what window does S actually need** — seconds, a deploy cycle, or longer?
3. **If adoption-confirmed (3): can S expose an ack**, and what should K do when it never arrives? A fallback that never revokes puts us back where we started.
4. **Does anything on the S side hold more than one K credential at a time?** If not, an overlap window is only useful if S can be told to switch mid-window.

### Why this is being asked now

@peter has asked for the bulk re-key path ([KS-576](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-576)), and it is blocked on this ticket by ruling. A bulk path built on non-revoking rotation would hand out N new credentials, leave N compromised ones live, and read as recovery — so the semantics have to be settled before the loop is built, and the cutover is the half that is yours.

No rush on my side today: [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578) (the key-listing fix) is independent and is what I am building now.

---
*Verified against `develop` `c8ce65dca`. Nothing built on this ticket yet.*

title: Bulk re-key: one admin-authorised rotate across a named set of externalRefs
description:
## BLUF

@peter asked for **one** admin-authorised action that re-keys a named set of Organisations by `externalRef`, instead of N separate `register-connector` calls during an incident. The loop itself is **1–2 days**.

**It must not ship before** [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) **(revoke-on-rotate).** Built on today's additive rotate, a bulk re-key would hand out N new credentials, leave N compromised ones live, and *look* like recovery.

## Detail

Today's single-org path is `POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector` with `rotate: true` — `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:476-729`:

* platform-admin only; guardrail 1 refuses a connector-authorised rotate with 403 (`:499-509`)
* resolves the org by `metadata->>'externalRef'` under platform scope (`:590-593`)
* mints a fresh `sk_` key via the security service (`:674-686` → `services/security/src/index.ts:800`)
* plaintext key returned exactly once (`:719-720`)

`runWithPlatformScope` (`packages/shared/src/db/tenant-guc.ts:102`) already handles the cross-tenant access, so multi-tenancy is **not** the hard part here.

**Scope**

* Extract `platform.ts:476-729` into a reusable per-org function; add a bulk route taking a list of `externalRef`s.
* Return a **per-ref result array** — partial success must be explicit. An incident operator has to know which refs failed and why.
* OpenAPI entry + `generate-openapi` regen + api-gateway rebuild (the gateway bakes the spec) + KS-380 preflight.

**Explicitly out of scope:** delivery of the key material for N keys. One response body carrying N live secrets is not the answer; that needs its own design and a security review (see the KS-480 sizing table).

**Cheaper alternative on the record** (raised because @peter asked not to have the manual path assumed away): a scripted loop over the existing admin endpoint gives one *operator action* today at near-zero build cost. It does not give one *authorisation*, which is the part actually being asked for.

**Done when:** an admin can re-key a named set of refs in one authorised call, each prior key is revoked per the [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) semantics, per-ref outcomes are explicit, and the [KS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-583) rehearsal passes all four steps.

---

*Split from* [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480) *per @kamil.kreiser's ruling 2026-08-07.* [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579)*–*[KS-582](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-582) *are @peter's own candidates carried over unchanged;* [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) *and* [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578) *are additions from the 2026-08-06 verification. Findings checked against* `develop` `c8ce65dca`*; Finding B confirmed live on the demo VM read-only.*

nodes.body: Re-filed as its own issue now the cap has cleared: **[PS-740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-740/sk-key-recovery-a-keyinvalid-state-a-supported-inlet-for-a-rotated)** — the S-side half of the grant-driven re-key (KeyInvalid state, rotated-key inlet, grant drain, expiry visibility). Linked Related from here.

## Proposal from the S side: make the re-key **grant-driven**, with S as the executor

Context: investigating key expiry/recovery after S's local provisioning key lapsed on 2026-08-31 (PS-319). Verified in code on both sides, S today has **no recovery path at all** — re-registration returns no key (§4), `rotate: true` is 403'd for a provisioning-key caller by Guardrail 1 (`platform.ts:503`), and even an admin-run rotation dead-ends because S has no inlet to receive the key (`EncryptedApiKey` is written only by the registrar's first mint). The full S-side write-up is on PS-319 (pending re-file as its own ticket — the workspace issue cap is hit).

**The shape.** Keep Guardrail 1's human-in-the-loop, but change *who executes*:

1. A platform admin mints a **re-key grant** — one-time, time-boxed (hours), naming an explicit list of `externalRef`s (or all-for-tenant), recorded as its own audited object.
2. `register-connector` accepts `rotate: true` from a **provisioning-scoped** caller **only when accompanied by a live grant** covering that `externalRef`; the grant is consumed per ref. Revoke-on-rotate (KS-577) folded in.
3. S's registration sweep, given the grant via its secret store, drains every dead-key row itself and stores the returned keys exactly as first registration does.

**Why this over the admin-executed bulk endpoint as currently scoped:** with the admin executing, N plaintext keys come back to a human who then has to get them into S — a path S does not even have today, and one that puts operational secrets through hands and clipboards. With S executing under a grant, plaintext never leaves the two systems, the *same* mechanism recovers a **greenfield S against a populated K** (the `AlreadyRegistered`-no-key terminal case from S's DR facts), and the grant *is* the approval artifact KS-582 is asking for.

**It answers KS-582's open questions directly:** approver = whoever mints the grant (two-approver batch = a grant needing two mints/co-signs once KS-579 gives per-person admins; one for a single-ref grant); the flow is request → approve (grant minted) → execute (S drains), with the grant as the record between steps; the ref list is fixed at mint, so it cannot be edited after approval; break-glass is the existing S-side `UseConnectorKeyAuth=false` fallback, already alarmed three ways, so no new break-glass path is needed here.

**Input for Stuart's KS-577 cutover question** (his decision, not mine): when S is the executor, the cutover window collapses — S holds the new key the instant the response lands and the old one is revoked in the same operation; anything in flight in that sub-second gap 401s once and is retried by the refresher, which already handles exactly that. No grace window needed.

**Companion ask, small and independent:** a `whoami`-style read returning the *calling* key's id/scopes/`expiresAt`. Nothing today lets a key learn when it expires, so S cannot warn ahead — the 08-31 lapse was invisible until it bit.

title: Sweeps 2026-08-05: untracked failures across 10 ops — response-schema recurrence (KS-498 residual), 3 genuine 500s, non-envelope 5xx on by-design-503 ops, undocumented status
description:
Findings from two runs on the same code, 2026-08-05: `full-2026-08-05T08-44-00Z` and `pre-merge-2026-08-05T09-18-45Z` (Schemathesis 4.24.3, 316/318 operations, 316/317 past auth, no health-check suppression, untruncated messages). Everything else in those runs maps to [KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) / [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data) / [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code). The operations below map to **no ticket**.

> **Read the counts as a FLOOR, not a total.** The two runs agreed on the failing *classes* but not the failing *operations* — five ops failed in pre-merge that were absent from the full sweep. Property-based generation samples; it does not enumerate. Verify a specific operation with a targeted probe, never by its absence from one run.

## 1. response_schema_conformance recurs on 4 NEW ops ([KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444) residual)

[KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444) is **Done** — closed 2026-07-29 having verified the class down to 2 ops, both [KS-515](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-515/write-path-requestresponse-schema-drift-27-ops-ks-430-recurrence-new) family. **None of these four are those two**, so this is a recurrence on different operations, not unfinished work. Filed fresh per the [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked)→[KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444) / [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks)→[KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks) precedent.

| Operation | full | pre-merge |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/m365/connections/complete` | 14 | yes |
| `POST /api/presentations/verify` | 13 | yes |
| `POST /api/wallets/verify` | 4 | yes |
| `PATCH /api/security/events/{id}/resolve` | 4 | yes |
| `POST /api/oauth/apps/{id}/rotate-secret` — **added 2026-09-10** from `pr-ks-971-2026-09-10T16-31-45Z-slot1` (Schemathesis 4.25.x, `pr` profile, slot 1, develop at `688f4dded` + the [KS-971 (2/2): slot-isolate the k6 performance harness, and prove it by fault injection](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-971-22-slot-isolate-the-k6-performance-harness-and-prove-it-by-34bc0f07c5ba) systemTest branch). Runtime answers `200 {"success":true,"clientSecret":"scs_…","warning":"Store the new client_secret securely — it cannot be retrieved later."}`; the declared 200 schema requires `id`. Handler `services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:1079`; the route reached develop between the 2026-08-05 sweeps and 2026-08-28 ([KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) oauth-apps work), which is why it is absent above. The 2026-08-19 baseline already lists its `positive_data_acceptance` pair ([KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks)) but NOT `response_schema_conformance`, so this pair fails the gate until fixed or baselined. | — | pr: yes |
| `GET /api/kyc/microsoft/session/{sessionId}` — **added 2026-10-22** ([KS-1511](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1511/audit-log-limit-follow-up-retire-the-stale-accepted-baseline-entry) control sweep `pre-merge-2026-10-22T11-15-40Z-slot1`, platform-k slot 1 on Peter's Mac, develop `f75b52721`, `pre-merge --seed 1511`). ST108 ×1: `"sessionId" is a required property` against the declared 200 schema (requires `sessionId`, `status`, `createdAt`). Same message as the sibling `GET /api/kyc/microsoft/result/{sessionId}`, already baselined under this ticket; whether both share one handler defect in `services/kyc/src/routes/microsoft-verification.ts` is not established. Not baselined, so it fails the triaged-baseline gate whenever drawn; seen intermittently before (before-only pair in a version-bump comparison, `systemTest/schemathesis/docs/known-issues-and-baseline.md` \~line 1099). | — | pre-merge: yes |

Three of the four **also** fail `negative_data_rejection` — likely one root cause ("nothing validated, so nothing shaped correctly"), not four independent drifts. Worth confirming before treating them as separate work. Fix per [KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444): runtime is truth, reconcile the declared response schema, regenerate with `npm run generate-openapi`, rebuild api-gateway on both targets (it bundles the spec).

## 2. Three genuine 500s on schema-compliant input

| Operation | Site | Mechanism |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/users/admin/create` | `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:177` | `data.email.toLowerCase()` with no type guard — a non-string `email` (e.g. `{}`) raises `TypeError` → 500 instead of a typed 4xx |
| `GET /api/users/admin/list` | `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:344` **and** `:398` | `parseInt(req.query.offset as string) || 0` — `-1` is truthy so it passes through; Postgres rejects it (`OFFSET must not be negative`) → 500. The `|| 0` fallback only catches `NaN` |
| `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` | not yet traced | 500 in the pre-merge run; absent from the full sweep |

**The negative-offset pattern is SIX sites across four services**, not the two the sweep reached:

* `auth/src/routes/users.ts:344`, `:398`
* `originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:1006`, `:1166` — raw `LIMIT ${limit} OFFSET ${offset}`, x4 queries
* `tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:556`
* `api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:374` — `Math.min` caps the upper bound only, no negative guard

**Not an injection risk** — the raw-SQL cases use Prisma `$queryRaw` tagged templates (parameterised) and `parseInt(...) || 0` always yields a number. The defect is the unvalidated negative reaching Postgres as a 500. A fix touching only `users.ts:344` leaves five siblings exposed. Suggested fix: `.int().min(0)` on `offset` at handler entry.

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r '.data.accessToken')

curl -i -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 'http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/list?offset=-1'
curl -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":{},"password":"Str0ng-Passw0rd!","role":"OWNER"}' http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/create
```

## 3. `integration_5xx_guard` fires on by-design-503 ops — non-envelope 5xx

| Operation | full | pre-merge |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/timestamps` | 4 | yes |
| `POST /api/credentials` | 1 | yes |

Both are on `_UNCONFIGURED_503_OPS` in `systemTest/schemathesis/config/checks.py` (blanket `not_a_server_error` disabled because they 503 by design when their provider is unconfigured). The [KS-268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-268/localdev-coverage-for-503-by-design-integration-endpoints-billing)/[KS-499](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-499/unconfigured-provider-503s-on-7-write-ops-beyond-ks-268s-3-exclusions) guard replaces it and **passes** a clean declared-503 envelope — so a failure here means a 5xx that is **not** a proper 503 envelope, i.e. a genuine server error the exception list is demonstrably not hiding. Worth confirming whether it is a raw 500 or a malformed 503 body.

## 4. Undocumented status — `POST /api/referrals/apply` (6)

`status_code_conformance` fails: the operation returns a status not in its declared response set. Distinct from [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code) (`GET /api/documents/{id}/sig-json`, still open) — same class, different operation. Fix per [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code): either stop returning the undeclared status, or declare it — whichever reflects intended behaviour, per the "spec is the contract" rule.

## Not included here

* `POST /api/presentations` failing `not_a_server_error` — **already fixed** under [KS-544](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-544/schemathesis-4242-4243-adopt-full-cli-parameter-surface-always) by adding it to `_UNCONFIGURED_503_OPS`; live-verified it 503s by design (`VC_SIGNING_KEY is required to sign a presentation. Refusing to emit an HMAC-signed presentation falsely labelled Ed25519`) when `holderDID` is present.
* New `negative_data_rejection` ops (`POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector`, `POST /api/users/admin/create`) and the still-failing status-list trio — registered on [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data), whose register is live and In Progress.

## Please run the full sweep before closing

The fast PR gate covers none of these classes — it does not validate response bodies, does not generate negative bodies, and does not fuzz these write paths:

```bash
cd systemTest/schemathesis
python3 scripts/run.py full        # local stack on :6882
```

**BLUF:** this adds one more genuine 500 on schema-compliant input to §2, in the same class. `POST /api/documents` answers **500** when `title` is longer than 500 characters, because nothing checks the length before Postgres rejects it. A KS-1042 live test found it on 2026-10-21. KS-1042 did not cause it: no product code changed, and slot 1 was built from develop `280fdbcd1`.

**New §2 row**

| Operation | Site | Mechanism |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/documents` | `services/originate/src/originate.openapi.ts` (`title: z.string()`, no `.max()`) → `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:97` (`title VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL`) | A 10,000-character title passes validation, reaches the insert, and Postgres raises `22001`. Nothing handles that, so it comes back as a 500. The published `DocumentCreateRequest.title` declares no `maxLength` either. |

**Measured** (slot 1, 2026-10-21, ISSUER_ADMIN, body `{"title": "x" * 10000}`):
```
POST http://localhost:6882/api/documents  →  500 Internal Server Error
originate: Raw query failed. Code: `22001`. Message: `value too long for type character varying(500)`
originate: Failed to create document
```

**Not measured:** the other create paths that write `documents.title`: certifications issue, `/:id/version`, sign-cert and sign-wallet. They write the same column, so they probably return the same 500, but only `POST /api/documents` was driven.

**Repro** (any account that can write documents; the token is not shown):
```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/documents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"title\":\"$(printf 'x%.0s' $(seq 1 10000))\"}"
```

**Fix direction (your call, Kamil):** add `.max(500)` on `title` in every schema that writes `documents.title`, placed after `.trim()` per KS-202. That also publishes `maxLength: 500` in the spec once it is regenerated. An over-long title should get a 4xx, not be truncated.

**Acceptance criteria for this row**
1. **Automated test:** the 10,000-character case of `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_fuzz_comprehensive.py::test_string_parameter_fuzzing` (added under KS-1042) goes from **500 (red)** to a 4xx with an error body (green). Add an originate route test pinning 400 at 501 characters and 201 at 500.
2. **Docs updated:** the published spec, where `DocumentCreateRequest.title` gains `maxLength: 500` via `npm run generate-openapi`. No other doc names the limit.
3. **systemTests updated:** nothing beyond the KS-1042 test above, which already drives this. Once `maxLength` is published, the Schemathesis sweep will also generate at the boundary.

For context: these results were measured on the KS-1455 branch (`feature/ks-1455-bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4294-4300-or-later-release`, PR https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1438), which is going to be merged today.

**Measured on Schemathesis 4.30.0 (KS-1455, 2026-10-09)**, across three runs on slot 4 at `bf9568582`: the `pr` tier, `full` seed 1455 and `full` seed 20261009. Five of this ticket's nine baseline pairs recurred:
* `response_schema_conformance` · `GET /api/security/audit/{id}`: all 3 runs
* `response_schema_conformance` · `POST /api/m365/connections/complete`: all 3 runs
* `response_schema_conformance` · `POST /api/presentations/verify`: both `full` runs
* `response_schema_conformance` · `POST /api/m365/connections/init`: seed 1455 only
* `status_code_conformance` · `POST /api/referrals/apply`: `pr` only

Not seen on any run: `integration_5xx_guard` on `POST /api/credentials`, and `response_schema_conformance` on `GET /api/kyc/microsoft/result/{sessionId}`, `PATCH /api/security/events/{id}/resolve` and `POST /api/verification/verify`. Two seeds isn't enough to call those fixed, so their baseline entries are kept.

Suggested acceptance criteria:
* Each operation's response matches its published schema, or the spec is corrected.
* A full Schemathesis sweep shows none of these pairs, and each baseline entry is removed only for the route measured green.
